jobs.occupation: Community of Practice (CoP) Lead, Global Sales
jobs.description:
The Global Sales CoP (Community of Practice) Lead connects global commercial strategy with regional execution through coordination, facilitation, and governance. The role combines community leadership, planning support, stakeholder alignment, and project delivery.

• Leads the monthly CoP agenda and quarterly Deep Dives, turning discussions into clear decisions, accountable owners, timelines, and measurable outcomes.

• Participates in monthly business reviews with regional and local management and contributes to local commercial planning. This keeps the role close to market realities, provides markets with a direct link to Global, and ensures global priorities are represented in discussions.

• Success requires strong listening and facilitation skills, sound business judgment to focus discussions on the most important topics, effective stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, and timely follow-up.

• The role sits within Global Sales, which encompasses Sales Excellence (performance data and global processes), Field Force Effectiveness, the Sales Cloud design and roadmap, and Pricing Excellence.

• The role reports into the Field Force Effectiveness team to maintain a close connection to the markets, while collaborating across all Global Sales functions and particularly with Marketing, Training, and Service, which have similar Community of Practice roles.

• The Global Sales team is a dynamic, multinational group with diverse sales backgrounds. This role is central to the team’s engagement with markets, while the monthly CoP meetings address topics from across Global Sales through a focused agenda.

The Demant Hearing Aid business operates through a shared Commercial Plan. The Global Sales Community of Practice (CoP) Lead is responsible for driving the successful execution of the Commercial Plan by connecting global strategy with local market execution. The role serves as a facilitator, coordinator, and business partner, ensuring alignment between Global Sales, market leadership teams, and cross-functional stakeholders.

As a lead within Global Sales, the role creates a platform for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and disciplined execution. The CoP Lead ensures that strategic priorities are translated into actionable initiatives, regional work maintains momentum, and commitments from planning forums, deep dives, and governance meetings are followed through to completion. The role also supports ad hoc regional projects.

Key Responsibilities

We are looking for two positions, one focusing on EU/Nordics and one focusing on US/Canada & High Growth Markets (HGM).

Community of Practice & Knowledge Sharing

• Lead the regional Community of Practice, aligned with Commercial Plan priorities.

• Foster cross-market collaboration, best-practice sharing, peer learning, and continuous improvement.

• Consolidate market insights, challenges, and opportunities to inform regional and global priorities.

Commercial Planning & Execution

• Support regional Commercial Plan development, annual planning, budgeting, and execution.

• Translate strategic priorities into clear initiatives, actions, ownership, and measurable outcomes.

• Monitor progress and help address barriers, risks, and dependencies impacting execution.

Business Reviews & Deep Dives

• Plan, coordinate, and facilitate quarterly market Deep Dives and other key business discussions.

• Enable fact-based discussions on performance, opportunities, challenges, and transferable practices.

• Ensure discussions result in clear decisions, actions, accountable owners, and follow-up.

Regional Projects & Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Lead and support cross-functional regional initiatives across markets and functions.

• Align Global, Regional, and Market stakeholders around priorities and deliverables.

• Ensure clear governance, ownership, timelines, dependencies, and progress across commercial plans, projects, CoP activities, and business reviews.

• Drive accountability and escalate material risks or delays as needed.

Experience & Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Finance, Economics, Project Management, or a related field; Master’s/MBA preferred.

• 5+ years of experience in sales, commercial operations, business development, or a comparable commercial role.

• Demonstrated experience working across regional, international, or matrix organizations and leading cross-functional initiatives.

• Hands-on experience with sales execution, business planning, governance, and strategic execution processes.

• Proven ability facilitating workshops, business reviews, planning sessions, and stakeholder alignment.

• Requires hands-on sales execution or commercial excellence experience, ideally gained in a market-facing role within a large international company, preferably in med-tech.

• Candidates may also come from a local role and be ready to move into a regional or global position.

Success Measures

• Progress and delivery against agreed Commercial Plan priorities and regional initiatives.

• Effective quarterly Deep Dives resulting in clear decisions, ownership, actions, and measurable outcomes.

• Strong Community of Practice engagement, with effective sharing and adoption of best practices across markets.

• Timely and transparent execution and follow-up of agreed actions and commitments.

• Successful delivery of regional projects and cross-market initiatives, supported by strong stakeholder alignment and collaboration.

Knowledge & Competencies

• Strong cross-functional leadership, stakeholder management, facilitation and influencing skills, including the ability to drive outcomes without direct authority.

• Skilled translator of strategic priorities into structured plans, clear ownership, actions, and follow-up.

• Strong business acumen and ability to use performance information to support fact-based discussions and decision-making.

• Strong communication, collaboration, organization, and project management skills.

• Ability to balance recurring governance and planning activities with evolving regional business needs.

Expected Travel

The role involves approximately 5% of travel for planning and regional initiatives.

Ready to join?

This is a full-time position based at our headquarters in Smørum, in the Greater Copenhagen area.

Please submit your CV and a short motivation through our online application portal no later than November 13th, 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Jacob Melchior, Field Force Effectiveness Lead, at jcem@demant.com.

We expect to conduct first-round interviews in week 47 and second-round interviews in week 48.

At Demant, we value diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) and are committed to fostering an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnic background, personality, age, gender, or educational background. Diversity is part of our cultural DNA, and we particularly encourage women in STEM fields to apply, supporting United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

About Demant

Demant is a world-leading hearing healthcare and technology group built on a heritage of care, health, and innovation since 1904. The Group offers innovative technologies, solutions, and expertise to help people hear better. In every aspect, from hearing care, hearing aids and hearing implants to diagnostic equipment and services and audio solutions, Demant is active and engaged. Headquartered in Denmark, the Group employs more than 21,000 people globally and is present with solutions in 130 countries where we create life-changing hearing health and high-end audio and video solutions. William Demant Foundation holds the majority of shares in Demant A/S, which is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen and among the 25 most traded stocks.

🚀 About the role

We're looking for a Founder Associate to work side by side with our CEO and make FLEXeCHARGE run better every week. Our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe, built by a highly specialised team in Copenhagen and Germany.

You'll split your time between three things: driving company priorities with the CEO, owning our People function, and running our Copenhagen office. You'll get things done day to day, and you'll find smarter ways of working through better systems and automation.

You'll be part of our Admin & General team, which also includes Finance. You'll work closely with your colleagues there every day, from payroll and budgets to vendor agreements and board material, so strong collaboration is a core part of the role.

⚡ What is special about this role

You'll sit at the centre of the company. You'll work directly with the CEO, see how decisions get made in a growing climate-tech scale-up, and own the follow-through that turns those decisions into results.

You're also our People function. You'll shape how we hire, onboard, develop and celebrate our team, and how our Frederiksberg office looks and feels. You'll organise the moments that bring us together, from Friday bars and workshops to company events.

Few roles give you this much exposure this early. If you like ownership, move fast and want to learn how a company is built from the inside, this is the seat for it. And you'll join a team of genuinely fun, innovative people who care about doing great work together.

🛠️ What you'll do

Roughly 40% strategy and execution with the CEO, 35% culture and workplace, 25% People operations. The mix will shift with the company's needs.

Strategy & execution with the CEO

• Co-design our next scaling phase. Shape the organisational development of the company together with the CEO.

• Own the alignment. Prepare leadership, management and all-hands meetings, capture decisions and make sure actions are closed.

• Lead strategic projects. Run high-priority initiatives end to end, backed by research and a clear recommendation.

• Support the CEO. Prepare board and investor material, manage priorities and calendar, and follow up with stakeholders.

People operations

• Lead recruitment end to end and build a hiring process that scales.

• Be the go-to for People questions on contracts, leave, benefits and policies, employee handbook, and handle sensitive matters confidentially.

• Run the review and development cycle, from remuneration reviews to development talks.

• Keep People admin running and improving: payroll for Denmark and Germany, the employee handbook, our work environment organisation (AMO) and compliance, and smarter systems.

Culture & workplace

• Turn our values into everyday practice through onboarding, recognition and internal communication, including the all-hands and company updates.

• Bring the team together with events and workshops, from Friday bars to the Christmas dinner.

• Keep our Copenhagen office welcoming and running, including supplies and service providers.

✅ What we're looking for

Must-have

• 1–4 years of experience in a fast-paced role such as startup operations, People operations, consulting, a founder's office or a graduate programme.

• A strong get-it-done mentality: you take ownership, move quickly and close loops without being chased.

• Structured thinking: you can take a messy problem, break it down and come back with a clear recommendation.

• Excellent organisational skills, discretion with confidential information and the ability to juggle priorities independently.

• Comfort with data and tools: you're confident in spreadsheets and slides, and you look for ways to automate repetitive work.

• Fluent written and spoken English. Danish or German are a strong preference.

Nice to have

• Working knowledge of Danish employment law and People practices.

• Experience with office management or workplace coordination.

• An interest in energy, climate tech or EV charging.

• Hands-on recruitment experience, from job posting to signed contract.

📈 Where this role can grow

This role grows with you and with the company. As you prove yourself, you'll take on bigger projects and more ownership.

• Toward Chief of Staff, owning company planning and the leadership agenda as the team scales.

• Toward Head of People, building out the People function as we grow across Denmark and Germany.

• Into a business role, such as operations, partnerships or customer success, once you know the company inside out.

You'll have regular development talks with the CEO to decide which direction fits you best.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXeCHARGE?

• Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• You're covered with pension contributions.

• Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities.

• You'll have opportunities for individual development, with a clear view of how the company is run.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• A 30-minute screening call with our CEO.

• A practical stage: a short case exercise on a real business or People challenge, followed by a discussion at our office.

• Meeting the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• We do not offer relocation services.

As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position: Adaptive and Distributed Foundation Model Inference across the Computing Continuum
jobs.description:
Postdoc Position: Adaptive and Distributed Foundation Model Inference across the Computing Continuum
We are seeking highly motivated and talented applicants for a 2-year postdoctoral position (with the possibility of extension) in the area of distributed foundation model inference.

Join us at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University, where we are advancing resource-efficient and distributed foundation model inference across the computing continuum, leveraging the computation resources at Edge and Cloud. Our research aims to enable scalable, low-latency, and resource-aware deployment of large foundation models.

Expected start date and duration of employment 
This is a full-time, fixed-term position for one year, starting on March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The initial appointment will run until Feb 28, 2029, or for 24 months from the actual start date.

Job description
• The successful candidate will contribute to cutting-edge research on topics including:
• Distributed and collaborative inference strategies;
• Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) placement and scheduling for inference acceleration;
• Token compression or Intermediate feature compression;
• Resource-aware and communication-efficient inference optimization.

You will work in a dynamic and collaborative research environment, with opportunities to publish in top-tier venues and collaborate with leading academic and industry partners within the Horizion Europe Project.

Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and talented candidate with a background in deep learning. The required qualifications include:

• Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field;
• Strong background in Deep Learning (e.g., Transformers, foundation models);
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch);
• Experience with distributed systems and edge AI;
• Strong publication record in reputable conferences or journals relative to career stage;
• Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.

Following qualifications will be considered as an advantage:

• Experience in working with stream data;
• Experience with collaborative, cross-cultural research environments.
Who we are
You will be based at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Aarhus University, a dynamic and growing department committed to excellence in research, education, and innovation. Our research spans Internet of things, machine learning, signal processing, to digital twins, all with a strong emphasis on high impact research and societal relevance.

This position will be supervised by Professor Qi Zhang, whose current research focuses on Edge Intelligence, Distributed Foundation Model inference, Internet of Things and Analytics on compressed data.

What we offer
We offer a vibrant and inclusive research environment with a clear commitment to real-world impact. Denmark is consistently ranked among the best countries in the world for work-life balance and quality of life. Family-friendly policies include generous parental leave, subsidised childcare, and access to excellent public healthcare and education. As a postdoc at Aarhus University, you will benefit from a supportive and flexible workplace culture that values diversity and offers excellent conditions for researchers and their families.

Specifically, we offer:

• Access to state-of-the-art facilities and computing infrastructure;
• Strong support for research career development, including mentoring and international networking opportunities;
• A commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all aspects of our work;
• A workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Helsingforsgade 10, 8200 Aarhus N, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Qi Zhang, +4541893253, qz@ece.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be submitted by December 6th, 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Om Aarhus Universitet

Aarhus Universitet er et fagligt bredt og forskningsintensivt universitet med høj kvalitet i uddannelse og forskning, og et stærkt engagement i samfundsudviklingen nationalt og globalt. Universitetet tilbyder et inspirerende uddannelses- og forskningsmiljø for 37.500 studerende inklusive ph.d.-studerende og har 9.000 medarbejdere opgjort i årsværk samt en årlig omsætning på 8,9 mia. kr. The Role: The Heart of the House

As our Guest Relations Officer you are the guardian of the guest’s journey. Your mission is to turn a standard hotel stay into an "Admiral Experience."

Whether you are welcoming a long-time regular back home or orchestrating a "wow" moment for a couple celebrating their 50th anniversary, you do it with a blend of professional grace and genuine, human warmth.

Your key responsibilities;

• 
You’ll be the friendly face our VIPs and loyalty members look for, building relationships that go beyond a simple "hello."

• 
You’ll have the creative freedom to identify special milestones and craft personalized gestures that stay with guests long after they’ve checked out.

• 
You’ll collaborate closely with our Housekeeping, F&B, and Concierge teams to ensure that every detail of a guest's stay is seamless.

• 
When things don't go perfectly, you’re the calm in the storm. You listen with empathy and turn feedback into a reason for a guest to return.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

• 
Truly enjoy making people feel special and seen.

• 
Can communicate our hotel’s historic charm with passion.

• 
Have  at least 2 years of experience in luxury hospitality or high-end guest service.

• 
Are tech-comfortable - we use Mews, so experience there (or a quick ability to learn) is a plus.

• 
Notice when a pillow is slightly askew or when a guest looks a bit lost before they even have to ask for help.

Why Admiral Hotel?

At Admiral Hotel, you will become part of an open and collaborative environment where you have the opportunity to make a personal difference in both our operation and development. We place great emphasis on employee well-being and are proud to maintain a high level of engagement and job satisfaction across the organization. This is something we can clearly see reflected in our results – and just as importantly, something you can feel when you walk through the hotel.

The position includes:

• 
A full time position starting as soon as possible, with start date flexibility for the ideal candidate.

• 
Access to our Super Colleague Program, granting up to 4 free stays per year at our hotels and resorts in the Nordics together with a lot of attractive food and beverage discounts.

• 
Massage scheme and a wide selection of employee discounts to support your well-being.

• 
Dedicated colleagues who value collaboration, positivity, and a strong sense of community—here, we support each other in both big and small tasks to ensure an enjoyable workday.

Ready to join us?

Submit your application using the form below. We look forward to hearing from you!

Admiral is situated in the heart of Copenhagen, where the sea meets the city, and where Copenhagen meets the world. Housed in a historic 18th-century warehouse along the scenic harbor, Admiral blends modern elegance with rich history creating authentic warmth. At Admiral, we strive for ambitious excellence in everything we do – from the smallest details to the most memorable guest experiences and with a culture rooted in attentive hospitality, we create a sense of home, where every interaction is infused with genuine care and a passion for service.

Admiral is more than a place to stay in Copenhagen. It’s a place to be.

jobs.occupation: Head of Group Compliance & Group Data Protection Officer
jobs.description:
**Lead a global compliance function and help shape how compliance enables the business

**Are you an experienced compliance, privacy or GRC leader who enjoys operating at the intersection of regulation, business and technology?

Do you thrive in a role where you can set direction, lead experienced professionals, advise Executive Management and the Board, and turn complex requirements into practical solutions?

Then this could be your opportunity to lead Aeven's Group Compliance function.

**The role

**As Head of Group Compliance & Group Data Protection Officer, you will lead the Global Group Compliance organisation of approximately 27 professionals across four teams and three countries.

You will have overall responsibility for the strategy, direction and development of the function, covering:

• Group Data Protection and the DPO function

• Regulatory Compliance

• Enterprise Risk Management

• Internal Audit

• ISO and external assurance

• Customer and supplier assurance

• Responsibility / ESG

You will lead primarily through your managers, creating clear priorities and accountability while empowering highly specialised teams to own their areas.

The role combines strategic leadership, independent oversight and senior business advisory. You will work closely with Executive Management and the Board, providing a consolidated view of Aeven's compliance, privacy, risk and assurance position and highlighting where action or decisions are required.

At the same time, you will work closely with the business to translate regulatory and customer requirements into clear, proportionate and commercially workable solutions.

****Your responsibilities

• Set the strategy, priorities and roadmap for Group Compliance and lead, coach and develop the management team.

• Advise Executive Management and the Board on significant compliance, privacy and risk matters and provide clear, decision-oriented Management Information.

• Act as Group DPO and oversee Aeven's data protection framework, including significant privacy risks, breaches, regulatory engagement and international transfers.

• Lead the organisation's approach to regulatory developments, including GDPR, NIS2, DORA-related customer requirements, AI Act, Data Act and digital sovereignty.

• Own the Enterprise Risk Management framework and consolidated enterprise risk view, while ensuring risk ownership remains with the business.

• Oversee Internal Audit and Aeven's broader certification and assurance landscape, including ISO and ISAE activities.

• Provide senior oversight of customer and supplier due diligence, audits and regulatory assurance requirements.

• Support significant incidents, investigations, escalations and remediation across the organisation.

• Continuously develop and modernise the function through simplification, automation, better Management Information and effective use of compliance technology.

A key part of the role is ensuring that compliance enables the business rather than unnecessarily slowing it down.

****Your experience

****We are looking for an experienced leader who is comfortable operating where regulation, risk and business strategy meet.

You bring:

• A relevant Master's degree, for example in Law, Business/Commercial Law or a related field.

• 10+ years of experience within compliance, data protection, GRC or a related area, including several years leading managers and international or multi-disciplinary teams.

• Strong GDPR and data protection expertise, including DPO experience.

• Proven experience advising C-level executives and Boards and communicating complex risks through clear Management Information.

• Experience with Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Audit and assurance.

• Working knowledge of ISO management systems (ISO9001, ISO27001 and ISO14001) and ideally ISAE 3000/3402 reporting.

• Knowledge of EU digital and cyber regulation, including NIS2, DORA, AI Act and Data Act.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

Experience from an international, regulated or technology-driven organisation is an advantage, as is experience with privacy certification, GRC technology, customer assurance, ESG or transformation.

**Who You Are

**You are a trusted and credible advisor who can challenge senior stakeholders constructively while building strong relationships across the organisation.

You lead through trust, clear direction and empowerment, and enjoy developing managers and creating high-performing teams.

You are strategic but pragmatic, with strong business understanding and the judgement to balance regulatory robustness with commercial realities.

You communicate complex issues simply, drive follow-through and are comfortable raising risks and challenging established ways of working.

Most importantly, you bring integrity, sound judgement, independence and a genuine desire to make compliance work for the business.

**Why Aeven?

**This is an opportunity to take on a broad and influential leadership role at the centre of Aeven's governance and business operations.

You will lead a highly skilled international team, work directly with senior leadership and the Board, and help shape how a technology-driven organisation responds to an increasingly complex regulatory environment.

If you are motivated by leadership, influence, complexity and the opportunity to make compliance a genuine business enabler, we would like to hear from you.

**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp! At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered. If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**Why this role is important to us

**_Are you ready to thrive in a dynamic, global environment? SimCorp offers a unique opportunity to join our finance team as a Group Transfer Pricing Director.

_For over five decades, SimCorp has been at the forefront of providing integrated investment management solutions. With a global team of over 4000 professionals from diverse backgrounds, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and innovative workplace.

The Group Transfer Pricing Director will be an integral part of our tax team, a specialized subset within Group Finance. Our team is responsible for overseeing the tax and transfer pricing compliance and strategy across all 40+ SimCorp entities.

Based at our headquarters in Copenhagen, this role offers an exciting opportunity to shape SimCorp's transfer pricing strategy and ensure compliance across our global operations.

Reporting directly to the Global Head of Tax, your primary responsibility will be to lead the transfer pricing team and devise SimCorp's transfer pricing strategies. Your team will be responsible for the tax modeling, documentation, and devising transfer pricing procedures.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**As a Group Transfer Pricing Director, you will play a critical role in supporting SimCorp’s global organization by providing transfer pricing solutions. Your work will involve analyzing and enhancing transfer pricing structures, ensuring compliance with global regulations, and continuously implementing improvements in our transfer pricing models.

You will be responsible for reviewing the transfer pricing documentation for SimCorp A/S and its subsidiaries. This includes leading the team to draft reports, collect and analyze financial data, and collaborate with subsidiaries' finance teams and other internal stakeholders to ensure accurate and compliant reporting. We take pride in contributing to SimCorp’s growth through high-quality work. We value a collaborative working environment where we balance hard work with an approachable and collaborative spirit.

As a Group Transfer Pricing Director, you will:

• Devise new transfer pricing policies and update existing policies to ensure compliance with OECD guidelines and local regulations.

• Develop vision, strategy and structure of the group’s transfer pricing models in the rapidly changing environment, including APAs.

• Guide the transfer pricing team to prepare and maintain comprehensive transfer pricing documentation for SimCorp A/S and its subsidiaries in collaboration with the finance teams.

• Review changes in global transfer pricing legislations and ensure the group’s transfer pricing models are efficient and compliant.

• Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, including finance, legal, and business, to ensure effective transfer pricing practices.

• Lead and manage transfer pricing projects, drive change, secure stakeholder buy-in, and ensure high-quality deliverables and outstanding results.

• Represent the group on transfer pricing audits and dispute resolution and influence decisions in complex negotiations with tax authorities globally

• Provide excellent and timely support to our business team and finance team on intercompany transactions such as transfers of intangible property, services, and loans.

• Develop a mature control framework to ensure transfer pricing documentation, returns, notifications, intercompany agreements and related deliverables are maintained.

• Collaborate closely with Group Finance, subsidiary finance teams to ensure that TP policies are accounted for correctly in the Group books during quarter end and year end closing, and local statutory account.

• Provide training to stakeholders both in finance and to business team on transfer pricing policies and changes in legislation.

• Manage external service providers and liaise with our statutory auditors on TP matters.

**What We Value

**Experience and Education:

• Minimum 10 years experience in industry and/or consultancy with emphasis on working with multinational groups.

• Relevant education such as lawyer, CPA, economist or education from tax administration or any combination thereof.

Skills and Knowledge:

• Excellent understanding and experience in dealing with international taxation and transfer pricing, OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, BEPS and local rules and regulations.

• Proven ability to lead complex transfer pricing projects, drive the team to deliver impactful results, and foster a positive, collaborative environment where team members and stakeholders feel engaged and valued.

• Act as an owner with a proactive approach to set directions, drive changes and improvements in transfer pricing practices.

• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build strong relations with internal stakeholders and teams.

• Excellent communication skills and able to communicate complicated issues in a precise and concise manner.

• Strong team player who can influence others and the ability to work independently.

• Good general accounting/finance skills and experience. Experience with financial systems (ERP, consolidation tools and management reporting tools) is a plus.

• Advanced communication skills, with fluency in English (both verbal and written). Knowledge of the Danish tax system is a plus.

• Proficiency in MS Excel, Word, and other MS Office tools.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients. SimCorp is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

**Next steps

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually. To make sure you receive our emails please check your junk/spam folder and add SimCorp to the safe list of your e-mail contacts.

**Please note: Only applications sent through our system will be processed.

**At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

**Job Description Summary

**As a Lead System Designer, you will provide technical leadership across the full product lifecycle, ensuring that product designs meet customer needs, business objectives, quality expectations, and regulatory requirements. You will lead technical decision-making within cross-functional teams and support the integration of requirements, risk management, verification, validation, and design transfer activities.

You will lead technical reviews, drive resolution of technical issues, and help teams make informed technical decisions while balancing performance, quality, schedule, and regulatory requirements.

For this role, you must be eligible to work in Denmark and on-site our facilities in Herlev, near Copenhagen.

**Job Description

**GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

**Essential Responsibilities

**

• Provide technical leadership within NPI and sustaining engineering programs throughout the product lifecycle.

• Serve as the technical lead within cross-functional teams, guiding technical decisions and product design direction.

• Review and approve product requirements are complete, feasible, testable, and aligned with customer and business needs.

• Accountable for development of system requirements and related Design Control deliverables.

• Define and drive Design Verification and Design Validation strategies.

• Lead Technical Design Reviews and resolution of technical issues.

• Lead defect management, technical investigations, and problem solving.

• Review and support risk assessments and FMEA activities, drive FMEA strategy ensuring effective integration of risk controls into product requirements, verification, and validation.

• Ensure traceability between customer needs, requirements, risks, verification and validation evidence.

• Support Design Transfer and technical knowledge transfer to manufacturing and service organizations.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Relevant Engineering degree.

• Significant experience in Systems Engineering, Product Development, or Technical Leadership within medical devices or another regulated industry.

• Strong understanding of Design Control, Risk Management, Verification, Validation, and Change Control.

• Experience leading complex product development activities across multiple engineering disciplines.

• Extensive experience working across software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, service, clinical, and quality functions.

• Extensive experience developing requirements, specifications, verification strategies, and technical documentation.

• Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions across cross-functional teams.

• Strong problem-solving, communication, and technical writing skills.

**Behaviors

**We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership – always with unyielding integrity.

**Total Rewards

**Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

**Inclusion & Diversity

**GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

******Additional Information

******Relocation Assistance Provided: No

**Join us to Make an Impact

**Innovation is in our DNA. We invented supercontinuum lasers and photonic crystal fibers and we constantly reimagine how our products can be used and improved. Our customers use our products in medical and life science research, quantum computing and space exploration.

We seek curious, creative and collaborative people to work in our cutting-edge company. Can you see yourself working in teams and providing solutions for innovators?

If you wish to apply, please contact us with your CV / Résumé. If you have a cover letter, please save this in one document with your CV / Résumé as you are only able to upload one document.

We look forward to hearing from you!

**Join Our Team as a Quality Control Manager

**We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Quality Control Manager to lead and develop our incoming quality control activities. This is a key role within our organization, ensuring that incoming materials and components meet quality requirements while supporting continuous improvement across our operations.

The successful candidate will play an important role in maintaining product quality, driving process improvements, and supporting production through strong quality leadership.

**Key Responsibilities

****Incoming Quality Control

**

• Take overall responsibility for Incoming Quality Control (IQC) activities.

• Ensure all incoming materials, components, and products comply with established quality requirements and specifications.

• Investigate and manage supplier-related quality issues and non-conformances.

• Work closely with Procurement, Supply Chain, Production, and Engineering teams to resolve quality concerns.

**Process Development and Improvement

**

• Lead the implementation of new procedures and standards for incoming inspection processes.

• Continuously improve inspection methods, quality controls, and efficiency.

• Develop and maintain inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and quality documentation.

• Support supplier qualification and supplier quality improvement initiatives.

**Quality Documentation

**

• Own and maintain controlled documents related to Quality Control activities.

• Ensure procedures, work instructions, forms, and records are current, accurate, and compliant with applicable standards and internal requirements.

• Support internal and external audits as required.

**Team Leadership

**

• Directly manage and develop one QC Technician.

• Conduct performance reviews, provide coaching, and support employee development.

• Foster a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Operational Support

**

• Participate in daily production meetings and provide quality-related input.

• Collaborate with production teams to address quality concerns and minimize disruptions.

• Support root cause investigations and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) activities.

• Monitor quality performance and drive actions to improve product and process quality.

**Qualifications

**

• Bachelor's degree in Quality Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, or a related technical field.

• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in Quality Control, Quality Assurance, or Manufacturing Quality.

• Previous leadership experience is preferred.

• Experience with incoming inspection processes and supplier quality management.

• Familiarity with ISO 9001 and other relevant quality management systems.

• Strong knowledge of incoming inspection methodologies, AQL (Acceptable Quality Level) sampling plans, CAPA, Root Cause Analysis, and Statistical Process Control (SPC).

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and quality management software systems.

• Fluent in English, both written and spoken.

**Personal Competencies

**We are looking for a candidate who is:

• Structured and detail-oriented.

• Proactive and solution-focused.

• Comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

• A strong communicator with excellent collaboration skills.

• Results driven with a continuous improvement mindset.

• Capable of balancing strategic initiatives with day-to-day operational responsibilities.

**What We Offer

**

• An exciting opportunity to shape and improve our quality processes.

• A collaborative and professional working environment.

• Opportunities for personal and professional development.

• Competitive salary and benefits package.

• The chance to make a significant impact on product quality and operational excellence.

We are rapidly growing, so we are looking for an additional engineer to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team.

Our NPI team is organized in Product Engineering within Engineering. NPI bridges the gap between product development and volume production, being the place where prototypes and first sales units are manufactured and tested.

NPI is working closely together with development engineers (optical, electrical, mechanical and software engineers) for maturing the product, but also with automation engineers on manufacturing processes.

When a product has proven it can be manufactured with satisfactory yield and volume justifies, it will be transferred to our Operations department, freeing up space and resources for the new next thing.

In NPI we have a team of highly skilled technicians and engineers. Our technicians are the crank as they are manufacturing by far the most prototypes and sales units.

As NPI Engineer you will:

• Mastering and improving existing production processes – training, and supporting technicians.

• Troubleshooting issues, performing failure analysis, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions.

• Analyzing test and manufacturing data to identify and implement improvements in quality and productivity.

• Collaborating with Operations and other departments to transfer mature products and processes into production.

**Qualifications

**To succeed in this role, you should have a technical background in one or more of the following areas: optics/photonics, electronics, or production engineering. You have a strong affinity for processes and enjoy enabling others to follow them accurately.

• Experience with complex technical systems (e.g., optical fibers, free space optics, or electronic test setups).

• A proactive and process-driven mindset.

• A few years of experience from a manufacturing environment.

• Proficiency in written and spoken English. Being able to speak Danish is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Join us in this role where you’ll support the Warehouse Management Department with standard procedures and processes across warehousing and operations. You'll play a key role in process mapping and implementation, SAP administration, inventory control, forecasting support, and ensuring that equipment and components are accurately managed across warehouse locations. You'll work closely with warehouse operatives, back-office colleagues, planners, and operational stakeholders to maintain efficient and compliant warehouse processes.

**Welcome to Warehouse Management

**You’ll be part of the Warehouse Management team where you, together with your colleagues, will ensure control over components used for Main Components Exchange and Cable Storage in SAP. You’ll make sure that equipment is registered and handled in SAP for both main components and cable storage facilities.

As a team, we value diversity, collaboration, and a non-hierarchical, respectful, and trusting work environment.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• supporting back-office functions in the department with forecasting

• creating and managing work orders for preparing gearboxes for shipment

• ensuring SAP reflects what we actually have on the shelve

• supporting our check-up teams with creating stock transformers in the system

• handling various minor ad hoc administration tasks.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• have an educational background in administration or related field (not mandatory)

• are IT literate, with knowledge of SAP or similar ERP systems, as well as the Microsoft Office package

• have professional experience in the offshore wind business (not mandatory but highly valued)

• possess strong organizational and time management skills

• have excellent communication and problem-solving abilities.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

Are you a senior programme professional with deep contextual understanding, strong strategic judgement and the ability to build trusted relationships in complex settings? Do you combine programme leadership with donor engagement, resource mobilisation and a commitment to rights-based, locally led change? Mellemfolkeligt Samvirke (MS) is looking for a Senior Programme Manager to lead and further develop our engagement in Syria and Lebanon.

About the role

You will be MS’s key focal point for a portfolio of three to four Danida-funded country programmes, including MS’s engagement with youth driven partners in Syria and Lebanon. You will hold responsibility for programme quality, strategic development and resource mobilisation across the portfolio. Working across MS and the wider ActionAid federation, you will turn contextual insight and strong partnerships into effective programmes and new funding opportunities.

Your main responsibilities

• Lead MS’s programme engagement and partner dialogue in Syria and Lebanon within the wider Danida-funded portfolio.

• Lead programme planning, implementation, monitoring, learning and adaptation with partners and ActionAid teams.

• Ensure sound grant and financial management, including budgets, risks, disbursements and donor reporting.

• Lead donor engagement, fundraising and the development of new proposals.

• Turn regional political, economic and social developments into strategic advice and programme decisions making sure, that young people are involved and included.

• Represent MS in relevant donor, policy and coordination forums and contribute to advocacy and communications.

Required qualifications

• At least six years’ experience in programme and project cycle management, including five years in a low- or middle-income country and experience from an NGO, civil society organisation or similar setting.

• Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder programmes and building trusted partnerships across cultures and locations.

• Strong grant and financial management skills, including budgeting, risk management and narrative and financial reporting.

• Experience with institutional donors and developing high-quality proposals and reports, including for Danida or the EU.

• Strong analytical, communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to turn strategy into action.

• Fluency in Danish and English and willingness to travel internationally for five to six weeks per year.

Desired qualifications

• Direct professional experience from Syria or Lebanon is highly desirable; substantial experience from the wider MENA region will also be considered.

• Professional working proficiency in Arabic.

• Experience with rights-based, locally led programming and the humanitarian–development nexus.

• Experience with young people, social movements, youth activism or campaigning.

Working at MS

You will join an informal, mission-driven workplace with committed colleagues, professional sparring and room to use your expertise. We offer flexible working hours, the possibility of working from home, professional development, paid leave between Christmas and New Year and a vegetarian lunch scheme.

Location and employment terms

The position is full-time and based at MS’s office at Fælledvej 12 in Copenhagen. It is a two-year fixed-term contract with the possibility of extension, with preferred start in 1 January 2027 or alternatively, 1 February 2027. You will join the International Programme and Partnerships team and report to Lisbeth Petersen, International Director for Programme & Partnerships. The role involves approximately five to six weeks of international travel per year. Salary and employment conditions follow the Danish collective agreement and the applicable AC agreement.

How to apply

Apply through our online recruitment system with your CV and a short motivation letter by Tuesday 10th November 2026, at 23:59 CET. First-round interviews will be held in week 48 & second-round in week 49. Questions can be directed to Lisbeth Petersen, International Director for Programme & Partnerships, at lpe@ms.dk.

About Mellemfolkeligt Samvirke

Mellemfolkeligt Samvirke (MS) works in Denmark and internationally to challenge inequality and strengthen people’s ability to claim their rights and shape their communities. MS is the Danish member of the international ActionAid federation.

We are committed to diversity and inclusion and encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of background, identity or personal circumstances.

_**Would you like to plan and execute clinical studies for a market leader within the medical device industry? And do you want to provide evidence to support products that make a real difference to people with intimate health care needs?

**_**Become part of a specialist community

**At our HQ in Humlebæk, you will join 9 colleagues in the Clinical Execution team in Clinical & Medical Affairs - Payers & Evidence.

We plan and execute clinical investigations within our Chronic Care and Wound Care portfolio.

**Ensure the optimal clinical investigations

**As an Associate Clinical Manager, you will, under guidance, take part in the planning, management, and execution of clinical investigations, becoming involved in the entire process from study start to completion.

To facilitate studies, you will collaborate and build great working relationships with relevant external health care professionals and hospital departments. Ultimately, your work will help provide some of the solutions doctors and nurses need to deliver the best possible care and treatment.

More specifically, you will:

• Contribute to the development of clinical investigation plans and study-related materials and assist with budget forecasting

• Support site identification, investigator qualification, selection, and training activities

• Support the process of obtaining approvals from health authorities and ethics committees
