Imagine a future where you are a key part of our Asset Integrity Team operating some of Denmark’s most important infrastructure assets both onshore and offshore

Welcome to Asset Integrity

You’ll be part of Asset Integrity where you, together with your engineering colleague will support the organisation with your mechanical engineering skills in the operation, inspection, engineering, integrity and asset management. As a team we foster collaboration and innovation. We are a group of ambitious professionals within different engineering disciplines, who are passionate and motivated and who value teamwork as an essential part of safeguarding our assets.

You’ll play an important role in:

• executing various engineering studies and tasks for onshore oil&gas terminals and offshore and onshore pipelines both internally and by defining scope of work and liaison with external engineering consultants

• performing inspection data analysis and integrity assessment of our approx 800km of pipelines

• supporting the offshore inspection and maintenance campaigns.

• liaison with Authorities, Contractors, Oil&Gas companies and other third parties.

• act as offshore company representative/supervisor onboard contractors’ vessels

• ensure and perform engineering and quality check and final delivery of inspection results to our Integrity engineers

• providing input to budgets and reporting to management.

Once familiar with our systems, you will be included in a 24/7 duty roster to respond to emergency situations.

To succeed in the role, you:

• have key focus on safety, which shall be embedded in all the work you do;

• hold an engineering degree, preferably in mechanical engineering

• have experience working with oil&gas plant and pipeline integrity and engineering both onshore and offshore

• have experience working with engineering companies, contractors and/or suppliers;

• have experience working with practical onshore and offshore pipeline operation and maintenance as well as experience in marine and subsea operations and inspection methods

• have a proactive and systematic approach to your work tasks

• possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills and can work independently in your area of responsibility and participate in a culture of knowledge sharing in an open, honest and trustful culture

• are a team player who thrives on solving complex problems together with your colleagues.

• speak and write English fluently and knowledge with a Scandinavian language is an advantage.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply. You’ll receive the training needed to maintain and further develop your competencies.

The role involves some travel, including two to three day trips per month to onshore sites, a two-week offshore campaign in summer, and a few conferences or courses each year.

Working at Ørsted

In the Asset Integrity department we have the responsibility for looking after some of Denmark’s most important infrastructure assets. We have highly skilled employees dedicated to safeguard and care for our assets.

We offer a collaborative, dynamic, and diverse workplace with constructive feedback and continuous learning, enabling our people to develop their expertise in asset integrity and engineering.

Shape the future with us

Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

Position salary range:

For this position, the expected base pay range is kr54,480.00- kr68,100.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

Our benefits package:

For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11 % contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3 % holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and well-being programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, and internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

Pre-employment background check:

This position requires a background check as part of the hiring process and the offer is dependent on the outcome of this check. You will receive more information during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

Are you ready to pursue your career within disruptive MedTech working with 3D scanners and software medical devices in a global setting? Then 3Shape offers a unique opportunity to work as Post-Market Surveillance Manager in the center of Copenhagen at Kongens Nytorv.

About the department

You will report to the Head of Scientific Affairs and you will be part of our growing global RA organization based in Copenhagen, which currently includes around 30 people. You will interact with a wide range of stakeholders and especially with Product Creation, Customer Support, Product Management, Global Sales, Resellers, and external consultants worldwide. You will assist with developing the future of disruptive MedTech in collaboration with the entire organization and enable people across the world to enjoy better lives.

Your new job in 3Shape

As our new Post-Market Surveillance Manager (PMS) you will lead and facilitate PMS activities in accordance with relevant global regulations to support our products with regard to safety and performance.

Your key responsibilities

• Lead and maintain the company's PMS program in accordance with EU MDR, FDA, ISO 13485, and other global requirements.

• Develop and maintain PMS Plans, PMS Reports, PSURs, PMCF reports, and trend analyses.

• Monitor and evaluate complaints, adverse events, customer feedback, and other post-market data sources.

• Identify safety and performance trends and support risk management activities.

• Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs, Product Creation, and Product Management to drive continuous product improvement.

• Lead vigilance assessments and regulatory reporting activities for adverse events, serious incidents, and field safety corrective actions (FSCAs), ensuring compliance with global medical device regulations.

• Manage submissions and maintenance of regulatory documentation within EUDAMED.

• Assist with audits and inspections

• Present PMS findings and recommendations to cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

Your profile

We are looking for a person with:

• Master’s degree in Life Sciences, Engineering, Biomedical Sciences, Public Health, Healthcare, or related field

• Relevant Quality, Regulatory or Vigilance operational experience from the medical device industry

• Knowledge of EU medical device regulations/directives, including ISO-13485 and ISO-14971

• Excellent planning, cooperation, and communication skills

• Basic AI knowledge preferable within tools used for PMS, Vigilance and trending

• Basic statistical knowledge

As a person, you are a good team player with strong interpersonal skills who thrives working with multiple stakeholders and partners, both internally and externally. Also, you have the ability to successfully handle multiple tasks while managing tight deadlines.

We offer:

• An attractive office environment in downtown Copenhagen, next to Kongens Nytorv

• An inspiring work environment in an informal atmosphere, with social, diverse, and highly skilled colleagues

• A professional challenge in a dynamic, globally-oriented business environment

• Empowerment and influence over your own tasks

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

The Company

˚MEQU is a Danish MedTech company behind the ˚M Warmer System, an innovative medical device that enables healthcare professionals to deliver warm blood and IV-fluids from the point of injury to the hospital. With customers across military, tactical, emergency, HEMS, and hospital environments worldwide, our ambition is to become the global leader in blood and IV-fluid warming solutions for pre-hospital and through hospital care. Learn more about ˚MEQU: www.mequ.dk

On behalf of ˚MEQU, Best Talent is recruiting an International Product Manager.

The Team

You will join a small, ambitious Marketing team with ambitious plans and great impact on the future growth of the company. Success is driven by close collaboration across Marketing, R&D, QA/RA, Operations, and Commercial functions in a fast moving and highly cross-functional environment.

International Product Manager

Drive global product strategy for an innovative Danish MedTech company

• Shape life-saving MedTech solutions through your clinical expertise

• Collaborate with leading healthcare providers, emergency services, and military organizations

• Play a key role in the international growth of a fast-scaling Danish MedTech company with a meaningful and global purpose

The Role

We are looking for an International Product Manager who can bridge clinical insights, users’ needs, regulatory requirements, and technical development to drive successful global product strategies and commercial execution.

You will own the global product lifecycle across emergency, tactical, and hospital segments. With the United States representing ˚MEQU’s most important growth market, you will play a key role in ensuring that product positioning, roadmap priorities, and value propositions algin with the clinical, regulatory, and commercial requirements of US military, EMS, HEMS, and hospital customers.

Working across the organization, you will ensure that user insights, market needs, engineering priorities and regulatory considerations are translated into clear product direction and commercially viable solutions.

As the internal subject-matter expert within pre-hospital blood and IV transfusion, you will convert clinical challenges into prioritized product requirements that guide product development and long-term portfolio decisions. The position reports directly to the COO and requires approximately 30-50 travel days annually.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Shaping global product positioning, value propositions, and market prioritization to support successful international expansion, and continuously monitor:

• Developments in clinical standards of care.

• Tactical and military medical protocols.

• Global procurement and reimbursement structures.

• Competitive and technological developments.

• International market dynamics and commercial opportunities.

• Develop instructions for use, training materials, user guides, and educational content to support sales teams, distributors, and clinical specialists globally.

Your professional background:

You bring a clinical background within emergency medicine, pre-hospital care, HEMS, military medicine, or tactical care, combined with hands-on experience with blood and IV transfusion in critical settings. You understand the realities and challenges faced by end users in high-pressure environments.

In addition, you have commercial insight into the MedTech industry and experience supporting product positioning, launches, and international market development. Experience working with institutional customers medical device markets and understand how to position, launch, and scale products internationally. Experience with institutional and public procurement structures is highly valued.

You understand medical device development and the regulatory environment and are able to translate complex clinical needs into structured product requirements that create both customers value and commercial impact.

Your personality – You are:

• A strong communicator with who bridges clinical technical, regulatory, and commercial perspectives.

• Commercially minded with a strategic and customer-centric approach

• Structured and analytical, with the ability to balance long-term strategy and operational execution

• Proactive, self-driven, and comfortable taking ownership in a dynamic scale-up environment

• Curious, collaborative, and motivated by improving patient outcomes through innovation

˚MEQU offers you:

You will gain international exposure across tactical, emergency, and hospital markets and collaborate closely with global distributors, armed forces, and leading healthcare institutions.

• A high-impact position with global strategic product influence

• A dynamic, international, and collaborative work environment

• A diverse team of 30+ colleagues headquartered in Copenhagen

• A mission-driven culture focused on improving patient outcomes

• Competitive salary with a pension scheme and up-to-date benefits

Application:

Please send your application in English, marked ”1947/International Product Manager” to job@besttalent.dk. Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Learn more about Best Talent at www.besttalent.dk.

• Execute thorough QA of suppliers’ projects deliverables.

• Coordinate the civil design input with our civil partners.

What You Bring

• Degree in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent) with 5+ years of experience in high voltage substation design and engineering

• Broad knowledge within subsystems included in the substation in any of the following areas: Air Insulated Switchgear, Gas Insulated Switchgear, Oil filled components, compensation systems, HV and MV cable systems and their terminations, Auxiliary systems, civil works

• Has proven experience in working under rules according to the Danish legislation 1608, as well as experience in the field of a High Voltage substations, either as a “Arbejdsleder” or similar position understanding the practicalities on the site.

• Basic understanding of cyber security in projects.

• Thorough understanding of interfaces and design flow between the sub-systems as well as the capability to break down the design work in appropriate steps for planning purposes.

• Project and customer focused combined with strong written and oral communication skills for co-working with technical and non-technical colleagues and stakeholders.

• Proven supplier management skills.

_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for an AI Business Manager to join our Digital Development team.

_**Team

**The AI team is a cross-functional team dedicated to embedding AI directly into CIP's business lifecycles and day-to-day operations across the platform and sits within the wider Digital Development team.

**Role

**The AI Business Manager is responsible for ensuring AI creates measurable business value across CIP's business lifecycles and works directly with lifecycle owners, product teams, delivery teams, and business stakeholders to identify opportunities, prioritize initiatives, drive adoption, and embed AI capabilities into day-to-day processes and ways of working.

The AI Business Manager serves as the bridge between business priorities and AI capabilities, ensuring that AI is integrated directly into the Investor, Investment, Fund & Investment Management, and Project lifecycles rather than delivered as standalone technology initiatives. The role is accountable for helping lifecycle teams identify where AI can accelerate outcomes, improve decision-making, increase productivity, and enhance user experiences while ensuring appropriate governance and value realization.

**Responsibilities will consist of, but are not limited to:

**Lifecycle Partnership and Business Engagement

• Partner with lifecycle owners and business stakeholders to understand priorities and strategic objectives, identifying where AI can improve outcomes, efficiency, and decision quality.

• Participate in lifecycle planning and roadmap discussions to embed AI initiatives into business plans from the outset, acting as the primary AI partner for assigned lifecycle domains.

AI Opportunity and Use Case Management

• Facilitate identification, assessment, and prioritization of AI use cases, maintaining the opportunity pipeline based on business value, feasibility, and strategic alignment.

• Develop business cases, value hypotheses, and success metrics, supporting initiatives from ideation and validation through deployment and value realization.

Embedding AI into Business Lifecycles

• Work with business and technology teams to integrate AI into core processes, products, and workflows, redesigning ways of working where relevant and driving adoption of AI-powered tools.

• Support the evolution of lifecycle operating models to treat AI as a native capability, scaling effective patterns across domains.

Governance and Responsible AI

• Ensure AI initiatives comply with governance, security, risk, privacy, and regulatory requirements, coordinating with legal, risk, compliance, and information security stakeholders as needed.

• Support lifecycle teams in navigating AI policies and approval processes, promoting responsible AI practices and appropriate human oversight.

Value Realization and Performance Management

• Track KPIs for AI adoption, utilization, and business value, measuring realized benefits such as productivity gains, cost savings, and risk reduction.

• Provide regular updates to leadership on AI portfolio performance and lifecycle impact.

Change, Communication, and Enablement

• Manage efforts for stakeholder engagement, communications, and change management for AI initiatives, supporting training and capability-building across lifecycle teams.

• Build and maintain networks of AI champions and subject matter experts, promoting a culture of experimentation and responsible AI usage.

**You

**You have a relevant educational background within business, data science, technology, or a similar field. In addition, you have a good understanding of business processes, operating models, and digital transformation, and 5+ years of experience working with technology transformation, AI, data, automation, or similar initiatives, with the ability to translate business challenges into practical AI opportunities and outcomes.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Good stakeholder management and communication skills, comfortable translating between business and technology audiences to turn emerging AI capabilities into practical business value.

• Experience driving change, adoption, and organizational enablement initiatives.

• Ability to manage multiple initiatives and priorities in a dynamic environment.

• Curious, business-oriented, and outcome-focused.

• Combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution and is motivated by delivering measurable impact through technology-enabled change.

**The process

**Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

As Adv Utilities Professional, you will keep the utility systems in building DF running reliably, so production can run with minimal stops. You will own the daily operation, maintenance and development of these systems, and make sure the building and utilities meet GMP requirements, including in audits and authority inspections. Your work supports a stable, compliant production environment, so medicines can reach people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine technical depth with a structured way of working, and you can turn complex technical and regulatory content into clear, usable documentation.

• An engineering degree or a similar technical education. Other academic backgrounds are relevant if you can show strong skills in technical or regulatory documentation.

• Hands-on experience with HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air or vacuum systems, and with BMS, FMS and CTS systems.

• Experience with documentation, quality, validation or technical support in a GMP-regulated setting.

• Strong written communication: you are precise, correct and professional, and you structure and review documents, so they are easy to use in practice.

• Working knowledge of GMP and ISO 9001 as they apply to daily tasks, and knowledge of CE marking.

• Good collaboration skills in a broad network of stakeholders.

• Experience with structured problem solving such as KATA and A3, or with water systems, calibration, room qualification and validation.

What you’ll do

You will be the process responsible for the operation and maintenance of the utility systems in building DF and the PS Warehouse, and the person colleagues turn to when something needs to be fixed, documented or decided.

• Operate, maintain and optimise utility systems such as HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air and vacuum, including technical upkeep that keeps unplanned stops to a minimum.

• Make the most of our FMS, CTS and BMS systems for monitoring buildings and room conditions and keep developing how they are used.

• Keep the building and utilities GMP-compliant, from validation and risk assessments to non-conformances, change requests and quality indicators.

• Write, update and review SOPs, service cards, maintenance instructions, machine documentation and validation documents in clear, precise language, and train colleagues in practice.

• Present your own area in audits and authority inspections, and handle urgent utility issues, escalating when needed.

• Drive and support structured problem solving, improvement work and projects such as rebuilds and new purchases, and plan and prioritise your own tasks.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Facility Management team within Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain to keep production running for the people who need our medicines. You will work closely with your team and with technicians, production departments and technical partners in building DF and the PS Warehouse, a site with a large network of stakeholders.

Externally, you will collaborate with facility management providers, the energy supplier in Kalundborg, the Hallas Park landowners’ association and Kalundborg Fire and Rescue Service, as well as other suppliers and Novo Nordisk colleagues. You will agree priorities for the building and shared utilities with production areas, and move between daily operations and cross-organisational coordination. The work is based in Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will work in a complex, GMP-regulated environment where your expertise is valued and your voice is heard. Strong written and technical skills matter here, and the role offers room to build the rest: you will be supported with on-the-job learning, relevant training and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. You are trusted to take ownership, and you will be part of a team that acts with clarity, speed and care for quality.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep critical utility systems stable, compliant and well documented, apply for the Adv Utilities Professional role by 6 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Carsten Joachim Hansen, Senior manager CJHH@novonordisk.com

Help grow Awaze’s commercial footprint across Germany, Austria and Switzerland by building high-performing travel agency relationships and strategic partnerships that bring our holidays to even more guests.

**Your mission

**As our new Senior Partnership Account Manager, your mission is to grow Awaze’s commercial footprint across the DACH region through two interconnected areas: developing our travel agency channel and building strategic commercial partnerships.

As you’ll be working directly with travel agencies and partners across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, you’ll need to be fluent in German, at native or near-native level, as well as confident communicating professionally in English.

You’ll own and grow relationships with travel agencies across the region, lead agencies through the transition from legacy booking systems to Awaze’s modern platform, and identify new opportunities to expand our network. Alongside this, you’ll develop strategic partnerships from initial prospecting and negotiation through to onboarding and ongoing account development.

Working closely with Marketing, Product, Commercial and leadership teams, you’ll use market insight and performance data to strengthen partner engagement, extend Awaze’s reach and deliver measurable commercial impact.

**What You'll Be Doing

**

• Own and develop relationships with travel agencies across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with a particular focus on chains and networks.

• Lead the end-to-end transition of agencies from legacy booking systems to Awaze’s modern platform, including change management, training and onboarding.

• Identify, develop and onboard new travel agency partners, maintaining a strong pipeline of prospective agencies.

• Proactively identify, pursue, negotiate and close new strategic commercial partnerships across the DACH region.

• Manage the full partnership lifecycle, from initial outreach and commercial negotiation through to onboarding and ongoing account development.

• Monitor agency and partnership performance, using data and commercial metrics to identify opportunities for increased adoption, engagement and growth.

• Collaborate with Marketing, Product and Commercial teams to ensure partners are effectively supported and positioned for success.

• Identify co-marketing and co-branding opportunities that create mutual value and extend Awaze’s reach and brand presence.

• Act as a source of DACH market intelligence, sharing relevant trends, partner feedback and commercial insights with leadership and product teams.

• Travel regularly across the DACH region to build and strengthen relationships with agencies and strategic partners.

**Who We’re Looking For

**You’ll thrive in this role if you’re a natural relationship builder who enjoys turning commercial opportunities into long-term, mutually valuable partnerships. You’re comfortable taking ownership of a varied portfolio, confident working independently and equally at home discussing performance data, negotiating a new partnership or helping an established agency embrace a new way of working.

Fluent German, at native or near-native level, is an essential requirement for this role. You’ll use German regularly to build trusted relationships and communicate effectively with travel agencies and strategic partners across the DACH region.

**We’re Looking For Someone Who Brings

**

• Several years of experience in account management, partnerships or business development, ideally within travel, hospitality or a related sector.

• A demonstrable track record of growing accounts and closing partnerships that deliver measurable commercial outcomes.

• Fluent German, at native or near-native level, alongside strong professional English, both written and spoken.

• Strong relationship-building, communication and presentation skills, with the credibility to engage agency owners, commercial partners and senior stakeholders.

• Strong analytical capabilities and confidence using performance data and commercial metrics to inform decisions and identify opportunities.

• An understanding of brand and marketing principles and the ability to represent Awaze consistently with external partners.

• A self-motivated and structured approach, with the ability to independently manage a large and varied account portfolio.

• Willingness and ability to travel regularly across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, as well as other locations when required.

• Bonus points if you have experience within the DACH travel agency landscape, legacy travel booking systems or digital platform transitions, or have worked within or alongside a major European travel group.

• An established network across DACH travel agencies or hospitality chains, or experience with GDS tools and partnership management platforms, would also be an advantage.

**How You'll Make An Impact

**

• Successfully transition and onboard travel agencies onto Awaze’s modern platform, driving strong adoption and engagement.

• Grow the number, quality and performance of active travel agency relationships across the DACH region.

• Build and maintain a healthy pipeline of prospective agencies and strategic partners, progressing opportunities through to successful commercial agreements.

• Strengthen retention, satisfaction and commercial performance across your agency and partnership portfolio.

• Turn performance data into clear insights and recommendations that help both our partners and internal teams make better commercial decisions.

• Work across Marketing, Product and Commercial teams to unlock partner support, co-marketing opportunities and additional commercial value.

• Bring relevant DACH market trends, partner feedback and insights into Awaze to help inform product and business decisions.

• Champion Awaze’s brands and standards across every agency and partner interaction.

**Why you’ll want to work at Awaze

**We offer a versatile position in a strong professional and social environment - one you’ll have the opportunity to influence and help shape. You’ll be part of an international company that invests in the future, and join a dynamic, fast-paced department with skilled and committed colleagues who support each other.

We’re a People-first Business - And We Know That Our Success Starts With Our Teams. Here’s a Glimpse Of What You’ll Enjoy

• Generous discounts on holidays across our brands

• Flexible hybrid working – with the autonomy to work how you work best

• Real opportunities to grow, learn and shape your role as well as careers progression vertically or horizontally, cross countries and responsibilities.

**About Awaze

**Our mission is clear - to create amazing holidays with Europe’s widest choice of holiday homes.

With more than 110,000 properties across Europe, we are the largest managed vacation rentals business in the region. Our ambition is not only to be the biggest, but the best provider of holiday homes in Europe.

As travel continues to evolve, we are focused on what comes next. We will keep strengthening our relationships with guests and homeowners, continuously improving the way we work, and delivering strong performance. By making things simpler and smarter, we are building a business that is ready for what’s next - powered by proud, passionate and inclusive people.

**Worth knowing

**

• This role can be based remotely in Germany or from our Virum office in Denmark.

• Regular travel across Germany, Austria and Switzerland will be an important part of the role, with travel to other locations when required.

**What’s next?

**If this sounds like the right next step for you, hit “Apply” and follow the instructions to submit your application. We tailor our recruitment process to each role to give both you and our hiring teams the best possible chance to assess whether this could be the start of a successful collaboration. You’ll hear from us shortly after we’ve reviewed your application.

We’re committed to running an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, and if you have any specific requirements or adjustments needed for the interview, just let us know when you accept your invitation - we’re happy to accommodate.

Join us in this role where you’ll act as the accounting lead on some of the world’s largest and most complex renewable energy transactions. Your IFRS expertise will help shape transaction structures and inform key investment decisions. You’ll assess the accounting implications of complex M&A transactions, advise on proposed structures, and translate your conclusions into clear insights that support commercial decisions.

**Welcome to IC Projects & IFRS

**You’ll be part of IC Projects & IFRS where you will act as the accounting lead on M&A transactions including acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships. You’ll join a highly specialised team of eight accounting professionals and work closely with our Partnerships and M&A organisation, external advisers, auditors, and a team of around 40 M&A professionals who originate and execute transactions across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific. In this role, you’ll support complex international transactions and help ensure high-quality accounting decisions across the Group.

As a team, we share knowledge, explore complex accounting questions together, and support one another in delivering high-quality advice. We value different perspectives, open dialogue, flexibility, and a healthy work-life balance.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• acting as the IFRS accounting lead on acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, structured financing arrangements, and strategic partnerships

• assessing accounting implications early in the transaction process and advising on proposed deal and investment structures

• preparing clear IFRS accounting assessments and technical memos that support commercial and management decisions

• reviewing draft contracts, term sheets, bid materials, and other transaction documentation from an accounting perspective

• participating in meetings with investors, external advisers, auditors, and internal stakeholders on transaction-related accounting matters

• contributing to wider Group Finance activities, including financial reporting, accounting policy development, and strategic accounting projects.

**

• bring deep IFRS expertise gained through technical accounting, IFRS advisory or a similar specialist environment

• have experience advising on the IFRS implications of M&A transactions within a listed company, international group, professional services firm, or a comparable organisation

• can translate complex accounting matters into clear, practical conclusions for management, commercial colleagues, and other non-accounting stakeholders

• build strong working relationships and communicate confidently across finance, Partnerships & M&A, management, external advisers, and auditors

• approach complex assignments analytically and systematically, take ownership of your work, and remain adaptable to changing transaction priorities

• hold a master’s degree in accounting, auditing, or a related discipline.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position: Endocrine Disruption in Fish with Focus on Histopathological Endpoint Development
jobs.description:
We invite applicants for a 3½-years Postdoctoral research position in Environmental Toxicology with a focus on histopathological and behavioral endpoints development in fish. The position is funded by the EU Partnership for Risk Assessment of Chemicals (PARC), the Danish EPA and University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will be carried out in the Ecotoxicology group at the Department of Biology, SDU. 

Qualifications: 
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Toxicology. A strong background in chemical risk and hazard assessment and regulatory toxicology is highly appreciated. This includes knowledge of EU chemicals legislation and regulatory frameworks such as REACH, OECD test guidelines, AOP development, and/or pesticide and biocide risk assessment. Furthermore, the following experiences and skills are required: 

• 
Strong proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

• 
Experience in teaching and supervision at the university level, including lectures, student examinations, and supervision of MSc students. 

• 
Hands-on experience in assessing endocrine disruption properties of chemicals using the Zebrafish (Danio rerio) model.  

• 
Strong documented knowledge of one or more endocrine pathways relevant to EU regulatory assessments (EATS modalities). 

• 
Extensive experience with OECD fish test protocols such as OECD TG 236 and OECD TG 210. 

• 
Documented experience in histopathology techniques, including tissue preparation, microtome sectioning, cryosectioning, H&E staining, microscopy, and image analysis. 

• 
Experience in behavioral assessment in zebrafish eleutheroembryos, e.g., using EthoVision XT or equivalent tracking and analysis software. 

The following qualifications are considered advantageous: 

• 
Experience with molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis (e.g., qPCR, transcriptomics). 

• 
Experience with immunohistochemistry and related imaging techniques. 

This position is particularly suited for a candidate with strong interest in bridging experimental ecotoxicology and regulatory chemical risk- and hazard assessment. 

Application deadline: 13. November 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time. 
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

• 
Ideally, you also have experience leading, standardising or developing other instructors

• 
Fluent English, spoken and written

How to apply

Ready to set the course for a role where you shape the standards for the next generation of pilots? Send us your application today – we look forward to hearing from you.

Good decisions start with good data. But good data does not just happen. At NORDEN, data comes from many places and is used across our business to understand markets, automate processes and make better decisions. Your job is to make sure that data is actually ready to be used.

As our new Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and datasets that move data through our organisation and turn raw information into something people can trust and work with.

As Product Owner, you will take full ownership of two global facility monitoring systems (FMS) that track environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, CO2, diff Pressure etc.) across Novo. The FMS supports product release and compliance, so they need clear direction and reliable delivery. You will bring that responsibility in-house, setting the strategy, priorities and budget that keep quality and supply moving.

What you’ll bring

You are preferably already working as a Product Owner and are ready to take clear ownership of a product’s strategy, priorities, backlog and finances.

You will also bring:

• An academic degree preferably in IT or business. Relevant experience counts as much as the path you took to get here.

• Around 3+ years of Product Owner experience, combined with broader relevant experience.

• Strong IT strategic understanding and experience shaping and owning the longer-term direction of a product.

• An understanding of technical and solution architecture at design level. You don’t need to be a deep technical specialist.

• Experience with cost management and budgeting.

• Strong written and spoken English. The team and stakeholder environment is fully international and works in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Understanding of compliance in the pharmaceutical industry.

• Experience from production or manufacturing.

• Knowledge of facility monitoring systems, including the FMS solutions used at Novo.

• Experience with agile ways of working.

On a personal level, you bring the maturity to take ownership, make decisions and prioritise competing demands while staying effective under pressure. You are also able to lead informally and build strong stakeholder relationships across functions and cultures.

What you’ll do

The two FMS solutions offer different functionality, so the right one can be chosen for each site and situation. Your job is to give both a clear direction and to make sure the product team delivers what matters most.

• Own the overall direction of both global FMS systems, setting the product strategy and longer-term roadmap.

• Own and prioritise the backlog, deciding what gets delivered and when, based on business needs and input from the product team.

• Lead the product team informally, aligning roles, responsibilities and deliverables so the team works effectively together.

• Manage costs, budgeting and the financial model, making sure costs are covered and following up on actual spend against budget.

• Manage stakeholders proactively. Spot potential issues early and bring the right people in before problems escalate.

• Act as the first escalation point when significant issues arise with the product or its implementations, and set a clear example on quality.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Monitoring and Control Solutions, the area that sets the strategic direction for global monitoring and control systems at Novo. The team is based at the Novo IT hub in Høje Taastrup, Denmark, and works closely online with stakeholders and the application vendor around the world. You can expect to spend much of your week in the office with your team.

Your closest colleagues will be your product team: a Product Manager, Business Analysts, Implementation Leads, a Compliance Partner, a Solution Architect and System Managers. Beyond the team, you will coordinate with Line of Business, implementation teams, lifecycle management, architecture and the application vendors. The systems serve factories and laboratories globally, so your priorities will affect sites across many countries and cultures. Your role is to bring these perspectives together, create clarity when things stall and keep work moving at pace.

What you can expect here

This is a role with real ownership. You will be trusted to make decisions about two global systems, and your voice will shape where they go next. You will build broad experience across IT strategy, finance, architecture and manufacturing-related compliance, all in one product area.

You will work in a team that values a quality mindset, honest dialogue and an informal working climate, where colleagues support each other and never compromise on quality. Clear priorities and ambitious goals mean your results will be visible and recognised.

jobs.occupation: PhD Stipend in Experimental Quantum Materials Physics
jobs.description:
Join the Physics Group at the Department of Materials and Production at Aalborg University and contribute to research on the quantum properties of matter at the scale of individual atoms and molecules. This is a full-time, fixed-term PhD stipend for three years, commencing on 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter

**Your work tasks

**The Department of Materials and Production is looking for a PhD candidate in experimental physics to investigate how molecular complexes can be used to engineer quantum properties in materials. The project addresses fundamental questions in quantum science while contributing knowledge that may support future applications within electronics, sensing and energy harvesting. You will become part of the Physics Group and work in an international research collaboration funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark.

Your research will focus on preparing and investigating molecular complexes on crystalline surfaces. You will deposit molecular complexes by electrospray techniques under ultra-high-vacuum conditions and study their structural and electronic properties using low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. The work will involve planning and conducting experiments, documenting methods and results, analysing and discussing data, and communicating findings clearly within the research collaboration and through relevant scientific channels. You will carry out a substantial part of the research independently while collaborating closely with researchers in the project.

Your competencies You hold a master's degree in physics, nanoscience or a closely related field. You have a solid experimental background within physics, surface science or nanoscience, together with documented experience in scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy, ultra-high-vacuum techniques, cryogenic systems, surface science and electrospray deposition.

You can organise and conduct experimental research in a systematic manner, from the planning of measurements to the documentation, analysis and interpretation of results. You communicate methods and findings clearly in English, both in writing and in dialogue with other researchers. The position calls for a researcher who can take responsibility for their own work while contributing constructively to a collaborative and international research environment.

**Qualification requirements

**PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

You will join the Physics Group at the Department of Materials and Production, where research activities explore materials and physical phenomena relevant to both fundamental science and future technologies. In this position, you will work at the intersection of molecular science, surface science and quantum materials research, with access to a research environment in which experimental methods and scientific discussion form the basis for developing new knowledge.

As part of an international collaboration, you will have the opportunity to engage with researchers across disciplines and contribute to a research project with both scientific depth and technological relevance. The position offers a strong foundation for further work in academic research, advanced experimental physics or research-intensive development environments.

**How to apply

**Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

**Salary and terms of employment

**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

Job Description:

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with wind turbine drivetrains or comparable large rotating machinery is preferred. Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. We also welcome specialists who want to broaden their understanding of the complete drivetrain.

What can you look forward to?

You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development.

The site will build core engineering capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, and industrialization of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be the development of an advanced aerospace signal intelligence product platform. The work will cover RF and system architecture, antenna system design, signal acquisition, embedded control, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for production and field deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior RF / Microwave Hardware Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s RF and microwave design capability.

You will design and develop RF and microwave hardware and subsystems, including receiver front ends, amplification, filtering, mixers and local-oscillator circuitry, RF signal routing, and PCB- and module-level implementation. The work covers RF performance analysis and design trade-offs, circuit architecture, schematic design, component selection, circuit and electromagnetic simulation, RF PCB implementation and layout, prototyping, debugging, and performance validation.

You will work closely with system architects, antenna systems engineers, SDR and signal processing engineers, RF test and characterization engineers, mechanical design engineers, and partner engineering teams. The role requires deep RF and microwave design expertise, technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototyping and validation to documented, manufacturable RF modules and subsystems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system requirements into RF hardware architecture, specifications, performance budgets, and design trade-offs.

• Design RF and microwave circuits, modules, and signal-acquisition paths, including amplification, filtering, switching, mixing, frequency synthesis, gain control, and supporting bias, power, and control circuitry.

• Perform RF performance analysis covering sensitivity, selectivity, gain, noise figure, dynamic range, linearity, stability, spurious responses, and interference resilience.

• Create RF schematics, select components, and own RF PCB implementation, including laminate and material selection, stack-up definition, and layout, with controlled-impedance routing, transmission lines, grounding, shielding, isolation, and high-frequency interconnects.

• Perform circuit and electromagnetic simulations, optimize designs, and correlate simulated performance with laboratory measurements.

• Lead prototypes bring-up, tuning, debugging, and design verification in collaboration with RF test and characterization engineers.

• Integrate RF hardware with antenna systems, data-conversion interfaces, mechanical assemblies, and platform interfaces.

• Contribute to design verification, EMC/EMI assessment, environmental qualification, reliability evaluation, and system-level validation.

• Prepare hardware specifications, design documentation, BOMs, analysis reports, design-review materials, test inputs, and production-release documentation.

• Own technical decisions related to component and supplier selection, manufacturability, testability, lifecycle risks, and design-risk mitigation.

• Collaborate with system, antenna, signal-processing, test, mechanical, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

Required qualifications and experience

• Master’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, RF/microwave engineering, applied physics, or a related field. A PhD is an advantage.

• 7+ years of professional experience in RF and microwave hardware design.

• Strong hands-on experience developing RF circuits, multilayer PCBs, modules, and subsystems from schematic design and simulation through layout, bring-up, tuning, and validation.

• Experience with receiver architectures and RF signal paths, including low-noise and gain stages, filters, switches, mixers, oscillators, PLL-based frequency synthesis, and supporting bias, power, and control circuitry.

• Strong understanding of RF system budgeting, chain analysis, and frequency planning, including gain, noise figure, sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, P1dB, IP3, phase noise, stability, spurious responses, isolation, and impedance matching.

• Practical experience with RF PCB implementation, including laminate and material selection, stack-up definition, controlled-impedance routing, transmission lines, grounding, shielding, isolation, and high-frequency interconnects.

• Hands-on experience with schematic capture and RF PCB layout using an industry standard ECAD tool such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro/OrCAD, or equivalent.

• Proficiency with one or more RF circuit and electromagnetic simulation tools, such as Keysight ADS, Cadence AWR Microwave Office, Ansys HFSS, or CST Studio Suite.

• Hands-on experience with RF measurement equipment, including vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.

• Demonstrated ability to bring up, tune, troubleshoot, and validate RF hardware and correlate measured results with simulations.

• Experience taking RF hardware through prototype manufacturing, assembly, design verification, environmental requirements and qualification, and production release.

Nice to have

• Experience with signal-intelligence, direction-finding, spectrum-monitoring, or radio-surveillance systems.

• Experience with SDR-based radio architecture.

• Experience designing wideband, high-dynamic-range, low-noise receiver systems.

• Experience with coherent or multichannel RF systems, including channel matching, phase stability, and synchronization.

• Experience developing aerospace, mission-critical, or ruggedized electronic systems.

• Experience developing RF and microwave hardware operating at frequencies up to and beyond 18GHz.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take technical ownership of one or more RF modules or subsystem areas.

• Establish the initial architecture, design approach, and development plan for the assigned RF scope.

• Deliver reviewed schematics, simulations, layout inputs, and supporting design documentation.

• Bring up and validate initial hardware prototypes, with clear correlation between expected and measured performance.

• Identify key RF, implementation, and integration risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with system, antenna, signal-processing, test, mechanical, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.
