jobs.occupation: Tenure Track assistant professor, associate professor or professor of Food Processing & Technology
jobs.description:
Tenure-track Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Full Professor of Food Processing & Technology
 Department of Food Science
 Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Food Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as Tenure-track Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Full Professor in Food Processing and Technology. Applicants must be capable of, and interested in, conducting and developing basic and applied interdisciplinary research of high international standard in the field of food processing and technology. The position will involve extensive collaborations within the department and with national and international academic groups and industrial partners. Research within the Department has a mission to unearth new solutions for society and industry to support sustainable food production, food security and safety as well as production of high-quality food promoting human health and wellbeing. The Department of Food Science is recognized for excellence in food research, education, and industrial collaborations. The Department is an international workplace with Danish and English as parallel working languages, however it is expected that the successful candidate will be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 3 to 6 years. We encourage applications from a range of disciplines within the food science and technology area, ideally covering the understanding of food macromolecular interactions on a mechanistic level, how processing and formulation affect or determine these interactions, and how this influences final product quality with focus on functional properties.

  We are seeking a candidate who will establish an internationally leading research program, and we encourage a diverse range of applicants whose work may center on one or more of the following disciplines:

   	
• Developing a mechanistic understanding of interactions of food macromolecules in complex matrices during processing or formulation spanning dairy, plant, and single-cell protein sources. 	
• How this knowledge can be used in the rational design of functional ingredients and healthy foods using established and emerging processing technologies 	
• Development and utilization of high throughput methods for characterizing and quantifying the physicochemical behavior of food macromolecules in complex matrices. 	
• Modelling and the use of machine learning/AI for simulation and prediction of the outcome of process unit operations on food and ingredient functionality. 	
• Formulation and fluid dynamics of complex emulsions and the mechanisms governing this.   In addition, it is expected that this position will be involved in a significant amount of collaboration with industry, and therefore it is expected that the successful candidate has a documented successful track record in industry collaboration and working with innovation-oriented research. Furthermore, we expect that the successful candidate has a genuine interest in leadership and the wellbeing and development of their group.

  Tenure-track assistant professor
 The tenure-track assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regards to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within the Tenure Track Assistant Professorship. To a limited extent the position may also include other duties.

  The tenure-track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.

  Assessment of applicants for the tenure-track assistant professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

  Associate professor and full professor

  Applicants are required to have university level teaching experience, documented teaching competencies and must be able to explain and reflect upon own teaching practice and portfolio. Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme for assistant professors is required.
 In particular, the candidate must actively contribute with research-based teaching on the BSc in Food Science and Nutrition, and the MSc in Food Science and Technology programs, with an emphasis on the specialization in Dairy Science and Technology.

  Duties include the applicant’s own research, development of the field, assessment tasks, grant applications, and research management such as supervision and training of research fellows and other staff. The successful applicant must also teach, supervise, prepare and participate in examinations, and fulfill other tasks requested by the Department.

  Assessment of applicants for the associate professorship and full professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  University of Copenhagen’s criteria for recognising merit
 General criteria apply to the appointment of assistant professor / associate professor / professor at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here:
 
 For tenure-track assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf

  For associate professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5b_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Associate_professors.pdf

  For professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5c_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-professors.pdf

  Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  The tenure-track assistant programme
 The tenure-track programme is a career programme and an assigned mentor will provide the tenure-track assistant professors with guidance related to career development, other academic topics and administrative procedures.

  Performance of the tenure-track assistant professor will be followed via internal yearly evaluations and a mid-term and final international evaluation by an assessment committee. If the ‘final appraisal’ is positive you will be promoted as associate professor. Performance and progression towards the criteria below will be evaluated with due consideration of differences between research fields.

  After a 6-year tenure-track period tenure-track assistant professors are expected to meet the criteria for appointment of associate professors at the University of Copenhagen.

  Salary and employment conditions
 The position is open from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is either as tenure track assistant professor, associate professor or professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  This position comes with an opportunity to negotiate a start package that will help leverage the candidate’s scientific deliverables in the initial years of employment. The negotiation for the start package takes place as part of the recruitment process. Please read about the contents of the programme and conditions, as well as UCPH’s extensive support for international researchers, here Start package programme – University of Copenhagen .  

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  The successful candidate will be a part of the Section for Ingredients and Dairy Technology. The section has internationally acknowledged expertise within novel sustainable processing technologies, protein, polyphenol and lipid chemistry, functionality, and modification of food components, kinetics, oxidation, food engineering, rheology, digitalisation, and advanced data analysis. The section is also equipped with pilot facilities for brewing, dairy and bioprocessing. The section has extensive collaborations on research projects with major food industries in both Denmark and abroad.

  Further information on the Department is linked at Department of Food Science – University of Copenhagen Inquiries about the position can be made to Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department, Colin Ray (+45 93565911, colin.ray@food.ku.dk) or Head of Section, Mogens Larsen Andersen (+45 3533 3262, mola@food.ku.dk).

  Filing of application
 The position may be applied for at the tenure-track assistant professor level, associate professor level or full professor level. Please note that it is possible to apply at more than one level. If applied at more than one level, separate applications must be submitted (see below).

  The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  Applying for the tenure-track assistant professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including: 	 		
• Please describe and document international network and relations 		
• Please describe and document internationally based activities 		
• Positions held at universities/research institutions outside Denmark 		
• Outreach activities, i.e. popular lectures or other activities in the media 		
• Grants held, personal or in part. Career development grants. 	 	 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent)    	
• Research plan - description of current and future research plans    	
• If available, description and documentation of teaching and supervision experience and qualifications- please describe and document: 	 		
• Experience with supervision of BSc and MSc students 		
• Teaching experience 		
• Formal pedagogical training 	 	    	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of up to 5 particularly relevant papers   Applying for the associate professorship or full professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including information about external funding  	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent)  	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans  	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 5 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Interviews will be held on 25 February 2027.  

  Please refer to the following no. in future communication in this case: 

  211-0262/26-2N, Tenure-track Assistant Professor of Food Processing & Technology.

  211-0759/26-2E, Associate Professor of Food Processing & Technology. 

  211-0366/26-2K, Professor of Food Processing & Technology.

jobs.description:
Love data and want to see your ideas make a real difference?

Do you get a kick out of turning messy processes into smart solutions? Are you curious about how AI can change the way a global company works? Then this could be the student job that kick-starts your career.

Role and impact

As our new Student Assistant in Global Facility Management, you’ll help keep Topsoe’s workplaces around the world safe, efficient and future-ready. Our team makes sure our buildings and workspaces work, so our colleagues can focus on developing the decarbonization technologies the world needs. You won’t be fetching coffee or filing paper. You’ll test AI tools on real problems, help run projects, and see your work make an impact from day one.

You’ll work with colleagues across building operations, maintenance, space planning, our service partners and workplace safety, and you’ll build a network across the organization. The position is part-time, approximately 15 hours per week, and we’ll plan your hours flexibly around lectures and exams.

What you’ll be doing

Building with AI: Take ideas from concept to testable solutions. Create and test AI models and assistants for real operational tasks, design prompts and workflows, and help validate and improve them together with colleagues across the business.

Driving projects: Help prepare project documents and proposals, and make sure projects get approved and followed up properly. This is a hands-on introduction to how projects move through a large organization.

Making our sites easier to navigate: Create maps and access information for visitors and external partners, and write clear guidelines and step-by-step work instructions.

Communicating what we do: Support our communication lead with updates on our intranet, internal social platforms, digital screens and signage at our sites.

Who you are

You’re studying for a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a field such as data science, IT, engineering, business administration, facility management or communication. Above all, you’re curious about data and AI, and maybe you’ve already played around with ChatGPT, Copilot, Power BI or Python in your studies or on your own. You like structure, you finish what you start, and you’re not afraid to ask questions or suggest a better way of doing things. You enjoy working with people from different backgrounds, and you’re comfortable communicating in Danish and English, both spoken and written.

Don’t tick every box? Apply anyway. We value curiosity and drive over a perfect CV.

Why you’ll love working here

Real experience for your CV: Apply AI and automation to real business processes in an international company. This is the kind of experience employers look for after graduation.

Room to experiment: You’ll get space to test ideas, learn from what doesn’t work, and see your solutions put into use.

A mentor in your corner: Experienced colleagues will guide you and help you grow, both professionally and personally.

A job that fits student life: Flexible hours that work around your studies and exam periods.

Purpose: Your work supports a company whose mission is to fight climate change.

Your new team

You’ll join a friendly team of facility management professionals who care about what they do and about each other. We share knowledge openly, help each other out, and like to have fun along the way. You’ll learn from colleagues with expertise in operations, project management and digital transformation, and you’ll be treated as a full member of the team.

If you want to be the person who leads All Gravy's product marketing, keep reading!

**🥞 The mission

**All Gravy is the frontline operating system. One platform for comms, learning, engagement, operations and scheduling, with built-in AI. Think WhatsApp meets Duolingo meets Claude for frontline workers. Used daily by 350+ brands like GAIL's, Dishoom, 7-Eleven, and Honest Burgers.

We're growing 3x year-over-year, and the product is moving faster than ever. We need product marketing that keeps up.

**🎯 The role

**You own product marketing. Fully.

Nobody hands you a task list. You decide what releases matter most, what we say, how we say it, and what gets created. And then you build most of it yourself. Copywriting skills, good taste in graphic design, website savviness is needed.

**🔥 What You'll Do

**

• 
Know our customers better than anyone. You dig into sales calls, customer interviews, reviews and our founders' heads. You know who we're for, and who we're not for.

• 
Own positioning. You make the hard choices about what we stand for and what we leave out, so we stand out in the market.

• 
Turn features into selling points. Product ships something new, you find the value in it and say it so simply a customer gets it in one line.

• 
See the whole picture. Every feature is part of a bigger story. You know where it fits, who it's for and how to serve it.

• 
Build the launch system. How big is this release? Who needs to know first? Sales, CS, customers, the market - you make sure it lands everywhere.

• 
Keep every touchpoint telling the same story. Website, sales deck, ads, socials, in-app. If we built it, it's on the site - and ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude know about it too.

• 
Drive adoption, not just launches. Product updates, changelog and in-app messaging, so customers actually use what we ship and stay longer.

• 
Give sales and CS what they need. Messaging, one-pagers, demo flows, battlecards. Stuff they actually use.

• 
Make the content. Landing pages, emails, explainer videos, clickable demos. Mostly you, with AI.

**🧠 Who you are

**

• 
You drive your own stuff. You pick your initiatives, set your priorities and run with it. We give you a goal, not a to-do list.

• 
You're obsessed with simplicity. Fewer words, fewer features in the pitch, one clear message. You'll push for the simple version even when it's super hard to dig out.

• 
You're fast. 80% in a day, ship it, make it better next week. You don't sit on things.

• 
You're AI-first. AI is how you work, it does most of your work and you fine-tune the rest. You use it for research, as a sparring partner and to build. You code, you design, you generate. You max out your tokens, because you can't help it. The shift has already happened here - for example, we build our website in Webflow with the Claude MCP - so you can make changes to anything, in minutes, and publish a new version of the site 10 times per day.

• 
You can write and you can sell. You find the one line that makes people go "oh, now I get it". In engaging English.

• 
You get product marketing. Big plus if you’ve owned launches and positioning in B2B SaaS, and you always start with the customer, not the feature list.

• 
You're the glue. You speak product with product, sales with sales, and get everyone running in the same direction.

• 
You have an eye for design. Taste, detail, a feel for what looks good. Big plus.

• 
You're excited about where this is going. The gap between an idea and getting it done is basically zero now. That should make you excited, not tired.

**🚩 Probably not for you if

**

• 
You do your best work when someone hands you clear structure and concrete projects.

• 
You work the same way you did three years ago.

• 
AI is something you use now and then, or something you're "starting to explore".

• 
You've got 15-20 years in product marketing but AI hasn't really changed how you work. For us, the way you work beats the years on your CV.

**📍 Practical

**

• 
Copenhagen, Nørrebro. Hybrid.

• 
Full-time.

• 
You'll work closely with marketing (video, events, growth), product, sales, customer success and our founders.

atNorth is a leading Nordic data center company providing cost-effective, scalable high-density colocation and built-to-suit services to industry-leading organizations across Iceland, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark.

With sustainability at our core, our data centers run on renewable energy and are designed according to circular economy principles. Through innovative design, power efficiency, and intelligent operations, we deliver reliable, secure, and high-performance infrastructure.

Headquartered in Reykjavik, Iceland, atNorth operates eight data centers across the Nordics, with additional sites under development in Finland, Denmark, Sweden and Norway.

We combine world-class technology with a people-first culture built on collaboration, ownership, and trust, empowering our teams to grow, take responsibility, and make a real impact.

By joining our international team, you will help shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure.

**Design Manager at atNorth

**As our Design Manager, you will lead the technical and commercial delivery of design and build-out projects for atNorth’s state-of-the-art data centers in the Nordic countries. Working in the Development team and with close collaboration with Procurement and Operations teams, you’ll ensure standardization, quality, and sustainability are embedded in every stage of our development process.

This is a key role where your decisions will directly influence the performance, reliability, and environmental impact of our data centers.

**Responsibilities:

**

• Lead and implement atNorth’s standard design and infrastructure solutions across Nordic sites.

• Act as the technical and commercial expert throughout project lifecycles.

• Oversee and manage all design phases and support construction, ensuring alignment with gating, cost, sustainability, and HSE processes.

• Coordinate external A&E consultants and internal stakeholders to deliver efficient, cost-optimized solutions.

• Assist site selection by evaluating brownfield/greenfield opportunities and master planning.

• Review Capex budgets and assess technical risk in expansion, retrofits, or new builds.

• Support technical incident investigations and drive continuous design improvements.

• Ensure sustainability opportunities are prioritized and environmental impact is minimized.

**Your Profile:

**

• 5–7 years of experience in relevant engineering fields such as civils/structural/architectural (CSA) or mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP)

• Experience in infrastructure or construction projects (preferably data centers)

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in relevant engineering disciplines (CSA or MEP)

• Understanding of data center equipment and critical infrastructure

• Basic knowledge of building management systems and CSA/MEP engineering (depending on which relevant engineering area is covered by a degree)

• Familiar with project and design management processes across multiple stakeholders, internal and external

• Fluent in English

• Proactive, self-driven, and adaptable mindset

• Willingness to travel across the Nordics, including outside regular business hours

**About The AtNorth Culture

**We believe that sustainable success starts with the wellbeing of our people. For us, an open, transparent, and inclusive culture is more than a priority, it is the core of how we lead and innovate.

We don’t just talk about culture; we nurture it. Through regular one-to-one engagements and monthly wellbeing surveys, we listen carefully to our teams, ensuring that every voice is heard and every opportunity for improvement is embraced.

We recognize that innovation and collaboration thrive where people feel truly connected, which is why we come together each week to share ideas, strengthen relationships, and nurture a sense of belonging, sometimes over a simple breakfast and good conversation.

At atNorth, we are building a community where you can do your best work and shape a sustainable future together. #99

Job Description

Do you want to help shape how a large IT company measures, manages and documents its information security? Are you motivated by turning data, risk and regulation into practical decisions? If so, you may be our next colleague in the newly established GRC team in Netcompany's Group CISO Office.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a member of the GRC team, you will help ensure that Netcompany has an accurate, data-driven view of the effectiveness of its security controls and its level of compliance. The team takes a pragmatic and technically grounded approach to governance, risk and compliance, and works closely with the Application Security team, the Operations organisation, Internal IT and other business functions across the group.

The GRC team is a small team of colleagues with complementary profiles. We do not expect any one candidate to cover every area described below. Instead, we are looking for broad profiles with solid experience across several of these areas and the motivation to develop within the rest.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

• Driving smaller security improvement projects from planning to implementation, combining coordination with hands-on execution

• Developing, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuityDeveloping, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuity

About you

You have broad experience within information security and a solid understanding of its technical aspects alongside a general understanding of the software development life cycle. You combine this with the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical solutions. Furthermore, you are pragmatic, take ownership of your work and prefer a hands-on approach.

To succeed in this role you:

• Hold a relevant degree or equivalent experience; within IT, engineering, computer science or a similar field.

• Strong analytic skills, with the ability to interpret data and draw meaningful conclusions independently.

• Experience within several of the areas listed in the overview of responsibilities in the role.

• Solid communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams, business functions, management and, on occasion, customers.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken).

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

We provide a structured career model that allows you to build on your existing experiences.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will support your development and help you achieve your personal and professional goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague in management gives you concrete insights into the various business areas and responsibilities that match your interests and desires.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars tailored to you and where you are in your career. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills. Partaking alongside colleagues from across the company helps you build a solid network and provides a strong foundation for your career at Netcompany, both professionally and socially.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen is seeking top early-career researchers for a number of attractive one- to three-year postdoctoral positions.

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences has strong research groups in many areas of applied mathematics, and has an active postdoc and visitors' program. Applicants in all areas of mathematics covered by the research groups of the department will be considered.

  There will be postdoc stipends in the following specific areas:

   	
• Insurance mathematics, optimization and operations research, mathematical finance, econometrics and financial economics, and applied probability theory, covered by the Section for Insurance and Economics. 	
• Probability theory, mathematical statistics and applied statistics, covered by the Section for Statistics and Probability Theory.   In particular, the following specific positions are open:

   	
• Variational analysis in the Wasserstein space of stochastic processes (contact Johannes Wiesel wiesel@math.ku.dk) 	
• Causal modelling and related questions in reliable machine learning (contact Sebastian Weichwald, https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us). Applicants are encouraged to describe a concrete research direction, what they bring to it, and why it fits the group’s work. 	
• Causal Inference and Interpretability in Complex Models (contact Nikolaj Thams, thams@math.ku.dk ) 	
• Optimization under decision-dependent uncertainty (contact Giovanni Pantuso, gp@math.ku.dk)    

  The postdoc’s duties will include research within mathematics as well as teaching. The teaching load is typically two half-semester courses per year, of which one usually is as a teaching assistant. The post may also include performance of other project-specific duties.

  The positions are open with starting date in 2027, ordinarily September 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. The salary is very competitive and researchers from outside Denmark may qualify for a reduced tax rate (see terms below).

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://www.math.ku.dk/ . Inquiries about the position can be made to the Head of Department Mogens Steffensen, mogens@math.ku.dk.

   

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae: 1-3 pages, including list of publications. 	
• Cover letter: Substantiate your qualification for the postdoc position and your motivations. 	
• Diplomas: Master and PhD degree or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date. 	
• Research plan: Description of current and future research plans (1-3 pages). 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers (not mandatory)    

  The deadline for applications is 15th of November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. We expect to send invitations for interviews in December 2026 or January 2027. The interviews will typically take place in January and February of 2026, and our search is expected to be concluded around April 2027.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

We are looking for a motivated Fundraising & Project Development Intern to help Pangaea Youth Network develop new projects and secure funding for our local and international activities. You will have the opportunity to work on real funding applications and contribute directly to the growth and development of a youth NGO.

LocationHorsensHorsens, Denmark/Hybrid

DurationFlexible, adjustable

TopicFundraising, Grant Writing, Project Development & NGO Management

TypeInternship

Description

Position Overview:

This is a hands-on internship where you will work closely with our management and project team to identify funding opportunities, develop fundraising strategies, create new project ideas, and prepare grant applications.

You will help turn ideas into real projects by researching funding programmes, developing project concepts, planning activities, preparing budgets, and writing applications for funding.

Our main focus is on Erasmus+ projects, Danish foundations, municipal funding opportunities, and international programmes supporting youth work, education, inclusion, community development, sustainability, and international cooperation.

Responsibilities:

• 
Fundraising Strategy: Research and develop fundraising strategies for PYN, identify potential funding sources, analyse funding requirements, and help create a long-term fundraising plan for the organisation.

• 
Funding Research: Identify relevant grants and funding opportunities from Erasmus+, Danish foundations, municipalities, EU programmes, and international funding organisations. Monitor application deadlines, eligibility requirements, funding priorities, and available budgets.

• 
Project Development: Help develop new local and international project ideas based on PYN’s mission, community needs, and funding opportunities. Contribute to defining project objectives, target groups, activities, expected results, and long-term impact.

• 
Grant Writing: Prepare and write funding applications, including project descriptions, needs analysis, objectives, activities, methodology, expected outcomes, sustainability plans, and dissemination strategies.

• 
Project Budgets: Support the preparation of project budgets, financial plans, funding requests, and cost estimates in cooperation with the management and accounting team.

• 
Partnership Development: Research potential local and international project partners, foundations, sponsors, and organisations. Support communication with stakeholders and help develop partnerships for future funding applications.

• 
Project Planning: Help create project timelines, work plans, activity schedules, responsibilities, and implementation strategies for proposed projects.

• 
Funding Database: Maintain an organised overview of funding opportunities, application deadlines, eligibility criteria, application progress, submitted proposals, and funding results.

• 
Organisational Development: Contribute ideas for improving PYN’s financial sustainability, expanding its activities, and developing new services or initiatives that could attract additional funding.

Skills & Qualifications:

We are looking for someone who is interested in fundraising, project management, international cooperation, and NGO development. And has:

• 
Good written English (preferably B2 or higher)

• 
Strong research and analytical skills

• 
Good organisational skills

• 
Attention to details

• 
Creativity

• 
The ability to work independently

You should feel comfortable using Google Docs, Google Sheets, or similar digital tools and be interested in developing and writing structured project proposals.

Nice to have:

Previous experience with Erasmus+, grant writing, fundraising, project management, budgeting, research, or NGO work. Familiarity with EU funding programmes, Danish foundations, or project application processes is an advantage but not required.

Personal qualities:

We appreciate people who are proactive, curious, responsible, detail-oriented, and motivated to learn. You should enjoy developing ideas, researching opportunities, solving problems, and turning concepts into practical project proposals.

Relevant study backgrounds:

Project Management, International Relations, Business Administration, Economics, Public Administration, Political Science, Social Sciences, European Studies, Nonprofit Management, or related fields. Students from other backgrounds are also welcome to apply.

Working Style & Environment:

Our office and youth space are located in Student Village Kamtjatka, in the city centre of Horsens, Denmark.

A hybrid working setup is possible, but we prefer interns who can be present on-site for teamwork, project development meetings, and organisational activities.

Typical office hours are around 9:00:00–16:30, Monday–Friday, with the remaining working hours arranged according to the internship agreement and team needs.

You will join a small, international team working across project management, fundraising, marketing, community events, accounting, web development, and youth work.

You will work closely with PYN’s management and receive guidance on project development, funding research, and grant writing. At the same time, you will have opportunities to take responsibility for your own research, project concepts, and application drafts.

What You Gain:

• 
Practical Fundraising Experience: Learn how NGOs identify funding opportunities, approach funders, develop fundraising strategies, and prepare grant applications.

• 
Real Project Development Experience: Participate in developing actual local and international projects, from the initial idea to a complete funding application.

• 
Erasmus+ Knowledge: Gain practical insight into European funding programmes, international partnerships, project planning, grant writing, and the management of EU-funded initiatives.

• 
Professional Development: Improve your research, analytical thinking, project design, budgeting, strategic planning, professional writing, and stakeholder communication skills.

• 
International Working Environment: Become part of a supportive international community and collaborate with young people, interns, volunteers, and partners from different countries.

• 
Networking Opportunities: Build connections with NGOs, foundations, international organisations, local stakeholders, and potential project partners.

• 
Erasmus+ Mobility Opportunities: Depending on your availability, eligibility, and participant profile, you may have opportunities to join Erasmus+ youth exchanges and training courses (typically 5–10 days), where travel, food, and accommodation are covered by EU funds.

• 
Meaningful Impact: Contribute to securing resources that help PYN organise free community activities, international learning opportunities, youth projects, and initiatives that benefit young people.

Note:

This is an unpaid internship. Pangaea Youth Network does not provide monetary compensation or financial support.

We offer practical professional experience, supervision, an international working environment, networking opportunities, access to relevant Erasmus+ activities, and opportunities to contribute to real projects with a positive social impact.

Join us in this role where you’ll be responsible for sourcing the right suppliers to secure the operation and fulfil the servicing needs of our offshore windfarms. You’ll be working with our procurement process and governance from developing the sourcing strategies to contract handover. In this role, you'll be coordinating with our category managers, business stakeholders and colleagues in supporting functions. You can look forward to a dynamic, fast-paced, and international environment, where you’ll have the opportunity to develop your career while making your mark on the transition to renewable energy.

**Welcome to Offshore Generation Procurement

**You’ll be part of the Offshore Services Procurement team where you, together with your colleagues, will support our offshore windfarms to produce power, by ensuring contracting of timely, compliant and competitive O&M services capacity. You’ll be working in a global team of highly skilled procurement professionals. An important aspect of your role is to proactively consolidate input from internal stakeholders to negotiate and sign fit to scope contracts ready for the end users’ purposes. In this role you’ll be working closely with colleagues organized in projects at our operational hubs.

As a team, we ‘re driven by an open working environment where everyone is encouraged to speak up, seek, and provide feedback. We actively take initiative, work on improvements, and seek learning opportunities.

You’ll play an important role in:

• being responsible for the end to end tendering process, qualifying suppliers, clarifying and evaluating bids, preparing and negotiating terms and conditions, and recommending and awarding suppliers

• ensuring compliance with internal and external tendering rules, policies, and governance by actively engaging and seeking input from key support functions

• preparing and presenting clear and thought-through gate documents to aim management and budget owners’ decision on recommended strategies

• leading communication with suppliers throughout the sourcing activities

• contributing to the quality assurance processes by reviewing peers’ documentation, sharing tendering and contract lessons learned, and providing feedback to category strategies

• handing over complete signed contract package with complete metadata ready for execution .

To succeed in the role, you:

• have significant experience with managing sourcing processes from drafting of sourcing strategies to contract signing. Experience running tenders according to EU-tender law is a plus

• have a passion for negotiating and possess considerable experience taking responsibility for planning and executing negotiation process

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integration of High-Temperature Heat Pumps in Industrial Processes - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want your research to help industry decide how to electrify its heat supply? At DTU Construct you will combine thermodynamics, optimisation and machine learning to build tools that make the business case for industrial high-temperature heat pumps clear, fast and reliable.

We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade low-grade waste heat to up to about 250 °C.

Your project will address decision making support for heat pump end-users from a first viability check to integration with the process, to flexible operation. You will demonstrate the findings in industrial use cases together with our partners.

Supervision: Prof. Ahmad Arabkoohsar and Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be, through adequate methodological advancements, to cuts the time and effort needed to assess where and how high-temperature heat pumps should be integrated into industrial sites, and what is their economic value. Your main task will be:

• Develop models to rapidly estimate performance and break-even point for specific sites
• Extent methods for heat pump integration that co-optimize heat recovery, electrification and flexibility provided by heat pumps
• Refine and validate methods during industrial secondments 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
 
You have:

• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
 
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Ahmad Arabkoohsar ahmar@dtu.dk and Professor Adriano Sciacovelli adrsc@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on integration of high-temperature heat in industrial processes: select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Are you our new Business Controller?
jobs.description:
Do you understand the story behind the numbers - and can you help the business act on it?

We are looking for an experienced Business Controller who can connect financial performance with the operational and commercial developments behind it. You will take ownership of key reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes, work closely with leaders across the organisation and turn financial results into clear insights, priorities and actions.

The department “Analytics & Modelling” works across Momentum Energy Group and provides reporting, performance analyses and financial decision support to business units, senior management and the Board. You will join a small team of 3 with broad exposure across the organisation and play an important role in strengthening how Momentum understands, forecasts and manages its financial performance.

Momentum Energy Group develops, invests in, owns and operates renewable energy assets across Denmark, Germany and Sweden. We are one of Denmark's largest owners of onshore wind turbines, with activities spanning the full lifecycle of renewable energy projects and a development pipeline comprising wind, solar PV and hybrid projects through a clear growth agenda.

What are your tasks?

As a Business Controller, you will contribute to, deliver, and coordinate central parts of Momentum's performance management cycle. You will work closely with business unit leaders and Group Finance to understand developments in revenue, costs, and profitability while ensuring these drivers are reflected accurately in our reporting and outlook. You will be a trusted financial partner who combines a deep financial understanding with a strong and curious commercial perspective.

Your responsibilities will include:

• As part of a team delivering the monthly management reporting, including timeline management, inputs, quality assurance and financial commentary based on consolidated accounts received from Group Finance.

• Analysing monthly performance against budget, forecast and prior periods and explaining the underlying revenue, cost, and profitability drivers.

• Working closely with business unit leaders to understand operational and commercial developments and translate them into financial implications.

• Participating in budgeting and forecasting processes for relevant business areas, including assumptions, risks, opportunities and scenario analysis.

• Following up on budgets and forecasts with the business and ensuring that deviations, risks and required actions are identified and addressed.

• Developing and maintaining relevant financial and operational KPIs that provide transparency into business performance.

• Preparing business cases, profitability analyses and ad hoc decision support for commercial and operational initiatives.

Who are you?

You are an experienced and commercially minded finance professional who wants to understand and communicate how the business operates. You build strong working relationships across functions, but you are also comfortable challenging assumptions and conclusions constructively. You can move seamlessly between detailed financial analysis and discussions with senior stakeholders, translating complex findings into clear, actionable insights.

You are motivated by working in a developing organisation where the role will evolve over time, creating opportunities to take ownership of new tasks and areas of responsibility as the business matures.

Qualifications

• At least 5-7 years of relevant experience within business controlling, FP&A, performance management or a similar finance role.

• A relevant degree within finance, economics, accounting, business administration or a related field.

• Strong experience with management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.

• A solid understanding of financial statements and the interaction between operational performance, profitability, cash flow and the balance sheet.

• Strong analytical and financial skills, including proficiency in Excel.

• Experience preparing concise management presentations and communicating financial insights clearly to financial and non-financial stakeholders.

• A proactive and independent approach, combined with strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

What we offer

You will join a small and ambitious team with broad exposure across Momentum and direct interaction with business unit leaders and senior management. We prioritise professional development, personal balance and an inclusive workplace.

You will work at new our office in Roskilde together with 70 colleagues. Benefits include health insurance and a healthy lunch and fruit scheme.

Do you want to be a part of the journey?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, please apply as soon as possible, and no later than November 17, 2026, as we will be reviewing candidates on a rolling basis.

For questions about the role, please contact Head of Analytics & Modelling, Karoline Nylander at kny@momentumgreenenergy.com.

At Momentum, we believe that diversity strengthens our team. We therefore encourage everyone—regardless of gender, age, background, or culture—to apply for this position.

jobs.occupation: Market Director Health and Public Institutions
jobs.description:
**Market Director Health and Public Institutions – Buildings & Industry

**__**Lyngby or Aarhus, Odense or Vejle

**_

_**Do you want to help shape some of Denmark's and the Nordic region's most important healthcare, education and public building projects? Can you build trusted relationships with key clients, grow business opportunities, and lead complex pursuits in a market with significant societal impact? And do you combine solid commercial acumen with deep insight into the health and public institutions sector? Then join COWI as our new Market Director for Health & Public Institutions within Buildings & Industry and apply your knowledge and curiosity to enable a better tomorrow.

**_

_**Shape the future of healthcare and public buildings

**_To strengthen COWI’s customer-centric approach, we are looking for a Market Director to drive business development and coordinate sales efforts within Health & Public Institutions in our Buildings & Industry sector.

This is a key role in one of COWI’s strategic growth markets, covering healthcare, education, research, cultural facilities and public development projects across Denmark and the Nordics. You will help position COWI on major hospital developments, universities, public institutions, refurbishment programmes and other complex projects that contribute to the development of society.

What makes this role unique is its pure focus on market leadership, where success is defined by customer value, business growth, and a strong market presence. Working closely with specialists, project managers and technical experts, you will build relationships, identify opportunities and grow COWI’s presence in the market. You will also become part of an experienced business development community that shares best practices and drives commercial excellence across COWI.

As part of a team of 25 experienced market professionals across COWI and Arkitema, you will work at the forefront of our business development efforts. Reporting to the Senior Market Director, you will collaborate closely with colleagues across the organization to deepen client relationships, unlock strategic opportunities, and lead pursuits from early engagement through to project win, contributing directly to the continued growth of our business.

With increasing investments in healthcare, public buildings and sustainable transformation, the market offers significant growth potential. Your sector insight, commercial mindset and customer understanding will help position COWI as a preferred partner for public clients and healthcare organisations across the Nordic region.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Grow business development and growth across the Health & Public Institutions market segment by identifying, prioritizing, and converting strategic opportunities.

• Build and maintain close relationships with key customers, partners, and decisionmakers, acting as a trusted advisor and Key Account Manager for selected clients.

• Develop and manage a healthy sales pipeline, manage Go/No-Go decisions, and drive capture planning for major pursuits and tenders.

Lead and support complex proposal processes, ensuring compelling value propositions and effective collaboration across disciplines and business units.

• Provide direction and coordination for the Business Development team supporting the market segment, ensuring effective collaboration and delivery of market priorities.

• Monitor market trends, upcoming investments, and customer needs to help shape market strategies and long-term growth initiatives.

• Represent COWI externally through customer meetings, industry networks, conferences, and strategic partnerships.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**Like us, you believe that successful business development is built on trust, collaboration and long-term relationships. You are motivated by creating opportunities, understanding customer needs and bringing together the best teams to deliver value for clients and society. You thrive in a collaborative environment and enjoy working closely with fellow Market Directors and multidisciplinary teams to achieve shared goals.

To perform well in this role, it is essential that you bring solid market insight and a well-established network within healthcare, public institutions or the built environment sector. Equally important is your ability to build internal alliances and leverage the collective expertise of the organisation rather than acting alone.

On top of that, you will have:

• A relevant educational background such as engineering, architecture, business or a related discipline.

• Extensive experience in business development, client management, or market leadership within healthcare, public institutions, architecture, construction, or engineering consultancy.

• Deep knowledge of public-sector customers, procurement processes, and market dynamics, combined with a well-established professional network.

• Demonstrated skill in building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and converting opportunities into long-term partnerships.

• Experience contributing to large and complex tenders, proposals, and commercial negotiations.

• Demonstrated ability to provide leadership, direction, and coordination across Business Development teams, account managers, and framework agreement holders, ensuring a shared focus on market growth and client development without formal personnel responsibility.

• Solid communication and stakeholder management skills, with professional proficiency in both Danish and English.

**A place to work and so much more

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability and strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices. We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and collaboration – because that is what brings out the best in you, both at work and at home. With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people bringing expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

**Got more questions?

**If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Senior Market Director Mikael Voldborg, Buildings & Industry, at mivo@cowi.com, or Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist, Janne Nielsen, at jane@cowi.com.

Get to know us better on our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we aim to achieve, and what it is like to be part of COWI.

**Before you apply

**All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or cover letter required. Please add a short motivation for the role (4–5 lines) at the top of your CV. When it comes to photos, we prefer to form our first impression face to face rather than from a picture. If relevant, please also attach your portfolio.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI – inclusion is key

**We are committed to creating a respectful and fair working environment where all employees feel a sense of belonging and have equal opportunities to thrive and develop. Our leaders act as role models for inclusive leadership and contribute to a culture where diverse perspectives and professional approaches are seen as a strength. We integrate diversity and inclusion into relevant decisions and processes, and when forming teams across architecture and engineering disciplines. We do this because it is part of our values – and simply because it is the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: Research assistant in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
jobs.employer_name: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
jobs.description:
Research assistant in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
Are you interested in turning IoT data into intelligent digital twins of real-world systems? The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for a 6-month research assistant position in the Robots4Green project, working at the intersection of IoT data, artificial intelligence and digital twin technology. The position is based in Aarhus, Denmark, and starts on 1 January or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 6-month position from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
We are seeking a motivated research assistant with a strong background in data science and machine learning to contribute to research on AI for IoT data and digital twin technology. You will work with sensor data and develop the models that allow digital twins to monitor, understand and predict the behaviour of physical systems.

Your tasks will include:

• Applying signal processing and feature extraction methods to sensor time series, for example wind and environmental data
• Designing, training and evaluating machine learning models for forecasting and anomaly detection, with an emphasis on interpretable and reliable models
• Contributing to data pipelines and to the integration of models into a digital twin platform together with the project team
• Supporting experiments and demonstrations together with project partners
• Documenting results and contributing to scientific publications and project deliverables

The position may also include assisting in supervision activities at the department.

Prior experience with IoT or digital twins is an advantage. You will gain hands on experience with IoT data and digital twin technology while working closely with researchers in the Networks and Analytics research group and with academic and industrial partners in the project. The position is an excellent stepping stone towards a PhD or a career in industry.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or a similar field.

We are looking for candidates with:

• Solid programming skills in Python for data analysis and modelling
• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as scikit-learn and PyTorch or similar AI frameworks
• A strong foundation in statistics, probability and signal processing
• A good understanding of time series analysis
The following qualifications are considered advantages:

• Experience with graph-based machine learning, such as graph neural networks, or graph signal processing
• Knowledge of IoT systems, sensor data or data platforms
• Familiarity with digital twin concepts and simulation
• Experience from research projects, including interdisciplinary collaborations
• Teaching or supervision experience

Personal skills
We value good communication skills in English, the ability to work independently as well as in an international team, curiosity and a proactive, structured approach to problem solving.

Who we are
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Aarhus University is a leading research institution with strong expertise in computer science, electrical engineering and wireless communication systems. We maintain active collaborations with industry partners and are involved in multiple national and international research projects on IoT, AI and digital twins.

You will be joining the Networks and Analytics (NAN) research group, which focuses on research and innovation in developing and applying internet technology across a wide selection of fields in electrical and computer engineering for real-world, large-scale applications. The NAN group has strong expertise in wireless networks, IoT, network security, data analytics, AI and cooperative multi agent systems, with extensive experience in smart energy grids, smart and integrated transport and satellite communication systems.

Our research group provides a dynamic and supportive environment where interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged, and where you will work with both academic researchers and industry professionals on projects with real world impact.

Department website: https://ece.au.dk

What we offer
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers:

• An exciting opportunity to work on applied research in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
• A well developed research infrastructure with access to laboratories, IoT equipment and computing facilities
• Close collaboration with industrial partners and direct pathways to real world validation
• An interdisciplinary and international research environment
• Opportunities to co-author scientific publications and build a foundation for a PhD
• A supportive work environment that values work-life balance, professional development and openness

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Helsingforsgade 10, 8200 Aarhus N (Denmark), and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Rune Hylsberg Jacobsen, +45 41893252, rhj@ece.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 17 November 2026.

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

**Your impact begins here

**As Senior Manager, Search & Evaluation, you will help Novo find and assess the external drug and technology opportunities that could shape our future portfolio. You will evaluate early ideas, take promising opportunities through due diligence and build the value story that helps senior leaders decide. Working globally with scientists, biotech companies and investors, you will help bring new science towards people living with diabetes, obesity and other serious chronic diseases.

**What You’ll Bring

**You combine scientific curiosity with business sense, and you can turn complex information into clear recommendations.

• A master’s degree in business or life sciences.

• 5+ years of experience in R&D, business development or professional services within the pharma or biotech industry, or in an equivalent role.

• Project management skills and experience.

• The ability to analyse complex ideas and data and turn them into clear, well-founded recommendations for senior stakeholders.

• Experience working in cross-functional teams, with clear communication and strong teamwork.

• Strong written and presentation skills.

• Strong networking, collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

• Strategic business and financial acumen, and a deep interest in life sciences and medicine.

• A self-driven, goal-oriented approach, and the ability to work well in a dynamic environment.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• An MD or PhD.

• Knowledge of, or experience in, clinical drug development in relevant therapeutic areas.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be part of the first step in how Novo brings in external innovation, from the first scouting conversation through to due diligence and negotiation support.

• Identify novel pipeline assets and enabling technologies through scouting, professional networks, literature, database and patent searches, and conferences across diabetes, obesity, CVD, liver, blood and endocrine disorders, and Consumer Rx.

• Support technical streams of evaluation and due diligence, from initial assessment through to due diligence project management.

• Build the value story for selected opportunities and prepare presentations for governance boards, so senior management can make well-informed decisions.

• Develop and maintain detailed therapy area landscapes with colleagues across Search & Evaluation, including external perspectives on competitors and their strategies.

• Keep a strategic overview of internal and business development pipeline assets, and use your internal and external networks to define which assets are needed and how they fit.

• Support Business Development in licence and collaboration negotiations, represent Novo as a preferred partner at scientific congresses and events, keep opportunity tracking in Inova up to date, and help improve due diligence and landscaping processes.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Search, Evaluation & Intelligence (SE&I), part of Global Business Development (GBD), and report to the Head of Global Evaluation. SE&I is the primary entry point for external drug and technology opportunities at Novo, running proactive scouting campaigns across start-ups, biotechnology companies and venture capital firms.

You will work closely with Business Development teams in Denmark and Cambridge, USA, and with colleagues across the value chain who help assess each opportunity. Externally, you will use and grow your network across biotech companies, venture capital firms and large pharma communities.

This role works globally, so you will bring different perspectives together, create clarity and keep opportunities moving.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will work independently on specific projects, with guidance from your manager and senior colleagues on broader strategy and significant decisions. Your voice and expertise will count in discussions that influence which science Novo pursues.

You will build new skills through exposure to different therapy areas, functions and external partners, and grow alongside colleagues in a global, fast-moving environment.

**What We Offer

**There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

• Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 y 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience. Further details to be shared during the recruitment process.

• Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

About the position and the assignments  

You will be based at the Danish Red Cross HQ in Copenhagen and will be part of the Health Team in the Technical Quality and Impact Unit of the International Department. The Health Team comprises technical advisors within health and mental health and psychosocial support. It ensures the availability of the necessary technical capacities to provide timely and relevant assistance and advice to DRC-supported operations, with a primary focus on the Africa, while also supporting MHPSS interventions in MENA, Europe and Asia regions as needed.

As a member of the Health Team, you will be working under the line management of the Health Team Lead and will also work closely with other colleagues at the DRC HQ and Regional and Country Offices (COs), as well as with NSs staff and volunteers. The position does not have programme management responsibilities but supports programmes through technical accompaniment, mentoring, and quality assurance.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

• Technical support and guidance: Provide evidence-based guidance and advice to DRC COs and National Societies on MHPSS priorities, approaches and activities, remotely or through country visits and missions to ensure that MHPSS interventions follow industry standards and good practice.
