Do you want to develop new methods for quantitative modelling of the shallow subsurface and geological processes? The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) is looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and an interest in combining geoscientific observations, numerical modelling and scientific software development. 

  The position is a three-year, time-limited researcher position in the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology (SURFACE) in Aarhus, expected to start on 1st of January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  About the position 

  The position lies at the intersection of geology, geophysics, glaciology, numerical modelling and scientific software development. You will develop computational approaches that combine geological and geophysical observations with process-based and probabilistic models to create quantitative representations of the subsurface and glacial environments. 

  You will initially contribute to two ongoing research projects, ICESYNC and DREAM, while also taking part in research and development related to the national groundwater mapping programme and other activities at GEUS. 

  In ICESYNC, you will work with process-based modelling of erosion, sediment transport and deposition and investigate how modelled ice dynamics and sedimentary processes can be linked to geological and geomorphological observations. The work includes development of reproducible modelling workflows and pilot studies in Greenland and Denmark. 

  In DREAM, you will contribute to the development of a high-resolution probabilistic geological modelling framework based on drone-based TEM data. You will work with the integration of high-resolution resistivity models and their uncertainties with geological prior knowledge and other geoscientific data. The aim is to develop a semi-automatic, open-source workflow for constructing detailed geological voxel models and to test the approach using synthetic and field data. 

  Across these activities, you will work with numerical, probabilistic and process-based approaches to geological modelling and with integration of geophysical observations, geological data and process-based models. An important part of the position will be the development of reproducible computational workflows and scientific software for geoscientific analysis and modelling. You will also contribute to geological interpretation and modelling in research projects and applied activities, including the national groundwater mapping programme. 

  The position includes publication and communication of research through peer-reviewed papers, project deliverables, presentations and open-source software. You will also be expected to contribute to the development of new research ideas, project proposals and collaborations with Danish and international partners. 

  Who are you? 

  You hold a PhD, or have submitted your PhD before the application deadline, in geoscience, geophysics, computational geoscience or a closely related field. 

  We are looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and a good understanding of geological processes, combined with experience in quantitative geoscience. This may include numerical modelling, geological modelling, probabilistic or statistical methods, inverse problems, geostatistics or related approaches. 

  You should have a good understanding of geophysical data and their geological interpretation and strong programming skills, with experience in scientific software development, for example in Python, Matlab or a similar language. You should be able to work independently and systematically while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment, and you should communicate well in written and spoken English. 

  Experience with TEM data, process-based modelling, 3D geological or voxel-based modelling, open-source scientific software or reproducible computational workflows would be valuable. Knowledge of Quaternary geology, glacial geology, sedimentology or groundwater geology would also be relevant, as would experience from externally funded research projects and preparation of research proposals. We do not expect applicants to cover all of these areas. 

  As Danish is the primary organisational language at GEUS, you should be prepared to learn Danish if you are not already a Danish speaker. 

  Meet your new colleagues 

  At GEUS, you will join the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology, where we conduct research on a wide range of topics related to the processes, resources and geology of the upper 300 metres of the subsurface, both onshore and offshore. 

  Based at the university campus in Aarhus, the department consists of around 35 enthusiastic colleagues working in an interdisciplinary environment. We combine field observations, laboratory analyses, and advanced modelling to address scientific questions and societal challenges. 

  As part of the team, you will work alongside colleagues committed to scientific excellence, collaboration, and knowledge sharing. We work closely with public authorities, universities, and international research networks, providing a strong platform for developing your research, building collaborations, and making a meaningful contribution to both science and society. 

  A working environment with a focus on professional development and well-being 

  There are many good reasons why you should choose a working life at GEUS. 

  We are a diverse staff of about 300 committed employees. Trust and flexibility are keywords. The working environment is lively, informal and international. Our tasks are versatile and there are plenty of opportunities for you to influence the development of your task portfolio.

  We prioritise professional development, among other things by offering access to courses and other relevant activities. Socialising is also very important at GEUS, and we have a rich social life with a staff club, an art association and more. 

  At GEUS, we prioritise the well-being of every single employee. We prioritise that the Heads of Departments are close to the employees, and we have flexible working hours that allow you to organise your life so that there is time for what matters to you. If you need to work from home occasionally, that is also possible. 

  Furthermore, we have associated physiotherapists. 

  Salary and terms of employment 

  Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the relevant trade union agreement. 

  The appointment area is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities and its institutions. 

  The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities considers diversity to be an asset and encourages anyone regardless of gender, age, religion or ethnicity to seek the position. 

  Further information 

  If you would like additional information, please contact the contact Acting Head of Department Verner Brandbyge Ernstsen Verner vbe@geus.dk or Senior Researcher Anders Damsgaard on andam@geus.dk. 

  If you are an international applicant, you can read more about living and working in Denmark on GEUS’ website.  

  Are you interested? 

  If you are interested in the position, we would like to hear from you. The application must include a CV incl. your ORCID, a list of publications with a separate indication of articles registered in ISI Web of Science and any copies of individual publications of particular relevance to the position. Please enclose master's and PhD diplomas in either Danish or English as well as other material documenting qualifications at senior level. 

  Please apply for the position by clicking “Apply for position”. We must have your application at the latest on Sunday 15th of November 2026 (Danish time). 

  Applications or other material received after the deadline will not be considered. 

  The employment procedure 

  A professional assessment committee consisting of one internal and two external assessors at minimum senior researcher level will carry out an individual assessment of all applicants’ professional qualifications, and the applicants will be assessed as qualified or unqualified for the position. Afterwards, an internal employment committee will decide which of the professionally qualified candidates will be invited for a job interview. This procedure is in accordance with the “Order on employment and assessment of scientific staff at the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland § 4 and 7”.

jobs.occupation: Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping (re-posting)
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology is looking for a highly motivated and independent Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping. The position is expected to commence on 1 January 2027 and is linked to the Lundbeck Foundation Experiment grant MINDtheCAP: A new role of RNA caps in intellectual disability.

  Our research
 The Section for Computational and RNA Biology combines experimental and computational approaches to investigate RNA biology, gene regulation and genome-wide molecular processes. The position will be anchored in the Vinther research group and will contribute to the section's research activities, collaborations and supervision environment.

  Your job
 The Staff Scientist will have scientific responsibility for the day-to-day implementation of MINDtheCAP and will independently plan and coordinate the work within the project's objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements.

   	
• Plan, prioritise and carry out the project in accordance with its scientific objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements. 	
• Analyse and interpret high-throughput sequencing and molecular data and refine the associated bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Coordinate project activities with laboratory technical staff and internal and external collaborators, and supervise students or junior researchers where relevant. 	
• Maintain research documentation and data-management practices and ensure compliance with laboratory safety, research-integrity and relevant institutional requirements. 	
• Prepare scientific publications, conference presentations, seminars, workshops, grant reports and relevant outreach activities. 	
• Develop follow-up research directions, collaborations and applications for further competitive research funding.   Because the work is research-driven, its detailed timing and sequence cannot be fully predetermined. Within the agreed scientific and institutional framework, the Staff Scientist will independently determine day-to-day priorities, experimental design and methods, the sequencing of experiments and analyses, and the coordination of collaborations.

  Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic Staff Scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Qualifications and Expectations 

   	
• A master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, RNA biology or a closely related field. 	
• Interest in and/or experience with RNA biology, RNA capping or RNA biochemistry. 	
• Experience with molecular biology techniques and laboratory work. Experience developing and optimising RNA-related methods, sequencing-library preparation and quantitative experimental controls is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience with or interest in analysing and interpreting transcriptomic data and in using or developing bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Interest in data analysis and bioinformatics. Experience with bioinformatic tools or workflows is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience preparing scientific reports, manuscripts and presentations is an advantage. Previous scientific publications are considered an advantage.  	
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment within agreed milestones and budgets. 	
• Good written and oral communication skills in English.   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience managing externally funded research projects and contributing to competitive funding applications. 	
• Experience coordinating interdisciplinary collaborations and working with molecular or neuronal cell-model systems. 	
• Experience supervising students, junior researchers or technical staff. 	
• Ability to work independently, solve scientific and technical challenges, and collaborate effectively across disciplines.   Place of employment
 The place of employment is the Section for Computational and RNA Biology, Department of Biology, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment, with access to facilities and expertise in RNA biochemistry, molecular biology, high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working time is 37 hours.

  The position is fixed-term for two years, from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2028.

  The position is classified as Staff Scientist (AC-TAP). Employment will be under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority) and there will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). The applicable pension contribution will be in accordance with the relevant collective agreement.

  Application
 If you are interested in the position, please submit your electronic application, including attachments, via the UCPH Job Portal (click the “Apply for position” link at the bottom of the job posting).

  Your application should be submitted in English and include:

   	
• A letter of application addressing the requirements, maximum one page. 	
• Curriculum vitae. 	
• A certified or signed copy of certificate(s) of education.   The application deadline is 9 November 2026

  Interviews are expected to be held shortly after the application deadline.

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Jeppe Vinther at jvinther@bio.ku.dk.
  

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

  The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Associate Director, Compound Management & Process Automation

Department: Research Workflow Operations

Location: Måløv, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Associate Director, you will lead the Compound Management & Process Automation department within Research Workflow Operations (ResWO), a team of 12 scientists and technicians. You will keep compound management reliable and make laboratory workflows faster, more consistent and more automated, in collaboration with protein and peptide research areas across Therapeutics Discovery. Your leadership helps early research projects keep pace towards lead candidate selection, and that progress matters to people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You have a genuine interest in people leadership and in building high-performing teams. To succeed in this role, you should have:

• An MSc or PhD in life sciences, or a related discipline, with relevant experience in drug discovery or development.

• Experience leading people in pharmaceutical research, or substantial subject matter expertise in digitalisation and automation of drug discovery or development processes.

• Experience improving laboratory workflows and translating scientific or operational needs into practical improvements.

• A strong interest in coaching, talent development and building collaborative teams, supported by experience developing people or mentoring colleagues.

• Proven stakeholder management skills and the ability to collaborate and influence across functions and organisational levels.

• An enterprise mindset, with the ability to balance department priorities with the needs of the broader research organisation.

As a person, you listen actively, build trust and value diverse perspectives. You are curious about better ways of working, and you bring clarity and a practical approach when priorities change. You enjoy co-leadership and shared accountability, and you are motivated by helping others succeed.

What you’ll do

You will turn shared priorities into clear plans and dependable delivery, while building a team that feels valued, motivated and proud of its work. More specifically, you will:

• Co-lead shared responsibilities with the Director of ResWO Module Delivery, and translate agreed priorities into clear plans and effective department delivery.

• Ensure reliable compound management activities and align department resources and capabilities with research needs.

• Drive optimisation of laboratory activities through automation, digitalisation and continuous improvement, to increase efficiency, quality and reproducibility.

• Build partnerships across research functions and with technology and digital teams, taking an enterprise perspective when prioritising improvements and resources.

• Lead, coach and develop your team, creating an environment with psychological safety, clear expectations, accountability and opportunities to grow.

Who you’ll work with

You will join ResWO within Therapeutics Discovery in R&D. The area was recently established to enable faster delivery at scale by strengthening execution of research activities within the protein and peptide pipeline across Therapeutics Discovery in R&D. ResWO will play a key role in supporting competitive research timelines for early research projects until lead candidate selection, by designing, deploying, and optimising high-throughput workflow-based research operations. Success is built on close collaboration with stakeholders across Therapeutics Discovery and a shared ambition to continuously improve how we work. You will help shape how we work and build a culture where people feel empowered to improve laboratory activities and contribute to shared results.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to lead and supported to perform at your best. In Therapeutics Discovery, we lead with intent so that everyone feels valued, motivated and proud of their work, and inclusive leadership is a key capability for this role. You will help build a culture where people feel able to improve laboratory activities and contribute to shared results, and you will have continuous learning and career development opportunities along the way.

If you are ready to co-lead an area that makes research workflows faster, more reliable and more automated, apply for the Associate Director role by 1 November 2026.

As Sr AI Process Designer in Rapid Enablement, you will help business areas across Novo rethink how work gets done with AI, rather than simply applying AI to what already exists. You will join cross-functional engagements that take an opportunity from an initial request to an evidence-based decision about what happens next. By designing future-state services around what AI and people each do well, and testing them with real users, you help the right ideas move forward fast.

What you’ll bring

You are proactive and structured, able to frame ambiguous problems independently, challenge an initial solution request constructively, and test a better future state under time pressure. You bring most of the following:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in service design, interaction design, human-computer interaction or a related field.

• 4+ years of experience applying service design, human-centred design or closely related methods to complex services or business processes, including researching and mapping end-to-end processes across multiple actors, systems, channels and organisational boundaries.

• Strong facilitation experience, including online and in-person creative workshops and co-design sessions with senior, multidisciplinary stakeholders.

• The ability to turn research and operational evidence into clear design opportunities and future-state services, and to prototype and test concepts iteratively rather than relying only on analysis and documentation.

• Excellent visual and verbal communication skills: you make complex processes understandable to non-design and technical audiences, and challenge existing ways of working with confidence.

• A pragmatic mindset: good today is better than perfect tomorrow. You balance great user experiences with project constraints.

• Strong planning and project management skills, with the ability to own larger deliverables independently and translate strategy into ambitious, testable goals.

• Comfort working at pace with incomplete information, and strong collaboration skills with business subject-matter experts, software engineers and AI specialists.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience redesigning knowledge-work or enterprise business processes.

• AI-enabled service or workflow design, including human-in-the-loop patterns.

• Experience in enterprise transformation, internal consulting, or regulated and highly complex organisations.

• Designing services that span digital and non-digital interactions.

• Experience with experimentation, rapid prototyping and discovery methods, and connecting design decisions to measurable business value.

Deep AI expertise is not required. You do need to understand the possibilities and limitations of AI well enough to design effectively alongside technical colleagues.

What you’ll do

You will work in short iterations and test the riskiest unknowns first, making quick progress while reducing risk. You will facilitate the process from start to finish, bring others along without formal authority, and share findings so decision makers can act.

• Plan and facilitate workshops and co-design sessions with business and technical stakeholders to understand real users’ pain points, surface risky assumptions behind AI-driven ideas, and build shared understanding of the problem, target outcome and success criteria.

• Identify where AI, automation or human judgement can materially improve a workflow, and design future-state services rather than digitising the current state.

• Work with team members and stakeholders to make hypotheses concrete through journey maps, service blueprints and prototypes.

• Test concepts with users and stakeholders, use the evidence to iterate, and help decide whether to proceed, change direction or stop.

• Capture rationale and evidence so a receiving team can continue the work after Rapid Enablement exits.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Rapid Enablement, a new and growing team within AI Employee Experience & Enablement, part of Enterprise AI in Enterprise IT & Quality. The team exists to rapidly accelerate high-value AI opportunities across the Novo value chain, from idea to an evidence-based proof of value, and to build reusable enterprise productivity agents.

In cross-functional engagements, you will work with business stakeholders, process owners, engineers and AI specialists. Together you will move from a first request to a clear decision on what should happen next, with a direct effect on how AI improves workflows and is adopted across Novo.

What you can expect here

You will work at the leading edge of how Novo turns AI ambition into proven, adopted solutions, with your design judgement directly shaping which opportunities move forward. You will operate independently on ambiguous, high-value problems and receive guidance mainly on the most complex issues.

Each engagement touches a different part of the value chain, so you will build new skills and broaden your view of the business while contributing your expertise from day one. Your work supports our shared goal of reaching millions of people living with serious chronic diseases and creating lasting health.

Start now

As Laboratory Technician in Research Bioanalysis, you will help early-stage research projects get the answers they need. You will develop and run immunoassays that measure proteins and peptides in biological samples, giving project teams data to predict how long new compounds stay in circulation and how they work in the body. Your work supports early research in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular diseases.

• A relevant education in laboratory technology or equivalent.

• A keen interest in data analysis and a drive to keep data quality high.

• A flair for IT and laboratory instruments, with the willingness to learn and adapt.

• A proactive attitude towards building your analytical technical skills, with an open mindset.

• An energetic, self-driven and organised way of working, and a team-player mindset.

• Hands-on experience with immunoassays such as ELISA, MSD or AlphaLISA.

What you’ll do

New projects often call for new ways of measuring different proteins and peptides. You will spend a significant part of your time developing tailored methods, alongside analysing samples with established ones.

• Develop and implement new immunoassays for the proteins and peptides your collaborators need to measure.

• Analyse samples from in vivo and in vitro studies using immunoassays

• Plan and carry out sample analyses, using robotics and IT systems to handle samples efficiently and track data.

• Analyse data and safeguard data integrity, so project teams can rely on the results.

• Proactively improve laboratory workflows and integrate new digital tools and AI

Who you’ll work with

You will join Research Bioanalysis, part of Therapeutic Discovery within Research & Development, in Måløv, Denmark. In Research & Development, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing. Curiosity, data, technology and collaboration come together to help meet future health needs.

Your team is high-achieving, multidisciplinary and international: seven laboratory technicians, one tech trainee, four associate scientists and eight scientists. You will also work with collaborators who provide the samples and rely on your data, and with colleagues in other departments as workflows are refined across the research process.

You will work in a department that is putting automation, digital tools and AI to use in everyday analytical work. Ballerup, Denmark

What you’ll bring

You enjoy turning technology into business impact. You don’t need deep expertise in every part of AI engineering, but you do have a solid foundation in software delivery, production AI and cross-functional product work.

Beyond your technical expertise, we are looking for someone who is collaborative, curious and self-driven, with strong listening skills and a genuine interest in staying current as the AI landscape evolves.

Day to day, you will often work in product teams in Commercial, Manufacturing & Product Supply and other business areas, alongside product managers, domain experts, data scientists and engineers. Job Description:

Are you a self-starting transformation driver, strategic thinker and pragmatic deliverer, who turns a long-term vision and complex objectives into step-by-step reality and a clear path forward? Do you possess strong project management skills with the ability to translate a multi-year roadmap into smaller bricks and actionable wins, keeping momentum high as requirements evolve? Are you a gifted communicator who breaks down silos and unites cross-functional teams around a lean way of working? Do you possess the business acumen and analytical skills to spot risks and interdependencies across projects and complex organizations? **If so, join us as S&OP Project Manager!

**What The Job Is ...

**We have embarked on a multi-year, enterprise-wide transformation program through 2030 to support the long-term growth and industrialization of Satair and Airbus Material Services. We are redesigning the Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD) across various domains and organizations, for a lean operating model powered by a Fit-to-Standard modern ERP and harmonized processes.

One of the key cornerstones of this transformation is the deployment of an integrated end-to-end Sales and Operations Planning process across various businesses.

In your position as S&OP Project Manager you will be part of a cross-functional and cross-organizational project team. In addition to designing and implementing the TO BE S&OP Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD), you will act as the key point between our external consultancy partners, internal business stakeholders and the broader enterprise transformation program.

Travel required: 15%

**How you will contribute to the team:

**

• PMTD and Architecture Design and Implementation: Design the target Process, Method, Tools and Data covering customer demand, supply capacity and feedback loop mechanisms, including scenario-planning and escalation protocols across and between businesses. Partner with IT and Digital to define the future ERP requirements for S&OP, ensuring a seamless and integrated architecture between Processes and Tools.

• Project Management: Define project roadmap, translate long-term ambition into short-term milestones, maintain project governance, ensure progress towards deliverables, identify and proactively manage interdependencies and risks.

• Stakeholder Alignment Beyond Silos: Proactively identify and engage senior stakeholders across functions and organizations in a complex environment to drive alignment on future ways of working, overcome organizational friction and secure global process simplification and standardization.

• Consultant Management: Lead the relationship with external consultants, steering their deliverables to shape our target S&OP Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD). Validate consultant proposals and recommendations against business needs and context, ensuring designs are scalable and implementable across various business units.

• Strategic Escalations & Executive Briefings: Prepare executive-ready decks, high-impact decision dossiers, trade-off analysis, recommendations and progress updates for executive forums and the central Transformation steering.

• ERP Fit-to-Standard (F2S): Drive business readiness and stakeholder participation across multi-functional teams for F2S workshops to design the future ERP requirements. Safeguard S&OP scope requirements within the central ERP system, ensuring seamless alignment between S&OP process and the future ERP capabilities.

• Ad-Hoc Initiatives: Lead other potential initiatives or projects related to S&OP.

**Candidate Profile & Qualificatio ns

**Core experience and background **:

**

• Education: MSc/MA in Business, Economics, Strategy, Finance, Supply Chain or a related field

• Experience and Track record: 5-8+ years of experience in Project Management, Supply Chain, Management Consulting or equivalent. Proven track record in project management, S&OP deployment, leading cross-functional teams or enterprise process redesigns.

• Methodologies: Mastery of structured project management and business process mapping.

• Languages: Fluent English is mandatory. Good command of French or German is a plus.

**Work style and soft skills:

**

• You are self-driven, proactive and autonomous

• You can translate complex long-term objectives into clear sequential steps. You have a strong focus on driving progress and delivering results, ensuring execution momentum even when requirements change.

• You can balance strategic thinking with tactical execution

• You are analytical, and enjoy understanding the intricacies of how things work

• You are excellent at stakeholder management and can navigate large organizations with ease

• You are a natural communicator and consensus builder, with the ability to understand and demystify complex concepts to obtain stakeholder buy-in

• You have the ability to influence senior leaders, negotiating trade-offs and overcoming organizational resistance.

• You have excellent analytical skills and business acumen, able to translate complex information into clear recommendations

**What does your next challenge look like?

**At Satair, we believe in sustainable aviation that allows people to travel and connect across the globe.

We are on a mission to provide world class material solutions that keep aircraft flying and extend their lifespan.

In Satair, you can challenge the status quo, pioneer new ways of working, and generate real value for airlines and suppliers worldwide.

Being part of the Airbus family gives us the opportunity to live a global mindset, working in international teams and collaborating across functions, sites and cultures.

If you want to work as one team embracing a can-do attitude in a demanding environment, then we offer a great place to explore, learn, and grow.

Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company!

**Satair offers first class material management solutions in the aftermarket business of the aviation industry. We are working to be the most customer-centric organization in providing commercial aviation spares parts to make the world continue flying. We are constantly taking customer experience to new levels by improving how we fulfill and deliver customers’ orders quickly and accurately, anywhere in the world. To meet this goal, Satair is continually striving to innovate and provide best-in-class service levels by pioneering new products and services in a fast growing business environment.

With our global functional organization spanning across 11 different sites and locations worldwide with more than 1.800 people and a turnover of $3.3 billion, you will be part of a truly global family.

Our customers have the ultimate goal to operate their fleet and our Airbus aircraft safely, efficiently in a cost-time-quality effective manner and of course with the expected comfort level for their customers. We at Satair do everything to support our customers in this.

If you want to know more about our business, have a closer look at our website www.SATAIR.com or check out our SATAIR Youtube Channel at www.youtube.com/sataircompany !

**At SATAIR, you will find much more than a job - we offer you the possibility of growing both your personal and professional capacities in a fun, supportive and informal working environment, where you will be encouraged to engage, share knowledge and ideas.

SATAIR is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We love to bring in people with different backgrounds and experiences as we believe it enhances our performance immensely!

**Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company

We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth.

The role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our product team in Aarhus.

This is not a role where you only write code. You are a systems developer. A real part of your time goes into discovery, meaning analysis and design: understanding the problem, shaping the solution, and deciding what is worth building. The rest goes into delivery.

We work AI-augmented. Modern AI tools are a natural part of how we design, write and review software, so more of the typing is handled for you. That makes the harder, more valuable work the judgement: what to build, how it fits together, and whether it holds up as the platform grows. We use AI to move faster, and we believe people are what make sure we build the right things.

Your work will reach hundreds of thousands of people across the Nordics: job seekers navigating labour market reforms, employment professionals adapting to new digitalisation strategies, and the institutions managing that change. Talking with the people who use the platform may be part of the job, so that what you build stays grounded in real needs.

What you will work on

Candeno serves municipalities, unemployment funds, and educational institutions across Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. The platform has three sides: candidates navigating the labour market, advisors guiding them through digitalisation and compliance workflows, and companies recruiting talent. One platform, many contexts.

We are actively building and improving core parts of the platform. You will:

Discovery (analysis and design)

• 
Work with product managers, designers and stakeholders to understand real user problems before we commit to building. AI helps us move fast, so the harder work is knowing what is worth building.

• 
Explore options, weigh tradeoffs, and decide what to build and how.

• 
Contribute to architecture and system design that keep the platform scalable and maintainable.

Delivery (development and operations)

• 
Design, build and maintain robust, scalable features across the platform.

• 
Write clean, maintainable code, using AI tools where they help and applying judgement to what they produce.

• 
Review code and designs, test and debug complex issues, and give constructive feedback.

• 
Operate what you build: CI/CD, containers and cloud, and refactor as the platform grows.

Quality and craft

• 
Meet security standards and protect user data in a data-sensitive sector.

• 
Share knowledge and mentor other engineers on craft and good practice. This is technical mentoring, not people management.

Who we are looking for

You are a senior engineer who is as comfortable in the problem as in the code. Your foundation is strong delivery, and your edge is at the front of the process: you know how to find the right problem before jumping to a solution, and how to do it at a pace that keeps up with a team that ships.

You will need:

• 
5+ years building software, ideally SaaS.

• 
Strong with PHP and Laravel, and with JavaScript and React.

• 
Experience with containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes) and running services in the cloud.

•

jobs.description:
Who We Are

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,500+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds in general.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated in our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

While striving to deliver client value, we believe it is vital to consider our people and our planet in every business decision we make. Acting responsibly is not optional. It is essential.

Why This Role is Important to Us

We are looking for Software Engineers at middle level to join our engineering team that builds fintech solutions for managing OTC (Over-The-Counter) financial instruments within our asset management platform, SimCorp Dimension and SimCorp One. Our work delivers value in two major areas. First, we implement new features that drive the business forward and shape the future of our platform. Second, we focus on extending and maintaining our established solutions to ensure our clients’ operations remain uninterrupted and always available.

What You Will Be Responsible For

• 
Designing, building, and extending existing solutions and APIs for our OTC asset management product, delivering value to customers incrementally.

• 
Working primarily in C#. Our codebase also includes OCaml and APL therefore prior experience with these languages is a strong plus.

• 
Understanding, refactoring and modernizing our legacy codebase without disrupting the business it supports.

• 
Focusing on the systems as a whole and being able address fundamental changes that improves the quality, performance and user experience.

• 
Collaborating closely with your product owner to refine requirements, clarify business needs, and shape how features get built.

• 
Working as part of a team of skilled engineers — pairing, reviewing code, and sharing ownership of the solution with fellow engineers.

• 
Following good engineering practice: clean code, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
Building, extending and consuming REST APIs.

• 
Communicating clearly with both technical and business stakeholders.

• 
Continuously learning — and helping the team and product grow with you.

Required Skills & Experience

• Interest in creating innovative features for a complex platform, working on areas such as API scalability, automation, performance, and operational resilience - having space to explore, design and influence the final solution.

• Good C# skills. This is the core language for the role; your level of seniority will determine how much ownership and architectural input you're expected to bring.

• Experience with, or genuine interest in, functional programming. Familiarity with OCaml, APL, F#, Standard ML, Scala or Haskell is a real advantage but not required — a willingness to learn is what matters most.

• Experience (or strong interest) in refactoring existing code and working with legacy systems.

• Good collaboration and communication skills, with fluency in English (written and spoken).

• A relevant degree (Computer Science or STEM) with demonstrated hands-on experience in software engineering.

Furthermore, We Value That You Are:

• motivated to work within the financial domain,

• comfortable working closely with a cross-functional team,

• willing to learn and pick up new languages and paradigms as needed,

• able to identify tech debt and help drive incremental improvement,

• a collaborative person willing to share knowledge and learn from your team members.

Our Team and Ways of Working

We deliver solution for large scale financial institutions with billions of dollars in managed assets. Therefore, our work impacts everyday of our customers operations. You will work in a small team of highly skilled engineers on whole SDLC process – from understanding customers' needs, through solutioning and design to coding, testing and maintaining our software. Our hybrid model of working includes two days (minimum) in our Copenhagen office and up to three days working remotely. Codebase includes a mix of C#, OCaml and APL which gives broad opportunities to upskill and drive your career with us. We invest a lot in your understanding of both the technical details of the solution and financial knowledge that will allow you to contribute to building the future of asset management.

Our Benefits

Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work-life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP innovation sprints, where you have dedicated time per quarter to spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

Next Steps

Please click below to apply. Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your CV in English as soon as possible. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is the right fit, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks. We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone's experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process, we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

Every year, European governments spend billions on mobility: subsidies, contracts, licences, public transport. Most of that money is spent with no clear idea of what it buys for society.

We're building the tech layer that changes that.

What we do

Impact Market builds MIMA, the Mobility Impact Market. On our platform, cities and transport authorities incentivise mobility operators (bike share, e-scooters, car-pooling, car sharing, bike leasing) for trips according to their benefit to society: a car trip replaced, emissions avoided, space and congestion saved, health improved, a neighbourhood connected. By estimating the socio-economic impact of each trip, we design smart incentives that get the most social value out of public funds.

The idea is much bigger than mobility: governments paying for the outcomes they want, with the evidence to back it up. Mobility is our first market, and we intend to move into other areas of public spending.

Where we are

• 
Funded with 12+ months runway

• 
Several paying public-sector clients

• 
A production platform (prod + staging), with live trip and rider-survey data from operators flowing in since August 2026

• 
A team of 3. You'd be number 4.

The role

You'll be our first technical hire and will lead product and engineering. For now that means hands fully dirty: you write the code. No agencies, no outsourcing.

• 
Own the platform. Rust, Postgres, cloud, our RiderSurvey API, and the data pipelines from operators. You'll inherit a working MVP and decide what to keep, what to rebuild and what to build next.

• 
Make the big calls, including the language. We chose Rust deliberately: we think a strict compiler and type system are the right guardrails for building fast with AI. If you have a better argument for something else, convince us.

• 
Be AI-native. We expect you to use AI seriously in coding and every other technical task. That's how a team of four does the work of fifteen.

• 
Build agents that run the company with us, for account management, client reporting and forecasting.

• 
Grow into the science. Together with a future R&D lead, you'll work on the statistical significance of measured impacts and on forecasting how markets respond to incentives.

• 
Shape the product with the founders and our clients. You'll be in the room with transport authorities, not behind a ticket queue.

You

• 
Have minimum 4 years of relevant experience shipping production software, ideally backend or data-heavy systems

• 
Senior and still love writing code every day? Even better.

• 
Know Rust, or are genuinely motivated to go deep in it (not just "willing"). (We are not dogmatic about Rust, but we have a working platform built with care, so changing direction would take strong conviction.)

• 
Already build with AI tools daily and have opinions about how to do it well

• 
Are comfortable with data: SQL, pipelines, and an appetite for statistics and forecasting

• 
Take ownership when things are ambiguous, and like it when nobody tells you how

• 
Care about the mission. You don't need to have read our founder's book, The Next Democracy, but its core ideas about how citizens and governments could work together - is fundamental to what we do. If they don’t excite you, this probably isn't the right fit.

Bonus points for experience in mobility or transport, govtech, causal inference or experimentation, or privacy-by-design and GDPR.

What we offer

• 
A real say in everything. Stack, product, architecture, culture and who we hire next.

• 
Title decided together. We're advertising this as CTO / Founding Engineer and will settle the title with you based on your experience and ambitions.

• 
Competitive startup salary plus a meaningful warrant package, designed to make total compensation comparable with bigger-company offers

• 
5 weeks of holiday and flexible hours

• 
Work that matters. Help redirect public money towards what actually improves people's lives.

Location

Copenhagen is our home, and we'd love you here; relocation is very welcome. If you stay elsewhere, you must be based in the EU and work in EU time zones. You'd spend your first 1–2 months with us in Copenhagen, then 2–4 days here every month after that.

Impact Market aims to transform public procurement like Google and Facebook transformed marketing. Impact Market facilitates payments for outputs, and allows public institutions to pay for the projects that create the outcomes they seek. Instead of choosing one service, public authorities can work with multiple companies, and allow them to compete and innovate in creating the results. About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• 
Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• 
Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• 
Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• 
Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• 
Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• 
Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• 
Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• 
Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• 
A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• 
Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• 
Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• 
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• 
Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• 
Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• 
Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• 
Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• 
Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like for the Team You'll Join

• 
Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• 
Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• 
Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• 
The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• 
The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• 
A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• 
A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• 
An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

Digital Operations Manager (Mid, DACH region) Aarhus or Hamburg | Full-time | Hybrid (3+ days a week in the office)

About AutoUncle

Buying a used car is one of the biggest purchases most people make, and one of the hardest to get right. Is the price fair? What will it really cost? AutoUncle was founded to answer those questions. Today, car buyers across Europe use our websites and apps to compare almost every used car for sale and see whether the price is right, for free.

The car dealerships that sell to those buyers are our customers. Over 700 of them use AutoUncle to sell more cars. We send them buyers who are ready to act, and we put tools on their websites that turn visitors into leads.

Now we're going a step further. CoDriver, our newest product, is an AI assistant that answers every lead a dealer gets, on every channel, day or night, and keeps the conversation going until the buyer is ready. We're no longer just sending buyers to dealers; we're helping them close the sale.

Why we’re hiring

AutoUncle is growing fast. More dealers are signing up, and more of them are choosing CoDriver, which connects directly to their CRM, lead providers and website. Every new customer means a new setup to get right and keep running.

The Digital Operations Team

That's where our Digital Operations Team comes in. Sales wins the customer; Digital Operations makes our products work for them. The team gets new dealers live, keeps their integrations healthy and fixes issues quickly when something breaks. A dealer only sees value once leads are flowing, so this team has a direct hand in whether customers stay and grow with us.

The team works across Denmark, Germany and Italy, and we're looking to add someone in the near future to our DACH team to support our growth in the region.

Your mission

Own the technical setup for a portfolio of 60–80 DACH customers, from first call to go-live and beyond. Make sure every product we deliver is properly integrated, measurable from day one, and keeps working.

Day to day, you’ll:

• 
Lead technical onboardings. Connect our products with dealer websites, CRM systems and inventory feeds, and coordinate more complex or tailored integrations.

• 
Join customer meetings alongside Sales, answer technical questions in German and set clear expectations on feasibility and go-live timelines.

• 
Pick up the phone to unblock setups. Reach out to web agencies, CRM providers and dealer IT contacts to solve problems quickly.

• 
Diagnose tracking and data issues. Investigate GA4, Google Tag Manager, consent mode and event tracking when numbers don’t add up, and find out why, not just what.

• 
Customize and improve. Adjust widgets with custom CSS and improve our standard integrations to give customers’ website visitors a better experience.

• 
Keep your portfolio healthy with regular health checks, inventory quality checks and proactive monitoring.

• 
Build repeatable systems. Turn recurring problems into standard workflows, documentation, and AI workflows and automations the whole team uses, and work with product and tech colleagues to drive improvements.

What you bring

• 
Native or near-native German, and fluent English (our company language)

• 
2+ years of experience in technical integrations, implementation, digital operations or a similar role, ideally in B2B SaaS

• 
Hands-on experience with web analytics and tracking (GA4, Google Tag Manager or similar). You understand events, conversions and consent mode well enough to troubleshoot them

• 
A basic understanding of APIs and how systems exchange data

• 
HTML/CSS skills for adjusting and troubleshooting website integrations

• 
Confidence picking up the phone and working with both technical (developers, CRM providers) and non-technical (dealers, sales teams) contacts

• 
A structured way of working: you run several setups at once, prioritize your own pipeline and follow through without being chased

• 
You already use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) to get real work done, and you can tell us about something you automated or made faster.

Nice to have:

• 
Experience in the automotive industry or at a web agency

• 
Experience with HubSpot or dealer CRM systems

What we offer

• 
€54,600–67,800 gross annual (final salary depending on experience)

• 
Extended social benefits; including 30 holiday days + local holidays, extended parental leave, etc. See more in our Employee Handbook!

• 
Structured training in your first three months, alongside experienced teammates, on our products (Traffic Performance, Website Booster and CoDriver),and how dealerships work

• 
A clear path to Senior Digital Operations Manager, by owning a specialist area such as data quality, website tracking or partner integrations

• 
A growth review every six months and support from your manager to plan your next step

• 
Impact you can see: when a dealer goes live and the leads start coming in, you made that happen

How we work

We're AI-native, and you'll help shape how we use AI in customer operations.

AutoUncle moves fast, and priorities can change from week to week. If you haven't worked somewhere like this before, that's fine. If the idea sounds exciting rather than stressful, you'll fit right in.

We hire for four traits we call "the Ticket": being ambitious, humble and coachable, with a bias for action. We also live by the Five Cs: Clear, Courage, Curiosity, Commitment and Compassion. Our Employee Handbook gives a good feel for how we work.

jobs.description:
Would you like to become the technical go-to person for the systems that keep a fleet of working vessels accurate and operational? At HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor, you will take ownership of dredging systems, survey equipment and onboard IT across the fleet, with plenty of freedom to shape how the area is run.

Take technical ownership across the fleet

HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor has delivered marine construction projects since 1958 and today works across Northern Europe within dredging, offshore wind, coastal protection and maritime infrastructure.

As the fleet grows, HØJ wants to bring more technical knowledge in-house. You will join the technical team in Horsens, where you will take specialist responsibility for the systems connecting dredging operations, positioning, survey equipment and onboard IT. While your colleagues cover other technical areas across the fleet, your primary focus will be the dredging systems and the related IT and survey technology.

Your main focus will be the 3D dredging systems across seven vessels, including Teledyne PDS, positioning equipment, sensors and the supporting IT setup. You will work closely with skippers, crews, project managers and suppliers and become the person they turn to when systems need to be set up, improved or brought back online.

Some days, you will work alongside your colleagues in the technical team in Horsens, planning and coordinating maintenance, configuring systems or supporting vessels remotely. Other days, you will be on board troubleshooting equipment, preparing a vessel for a new project or carrying out planned service and maintenance.

The aim is not only to solve problems when they occur, but to create a more consistent, well-documented and reliable setup across the fleet.

More specifically, you will:

• Take technical ownership of the fleet’s dredging systems and Teledyne PDS setup

• Work with positioning, sensors, multibeam and other survey equipment

• Support and improve onboard IT, networks and communication systems

• Plan preventive maintenance, calibrations and service

• Document the technical setup on each vessel and prepare relevant reports

• Support crews and project managers with troubleshooting and project preparation

One of your first tasks will be to map the existing system landscape across the vessels. You will also help commission the dredging system on a new vessel and establish clearer standards across the fleet.

Mechanical Engineer – FLOWVISION A/S

About FLOWVISION A/S

FLOWVISION A/S is a Danish engineering company founded in 2006, specialized in designing and delivering advanced emission abatement systems for combustion-based power plants worldwide. Since 2021, the company has been part of AXENS GROUP, while continuing to operate as an independent business with its own organization, commercial responsibility, and market-facing role.

The company operates in an international EPC environment and delivers technically advanced solutions to customers within the energy, oil & gas, and industrial sectors across multiple global markets. FLOWVISION collaborates closely with major international players and is recognized for its strong technical know-how, high-quality standards, and ability to solve complex engineering challenges.

Today, FLOWVISION employs around 20 highly skilled specialists, creating a strong concentration of technical competencies and deep industry expertise. This gives the company the agility and close collaboration of a small expert team, combined with the backing and broader industrial context of being part of Axens.

FLOWVISION offers a flat organizational structure, short decision-making processes, and a collaborative culture where openness, knowledge sharing, and teamwork are essential parts of everyday life.

The company is currently experiencing significant growth and a strong order intake, creating attractive opportunities for professionals who want to influence both project execution and the continued development of the business.

The position

As Mechanical Engineer, you will become part of FLOWVISION’s highly specialized engineering environment and play a key role in the execution of technically advanced international EPC projects.

You will work closely with our Lead Mechanical Engineer, Project Managers, workshops, suppliers, and external engineering partners to ensure that mechanical designs, fabrication documentation, and technical solutions are delivered with high quality and according to demanding project timelines.

The role combines hands-on engineering with close interaction across fabrication, welding, procurement, and project execution activities. You will contribute throughout the entire project lifecycle — from bid clarification and design reviews to fabrication support, inspections, and final documentation.

This is a role for someone who enjoys solving practical engineering challenges, working close to production realities, and operating in an environment where technical quality, collaboration, and execution are critical to success.

You will also have the opportunity to influence engineering processes and contribute to the continued professionalization and growth of the business.

Key responsibilities

Mechanical project execution

• Participate in technical reviews of RFQ packages and specifications during bidding and project execution phases.

• Support clarification processes and ensure alignment of technical scope, assumptions, and interfaces.

• Define mechanical design requirements and coordinate engineering inputs towards external engineering and drafting partners.

• Work with mechanical drawings and technical documentation, including general arrangements, structural steel drawings, piping layouts, isometrics, and fabrication documentation.

• Support structured engineering milestone reviews and contribute to design acceptance and design freeze activities.

• Identify and resolve technical issues, deviations, and design changes throughout the project lifecycle.

• Assess manufacturability and propose practical engineering improvements related to fabrication, welding, installation, and assembly.

Fabrication, welding & workshop interface

• Act as a daily technical interface towards workshops and fabrication partners.

• Handle technical clarifications during fabrication and pre-assembly activities.

• Participate in workshop activities such as PIM, pre-FAT, FAT, inspections, and technical follow-up.

• Support resolution of punch items, deviations, and non-conformities together with Project Management and QHSE.

Documentation & engineering coordination

• Prepare and consolidate mechanical engineering documentation for customer deliveries.

• Work actively with engineering data, revisions, BOM structures, and document control processes.

• Support procurement activities through technical review of supplier quotations and deviations.

• Contribute to maintaining technical quality, traceability, and compliance across all project phases.

Qualifications

We expect you to have:

• A technical degree within Mechanical Engineering or a similar engineering discipline.

• Experience from project-based engineering environments, fabrication, workshops, or EPC project execution.

• Practical exposure to welding, piping, valves, structural steel, or process equipment.

• Strong ability to read, review, and assess mechanical and fabrication drawings.

• Familiarity with relevant standards such as ASME and EN1090.

• Experience working with AutoCAD or similar 2D/3D CAD systems. Plant3D is preferred.

• Experience working with drawings, revisions, BOM structures, and document management systems.

• A structured, analytical, and proactive mindset with strong attention to detail.

• The ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, quality, procurement, and project functions.

• Strong English communication skills, written and spoken. Danish is considered an advantage.

Practical information

• Location: FLOWVISION A/S, Odense, Denmark

• Reporting line: COO / Lead Mechanical Engineer

• Travel activity: Approx. 20–30 days annually depending on projects

What we offer

FLOWVISION offers a unique opportunity to become part of a highly specialized and growing international engineering company where technical know-how and collaboration are the core drivers of success.

We offer:

• A key technical role in an international and rapidly growing engineering company.

• The opportunity to work on technically advanced and highly challenging international EPC projects.

• A unique environment with a strong concentration of specialist competencies and technical expertise.

• Excellent opportunities for professional and personal development as the company continues its growth and professionalization journey.

• A high degree of influence on engineering solutions, project execution, and ways of working.

• A flat organization with fast decision-making and close collaboration across the company.

• A versatile and dynamic workday characterized by openness, cooperation, flexibility, and humor.

• A strong development culture with high ambitions regarding quality, innovation, and employee well-being.

• Office location in Odense with international exposure and limited travel activity.

FLOWVISION is a company where highly skilled people work closely together to deliver complex solutions to global customers — and where the right person will have the opportunity to make a visible impact on both projects and the future development of the business.

Application

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with expertise in kinematics and control systems to join our On-Machine Software team in Odense, Denmark, or Stockholm, Sweden. In this role, you will develop the software that enable construction machines to operate with greater precision, automation, and autonomy.

About the role

You will be part of the On-Machine Software department, where we design and develop developing technology used every day on construction sites around the world. Our software allows construction machines to understand their surroundings and execute precise movements.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will contribute across the full software development lifecycle, from concept and architecture discussions to implementation, testing, and operational support. You will collaborate with software, hardware, and product teams to deliver robust, high-quality solutions.

A particular focus of this role will be supporting and evolving key machine control applications while contributing expertise in system design, software architecture, kinematics, control systems, sensor integration, and advanced software development practices.

What you’ll do

• Develop and maintain software for machine control and automation systems.

• Contribute to technical decisions, architecture, and system design.

• Take ownership of key software components and drive improvements.

• Collaborate across software, hardware, and product teams to deliver reliable solutions.

• Develop machine guidance, automation, and control functionality.

• Participate in technical reviews and mentoring of colleagues.

• Work with sensor integration, positioning technologies, and control algorithms.

• Contribute to technical investigations and innovation initiatives.

What you'll bring

You have a degree in Software Engineering, Robotics, Control Engineering, or a related technical discipline and several years of professional software development experience.

You thrive on tackling complex system-level challenges and are often the person colleagues turn to for technical guidance. While you work well independently when needed, you also enjoy collaborating with others and sharing your expertise in our global organization.

We expect you to have:

• Strong C++ development skills.

• Experience developing software on Linux-based platforms.

• Experience working across the full software development lifecycle.

• Understanding of software architecture principles and object-oriented design.

• Experience developing sensor-fusion and state-estimation solutions.

• Deep understanding of kinematic modelling and control systems, ideally applied to robotics, mobile machinery, hydraulic systems, or automation.

Additional experience:

Would you like to grow professionally in a company that develops and maintains highly complex, mission critical systems for a global market within sortation of luggage in airports and parcels for logistics companies? Then take this opportunity to create something that matters.

Join us to apply your expertise within portfolio management of complex software solutions for logistics centres and airports worldwide. Take on this exciting and demanding leadership challenge to help us deliver vital infrastructure solutions.

Join a software center of excellence

You join BEUMER Group to manage a portfolio of technically complex software projects & products for automated baggage handling systems and parcel sorters. These mission critical systems are installed across international airports and logistics centers as a completely essential part of daily operations 24/7/365. We have the leading products on the market, and the office in Aarhus, Denmark, is an international center of excellence within the BEUMER organization.

Set the direction

Specifically, you become a member of the software leadership team in Aarhus, where you assume the overall responsibility for a growing software department of +30 project managers, architects and developers. Here, you set the direction and run the portfolio of Software Customer Support projects including coordination with teams from other Group Companies. You also contribute to and review proposals and do capacity planning for current and future activities. This includes utilizing resources from other Group Companies.

Take on budget and project responsibility

You become accountable for the budget and project execution of all Software Customer Support projects up to medium size, overseeing up to 50 projects of duration from a few months up to 2-3 years. It is your job to guide, support and coach the responsible software project managers, so we can deliver on-time and within agreed budget, scope and quality.

Software Product

Our solutions are built on a number of core products developed by BEUMER. You provide input and ideas to product managers in the product department but in the Software Customer Support department you also take responsibility for maintenance of the legacy products developed by BEUMER.

Facilitate great collaborations

As you do so, you monitor the progress of the project portfolio, implement corrective actions when needed, and provide your support by attending meetings with customers, partners and suppliers. But just as important, you collaborate with your peers in other divisions and departments to facilitate good collaboration in order to ensure that the software and electro mechanic components come together as an integrated system.

Skilled portfolio manager

As Head of Software Customer Support Projects, your task is to enable your organization, so it can deliver the high-quality software projects needed for mission critical systems. To do so, we believe you:

• Have a master’s degree and have worked in a similar role, as department or portfolio manager, where you have managed complex software development projects, including budget management.

• Knows about application management / product lifecycle management

• Thrive in a fast-paced international project environment, where making decisions, handling several projects at once and keeping good relations to stakeholders is the key to your success

• Are an experienced leader of leaders and know how to develop and support employees, creating buy-in and setting a direction.

• Knowledge about software development processes like Scrum, CMMI, ITIL and similar methods and standards would be an advantage.

• You are PMI, IPMA or Prince2 certified or have a similar training/certification

About the Role

304879

Denmark

Ballerup

Wind Power
