A Snapshot of Your Day

You will most likely start in a wind turbine development project that is still in its early stages. Using our MATLAB controller tuning tools and BHawC (our in-house aeroelastic wind turbine simulation code), you will investigate controller solutions to optimize the balance between turbine loads, turbine behaviour, and power production.

Working closely with experienced colleagues, you will review simulation results, apply engineering judgement to identify the next steps, and coordinate with teams across Turbine Loads, Software, Certification, Testing, and component design.

As you gain experience and the project progresses, you will also work with prototype data and support turbine validation activities at our test site in Østerild.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on wind turbine controller development, tuning and validation. It is not a project management or software development position, although you will collaborate closely with both disciplines.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• 
Tune the wind turbine controllers using aeroelastic simulations and engineering analysis.

• 
Analyze simulation and test results to understand turbine loads, performance and behaviour.

• 
Support the development of new controller functionalities, from early simulation studies through prototype validation.

• 
Identify opportunities to improve engineering tools, reports, methods, and processes, and take an active role in implementing improvements.

• 
Collaborate with Turbine Loads, Certification, Testing, Software, and component design teams, while ensuring technical findings and progress are effectively communicated.

What You Bring

• 
A degree in Control Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another relevant engineering discipline.

• 
Relevant engineering experience from industry, research, or technically complex projects, combined with the ability to critically evaluate results, challenge assumptions, and raise concerns when something does not add up.

• 
Strong MATLAB skills and experience with, or interest in, Python for engineering tools and data analysis.

• 
Experience with wind turbines, aeroelastic simulations, control engineering, or prototype measurements is an advantage. We do not expect candidates to bring experience in all of these areas.

• 
A collaborative and responsible way of working, with the ability to communicate progress, seek alignment, and take ownership of the overall engineering challenge, not just your assigned tasks. Fluent English communication skills, both written and spoken.

About the Team

Optimization & Validation is part of the Turbine Control Department within R&D. Our team consists of six full-time employees and two student assistants based in a new office in Ballerup, Denmark. We are proud to be an international team with colleagues from four continents: North America, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Our working language is English.

The team plays a key role in offshore wind turbine development projects. During the early stages of a project, we scope and tune the controller using BHawC simulations, support certification activities, coordinate controller changes with the Software Department, and discuss simulation results with Turbine Loads and component design teams.

As projects move towards prototype testing, we perform extensive validation activities, ensuring turbine and controller performance matches simulation predictions. Much of this work is based on data collected from our prototype offshore turbines installed in Østerild.

We encourage open technical discussions and value diverse engineering perspectives. Constructive disagreement is welcomed when it helps identify a problem or reach a better technical decision.

Who is Siemens Gamesa?

Siemens Gamesa is part of Siemens Energy, a global leader in energy technology with a rich legacy of innovation spanning over 150 years. Together, we are committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. As a leading player in the wind industry and manufacturer of wind turbines, we are passionate about driving the energy transition and providing innovative solutions that meet the growing energy demand of the global community. At Siemens Gamesa, we are constantly seeking individuals to join our team and support our focus on energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Gamesa: https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/careers/working-with-us.html

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by multiple nationalities. We celebrate character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

jobs.occupation: Talent Product Consultant Learning and Development - Assistant Director
jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

**The opportunity

**Help define and advance the future of learning through Microsoft Viva Learning - enabling thousands of employees to build skills every day, in the flow of work.

We’re looking for a Learning & Development Product Consultant to lead key aspects of the firmwide deployment of Microsoft Viva Learning and help drive the end-to-end success of the platform. Working as a trusted partner to the Global Learning & Development Product Owner, senior Talent leaders, functional leads and regional teams, you will help shape strategic priorities, translate them into a practical roadmap, drive adoption at scale and deliver a modern, personalized learning experience aligned to business priorities.

As a global product consultant, you will sit at the heart of Talent, bringing together L&D, Technology and regional stakeholders to transform how learning is curated, delivered and experienced across the firm.

**In this role, you will:

**

• Partner with the Global L&D Product Owner and functional leads to set direction, align priorities and advance Microsoft Viva Learning as a global learning platform

• Translate strategy into a clear roadmap, practical governance and measurable success outcomes

• Drive adoption, engagement and measurable business impact across a complex global stakeholder landscape

• Use data, insights and stakeholder feedback to inform decisions, optimise performance and improve the learner experience

**What will help you succeed:

**

• Proven experience in product ownership, platform leadership or digital product delivery

• Strong background in Talent, Learning & Development or HR transformation

• Hands-on experience with Learning Experience Platforms, Microsoft Viva Learning or the Microsoft 365 ecosystem

• Ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity and lead change in a complex global environment

This is a standout opportunity to help build a skills-led, experience-driven Talent ecosystem, powered by Microsoft Viva Learning — at global scale.

If you’re passionate about learning, product thinking and digital employee experience, we’d love to hear from you.

What we offer you

At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create an equitable and inclusive experience during the recruitment process, please inform us as soon as possible about any disability-related adjustments or accommodations you may need.

**EY | Building a better working world

**EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

Do you want to help build one coherent way for a global technology organization to deliver, bringing scaled product-centric ways of working project and program execution _together into a single system, rather than running them as separate worlds? Are you as comfortable helping shape that system and turning it into ways of working people actually use in the room with the people who'll actually use it?_We are hiring a Manager, Delivery Enablement to help shape and evolve how Pandora's D&T organization delivers. D&T spans the full range of technology that keeps Pandora running: from customer-facing platforms to manufacturing systems, ERP, logistics and operations, security, covering build, run, and operate across all of it. This role does not carry people-management responsibility. Your impact comes through the quality of what you build and how well it lands across the organization.

You'll join Delivery Enablement, a team combining operating-model design and implementation, coaching, and delivery tooling capability. It's built to make Digital & Technology (D&T) faster, clearer, and more coherent at scale. Delivery Enablement sits within Delivery Excellence, alongside the Scrum Masters, Delivery Leads, and Project and Program Managers. You will work with the wider team to shape ideas and turn them into practical ways of working across D&T.

**Your Role

**You will help harmonize and evolve how scaled agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery work together, building on what already exists across D&T rather than replacing it, closing gaps only where they cause real friction. This is as much about leading change as it is about designing structure. You will also advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape, and help teams and entities build the capability to adopt the model as it evolves.

You will work closely with the wider delivery community, as well as product, engineering, and leadership more broadly, to facilitate structural workshops, build the case for change, and make sure what gets designed is something people actually want to use, not just a document on a shelf. A key part of the role is building the relationships, networks and momentum needed to bring ideas to life across D&T.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Co-design and evolve how scaled agile and structured, plan-driven delivery work together, harmonizing and building on existing practice rather than replacing it

• Advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape

• Lead workstreams that take new or improved delivery processes (for example dependency management or capacity planning) from idea through pilot, rollout, adoption and continuous improvement

• Support onboarding and capability-building for teams and entities adopting the model, working alongside the team's wider coaching capability

• Facilitate structural workshops and working sessions with the wider delivery community to shape and pressure-test the model

• Build relationships, networks and communities that help change spread and stick across D&T

• Pilot approaches, learn from feedback, and scale what works

• Help translate high-level decisions about how delivery is prioritized, funded, resourced, and executed into practical structures and standards teams can use

• Help projects and programs connect into the wider D&T Operating Model, including common governance, planning, dependency management and delivery tooling

• Contribute to keeping the model coherent as it evolves, spotting where new structures overlap or conflict with what already exists

• Provide point-in-time advisory support where operating-model gaps are most costly

• Document how the operating model works and how it evolves over time

• Build strong relationships across the wider delivery community and leadership to ensure what gets built is genuinely adopted

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• ignificant experience in delivery transformation, operating-model implementation, PMO, program/project delivery or organizational change within a large, complex technology organization

• Demonstrated experience working across both scaled/product-centric agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery, with enough understanding to contribute credibly to how they work together

• Track record of taking new ways of working from idea through implementation, adoption and continuous improvement

• Ideally a mix of hands-on delivery experience and consulting or advisory experience, but real, first-hand delivery experience matters more than advisory polish alone

• Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, and narrative-building skills across senior and operational levels

• Comfortable leading through organizational change: helping people, not just structures, adapt as delivery models shift

• Able to build trust, networks and momentum without relying on formal authority

• Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate your own analysis, design, and documentation work

• Working understanding of how delivery tooling (e.g. Jira/Confluence, or equivalent) underpins an operating model, enough to design frameworks that translate into practice, not to configure the tooling yourself

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: building on foundations already in motion, while still shaping significant parts of the model from scratch

• Systems thinking: able to see cross-domain and cross-entity dependencies, not just local fixes

• Pragmatic bias toward incremental, adoptable change over comprehensive upfront design

• Relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2, SAFe) are an advantage

**Did we get your attention?

**We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

About Envira

Envira turns satellite and geospatial data into climate-risk intelligence for banks, insurers and public authorities. Envira Flood covers flood and storm-surge risk at building level; Envira Agro covers crop and climate risk across agricultural portfolios. We're based in Copenhagen and won the EU Big Data from Space Award 2025 plus the Danish Grunddataprisen 2026.

The role

Full-time, on-site in Copenhagen five days a week. You'll own the platforms our customers use, working closely with our data scientists and leadership, with real influence on how our products are built and run. This isn't a standard corporate job: we're looking for people who ship and want to grow fast. There will be pressure, and real ownership to match.

What you'll work on

• Building and extending our web platforms and APIs

• Connecting our geospatial data and risk models to customer-facing applications

• Running and improving our Azure infrastructure: deployment, monitoring and reliability

• Data security and access control, in line with what financial-sector customers expect

Our stack

Python and FastAPI · React and TypeScript · Postgres · Azure · Docker

About you

• Newly graduated or up to 3–4 years of experience, with a degree in computer science, engineering or similar

• You've built something, run it in production yourself, and kept it running

• Comfortable across backend, infrastructure and frontend

• You use AI tools daily, and review, question and discard what they produce when it's wrong

• You prefer small, simple solutions that work over impressive architecture

• You raise problems early and make decisions without waiting to be told

• You live in Denmark and can work from our Copenhagen office five days a week. We don't offer remote work or visa sponsorship

Our working language is English; Danish is a plus.

What we offer

• Salary based on experience, with potential for warrants

• Free lunch at the office

• Ownership of real products used by banks, insurers and public authorities

• The opportunity for tremendous growth

Our process

Short screening call → two-hour practical task on realistic data with your usual AI tools (no whiteboard puzzles) → interview where you walk us through your solution and meet the team.

How to apply

Please apply through our application form (about 10 minutes; we ask for your CV, grades, GitHub link and salary expectation). We review applications on a rolling basis, so apply early.

PanTarg is a Danish biotechnology company developing novel anti-cancer therapies in the form of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of aggressive cancers with high unmet medical need.

Our work is based on more than 30 years of research conducted at Rigshospitalet and University of Copenhagen, and our vision is to enable novel treatment options for cancer patients via a novel first-in-class approach to targeted therapy.

We are currently incubated at the BioInnovation Institute (BII), a Copenhagen-based incubation hub for biotech startups in Europe. Here, we are currently progressing through preclinical development, aiming to reach a stage of clinical testing within a few years.

The position

We are looking for a scientist to join our team on site at BII. We are primarily looking for a candidate with several years of hands-on experience, especially within immunohistochemistry (IHC) techniques and target expression analyses. The candidate will be responsible for generating and analyzing data that will be essential for several key readouts and business decisions, including safety assessments and clinical indication selection.

Qualifications

• 
Primary qualification: Documented experience in histology and IHC, including target/biomarker scoring, tissue microarrays (TMA), and spatial analysis. Experience with tissue handling, sectioning, and staining is highly desirable, ideally combined with experience using digital image-analysis software such as QuPath or equivalent.

• 
The optimal candidate will have obtained a PhD degree and have at least 3-5 years of experience from either pharma, biotech, or as a post doc. Robust and documented (5+ years) relevant hands-on experience without a PhD degree may also be acceptable, if the primary qualification is met.

• 
Secondary qualification: Hands-on experience with in vitro biology & pharmacology in the form of mammalian cell culture, in vitro dose-response studies and characterization of drug activity, cell viability/cytotoxicity assays, flow cytometry, ELISA, and related cellular assays, will be a highly desired skillset.

• 
Good scientific communications skills, and the ability to clearly and precisely present data to a professional audience.

• 
Good interpersonal skills, and the ability to thrive in a startup environment where flexibility and a can-do attitude is part of everyday work life.

• 
Fluent in the English language, written as well as spoken.

General information and how to apply

• 
You will be reporting to the Chief Scientific Officer.

• 
The position is full time, and on-site presence at the BioInnovation Institute in Copenhagen will be required.

• 
Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, and the selected candidate will start as soon as possible.

• 
Application takes place via the application system here at LinkedIn.

• 
Please provide and combine, in a single file for the LinkedIn application system, a one-page CV, as well as a short, motivated application letter (also one page), summarizing your relevant experience, key responsibilities in previous roles, and motivation for applying for the position.

• 
Questions about the open position should be addressed to the e-mail address jobs@pantarg.com

At Factbird, we help manufacturers see what’s really happening on their lines, so they can make better, faster decisions. Our plug-and-play hardware and cloud platform turn live production data into clear insights, and we’re scaling fast across sites, teams, and countries.

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

About the role

Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

**

The team mission we are on:** Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

What You'll Do

• Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how

• Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.

• Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.

• Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes

• Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.

• Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.

• Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.

• Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.

• Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.

• Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.

• Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

About you

You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”

You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.

You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:

• A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).

• Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.

• Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.

• Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.

• Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.

• Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.

• Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.

• A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We’d love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Khristel, our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead at khma@factbird.com

_At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

_

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws._

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird._

About Factbird

Great people make great things happen

Factbird is on a mission to make manufacturing more efficient. We build intuitive tools that give frontline teams the insights they need to reduce waste, improve processes, and stay ahead. Since 2016, we’ve helped manufacturers worldwide drive real change. Now, we’re searching for great people to help us do even more.

If you are ready for a new challenge, personal growth, and a workplace that genuinely values your development, we have the perfect opportunity for you. Join the team as a temporary worker at DSV in Horsens.

work tasks includes:

Randstad is the world’s largest talent company and a partner of choice to clients. As a Partner for Talent, we are committed to providing equitable opportunities to people from all backgrounds and helping them remain relevant in the rapidly changing world of work.

jobs.occupation: Data Platform Engineer – Offshore Wind Industry
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building and running reliable, scalable and secure cloud data platforms? Do you want to work in the offshore wind industry, where your engineering skills will help secure a sustainable future based on renewable energy? Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Food Science programme. The position is available from 15 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Understanding supramolecular protein structures in multiphase food

Research area and project description
To move the green transition of the food sector forward, there is a need for novel ingredients from sustainable sources that provide the required functionality in food. Designing formulations with plant-based ingredients therefore requires an in-depth understanding not only of their structure and function in isolation but also of their interactions with other ingredients and their dynamics during processing.

This project will focus on protein structure–function relationships using complex model systems, such as emulsions, foams, and gels, applying advanced colloid science and soft matter techniques to embrace the complexity of food. The studies will be conducted at various length to move the green transition of the food sector forward; there is a need for novel ingredients from sustainable sources that provide the required functionality in food. Designing formulations with plant-based ingredients therefore requires an in-depth understanding not only of their structure and function in isolation but also of their interactions with other ingredients and their dynamics during processing.

This project will focus on protein structure–function relationships using complex model systems, such as emulsions, foams, and gels, applying advanced colloid science and soft matter techniques to embrace the complexity of food. The studies will be conducted at various length scales, from molecular to supramolecular and bulk, using methods such as scattering, microscopy, and rheology scales, from molecular to supramolecular and bulk, using methods such as scattering, microscopy, and rheology.

jobs.occupation: Advances in NMR techniques for next generation Foodomics
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Food Science programme. The position is available from 01 February 2026 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Advances in NMR techniques for next generation Foodomics

Research area and project description
The Department of Food Science at Aarhus University is inviting applications for a Ph.D. student position focused on the development and applications of NMR spectroscopy in the characterization of foods - Foodomics.

Foodomics is a scientific approach that studies food, nutrition and their effects on health using omics technologies. NMR spectroscopy has played a key role in establishing Foodomics and has offered distinctive insights into foods’ health-promoting potential as well as their functional characteristics. However, ¹H NMR spectroscopy, which is the current workhorse of NMR-based Foodomics, has some analytical limitations. Thus, spectral overlap renders substantial parts of the food metabolome unidentified.

This PhD project aims at developing and examining new and alternative NMR-based approaches within Foodomics. This includes elucidating the potential of ¹³C NMR spectroscopy, which so far has been limited applied in Foodomics. For this purpose, sensitivity-enhancement strategies will be explored, including a dissolution dynamic nuclear polarization technique (d-DNP). This will be done in collaboration with a prominent European d-DNP group.

The PhD project will entail studies on new foods of alternative sources and/or derived from innovative biotechnological processing techniques and solutions.

Tasks and responsibilities include:

• 
Conduct research on development and applications of NMR spectroscopy in food science.

• 
Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team including a 4-6-months stay in an international research environment abroad.

• 
Design and implement experiments, collect and analyse data, and interpret results.

• 
Present findings at conferences and publish research in reputable peer-reviewed journals.

• 
Participate in outreach activities to disseminate research outcomes to stakeholders and contribute to teaching in the department

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants must have a relevant master’s degree (120 ECTS) in chemistry, biotechnology, food technology, or in a related field.

The preferred candidate has substantial hands-on experience in NMR spectroscopy. Relevant expertise in food science, foodomics, multivariate data analysis and good analytical skills is an advantage.

jobs.occupation: Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development (combined position)
jobs.description:
Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development 

A combined position as Professor (50%) and as Research Director (50%) is vacant at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and at the Centre for Shared Decision Making, Lillebaelt Hospital, Vejle, respectively.

The position is offered for five years, with the possibility of extension.

The academic position
The professor will advance research into shared decision-making (SDM) and the involvement of patients and their relatives, as well as the professional development required to integrate these approaches into clinical practice. The professor will be part of the management team at the joint centre at Lillebælt Hospital and will foster coherence between research, education and implementation. The professor will be appointed at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, SDU. The academic field combines SDM with professional development for healthcare professionals. Interdisciplinary research and collaboration across clinical settings are expected and central to the position.

Research leadership and responsibilities
At Lillebaelt Hospital, the professor/appointee will serve as Research Director. Together with the Centre Director, the Research Director forms the joint center leadership. The Research Director has line management responsibility for academic staff and overall scientific and strategic responsibility for research activities associated with the Center for Shared Decision Making (CFFB) and the Center for Involvement of Relatives (CEPI). The two leadership roles work closely together on the development of the centers.

The professor is expected responsible for:

• 
Strategic Research Leadership and Centre Management
The position as professor includes overall scientific and strategic responsibility for the research units affiliated with both CFFB and CEPI as well as their interdisciplinary research group. This includes line management and academic leadership of researchers, ensuring the stable operation of the centers, and maintaining strategic oversight of the centers’ grant portfolio and funding pipeline.

• 
Fundraising and External Research Funding
The professor is expected to secure substantial external research funding from national and international funding bodies to ensure the long-term sustainability and development of the centers’ research activities.

• 
Practice-Oriented Empirical Research
The professor is expected to develop and lead empirical research SDM projects with a particular focus on the perspectives of patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals within different diseases, specialties and healthcare settings, while contributing to the advancement of qualitative and applied research methodologies such as action research.

• 
Development of Educational Resources, Curriculum Design, and Educational Transformation
The position requires designing and developing practical educational tools and implementation resources — e.g., learning materials — that support healthcare professionals’ learning and continuing professional development in clinical practice performing SDM.

• 
Teaching, lecturing, supervising and disseminating knowledge
The professor should teach and mentor postdocs, PhD students, and undergraduate students. Participation in assessment work is part of the position. Additionally, profiling this research area in the public eye will be an important task.

Research activity, network and collaboration
The candidate is expected to demonstrate prior experience with research activities in terms of networks and collaborations. The professor is expected to increase research activity at the research unit and to expand collaboration with other researchers at hospitals in the Region of Southern Denmark, at SDU, the rest of Denmark and internationally.

The position as Research Director at the Centre for Shared Decision Making (CFFB)
The Professorship in Shared Decision-making and Professional Development at the Center for Shared Decision Making, Vejle, Denmark, is established to support the continued implementation of Lillebaelt Hospital’s research strategy and the hospital’s overarching commitment to placing the patient at the center of care.

Over the past decade, the Center has conducted research on evidence-based approaches to SDM and has demonstrated that SDM is associated with high patient satisfaction and improved adherence to agreed treatment plans. The professorship will build on this strong research foundation by advancing knowledge on the implementation of SDM and the continuing professional development of healthcare professionals. International research consistently shows that achieving sustained and authentic SDM practice in everyday clinical care remains a significant implementation challenge. Changing professional practices and departmental cultures requires more than time-limited projects or implementation initiatives. Sustainable integration of SDM depends on ongoing and continuous competence development that supports long-term changes in clinical practice.

This professorship is positioned at the intersection of health sciences research, implementation in clinical practice, and professional development through applied educational research. The core purpose of the position is to strengthen and transform the healthcare system’s capacity for meaningful patient and family involvement through SDM.

The professorship requires strategic research leadership from a scholar with extensive expertise in lifelong learning, learning theory, curriculum theory, and action research, and with the ability to translate this knowledge into continuing professional development for healthcare professionals. The professor is expected to lead the national and international research agenda on how SDM can be integrated meaningfully and sustainably into routine clinical practice, to achieve enduring behavioral change among healthcare professionals.

Qualifications
The required qualifications:

• 
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent post-graduate research qualification and demonstrate scientific achievements at a level appropriate for appointment as Professor.

• 
The position calls for expertise in educational science as applied to the professional development of healthcare staff or other types of welfare staff, together with substantial knowledge of and research contributions to SDM.

• 
The applicant should be able to demonstrate experience of teaching and lecturing at university and postgraduate level, as well as experience as principal supervisor on PhD projects and academic assessment work, as evidenced by the teaching portfolio.

• 
Danish language skills are not required at the time of appointment, but must be mastered at proficiency level C1, at the Common European Framework of References for Languages within the first 2 years of employment.

The ideal candidate preferably demonstrates:

• 
The candidate should demonstrate experience with leadership capacity with the ability to lead research teams, drive cultural change, and contribute strategically to the development of the centers.

• 
The candidate holds experience in research management, interdisciplinary collaboration, and attraction of external funding for professional development and/or SDM-oriented activities will be considered an advantage.

• 
The candidate preferably demonstrates experience with practice-oriented empirical research. Research that is aimed at both an international research community, and ideally also at the target group of professionals in Denmark; therefore, publications and outputs are welcome to be in Danish – whether in the form of books, leaflets, journal publications or other material designed to ensure that both professionals undertaking continuing professional development in Denmark and students on undergraduate program are best supported and thereby ensuring impact.

• 
The candidate has prior experience with developing, implementing, and/or evaluating educational programs, frameworks, and curricula for continuing professional development, preferably in terms of SDM-related competencies. Experience of developing and evaluating continuing professional education in clinical settings is valued.

• 
The preferred candidate can motivate and supervise, has proven research management skills, good interpersonal skills in charge of a research group, and has a clear vision for how to further strengthen the research unit at CFFB as strong interpersonal and collaborative skills are essential.

• 
The successful applicant will have documented experience of leading research and researchers, obtain external funding and work across disciplines and organizations.

Employers
CFFB is a national knowledge and competence center based at Lillebaelt Hospital. Since 2014, it has researched SDM and since 2019 developed approaches for implementation in clinical practice. CEPI works to strengthen meaningful involvement of relatives. The centers retain their distinct areas of responsibility while collaborating closely on research and practice. Lillebaelt Hospital provides somatic and mental healthcare across sites in Vejle, Kolding and Middelfart. Patient and family involvement is central to their approach to care.

SDU's Department of Regional Health Research links research and education with hospitals and clinical environments across the Region of Southern Denmark. The Department of Regional Health Research supports research in relation to the person as a whole, the good life and the more common diseases, makes out a platform for scientists and educators and builds a bridge between University of Southern Denmark, The Region of Southern Denmark, the hospitals in the region and the patient. The department focuses on the continuity of patient care across sectors, hospitals, and specialist fields.

Reference 
The professor and research director will refer to the hospital management regarding matters concerning the management of the centres, and to the Head of the Department of Regional Health Research, Mikkel Brabrand, in matters regarding the professorship.

Contact information

•

•

Salary and terms of employment
The successful applicant for the professor position will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Professor is salaried in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and on terms corresponding to salary grade 37 of the Danish state salary system. Additional qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Center for Shared Decision Making (Center for Fælles Beslutningstagning), Beriderbakken 4, 7100 Vejle, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Real World Evidence for Knee Osteoarthritis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to help advance PROBE, an Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) public-private partnership focused on patient-relevant osteoarthritis endpoints using big data. You will be anchored in Novo Nordisk’s R&D Real World Evidence (RWE) area, with access to its scientific expertise and support network, and work closely with our Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) team and partners across the consortium.

Your main research focus will be PROBE Work Package 4 (WP4): analysing patient characteristics and identifying factors (such as clinical variables and biomarkers) associated with osteoarthritis progression, meaningful patient subgroups, and potential surrogates of clinically relevant outcomes. You will also help establish the infrastructure and authorised access needed for analysis in the federated database network and contribute to deliverables across other work packages.

What you'll bring

You have a PhD in epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, biomedical informatics, computational biology, public health, or a related field, together with experience analysing complex health data. We expect you to bring:

• 
Strong programming and reproducible analysis skills in R or Python, knowledge of modern machine learning/AI methods, and sound statistical reasoning.

• 
Experience with observational, registry, electronic health record, clinical, or other longitudinal patient-level datasets.

• 
The ability to formulate research questions, assess data fitness, interpret results responsibly, and explain findings to both technical and nontechnical colleagues.

• 
The organisation and initiative to move collaborative research forward across teams and institutions, with fluent written and spoken English.

• 
Experience in osteoarthritis or musculoskeletal research, patient stratification, biomarker research, distributed or federated analytics, and health-data governance would be an advantage.

You do not need experience in every area to apply.

What you'll do

• 
Design and conduct reproducible analyses of patient demographics, clinical characteristics, disease burden, and longitudinal outcomes across relevant osteoarthritis datasets.

• 
Investigate prognostic variables, patterns of disease progression, patient subgroups, treatment effectiveness, and candidate biomarkers or surrogate outcomes in support of relevant research questions.

• 
Work with data owners, WP3 infrastructure partners, internal data specialists, and governance teams to help establish data connections, permissions, harmonised definitions, and practical access to the federated database network.

• 
Apply appropriate statistical and machine-learning methods to heterogeneous real-world data, documenting assumptions, data quality, limitations, and validation results.

• 
Translate findings into scientific reports, presentations, publications, and consortium deliverables, including contributions to other areas where your analyses are relevant.

• 
Coordinate closely with the R&D RWE team and PPP team, and communicate progress and results to multidisciplinary public and private partners.

Who you'll work with

Within R&D RWE, you will work alongside epidemiologists and data scientists who use real-world patient data to inform disease understanding and research decisions. The PPP office will be a close partner in consortium coordination, scientific communication, and delivery of PROBE commitments.

About PROBE

Knee osteoarthritis affects people differently, making it difficult to predict progression and identify who may benefit from specific treatments. PROBE brings together patient data and expertise across academic, healthcare, industry, and patient partners to improve patient stratification, predictive models, endpoints, and clinical trial design. Its federated approach is intended to enable analysis across datasets while respecting applicable governance and privacy requirements.

jobs.occupation: SENIOR BIOLOGIST - DHI MUSE AND AVIAN ECOLOGY
jobs.description:
Do you want to lead the ecological interpretation of complex offshore bird-monitoring projects? Can you turn radar, video, acoustic and environmental data into scientifically defensible conclusions for clients and regulators? Join DHI and take scientific ownership of projects at the intersection of avian ecology, technology and offshore wind.

Responsibilities and challenges

We are looking for a Senior Biologist to provide project-level scientific leadership for DHI MUSE and other avian ecology assignments. You will define research questions and analytical scope of projects, guide ecological interpretation, own the scientific reporting and act as external and internal stakeholders’ scientific point of contact. You will work closely with other biologists, data scientists, radar experts, offshore engineers, software developers and project managers.

Your main responsibilities and challenges will include:

• Lead the scientific scoping, study design and research question definitions for assigned projects.

• Apply and assist in developing methods for analysis in flight trajectories, avoidance behaviour, collision risk, barrier effects, bird flux and species distribution modelling.

• Plan and oversee biological review of video and acoustic material, including species identification, behaviour annotation, reviewer guidance and quality assurance.

• Interpret results of data analysis in their ecological context and account for sensor performance and other confounders.

• Own scientific reports, technical notes, presentations and the scientific content of client proposals through internal review and client approval.

• Act as scientific point of contact in dialogue with clients, regulators, project teams, suppliers and subcontractors.

• Review scientific deliverables and proposals, respond to review comments and advise when available evidence cannot support a requested conclusion.

• Help maintain consistent scientific working practices and actively share knowledge within the team and company.

Qualifications and personal skills

We are looking for a colleague with the following qualifications:

Required:

• Master's degree or PhD in biology, ecology, ornithology or a closely related discipline, or otherwise relevant experience in ornithology.

• Substantial professional experience in ecology, environmental monitoring, ecological consultancy or a comparable applied field.

• Demonstrated experience designing ecological studies and interpreting complex, multi-source datasets.

• Strong scientific and technical writing skills, including ownership of client-ready reports

• Ability to use AI to speed up delivery without loss of quality.

• Demonstrated experience of explaining complex results to non-experts.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

• Ability to lead scientific work across disciplines while maintaining clear ownership and escalation boundaries.

Desirable:

• Experience with offshore wind, environmental impact assessment, collision-risk modelling or bird-migration studies.

• Experience with radar, camera, acoustic or other remote-sensing data used in wildlife monitoring.

• Experience in R, Python or other tools used for data analysis.

• Knowledge of reproducible analysis, data quality assurance or quantitative ecology.

• Instrumentation experience, i.e. developing test plans, conducting test, evaluating results and deriving performance specifications for some equipment.

• Fluent in Polish, written and spoken.

Personal qualities:

• Scientifically rigorous and comfortable making evidence-based decisions.

• Proactive, structured and able to manage competing project priorities.

• Clear and confident communicator who builds trust across disciplines.

• Collaborative and willing to support the development of less-experienced colleagues.

About DHI

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE and MUSE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

DHI MUSE specifically is dedicated to managing the interplay between avian fauna and offshore wind energy. The product and associated work ultimately aim to automate bird monitoring, and as an add-on do curtailment of specific turbines when there is a risk of collision.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminate our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

We offer

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that addresses complex challenges in water and the environment. We will offer you:

• A role where ecological science is applied directly to offshore wind and environmental decision-making.

• Collaboration with biologists, data scientists, analysts, instrumentation specialists and project managers in a novel technology domain.

• Professional and personal development, with room to grow your scientific and client-facing responsibilities.

• Flexible working opportunities.

• A diverse, international network of highly skilled colleagues.

• The opportunity to contribute to the continued development of DHI MUSE and avian ecology services.

Office location

• The position is based at DHI's office in Hørsholm, Denmark, with flexible working opportunities in accordance with DHI policy.

How to apply

• Please submit your application and CV via the relevant job posting on DHI Careers.

• Application deadline: 2026-11-10.

• For further information, please contact Måns Karlsson, Scientific Lead, moka@dhigroup.com, +45 4516 9146.

jobs.occupation: Senior Consultant to Sustainability & ESG – Climate specialization
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit & Assurance, Tax & Legal, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About the team

Our Sustainability Team is made up of experts from different backgrounds, each bringing skills that complement one another. We work together to find practical solutions that help our clients make meaningful progress in sustainability. By understanding their challenges, we develop strategies that create lasting benefits for both businesses and the environment. Our team thrives on collaboration and innovation, ensuring that each project we take on leads to real, measurable improvements in sustainability practices.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced and practically minded Senior Consultant with a specialisation in climate to join our team and support large public- and private‑sector clients in planning and delivering credible decarbonisation and net‑zero strategies. The role combines technical GHG accounting and target-setting expertise with commercial consulting skills to design actionable pathways that reduce emissions, manage climate risk and meet emerging regulatory and investor expectations.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Lead and deliver end‑to‑end GHG accounting engagements across Scope 1, 2 and complex Scope 3 categories, ensuring methodologies align with the GHG Protocol and recognised standards (e.g. CDP, SBTi and ISO).

• Lead SBTi target development and submission projects end-to-end, including scoping, target calculation, documentation, internal alignment and submission support; coordinate validation queries and evidence provision.

• Design, model and present decarbonisation and net‑zero pathways (short, medium and long term), quantifying emissions reductions from levers such as energy efficiency, fuel switching, electrification, renewables procurement (PPA/RECs), process improvements, product design and supply‑chain interventions.

• Build robust emissions models and scenario/modelling frameworks (e.g. marginal abatement cost curves, scenario sensitivity, pathway comparisons) to support strategic decision making.

• Provide guidance on carbon removal, offsetting principles and credible use of removals in net‑zero strategies (aligned to SBTi Net‑Zero Standard and best practice).

• Advise on climate‑related disclosure and compliance (CSRD, TCFD/ISSB-aligned disclosures, CDP), and shape clients’ governance, risk management and climate strategy integration.

• Lead supply‑chain engagement programmes to improve data quality, develop Scope 3 models, and evaluate levers/initiatives (incl. supplier questionnaires, segmentation, data collection tools, supplier capacity building).

Qualifications

We seek a candidate with a solid foundation in climate sustainability and a keen interest in consulting. Experience with climate frameworks, the GHG Protocol, SBTi standards and methodologies and decarbonization approaches is a must. Strong communication and problem-solving skills are essential to succeed in this dynamic environment.

What you bring to the team:

• 3-5+ years’ relevant experience in climate sustainability, GHG accounting and decarbonisation advisory — previous experience at large consultancies and/or engineering background

• Hands‑on experience applying the GHG Protocol (including Scope 3 guidance) and SBTi criteria and methodologies.

• Proven track record delivering SBTi submissions and/or net‑zero strategies that have progressed through validation or board approval.

• Strong quantitative and modelling capability — able to build, interrogate and explain emissions models (Excel; experience with Python/R, SQL or specific decarbonisation tools such as SimaPro, GaBi, or bespoke models is desirable).

• Practical knowledge of energy markets and renewable procurement options (corporate PPAs, I‑REC, GO/REC frameworks), and of carbon removal/offset markets and quality principles.

• Strong project management skills with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders

• A genuine passion for consulting and helping clients achieve their sustainability goals and a proactive approach to driving climate impact

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application and CV by 09th November 2026. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: 4th January 2027

Please do not hesitate to contact Anna Boss at anboss@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Passionate Senior Site Reliability Engineer wanted for strong, supportive team
jobs.description:
Design solutions that solve whole classes of problems rather than individual tasks. As a Senior SRE at Systematic, you keep the systems running that healthcare staff and patients depend on.

Would you like to shape the future of our infrastructure by designing scalable, elegant solutions that solve classes of problems rather than individual tasks? Join our skilled Site Reliability Engineering team where you’ll have the opportunity to think beyond the immediate fix and architect systems that transform how we operate at scale. Your work will keep healthcare solutions running for the clinicians and care staff who depend on them.

The job

As a Senior SRE with a systems engineering mindset, you’ll work at the intersection of deep technical expertise and strategic thinking. You’ll identify patterns across our diverse infrastructure, from Kubernetes clusters to Azure VMs, and create unified solutions that eliminate entire categories of operational toil. This isn’t about fixing one deployment pipeline; it’s about building a framework that makes all deployments reliable. This isn’t about patching one vulnerability; it’s about architecting a security posture that scales across our organization.

You’ll have access to cutting-edge technologies and the autonomy to innovate, with opportunities to work across multiple environments including our ao-admin Kubernetes cluster, Docker-based deployments, Azure-hosted infrastructure, and healthcare-focused systems. When you are ready, you will join the SRE team’s on-call rotation.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Architect automation systems that eliminate classes of manual work, thinking in terms of platforms and capabilities rather than individual scripts

• Develop infrastructure tooling that empowers development teams to self-service their operational needs while maintaining reliability standards

• Build observability frameworks that provide unified insights across diverse environments, making patterns visible and actionable

• Create abstraction layers that hide complexity while providing powerful capabilities, whether through Terraform modules, Helm charts, or custom operators

• Drive infrastructure evolution by identifying systemic improvements and leading their implementation from concept to production

• Collaborate with development teams to understand their patterns of needs and design operations-ready solutions that scale

• Mentor team members in systems thinking and architectural approaches, sharing your problem-solving methodology

• Apply best practices in site reliability engineering, advocating for solutions that improve reliability, security, and maintainability at scale

• Research and prototype emerging technologies and approaches, evaluating their fit for solving our systemic challenges

Joining the team

You’ll join one of our two skilled SRE teams, each consisting of approximately 10 professionals working from our offices in Aarhus and Bucharest. Our teams operate with a DevOps philosophy and use a mix of Scrum and Kanban methodologies depending on the project needs.

We value engineers who can see the forest and the trees, who understand both the technical details and the broader patterns. You’ll work with colleagues who manage everything from Kubernetes clusters to Windows VMs, from Terraform modules to Prometheus monitoring, and you’ll help us find the common threads that allow us to operate more efficiently and reliably.

This is a role with significant room to manoeuvre and influence. You’ll have the opportunity to work with the newest technologies while solving real operational challenges that impact critical systems across multiple domains. Our healthcare solutions, such as Columna, support the continuum of care across hospitals, communities and private homes, so your work contributes directly to patient safety.

Your qualifications

Our ideal candidate is someone who gets excited about patterns, who sees a specific problem and immediately starts thinking “what other problems does this represent?” You’re the engineer who, when asked to automate a deployment, designs a deployment framework. When asked to fix a monitoring gap, you create an observability strategy.

Our ideal candidate would have:

• Experience as a Senior in site reliability engineering, systems engineering, or platform engineering roles with demonstrated impact on infrastructure scalability

• Solid understanding of abstraction and design patterns in infrastructure, with experience creating reusable frameworks, modules, or platforms

• Experience with observability at scale, including metrics, logging, and tracing systems (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack, or similar)

• Strong communication skills to articulate architectural decisions, document systems, and mentor others in systems thinking

• Proven ability to architect solutions that solve multiple problems simultaneously, with examples of platforms or systems you’ve built

We value diverse backgrounds and encourage candidates who are passionate about systems thinking, infrastructure architecture, and solving problems at scale to apply, even if they do not meet every requirement perfectly!

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

As a person, you are proactive, structured and solution-oriented. We work closely with Operational Maintenance, Engineering, production areas and laboratories, and we support both daily operations and strategic site changes. Together, we are helping LEO Pharma close one chapter in a responsible way while preparing for the next generation of innovative production.

**

Contact and application**

For additional information, please contact Adam Lundsby Rejkjaer, Senior Team Leader, Maintenance Support at BDYDK@leo-pharma.com

Beyond the skin

Join LEO Pharma, a global leader in medical dermatology, as we go beyond the skin to make a lasting impact.  Our innovative approach sets us apart. We are dedicated to leaving a legacy that positively impacts patients, colleagues, and our planet.

At LEO Pharma, we believe in the power of individuals to drive change. Our flat organizational structure empowers you to make a visible impact and offers versatile roles for professional growth. Today, we're proud to be among Europe's five largest wood-burning stove manufacturers, exporting 90% of our production.

Innovation is at the heart of what we do. Several of our products are patented, and we're constantly working to develop new solutions that push the boundaries of our industry.

Sollten wir Ihr neuer Arbeitsplatz sein?

At Aduro, you'll join a growing, dynamic company with a strong entrepreneurial spirit. We believe in sharing ideas, taking responsibility and helping each other succeed. Our working environment is informal and collaborative, with plenty of opportunities to grow both personally and professionally.

We're proud of what we've achieved along the way. We've received the prestigious Gazelle Award seven times, recognising our strong growth. In 2024, we were also finalists for EY's Entrepreneur of the Year award and won the SME Inspiration Award in the Internationalisation category for our international outlook.

At our headquarters, you'll become part of an international team representing seven different nationalities. Different cultures and perspectives come together in an energetic workplace where ambition, teamwork and a good sense of humour go hand in hand. We offer modern facilities, social activities, a company lunch scheme and opportunities to develop your skills and take on new challenges.

Great code is only half the job

Cadpeople is hiring a frontend developer in Aarhus who writes solid code, understands the client, designs the system, and makes it feel right.

For 30 years, we've made the complex simple for companies like Vestas, Ørsted, Grundfos, Novo Nordisk and Fred. Olsen. We do it with 3D, XR, digital training simulators, virtual campuses, and digital learning, all built on our in-house frameworks.

The craft is changing too. AI tools already have a big impact on how we develop, and we're on a journey to strengthen our AI coding capabilities. But AI only pays off in the hands of developers with real knowledge and experience. That's why we look for systems thinking, client dialogue, and close collaboration with our creatives, as much as we do code.

What you'll do

You'll build bespoke applications for large enterprise clients, from the first workshop to the live solution. Typical work:

• Turn client needs into systems. Join client meetings and workshops, ask the right questions, and shape the solution before anyone writes code.

• Think across frameworks. Combine our in-house building blocks (Vue.js and Three.js frontends, Digital simulators, Umbraco headless CMS, .NET microservices on Azure, and Electron for offline use) into the right architecture for each case.

• Use what we've already built. Draw on experience from delivered projects to show the client what's possible, and to avoid building the same thing twice.

• Help shape how we build with AI. Use AI tools in your daily work, and help us strengthen our AI coding capabilities as we go.

• Work closely with creatives. Art directors, 3D artists, learning specialists, and project managers are your daily team. You make their ideas run in the browser, on a kiosk, or in a headset.

• Strengthen the foundation. Improve the frameworks on which every future project stands.

Who you are

We don't expect you to know it all. But you'll recognise yourself in most of this:

• You have at least 3 years of experience as a frontend developer, with solid JavaScript/TypeScript and Vue.js skills.

• You think in systems, not just screens: APIs, data, hosting, security and how it all fits together.

• You use AI coding tools fluently, and you still understand, review, and own every line that ships.

• You can explain technical choices to a client who isn't technical, in English. Danish is a plus.

• You care about how things look and feel, and you enjoy working with designers and 3D artists.

• You think big. A request for "an e-learning module" makes you wonder whether it should be a simulator, a virtual campus, or an AI coach.

• It's a plus if you know Three.js, WebGL, Umbraco, Node.js, .NET, Azure, CI/CD and security by design (OWASP Top 10).

Your education matters less than your curiosity and how well you work with others.

What you get

• Work that matters. Train wind turbine technicians, onboard energy workers, and help industrial companies explain products that change the world, often with a sustainability angle.

• Big clients, small team. Enterprise-scale projects with the speed and closeness of a 50-person agency in Aarhus and Edinburgh.

• A global parent with reach. Cadpeople is part of RelyOn, a global safety and training provider with more than 50 facilities worldwide. That gives us stability, new clients, and the chance to see your work train people in safety-critical jobs around the world.

• A head start on every project. Our own tested frameworks mean you start from a solid foundation, not a blank page.

• A say in what comes next. We're building up our AI coding capabilities, and this role can help shape how we get there.

• A creative workplace. An office in the heart of Aarhus, surrounded by people who make 3D, film, XR and learning. See our culture.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short application. A classic application is welcome, as long as it sounds like you. Generic AI-written applications will not be prioritised.

Want to stand out? You can add something small that shows your character and how you'd fit in at Cadpeople. It's optional, and it doesn't need to be big or complex. For example:

• A story about a time you turned a vague client need into something that worked.

• A short video, even filmed on your phone, about something you built or care about.

• A skill or tool, like a small AI agent, workflow or utility you made to work smarter.

• A thought on one of our cases: what you'd have done differently, or how you'd take it further.

Our office language is Danish, and we use English with many of our clients. You don't need to be fluent in Danish, but it helps if you understand it.

Questions about the role? Contact Nikolaj Have, CTO, at nikolaj.have@cadpeople.dk.

Start as soon as possible, or by agreement. All applications are treated confidentially, and submitted material is deleted after 6 months in line with GDPR.

**About The Company
