jobs.description:
The Department of Anthropology, School of Culture and Society, invites applications for a three-year position as assistant professor in relation to the research project “Stories from my new life: Mobile transitions and social becomings among resettled refugees in Denmark” (TRANSIT).

An assistant professorship is a full-time, three-year training position that involves research and teaching at the BA and MA level and includes an obligatory course in university teaching for assistant professors. The position will commence on 1 February, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Place of employment: Department of Anthropology, Moesgaard Allé 20, 8270 Højbjerg, Denmark.

The Faculty of Arts is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.

The position
The position will be associated with the research project TRANSIT at the Department of Anthropology and is a combined teaching and research position.

Here is a brief description of the TRANSIT project:

In 2021-2024 app. 600 Congolese women and children were resettled in Denmark under the UNHCR resettlement program. TRANSIT is concerned with resettled refugees’ life transitions, understood as a set of complex legal, social and existential transitions that are particularly urgent in the context of resettlement: 1) the transition from youth to adulthood; 2) the transition from being single to being married; and 3) the transition into old age and, ultimately, death. The project aims to establish a collaboration between Aarhus University, VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research, FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark, DFUNK – Dansk Flygtningehjælp Ungdom and a large group of resettled families in order to: a) create a mobile pop-up exhibition to be presented across Denmark in 2029; b) develop research-based teaching materials for pupils in the final years of Folkeskolen and in Gymnasiet on what it means to be resettled and start a new life in Denmark; and c) publish articles in leading peer-reviewed journals – based on a range of qualitative and quantitative data – on storytelling and life transitions following resettlement.

The selected candidate is expected to do individual fieldwork, be main responsible for a work-package (developing research-based teaching material with FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark), and to be a dedicated member of the project team and engaged in all the project activities and responsibilities.

The position is offered with a view to attracting qualified applicants with an established and well-documented research record in innovative and internationally recognized research within anthropology and a specialization in migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination. 

Research
The selected applicant will be expected to contribute to core activities at the School of Culture and Society and Aarhus University in general and contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s research activities and output in particular. They will be expected to take an interest in interdisciplinary research collaboration within the Department of Anthropology, the School of Culture and Society, the Faculty of Arts, and beyond. 

The selected applicant will also be expected to develop new research projects with internal and external partners and to raise external research funding. The applicant’s research credentials and publication record within the field, e.g. anthropology, migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination, will be assessed not just on existing publications and other research contributions but also on research potential.

Past research output will be assessed based on the active research time of the applicant in question. We therefore ask applicants to specify any career breaks they have had (for instance due to maternity/paternity leave or sick leave) so we may discount these periods when assessing research productivity.

Teaching
The position will involve some teaching (up to 33% of the time) as agreed upon with the Head of the Department and the project PI. The selected applicant will be required to teach and supervise at BA and MA levels of the department’s degree programs in Anthropology and Human Security and will be expected to have teaching experience at university level. 

We emphasise the importance of maintaining a professional and respectful relationship between staff and students, so applicants should be able to demonstrate and exemplify their commitment to participatory teaching initiatives and student involvement as part of their teaching portfolio.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualifications in anthropology or a related discipline. They must also be able to document the following: 

• An internationally oriented research profile documented through relevant academic publications, and possibly other research contributions, at the international level
• Experience of university-level teaching and a commitment to teaching development and the supervision of student projects
• Experience of or interest in active participation in international research collaboration
• Experience of or interest in obtaining external research funding
• Experience of or interest in research dessimination for a non-academic audience
Applicants are asked to submit:

• A concise statement of motivation for applying for the position, including a description of experience with public research dessimination (maximum two pages).
• A full CV (one page).
• A full publication list (research outputs and public dissemination)
• A maximum of two publications.
Only submitted publications will be assessed; a list of publications is not sufficient. As a result, applications without submitted publications will not be assessed.

References or recommendations should not be included with the application. Applicants who are selected for a job interview may be asked to provide professional references.

Language and further information
Applicants can teach and supervise in English at university level.

If the selected applicant is not fluent in Danish, they will be expected to acquire the language within a period of approximately two years. 

To maintain and develop the department’s research environment, the person appointed is expected to be present at the department on a regular basis.

Applications must be uploaded in English.

For further information about the TRANSIT project (including the project description), please contact, PI, Professor Mikkel Rytter, mikkel.rytter@cas.au.dk

For further information about the application procedure, please contact Human Resources: iks-hr-sag@au.dk.

Knowledge exchange
It is expected that the selected applicant will engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy for the Faculty of Arts Strategy Arts 2020-2025 (au.dk), for instance research cooperation with private companies, government consultancy, cooperation with civil society partners or the public dissemination of knowledge. Applicants should document any prior experience within the field of knowledge exchange.

School of Culture and Society
The School of Culture and Society is a vibrant research community engaged in understanding the cultural and social conditions that shape human life. Our work examines how people interact with their environments, from prehistory to the present and across both local and global contexts. Through cross-sector and cross-disciplinary partnerships, we aim to support research innovation and contribute to addressing the major questions facing society. In both research and education, we are committed to bringing the humanities into active dialogue with partners beyond the university.

The School is committed to:

• Promoting an international environment characterized by active academic and interdisciplinary collaboration.
• Encouraging innovative and experimental approaches to research, teaching, and communication.
• Cultivating environments that generate new knowledge and educate students for the future.
• Advancing broad engagement with digital humanities.
• Upholding a deep commitment to addressing both local and global societal challenges.
• Creating an inclusive, diverse, and sustainable workplace and organization.
Read more about the school here School of Culture and Society - Aarhus University

International applicants
International applicants are encouraged to check Family and work-life balance in Denmark (au.dk) and Attractive working conditions (au.dk) for further information about the benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a Relocation and onboarding services for international AU staff and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see Taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU.

Qualification requirements
Applicants should hold a PhD or equivalent academic qualifications.

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and examples of academic production (mandatory, but no more than two examples). Please upload this material electronically along with your application. Please note that although the application process can be completed in the Aarhus University system without up-loading publications or a teaching portfolio, applications that do not include uploaded publications as well as a teaching portfolio (or equivalent documentation of teaching experience and qualifications) will not be considered.
If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts:  shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as Assistant Professorship at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About Arts
The Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts |  Aarhus University

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: (Senior) Project Manager/Process Specialist, Drug Substance Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with outsourced chemical manufacturing of starting materials, intermediates and APIs? Are you passionate about science-driven development and manufacturing support in collaboration with contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs)?

_If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new (Senior) Project Manager or Process Specialist.

_

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a skilled project manager/specialist to join our growing team. As a key member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in our team for commercial chemical manufacturing for projects having reached the stage of process qualification and commercial manufacturing. The manufacturing processes comprise peptide synthesis, peptide conjugation and purification and classic organic chemistry for small molecules and polymers. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will be joining the Chemical Manufacturing team consisting of 6 colleagues, and report directly to Birgitte M. Malle, Senior Directorwho is based in Hellerup_._ You will be based in Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Manage and coordinate outsourced commercial manufacture of peptides, chemical starting materials, intermediates and APIs including technology transfer, process validation (PPQ), post PPQ optimizations, risk management, control strategies and continuous process verification programs (CPV)

• Trouble shooting in collaboration with CMO's including Deviation and Change management as subject matter expert

• Support master batch record update and release of batches together with QA

• Write and support regulatory submissions for marketing approval and post-approval

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a Master of Science or a Ph.D. in organic chemistry, peptide synthesis, chemical engineering or equivalent - and have at least 5 years of experience within pharmaceutical development or manufacturing industry.

Furthermore, you have:

• Relevant hands-on experience from laboratory, pilot and/or manufacturing facilities

• GMP experience

• Proficient English professional skills

• MS Office skills including experience with SAS JMP or other data management tools

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, have attention to details, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to be a highly motivated individual who enjoys being challenged and working in collaborative environments. Strong interpersonal skills are necessary as your job is to establish and maintain good and productive collaboration with CMO's. A proven ability to communicate with stakeholders of other functions and disciplines is crucial.

Travel: up to 10-15 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Senior Director for Chemical Manufacturing, Birgitte M. Malle, bmm@ascendispharma.com

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation.  Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed.  If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.occupation: Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead; DK - Frederikshavn
jobs.description:
Do you have a strong electrical background and are you motivated by technical leadership and the opportunity to help shape the construction of Denmark’s new Arctic ships? As Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead at Semco Maritime, you will take ownership of the electrical installation scope in a nationally significant naval project.

Your position 

In this role, you will be part of a multidisciplinary team working closely with design, procurement, fabrication, and quality control. You will help turn technical requirements and design into practical, high-quality installation solutions and ensure efficient production throughout all phases of shipbuilding, in compliance with naval and classification standards. The final title will depend on your experience and qualifications.

Your work will have a direct impact on the successful delivery of the Arctic ships and on the continued development of the Danish naval shipbuilding industry.

The position will be based in Frederikshavn, where the Arctic ships will be assembled, and is a full-time, permanent position.

Your tasks & responsibilities 

As Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead you will plan, coordinate, and lead the electrical installation scope throughout ship production, ensuring alignment between engineering, procurement, suppliers, and production teams.

Your tasks will include, but are not limited to:

• Defining and planning electrical installation methods from design through production, including installation sequencing, equipment installation, and coordination with relevant stakeholders
• Participating in the production engineering process to support quality, safety, and efficiency
• Supporting the development of electrical discipline project plans and resource estimates
• Lead parts of the installations scope when in construction
• Acting as the technical point of contact internally and with suppliers for electrical and instrumentation matters
• Providing technical input to procurement and defining requirements for electrical installation equipment and tools
• Ensuring compliance with naval, military, and classification standards as well as health, safety, and environmental requirements

Your profile & qualifications

We are looking for a proactive and responsible engineer who can act as lead by combining strong technical understanding with hands-on problem-solving skills.

You work in a structured and quality-focused way, communicate clearly across disciplines, and bring high personal integrity and strong safety awareness.

Even if you do not meet all the desired experience requirements, we encourage you to apply if you believe you are a talented individual with the right mindset, strong motivation, and a willingness to learn and grow in the role

To succeed in this role, we expect that you have
:

• A BSc or MSc in marine or electrical engineering
• Solid experience in shipbuilding, heavy industry or offshore projects (oil and gas / wind)
• Min. 5 years relevant experience
• Familiarity with international classification rules, such as DNV or ABS
• Fluency in English, written and spoken
• Danish language skills
• Knowledge of naval or defence standards would be an advantage

Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the planet. By joining us, you will become part of a community of over 2,300 dedicated thinkers and doers who drive meaningful change and leave their mark on the world. Change is essential, and we always keep our eyes on the journey - how to get there.

We provide the answers needed to make change real, believing that ambitious goals can only be achieved through hard work and innovative, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a better future.

So yes, working for us will spark change – and may well change you too.

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

Mechanical Design Engineer: Develop robust medical devices from concept to production

Would you like to use your mechanical engineering expertise to develop medical devices that make a real difference for people with intimate healthcare needs?

Working with engineers, scientists and project managers, you will turn product requirements and concepts into robust mechanical solutions, combining creative problem-solving with engineering rigour from concept evaluation through to production.

Welcome to CC & BC Mechanical Engineering

At our headquarters in Humlebæk, Denmark, you will join CC & BC Mechanical Engineering within Product Development, developing products for Continence Care and Bowel Care.

Mechanical design connects what users need with how a product performs and how reliably it can be manufactured. Our work brings together functionality, materials, tolerances and production considerations to create practical solutions that perform consistently in everyday use.

You will work closely with colleagues across Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, Technical Design, Materials, Systems Engineering, Usability and Test Engineering, as well as Manufacturing Systems Development and Centre of Excellence specialists.

Turn product concepts into reliable, manufacturable solutions

As our new Mechanical Design Engineer, you will plan and deliver mechanical design activities in Product Development projects. Your work will span concept development and evaluation, detailed design, verification support and transfer to production.

You will take ownership of your mechanical deliverables and provide clear technical conclusions and recommendations. Working within the agreed project scope, you will identify risks early, make design trade-offs visible and bring in the right expertise to move decisions forward.

More specifically, you will:

•    Develop and evaluate mechanical concepts, translating product requirements into practical design solutions in collaboration with Systems Engineering and relevant specialists.

•    Develop and document mechanical designs using 3D CAD, working closely with Technical Design on drawings and specifications.

•    Apply robust design methods and tolerance analysis to understand variation and secure reliable product performance.

•    Apply Design for X principles to balance performance, manufacturability, sustainability and cost, involving manufacturing specialists early.

•    Use calculations, simulation, prototypes and test evidence to evaluate solutions and support timely design decisions.

•    Contribute mechanical expertise to risk assessments, verification planning, technical reviews and design documentation.

•    Plan and deliver your activities against agreed project commitments, communicating risks, dependencies and the impact of proposed changes early.

•    Share technical learning and help improve mechanical design practices across projects.

A mechanical engineer with practical judgement and a collaborative approach

You enjoy both exploring concepts and working through the details that make a design reliable. You can turn analysis into clear recommendations, explain design trade-offs and challenge unclear assumptions constructively.

You take a structured approach without making solutions more complex than necessary. You understand when further analysis is needed and when the available evidence supports moving forward. Above all, you take responsibility for your work while recognising that strong product solutions depend on contributions from several disciplines.

We imagine that you:

•    Hold a BSc or MSc in mechanical engineering, mechanical design, product development or a related discipline.

•    Have experience developing mechanical solutions, including plastic components for injection moulding and high-volume production.

•    Work confidently with 3D CAD, preferably SolidWorks.

•    Have experience with robust design, tolerance calculations and design for manufacture.

•    Can apply engineering theory, calculations and data analysis to practical design challenges.

•    Communicate technical ideas and conclusions clearly, both visually and verbally.

•    Work effectively across disciplines and document your work clearly.

•    Communicate confidently in English.

Experience in medical devices or another regulated industry is an advantage. We also value experience with simulation and an interest in using digital tools, including AI where relevant, to improve engineering analysis and development efficiency.

You do not need to know every method from the outset. Curiosity, sound engineering judgement and a willingness to develop your expertise are important.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Jesper Bruun Jensen, Head of Continence Care & Bowel Care Mechanical Engineering, at DKJBRJ@coloplast.com.

We review applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

Visit us on Coloplast.com.

Watch the film. Follow us on LinkedIn.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager in the Climate and Energy Policy Division - DTU Management
jobs.description:
We are pleased to announce an opportunity for joining the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as a project manager in the Climate and Energy Policy Division, at the Department of Technology, Management and Economics – in short DTU Management. 

We are looking for a skilled and experienced project manager with knowledge about energy systems and planning, who will help manage and support several new research projects funded by EU and Danida. 

Responsibilities
The job will include organisation of project meetings, dissemination activities, data handling and management, and different administrative support to our projects. 

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Take responsibility and support for project deliverables, technical reporting and milestone monitoring in EU projects.
• Foster project synergies and collaborations across our projects consortia and stakeholders to meet EU requirements for deliverables and reporting.
• Contribute to project governance, project performance, and project-specific decision-making across our projects. 
• Administrative support to our Energy Planning course, funded by Danida
• Contribute to the projects’ scientific dissemination and research communication in the consortium projects for the stakeholders.
• Handling of data in some of the projects
• Write project deliverables for scientific reporting and prepare for publications in collaboration with the consortium.
Our expectations of you
We are looking for a talented colleague who delivers results through positive and effective teamwork. You should thrive in an interdisciplinary, multicultural, and highly collaborative environment, where knowledge sharing and cooperation are key to success.

We expect that you have:

• A relevant master’s degree (or equivalent)
• Practical experience with project management and dissemination 
• Experience with handling different types of data
• Knowledge on energy systems and planning
• Experience with Microsoft Suite software and LaTeX collaborative environment 
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international atmosphere with the focus on research, teaching, innovation and scientific advice for the benefit of the surrounding community. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. In the area of technical and natural sciences, DTU is one of the leading research and education institutions in Europe.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Employee. 

In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The position is a full-time position for 2 years. The start date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). 

The workplace is DTU Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Section, Professor Dogan Keles (dogke@dtu.dk) or Senior Researcher Per Sieverts Nielsen (pernn@dtu.dk). 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. You can read more about the Department at DTU Management.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Who are we?
DTU Management conducts excellent research at the intersection of management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master, and PhD levels across DTU's study programs. The department has 250+ employees with around half of staff coming from abroad. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

**Senior Business Consultant, Change Management

**Join NNIT as a Senior Business Consultant in Change Management

**Transformations succeed when people are ready, equipped and motivated to adopt new ways of working. As a Senior Business Consultant in NNIT’s working group for Change & Communication Consulting, you will help clients turn transformation ambitions into sustainable business outcomes.

Change & Communication Consulting is situated within the Life Science Project Consulting (LSPC) department. We deliver standalone and complementary services to project management, supporting clients across the people side of technology, process and organizational transformation.

You’ll join a professional, collaborative department that values quality and customer focus, while also making time for team socials, and casual get-togethers.

Location: This role will be based in Copenhagen, Denmark and will require onsite/office-based presence at customer sites as well as NNIT.

****The Role:

****As a Senior Business Consultant, you will lead change management workstreams in complex transformation programs. You will advise senior stakeholders, shape change strategies, and ensure that affected employees are prepared to adopt and sustain new processes, technologies, and ways of working.

You connect change plans to business benefit realization - ensuring adoption translates into measurable business outcomes, not just completed activities.

You will work closely with project managers, client teams, and colleagues across NNIT. Depending on the engagement, you may lead the change management track, provide strategic advisory support or contribute your expertise to a broader program.

Depending on the experience you bring, the successful candidate will be offered a position as Advanced, Senior, Principal or Managing Consultant.

****Your Responsibilities:

• Develop, implement and lead change strategies, plans, and activities in complex transformation programs.

• Assess organizational readiness, stakeholder needs and project health

• Build and coach sponsor coalitions to ensure visible, active leadership of the change

• Plan and coordinate communication, training and engagement activities

• Define and track adoption and readiness metrics

• Identify risks, resistance and adoption barriers, and develop practical responses

• Facilitate workshops with teams, functions and stakeholders across cultures.

• Translate transformation objectives into clear messages and actionable change activities

• Support the development of proposals, Request for Proposals, Statements of Work, client presentations, use cases, and thought leadership.

• Mentor and support consulting talent of tomorrow in junior-senior setups

• Contribute to the continued development of change and communication methods, tools and services.

Our approach is anchored in the Prosci® framework, while remaining adaptable to each client’s context, objectives, and needs.

****Your Qualifications:

****We are looking for an experienced profile who combines strong change management expertise with sound business understanding and the ability to work confidently with senior stakeholders.

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in delivering complex change management projects within the Life Science sector. You may have worked as a Change Manager, Transformation Consultant, Senior Consultant, Project Manager, or in a similar role.

**We Expect That You Will Have:

**

• Several years of experience with change management methods, tools, and processes

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills

• The ability to translate complex changes into clear actions and messages

• Experience with communication planning, training, and adoption activities

• Experience integrating change plans with a project's delivery methodology (agile, hybrid or waterfall) so change activities land at the right time

• Experience with advisory, presales, proposals, or commercial support

• Strong facilitation skills and confidence working with senior stakeholders

• Confidence working independently while collaborating across multidisciplinary teams

• Excellent English skills, both written and spoken

**It Is a Distinct Advantage If You:

**

• Have experience working in or for regulated industries such as life science or finance.

• Understand digital transformation in Regulatory, Safety, Clinical, or related life science areas.

• Are a Prosci® Certified Change Practitioner.

• Have experience from consultancy or customer-facing roles

• Are curious about human behavior, learning, culture and group dynamics.

• Are a well-liked colleague.

****Your Personal Profile:

****You are motivated by helping people and organizations succeed with change. You create clarity, build trust, and help stakeholders understand what is changing, why it matters, and how to move forward.

You are proactive, structured, and able to balance strategic direction with practical execution. You communicate clearly, collaborate naturally, and take responsibility for delivering results together with your team and customers.

****Why Join NNIT:

****At NNIT, you will join a company with strong roots in IT services, digital transformation, and regulated industries. We help customers develop, implement, and manage business critical solutions with high demands for quality, security, and reliability.

**We Offer:

**

• A professional and collaborative working environment

• Opportunities to work on meaningful projects for leading customers

• Skilled colleagues with strong business and technology expertise

• Room to grow your career and develop your consulting and change management capabilities

• A culture built on responsibility, respect, and delivering quality

****About NNIT:

****NNIT is a leading provider of IT services and consulting. We deliver solutions that support digital transformation and business critical processes for customers in Denmark and internationally. Our work is guided by a strong commitment to quality, trust, and long-term customer relationships.

**Apply now

**If you are ready to help organizations succeed with change, we look forward to hearing from you.

Please submit your CV and application through our recruitment system. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

****About NNIT

****NNIT is a publicly listed company that specializes in IT solutions to life sciences internationally, and to the public and enterprise sectors in Denmark. We focus on high complexity industries and thrive in environments where regulatory demands and complexity are high. We advise on and build sustainable digital solutions that work for the patients, citizens, employees, end users or customers.

NNIT consists of group company NNIT A/S and subsidiaries SCALES, Excellis Health Solutions and SL Controls. Together, these companies employ more than 1,600 people in Europe, Asia, and USA.

We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. We actively work to eliminate bias and ensure an inclusive workplace where everyone has the right to be seen and heard as they are. We invite interested candidates to apply, no matter their background.

In the interest of fostering a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request candidates to refrain from including their pictures in their applications.

Learn more about working at NNIT

Apply now and liberate your talent!

jobs.occupation: 171626 Associate professor in Clinical Proteomics and Data-Driven Biomarker Discovery for Neurodegenerative Disease (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position: 

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) engineering: internalization and lysosomal delivery
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC) / Finsen Laboratory, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  A 3-year PhD fellowship is available in the research group of Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm. Expected start: 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project

  Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on efficient internalization and lysosomal processing to release their cytotoxic payload. Inefficient trafficking limits potency and restricts current ADCs to targets with very high receptor density. The PhD project will engineer and test next-generation ADCs with improved internalization and lysosomal routing. This includes bispecific constructs that combine our established ADC targets (uPAR, MMP14, uPARAP and the Mannose Receptor) with receptors that drive lysosomal delivery, such as IGF2R. Lead candidates will be evaluated in cancer cell models and in vivo, including models of sarcoma and glioblastoma.

  The project is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Distinguished Innovator project "Breaking Barriers: Engineering ADCs for Efficient BBB Transport and Lysosomal Targeting", in collaboration with Professor Matthias Herth (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, UCPH) and Professor Katrine Qvortrup (Department of Chemistry, DTU).

   

  Main tasks

   	
•  	Production, purification and validation of recombinant and bispecific antibodies

 	 	
•  	Conjugation of antibodies to cytotoxic payloads and characterization of the resulting ADCs

 	 	
•  	Cell-based assays: antibody uptake and internalization, flow cytometry, drug screening and cytotoxicity/cell viability assays

 	 	
•  	In vivo efficacy studies of ADC candidates in tumor models

 	 	
•  	Writing scientific publications and presenting at international conferences

 	    

   

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
•  	Carrying through an independent research project under supervision. 

 	 	
•  	Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points.

 	 	
•  	Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team.

 	 	
•  	Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project

 	 	
•  	Teaching and disseminating your knowledge.

 	 	
•  	Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project

 	    

  PhD Programme Description:
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., [relevant degrees]).

   

  Qualifications

  We are looking for a candidate with a strong, hands-on background in ADC research. Applicants must have:

   	
•  	An MSc degree (120 ECTS, or equivalent) in pharmaceutical biotechnology, biotechnology or a closely related field, with an excellent academic record

 	 	
•  	An MSc thesis or equivalent research project on antibody-drug conjugates or antibody-based cancer therapeutics

 	 	
•  	Documented hands-on experience with production, validation and payload conjugation of recombinant antibodies

 	 	
•  	Experience with cytotoxicity, cell viability and drug screening assays in mammalian cancer cell lines

 	 	
•  	Experience with flow cytometry

 	 	
•  	Experience with laboratory animal work

 	 	
•  	Experience from an international research laboratory and excellent written and spoken English

 	   Experience with functional genomics (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 screening) and with sarcoma models is an advantage.

     Place of employment

  The place of employment is BRIC, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. 

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 15 January 2027 or after agreement.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the Faculty’s rules on achieving the degree. 

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,200 EUR (August 2026 level) plus pension.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm, lhe@finsenlab.dk.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

   

  Application procedure
 Your application must be submitted electronically by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. The application must include the following documents in PDF format: 

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page)

  2. CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

  3. Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufm.dk/en/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science

  4. Publication list (if possible)

   

  Application deadline: 6 November 2026, 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritized assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You find information about the recruitment process at: http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicants will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 49

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

Experience from the medical device industry, working under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements, or using a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Planetary is looking for a Managing Director (Fondsdirektør) to lead Planetary A/S and the continued development of its two investment funds: Planetary Impact Ventures and Planetary Soil Fund.

At Planetary, we invest in companies and farmland aligned with our guiding principles. We invest in companies with a focus on long-term business models within planetary boundaries, and in degraded farmland and partners who are committed to soil regeneration. Our commitment is manifested in our evergreen structure. Our focus is biodiversity, agriculture and food, and we aim to provide a fair financial return. We want to inspire and contribute to a restructuring of our economic systems, a redefinition of what value is, and increase our understanding and reconnection with nature and life on the planet.

At Planetary, our work does not stop with investments. Our theory of change is focusing on a systemic and broad approach. We work to nourish and contribute to the community around us. We believe that value alignment between investors, us as intermediaries, and our portfolio companies is essential to the success of our shared mission. These principles are instrumental to the way we work – and who we are.

The role

As Managing Director, you will have the overall responsibility for Planetary A/S, ensuring strong governance and compliance, performance and development of the funds. You will report to the Board, and work closely with all the people working at Planetary.

Your work will be grounded in a deep commitment to systems change and a transition towards organic-regenerative food and agriculture.

Key responsibilities

Planetary and organisational leadership

·      Lead and develop Planetary’s organisation and its two funds in close collaboration with the Board, the active Partners, the Investment Committees and Fund Directors.

·      Take responsibility for Planetary’s financial management, budgets and allocation of resources.

·      Lead fundraising and relationships with LPs and key stakeholders.

·      Take responsibility for company-level reporting and compliance in coordination with our fund directors.

·      Ensure strong governance, transparent Board reporting and effective follow-up on decisions.

·      Ensure that Planetary’s impact objectives are integrated into investment strategy, portfolio management and decision-making across both funds.

·      Lead according to the culture rooted in Planetary’s values, combining intellectual curiosity, courage and humility with collaboration, care for people and planet, sound commercial judgment and high standards.

Together with the Fund Directors

·      Support the investment teams, ensuring sound investment practices, high-quality investment decisions and effective collaboration with the Investment Committees and the Board.

·      Support founders and management teams of the companies where Planetary can contribute experience, perspective and network.

·      Maintain oversight of portfolio performance, risks, opportunities and capital requirements.

·      Take board roles in portfolio companies.

You have:

·      Experience with investing.

·      Proven track record in operational leadership and business development.

·      Strong analytical and financial management skills.

·      Experience in people leadership and organisational development.

·      Good communication, interpersonal skills and stakeholder management abilities.

·      A deeply rooted commitment to contributing to a healthier planet.

You are likely to have:

·      Several years’ experience from venture capital, impact investment, private equity or another relevant investment environment.

·      A solid understanding of fund economics, fund raising, portfolio performance and investments.

·      An understanding of impact management and the integration of financial and impact objectives.

Experience within food and organic-regenerative agriculture is an advantage, but not a prerequisite. Commitment to transforming the food system towards a more regenerative and resilient future is essential.

The right candidate

You are an experienced leader with a strong understanding of investments and of how capital can contribute to systemic change.

You combine sound judgement and the ability to create momentum with curiosity, collaboration and humility. You enjoy working in a small organisation where people remain close to the work and are motivated by long-term development.

__________________________________________________________________________

Location

Our office is at an organic farm in Humlebæk.

Timeline and application

Please apply before November 6th, 2026. Applications should be sent to Annette Hartvig Bohé at ahb@planetary.dk . Applications will be evaluated on an ongoing basis.

Questions

If you have questions about the job, feel free to reach out to Chair Jacob Jelsing, jj@planetary.dk, or Director Annette Hartvig Bohé, ahb@planetary.dk

Our guiding principles

Stay humble: Seeking to understand and improve the conditions for life on the planet is a task of infinite complexity. Grounded by nature, we stay humble and sincere in everything we do.

Learn with nature: Inspiration in nature and its biological processes will guide our investments. We shall adapt ourselves to nature, rather than forcing nature to comply with us.

Perceive wealth holistically: True wealth is much more than money in the bank. We perceive wealth as well-being and harmony between humans, nature and the economy.

Trust patient capital: Real value takes time to manifest. We support long-term business models and real value creation over quick profit maximisation.

Build strong communities: Strong communities build resilience and awareness. We strive to create movement and stronger connections within the networks we grow with.

Advocate for change: Real change depends on systemic change. We dedicate ourselves to create real, tangible change and assume leadership towards a new paradigm.

jobs.occupation: One or more Professors in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for one or more professors in the field of Cyber Security as per March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The positions are permanent.

**Who we are

**In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems is ranked among the top 50 in the world in the Shanghai Ranking (GRAS). The department employs more than 200 people, of whom approximately 90 are PhD students, and around 40% of all employees are international. In total, the department has more than 800 students enrolled in its BSc and MSc programmes, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and laboratory facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and research results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department here www.es.aau.dk.

The Cyber Security Research Group at Aalborg University (Cyber Security Research Group) is a young and growing research group within the Department of Electronic Systems, focusing on cyber security from various perspectives. Its core research areas are network security, IoT/OT security, applied cryptography, and privacy and security in machine learning. The Cyber Security Research Group consists of 16 members and offers a young, international research environment. The group is responsible for teaching activities in the Master’s programme in Cyber Security, which is taught in English and has more than 100 active Danish and international students. Moreover, the group is strongly engaged in community-building activities, with the AAU Copenhagen campus serving as a hub for weekly CTFs and ethical hacking activities involving dozens of participants.

Your work tasks

You will lead the academic direction of cyber security research and education. The role combines independent academic leadership with close collaboration across the department, within the section, with other research environments, external organisations, and international partners.

Your research and teaching will address one or more areas within applied cryptography, IoT and/or cloud security, security and privacy for big data and machine learning, risk management and threat modelling, mobile security, secure software development, and systems security and privacy. You will initiate and lead research projects, secure and manage external research funding, publish research at an international level, and develop collaborations with industry, public-sector organisations, and universities in Denmark and abroad.

You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, develop courses and teaching materials, and contribute to the planning and coordination of programmes built on problem-based learning. You will also supervise doctoral researchers and early-career colleagues, contribute to relevant committees and academic activities, and take part in developing the department’s research and educational priorities. International collaboration, including participation in networks, conferences, and joint research activities, forms an integral part of the position.

Your competencies

You hold a doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. You have documented original research contributions at an international level within cyber security and a strong publication record in recognised journals and conferences. You can demonstrate a proven track record of attracting, establishing, and managing externally funded research activities, and you have the academic judgement required to develop a coherent research agenda with clear societal and technological relevance.

You bring substantial experience in university teaching, supervision, course development, examination activities, and the development of educational programmes. Familiarity with problem-based learning is relevant, particularly because the role includes contributing to programmes in which students work collaboratively on complex and practice-oriented challenges. You communicate confidently in English, both orally and in writing, and you are willing to develop Danish language skills over time.

You set a clear academic direction while creating constructive working relationships with students, colleagues, and collaborators. You contribute with sound judgement, curiosity, and an ability to turn research ideas into well-organised projects and partnerships. You support the development of early-career researchers, engage openly across disciplines, and help maintain a respectful and collaborative research culture.

**Qualification requirements

**Applicants must be able to document a high degree of original academic production at an international level and experience from teaching at different levels. Including tests/exams, course/study programme management as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material.

Emphasis is placed on the extent, to which the applicant, has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.

Emphasis may moreover be placed on the applicant’s ability to carry out and develop research-based public-sector consultancy. Also, emphasis will be placed on an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks and possibly fulfil other functions, for example in relation to the university’s external cooperation.

Emphasis will also be placed on the applicant's ability to undertake pedagogical supervision, supervision and academic assessment work.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Professor”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners.

Successful candidates must document:

• Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE)
• Python programming skills
• Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar)
• Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria:

• Atomistic modelling and DFT experience
• Python programming experience
• Machine learning experience
• Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Communication skills

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Catalytic CO₂ Conversion to Carbon Nanotubes - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Can we transform greenhouse gases into some of the world's most valuable advanced materials? 
At DTU Physics, we are looking for a talented and ambitious PhD candidate to help pioneer a completely new route for carbon utilization. The project aims to discover catalytic materials capable of converting CO₂ directly into carbon nanotubes (CNTs), combining climate-change mitigation with the sustainable production of next-generation functional materials. 

Carbon nanotubes are among the most sought-after nanomaterials due to their exceptional strength, low weight, electrical conductivity, and thermal stability. They are key components in future energy technologies, electronics, and lightweight structural materials. Yet, conventional CNT production relies on fossil-derived feedstocks and carries a substantial carbon footprint. This PhD project seeks to establish an entirely new catalytic paradigm in which captured CO₂ becomes the raw material for producing high-value carbon nanomaterials. 

You will join the Catalysis and Operando Characterization (CATOC) group at DTU, an international research environment at the forefront of catalyst development and operando characterization. Working in close collaboration with Leipzig University, you will combine catalyst synthesis, catalytic testing, advanced electron microscopy, and operando X-ray characterization to reveal how catalysts form, evolve, and produce CNTs under realistic reaction conditions.

As a PhD student, you will have access to world-leading infrastructure, including advanced electron microscopy, in situ and operando characterization tools, and state-of-the-art facilities for catalyst development and testing.

If you are excited by tackling fundamental scientific questions while contributing to sustainable technologies, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be to discover and develop novel catalytic materials that enable the conversion of CO₂ into carbon nanotubes.

The project will include:

• Development of mono- and multimetallic catalyst materials based on metal silicates.
• Catalytic testing and performance evaluation under realistic reaction conditions.
• Investigation of CNT growth, harvesting, and catalyst regeneration strategies.
• Advanced in situ and operando characterization using electron microscopy and X-ray based methods.
• Establishing structure-activity relationships that guide the design of next-generation catalysts.
You have a strong background in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, physics, nanotechnology, or a related field. Experience with catalysis, materials synthesis, electron microscopy, or characterization techniques is an advantage.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.description:
Small-scale ocean processes play an important role in shaping ocean circulation and freshwater distribution in the Arctic. Yet, they remain difficult to observe and represent in numerical models. This limits our ability to understand and predict the ocean and its response to a changing climate. SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography) provides high-resolution observations of sea-surface height that can be used to better constrain these processes and the ocean state. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
This PhD will focus on assimilating SWOT observations into a high-resolution ocean model with a focus on the Polar Regions. An emphasis will be on developing surrogate models using Scientific Machine learning to reduce the computational cost of simulations and enable efficient prediction and exploration of ocean processes.

The candidate is expected to have a background in ocean modelling and remote sensing, preferably with experience in satellite altimetry and ocean modelling using the MITgcm (MIT’s General Circulation modelling framework). 

The candidate will work in a stimulating environment at DTU Space, with close collaboration with SWOT researchers, other DTU departments, and international partners. The candidate should be motivated to work in an international environment and participate in relevant research travel.

This project will use a recently developed soft X-ray imaging method to probe the dynamics of light-induced phase transitions at the nanoscale using X-ray Free Electron Lasers. The work will also combine lab-based experiments on time-resolved nonlinear optics.
