jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Crop root development, and its effects on root zone water and nitrogen dynamics
jobs.description:
Department of Plant and Environmental Science, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen is offering a 34-months Postdoc position in Crop root development, and its effects on root zone water and nitrogen dynamics commencing February 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://plen.ku.dk/english/.  Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Kristian Thorup-Kristensen, email: ktk@plen.ku.dk.

  Job description
 The postdoc will be working on crop root and root zone research in our newly established root research facility RootAccess (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/rootaccess/). The facility is equipped to allow the study of crop root growth to 3 meters depth and to follow the dynamic effects on soil water and nitrogen (uptake, leaching and denitrification) to the same depth. During the project, a number of common crops will be grown in rotation in the facility, allowing the study of their different exploitation of the root zone for water and nitrogen, both during the crop growth seasons as well as during periods without crops, to cover rotational effects over the years. Studies will be based on soil water sensors, minirhizotrons, soil water suction cells, and soil gas samplers, all installed at several depths in the soil profile. Furthermore, we use isotopic tracers to follow root uptake. The postdoc will be part of the team working on the project and facility, and co-responsible for running the experiments in the facility. Apart from the experimental work and contribution to publishing the results, a main task for the postdoc will be to produce well organized datasets and clear result presentation, continuously updated during the project.

  Description of the scientific environment
 The postdoc will be hosted in the Crop Physiology and Production Systems research group (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/), which focuses on crop growth and quality at the crop, crop rotation, and cropping system level. The group has a specific focus on crop root research, using field-scale root research facilities, including the RadiMax root phenotyping facility as well as the newly developed RootAccess facility.

  Required qualifications
 The applicants should hold professional and personal skills and qualifications as stated below:

   	
• A PhD degree in agricultural science, or related disciplines. 	
• Solid knowledge of whole plant and crop physiology, including plant and soil water and nutrient relations. 	
• Good technical skills and practical experimental experience with whole plant or preferably field crop experiments, as well as modern plant analyses and monitoring techniques. 	
• Competent on data management and statistical analysis, etc. 	
• Good record, considering your early career stage, of peer-reviewed scientific publications

Are you interested in developing innovative robotic systems that can adapt their mechanical properties to interact safely and effectively with their environment? Do you have a background in robotics, mechatronics, and control, and enjoy combining mechanical design with hands-on experimental research? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to develop and validate novel robotic technologies integrating compliant mechanisms, variable stiffness, and advanced control strategies. Your research will contribute to the development of adaptable robotic systems capable of performing complex physical operations in challenging and uncertain environments.

The PhD position is part of RESSORT, a European research project aimed at advancing soft and adaptive robotics through the integration of innovative materials, compliant structures, sensing, and intelligent control. The project addresses the limitations of conventional rigid robotic systems by developing solutions capable of adapting their mechanical behaviour to different tasks and operating conditions.

Your research will focus on the design, modelling, and control of robotic systems incorporating soft and variable-stiffness mechanisms. Particular attention will be given to the integration of mechanical adaptability and control to improve physical interaction, operational stability, and performance. The developed methods will be implemented and experimentally validated on robotic platforms, including adaptive and morphing aerial systems.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to investigate and develop mechatronic and control solutions for soft and adaptive robotic systems. The research will combine mechanical design, dynamic modelling, control development, and experimental validation, addressing the challenges associated with integrating compliant structures into robotic platforms.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Design and develop compliant and variable-stiffness mechanisms for robotic applications.
• Develop mathematical and dynamic models of robotic systems incorporating flexible and adaptive mechanical structures.
• Investigate control strategies to manage changes in mechanical configuration, stiffness, and interaction forces.
• Integrate actuators, sensors, and embedded control systems into experimental robotic platforms.
• Develop methods for stable and efficient robotic operation under varying mechanical and environmental conditions.
• Implement and validate the developed technologies through simulations and experiments on real robotic systems.
• Collaborate with international research and industrial partners and disseminate research results through scientific publications and conferences.
We expect you to have a strong background in mechatronics, robotics, mechanical engineering, control engineering, or a closely related field. Solid competences in mechanical design, dynamic modelling, and control of robotic systems are particularly important.

Experience with CAD tools, actuators, embedded systems, and experimental prototyping will be considered an advantage. Good programming skills in MATLAB/Simulink, C++, and/or Python are expected. Familiarity with compliant mechanisms, soft robotics, variable-stiffness systems, or aerial robotics will be beneficial.

We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy combining theoretical developments with practical implementation and experimental work. You should be motivated to develop innovative solutions, work independently, and contribute actively to a multidisciplinary and international research environment.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of applicants will be based on their academic qualifications, research potential, and relevance of their technical background to the proposed PhD project. Particular emphasis will be placed on competences in mechatronic design, dynamic modelling, and control, as well as demonstrated experience in the development and experimental validation of robotic systems.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Matteo Fumagalli, mafum@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the department at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 5 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A brief description (maximum one page) of relevant technical or research projects, highlighting the applicant's individual contributions to mechanical design, modelling, control development, and experimental validation of robotic systems
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Regulatory Affairs Manager (Denmark) - Nordic Marketing Company
jobs.description:
Are you ready to shape patient access across the Nordics by turning science into approved, available medicines? Do you thrive in complexity, navigating multiple indications and evolving legislation to find clear paths to approval? Then this could be your next step with us at AstraZeneca!

Our AstraZeneca Nordic Marketing Company employs around 550 people and has offices located in Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo, and Espoo. AstraZeneca Nordic is a recognized leader in its core therapy areas and aims to improve the lives of millions of people. This is an area where you are free to grow - you are encouraged to challenge traditional ways of working and exercise your curiosity. We drive innovative science, deliver key launches, build close collaboration and partnerships within health care.

Introduction to role:

In this Denmark-based role covering all Nordic countries, you will drive timely management of regulatory submissions and approvals, successful launches, and seamless lifecycle management to facilitate earlier access and safer use of our medicines. You will act as the regulatory affairs voice within brand and franchise teams, partnering closely with Market Access, Medical, Logistics, and others to connect regulatory strategy to real-world outcomes for patients and the business.

You will collaborate with European and global regulatory colleagues to influence plans with local insights, while being empowered to work independently and make decisions at pace to align science, policy, and patient need.

Accountabilities:

• Regulatory Strategy and Execution: Lead regulatory activities across launched products and pipeline assets to secure rapid, high-quality approvals and timely patient access.

• Intelligence and Foresight: Monitor changes in legislation and competitive activity to turn insights into advice, risk mitigation, and opportunities that shape plans and timelines.

• Authority Engagement: Build and maintain productive relationships with national health authorities; manage communications on pending issues and evolving requirements to de-risk regulatory approvals.

• Global Collaboration: Keep European and global regulatory teams current on local requirements and external dynamics; influence global strategies with Nordic perspectives.

• Compliance and Quality: Ensure labelling and compendial texts meet external requirements and AstraZeneca policies.

• Team Contribution: Drive ways-of-working improvements, contribute to department development, and share best practices that raise team effectiveness.

Essential Skills/Experience:

• Master's degree in Pharmacy or equivalent.

• Demonstrated experience with regulatory work.

• Experience from pharmaceutical development or manufacturing.

• Experience from working with health authorities.

• Excellent knowledge of English and at least one of the Nordic languages.

• Good knowledge of relevant legislation requirements and procedures.

• Solid business acumen and a good regulatory affairs toolbox to apply.

• Good at influencing and building relationships with senior and cross-functional stakeholders.

• Ability to plan, communicate and drive processes and projects all the way to the finish line.

**

I&D**

We are proud to have a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration. Here, employees are empowered to express diverse perspectives - and are made to feel valued, energized and rewarded for their ideas and creativity.

Why AstraZeneca?

When we at AstraZeneca see every opportunity, no matter how small, as the beginning of something big. We are proud to have a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration. Here, employees are empowered to express diverse perspectives and are made to feel valued, energised and rewarded for their ideas and creativity.

We strive to unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

So, what is next?

Are you already imagining yourself joining our team? Great, because we cannot wait to hear from you!

Welcome with your application, in English, latest by the 4th of November 2026!

Applications will be reviewed continuously throughout the application period.

**Where can I find out more?

**Follow AstraZeneca on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/1603/Inclusion & Diversity: Inclusion and diversityCareer site: https://careers.astrazeneca.com/Denmark: AstraZeneca Denmark

AstraZeneca embraces diversity and equality of opportunity.  We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team representing all backgrounds, with as wide a range of perspectives as possible, and harnessing industry-leading skills.  We believe that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be.  We welcome and consider applications to join our team from all qualified candidates, regardless of their characteristics.  We comply with all applicable laws and regulations on non-discrimination in employment (and recruitment), as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements.

Our Philosophy

AstraZeneca is a global, science-led, patient-focused pharmaceutical company committed to excellence in the research, development and commercialisation of prescription medicines. With approximately 90,000 people in 85 countries, our aim is simple: to unlock the power of what science can do, for people, society and the planet. From Clinical Development, Regulatory and Medical Affairs to Finance, IT, Digital, Manufacturing and Supply, the opportunities to make an impact are limitless. Our workforce reflects the diversity of the patients we serve – it is embedded in everything we do. We're at our best and most creative when we seek out different perspectives, experiences and strengths. At AstraZeneca, you'll have the chance to grow your abilities, skills and knowledge constantly in a place that never stands still. Discover why we're a great place to work and see what science — and you — can do.

**A Snapshot of Your Day

jobs.occupation: Software Architect: Agentic AI & Java, SitaWare Insight
jobs.description:
**Software Architect:

Agentic AI & Java, SitaWare Insight

**_Are you passionate about building sophisticated AI agents that solve real world problems? Join our Agentic AI team within SitaWare Insight, designing multi-agent workflows in Java and Python that power critical decision-making and help our customers get the job done faster and safer.

_**The job

**As Software Architect on this team, you will combine deep software architecture expertise in Java with strong LLM and AI engineering fundamentals to shape the technical foundation of our AI-driven solutions. You will define the technical vision and architectural strategy that enable our product, AI agents and multi-agent systems to scale, while also designing and implementing the software solutions that bring this vision to life.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Converting customer needs into robust software architectures for AI agents, multi-agent orchestration and RAG pipelines

• Designing and implementing AI agents, including tool definitions, action groups and knowledge base integrations

• Ensuring safe and predictable outcomes through human-in-the-loop design and guardrails, and building traceability and transparency into our AI-based solutions

• Writing production-grade Java code with full test coverage, structured logging and robust error handling

• Establishing and maintaining technology standards, and evaluating new technologies as they emerge

**Joining the team

**You will join a growing team within the SitaWare Insight program, close to 50 engineers, architects and testers across five Scrum teams, spanning Aarhus and Copenhagen. We are building a brand-new team around this role:

an architect, a data scientist, five to seven developers and a tester, working closely with our Product Manager and UX designer. Java is our primary backend language, and we also work in Python for our AI tooling, and we collaborate with researchers to give our LLMs geospatial situational awareness, the ability to understand tactical maps and follow events across an evolving timeline. If you enjoy figuring out how to make new AI capabilities work safely and reliably in a domain where the stakes are real, you will feel at home here.

**Your Qualifications

**

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience in a software architecture role, designing and specifying system structures, interfaces and dependencies

• Strong backend development experience in Java, and familiarity with frontend architectures such as Angular or similar

• Strong understanding of microservices architecture, message queues and system integration patterns

• Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, and a solid grasp of how these fit into system architecture and deployment strategy

• A proven track record of defining technical vision and architectural strategy that supports product scalability and evolution

• Solid software engineering practices, including testing, logging, observability and version control, along with the ability to establish technology standards across a team

For more senior profiles, we are also looking for:

• At least two to three years focused on LLM or AI systems, including architecting and overseeing the deployment of AI-powered applications in Java and Python

• Deep understanding of orchestration frameworks, RAG architectures, vector databases, embedding models, hybrid search and tool-use/function-calling patterns

• Experience designing multi-agent systems, including orchestration patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation and result aggregation

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation frameworks and metrics, such as relevance, faithfulness and hallucination detection, and how to build evaluation and observability into system architecture

You should expect around two to four weeks of travel per year, giving you the chance to collaborate across our Aarhus and Copenhagen teams.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

**Welcome to Systematic Copenhagen

**When you join us in Copenhagen, you're not just getting a desk at one of the city's best locations — you are stepping into a workplace where community matters. Our Employees Club keeps things lively with monthly social events, and our office catering makes sure you are always well taken care of. Whether you are into casual games or just good company, you will find both at our foosball table or during our relaxed Friday bar gatherings.

**Never stop developing

**Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

**Start your development here

**We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Allan Carstens, Senior Manager, SitaWare Insight.

Get in touch

Tobias Falck Jensen

Are You the One We’re Looking For?

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

jobs.description:
Taffelbay is a bakery chain in the Copenhagen area. We are looking for a Head of Procurement and Stock Control to make sure our bakery always has the right ingredients and supplies, in the right quantity, at the right quality and at the right price. You will keep production running without shortages, limit waste and keep the cost of raw materials under control. 

What you will do 

• Own the ordering of raw materials, packaging and consumables, and place orders on time based on production plans, expected sales and busy periods such as Fastelavn, Easter and Christmas

• Coordinate with the Head Baker, the Scaling Room and the Dough and Laminated Pastry teams, so production needs are known well in advance 

• Prepare a stock plan for peak periods that covers the extra demand, and agree it with the Head Baker

• Accurate, with a good head for numbers

• Clear communicator with suppliers and colleagues 

• Good understanding of bakery ingredients and production

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in big data analytics in teen substance use at the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research at Aarhus University in Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited from early-career postdoctoral researchers who can demonstrate an established track record in big data analytics within the field of substance use. The two-year full time position will commence in February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. You will get the opportunity to analyse and publish on big data from a very large RCT examining out-of-the-box brain-based interventions for adolescents engaged in alcohol use. You will also get unique opportunities to examine risk and protective factors for substance use and related behaviors across large adolescent datasets. 

You will be working under the strong mentorship of Professor Kristine Rømer Thomsen at Aarhus University and Professor Sarah W. Feldstein Ewing (UConn Health, U.S.), and in close collaboration with other prominent researchers in the field. The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is part of the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences at Aarhus University and provides a vibrant and stimulating research environment in the charming city of Aarhus.

About the applicant
We are thrilled to welcome individuals of any nationality to come live in Denmark and join the project. Appointment as postdoc requires scientific qualifications at the PhD level in a relevant field. You must be able to demonstrate a track record in big data analytics in, or closely related to, the substance use field, and the capacity to not only conduct advanced quantitative analyses, but also the capacity to easily communicate those analyses, e.g., chat with colleagues on the project; write up relevant analytics plans and output in English, including for high impact international journals. The data collection was recently completed, offering attractive opportunities to examine and publish on large datasets and be part of a nationally and internationally strong research team.

Who we are
Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is an interdisciplinary social science research center. Our research focuses on treatment, prevention, policy, drug markets and recreational use. We study both legal and illegal substances. The Centre is interdisciplinary, and researchers have backgrounds in psychology, sociology, anthropology, criminology, political science and public health. Our task is to conduct research projects, provide education, disseminate knowledge about alcohol and substance use, and collaborate with national stakeholders as well as international research institutions.
See also www.crf.au.dk

The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences is part of Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University – a top 100 university. Aarhus BSS has achieved the triple-crown AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations. 
At the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, we teach and conduct research into the most significant subject areas of psychology. The department employs around 55-60 academic staff members and 40 PhD students. Our researchers have a strong tradition for collaborating with Danish as well as international researchers from many different academic fields such as health and psychiatry, education, pedagogic, linguistics, philosophy, religious studies, organizational development and management, economics and neuroscience.
For more information about the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, please visit: http://psy.au.dk/en/

Further Information
Further particulars on the position may be obtained from Professor Kristine Rømer Thomsen, Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, e-mail: krt.crf@psy.au.dk, Tel.:+45 2991 6092.

If you require assistance with uploading your application or have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact: Charlotte Thomsen, HR coordinator, e-mail: charlotte@au.dk, Tel.: +45 8716 5362.

The place of work is Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Bartholins Allé 11, 8000 Aarhus C

International applicant?

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information here: https://internationalstaff.au.dk/relocationservice/

Please find more information about research opportunities at Aarhus University here: http://international.au.dk/research/

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here: 
http://talent.au.dk/junior-researcher-development-programme/

Terms of employment

Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as postdoctoral fellow at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure

When you apply for this position it is mandatory to attach the following:

• 
Application

• 
Curriculum Vitae. You are encouraged to declare any periods of leave without research activity, including, for example, maternity leave, since your research activities are assessed in relation to your actual research time

• 
Education (diploma for master's, PhD and possibly higher doctoral degree)

• 
List of publications (the enclosed publications must be clearly marked on the list of publications)

• 
Publications. Up to three publications can be included in the application. In the event of several authors the publications must be accompanied by a co-author statement concerning the applicant's share of the collaborative work with the consent of the co-authors. This template may be used for the purpose

Materials which cannot be uploaded together with the application may be submitted in three copies to Aarhus BSS HR & PhD, Aarhus University, Bartholins Allé 16, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

Read more about how to apply for an academic post at Aarhus BSS here

The evaluation process
After the application deadline, an assessment committee is appointed. Please note that the assessment of applicants is based solely on the material received prior to the application deadline. For further information, see Guidelines for Assessment Committee, Aarhus BSS.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment to its 37,000 students (FTEs) and 8,700 employees and has an annual revenue of EUR 1.106 billion. jobs.occupation: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
jobs.description:
Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring.

This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. 

Job description
The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere.

You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics.

Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage.

Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. 

What we offer 
The successful candidate is offered:

• Access to a well-developed research infrastructure
• Office space and shared equipment
• a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

A central part of your role will be ensuring that commissioning and qualification activities are effectively planned, coordinated and aligned with construction milestones, equipment installation requirements and phased building handovers.

You will work closely with contractors, engineering specialists, validation colleagues, IT, equipment owners and other project stakeholders to manage technical dependencies, identify risks and ensure the successful progression of the utilities workstream.

Experience working within regulated or process driven industries where safety, quality, documentation and controlled operating procedures are essential.

The Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).

The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.

As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.

The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

• 
Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

• 
Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

• 
Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

Operational responsibility

Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

jobs.occupation: Tender Manager, Renewable Offshore Services; Location: DK - Esbjerg, DK - Copenhagen, DK - Aarhus, UK - Grimsby
jobs.description:
Are you motivated by turning complex customer requirements into competitive and commercially robust proposals? Do you thrive on creating structure, coordinating specialists, and driving tender processes from opportunity to contract award? Then you could be our new Tender Manager.

Your position 

As our new Tender Manager, you will play a key role in securing renewable offshore service opportunities, with a particular focus on offshore wind. You will lead the complete tender lifecycle, from initial qualification and bid strategy through proposal development, internal approval, submission, clarification, negotiation, and handover to project delivery. 

Working closely with colleagues across Sales, Engineering, Operations, Legal, Finance, Procurement, and HSEQ, you will bring together the right expertise and turn complex requirements into clear, compliant, and customer-focused solutions. You will create structure throughout the process, maintain tender governance, manage commercial risks, and ensure that every submission is delivered on time and to a high standard. 

In this full-time position you will report to the Sales Director, Service. Your place of work will be Esbjerg, Aarhus, Copenhagen or Grimsby, UK and travelling for customer meetings, site visits, negotiations, and other tender-related activities should be expected. 

At Semco Maritime, safety is a core value. In this role, you will contribute to maintaining a strong culture of safety, quality, compliance, and integrity throughout all tender activities.

Your tasks & responsibilities 
As Tender Manager, you will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering assigned tenders while ensuring clear ownership, effective collaboration, disciplined governance, and alignment with our commercial objectives. 

Your tasks will include, but are not limited to:

• Leading renewable offshore service tenders from qualification and bid/no-bid assessment through submission, negotiation, award, and structured handover.
• Establishing tender strategies, plans, timelines, responsibilities, review gates, and communication routines across the bid team.
• Coordinating technical, operational, commercial, contractual, procurement, finance, and HSEQ contributions into coherent and compelling proposals.
• Managing pricing inputs, assumptions, exclusions, compliance, risks, opportunities, clarifications, and internal approval processes.
• Preparing and quality-assuring customer-focused submissions while capturing lessons learned and contributing to the continuous improvement of tender processes, tools, and content.
Your profile & qualifications 

We are looking for a commercially aware and structured tender professional who enjoys bringing people and specialist disciplines together around a shared deadline. You take ownership, maintain an overview when the process becomes complex, and communicate clearly with stakeholders at different levels of the organisation. 

You combine attention to detail with the ability to understand the bigger commercial picture. You are comfortable challenging inputs, following up on deliverables, and ensuring that the proposed solution is both competitive and operationally achievable. 

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have: 

• Relevant experience in tender or bid management within offshore wind, renewable energy, maritime, oil and gas, engineering, or technical services. 
• Experience leading complex, multidisciplinary tenders involving several internal and external stakeholders. 
• A strong understanding of tender governance, compliance, cost estimation, pricing, contractual risk, approvals, negotiations, and handovers. 
• Excellent written English and strong communication, editing, planning, and stakeholder-management skills.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in fungal genomics and predictive modelling - DTU Food
jobs.description:
Fungi are increasingly causing health issues globally. Such infections are not only increasing in humans and animals, but also in crops and as contamination of food products with mycotoxins.

We have recently been awarded funding to develop online webservices for genomic characterization of all pathogens capable of infecting animals, humans and plants, which includes fungi. However, genomics methods and workflows have so far not gained enough attention in relation to plant infecting or mycotoxin producing fungi. 

Databases of genomes of known fungal species have already been developed, as has gene databases of mycotoxin producing gene clusters, but an extensive linkage to fungal taxa is poorly described. Furthermore, it is known that a number of fungi including some used in food production have the gene cluster for mycotoxin production but do not express them.

There is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the genomics of fungi, as well as to translate this into online services.

Thus, as part of our GPAP project (www.gpap.global) and our responsibilities as advise provider to the Danish Food Administration we are seeking a PhD-candidate in fungal genomics with a focus on correlating genomes to phenotypes and developing webservices. This will include whole genome sequencing of fungi, culturing and phenotypic characterization and implementing tools in our widely used online webservice.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to create a webservice for identifying fungal taxa, mycotoxin-producing gene clusters and predict phenotypes under different growth conditions. You will perform complete genome sequencing (including the analyses) of a selected range of fungal to create an improved database of reference genomes.

You will also:

• develop a web-based tool for species identification and detection of known toxin-gene clusters, virulence genes and regulatory genes.
• conduct phenotype to genotype association studies based on a large collection of phenotypically characterized Fusarium isolates and develop and improve the online tool.
• With assistant from other group members, you will analyse the output, draw conclusions and present the outputs. 
• communicate research results by presenting data at project meetings and international conferences and write reports and manuscripts for publication.
• engage in the general work carried out by the research group, including discussions and planning of strategies and projects, drafting research grant proposals, etc.
Daily work will be in close collaboration with other researchers in the Genomic Epidemiology group at DTU Food and the Applied Mycology group at DTU Bioengineering, as well as national and international partners.

The ideal candidate has experience in coding in python and experience with Unix-based systems and in machine and deep learning.

Other desired qualifications are:

• extensive knowledge in microbial genomics including phylogenetic analysis
• extensive knowledge of existing bioinformatic algorithms and tools.
• experience with DNA-based workload from microbes
It is a great advantage if you have experience in general microbiology and preferably fungal culturing.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
The position is a collaboration between DTU Food and DTU Bioengineering, with the employment at DTU-Food. Further information may be obtained from Associate professor Christian Brinch, cbri@food.dtu.dk or Associate professor Jakob Blæsbjerg Hoof, jblni@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU National Food Institute at DTU National Food Institute and DTU Bioengineering at DTU Bioengineering .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship/scholarship, Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Mekanik og Produ
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Mechanical and Production Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for highly motivated and independent candidates with the intention to complete a 3-year PhD at Aarhus University. The ideal candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:
 
• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.
• In-depth knowledge in fluid mechanics and cardiovascular applications.
• Experience with cell culture and tissue engineering
• Familiarity with numerical modelling (CFD), and software such as COMSOL, SimVascular, or similar software
• (optional) Previous exposure to agent-based modelling or systems biology
• excellent written and spoken English (optional Danish).

Place of employment and place of work:
