• 
Experience from management consulting, business development, finance or strategy, combined with a motivation to turn problem-solving into hands-on implementation

• 
A solid understanding of how to identify and create value in a production environment

• 
Experience from manufacturing, operations, Lean or Six Sigma is an advantage, but not a requirement

• 
Fluent English communication skills, both written and spoken.

What do we offer?

As our new Business Development Manager, you will work close to the strategic core of Kruså Dairy and influence decisions with tangible impact. The role offers broad exposure across strategy, operations, finance and continuous improvement, along with the autonomy to shape your agenda and support from the site leadership team and wider Arla network.

Would you like to join us?

If you want to combine strategy with implementation and help shape the future of Kruså Dairy, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply as soon as possible, as we will review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis. The recruitment will close once the right candidate has been found. For questions, please contact Site Director, Nicoline Akkerman at +45 91315826.

Do you enjoy finding the biggest commercial opportunities, improving customer journeys, and turning data into initiatives that drive measurable growth? Keep reading!

At Limepack, E-commerce is at the heart of how we acquire and convert customers across Europe. As we grow, we see significant potential to improve the customer journey and webshop performance across our markets, while becoming much better at what happens after the first purchase: building stronger relationships, increasing repeat purchases, and growing customer lifetime value.

With our current E-commerce Manager going on maternity leave, this role has a unique starting point. You’ll initially take ownership of E-commerce growth and customer journey optimisation, but this is not simply a 10–12 month maternity cover. The role is designed to evolve with you: over time, your focus will shift towards becoming Limepack’s Loyalty Lead, taking long-term ownership of Post-Purchase, CRM & Lifecycle.

This is a role for someone who combines commercial thinking with strong execution. You’ll use data to identify where the biggest opportunities are, set priorities, and drive initiatives across teams, taking responsibility for turning ideas into measurable results.

📋 Your responsibilities and impact

Your focus will evolve as you grow into the role: starting with E-commerce and gradually taking ownership of Loyalty, CRM, Email and Lifecycle.

• Grow E-commerce performance: Own and improve webshop conversion, customer journeys, AOV and revenue across markets. Identify the biggest opportunities and turn them into scalable improvements.

• Lead and collaborate across our tech setup: For the first 10–12 months, you will lead Alexander, our UX/Frontend Developer, who will report to you, while you report to our CCO. You will also work closely with our two Backend Developers and external partners to bring initiatives from idea to implementation.

• Turn data into priorities: Use customer and commercial data to understand where we should focus, build a clear roadmap, and follow up on the KPIs that matter.

• Drive projects from idea to impact: Lead high-impact initiatives across teams, create clear ownership, and make sure the right people and resources come together to deliver on time.

• Build for scale: Look beyond one-off improvements and create solutions that can work effectively across Limepack’s European markets.

• Build our Loyalty engine: After 10-12 months, own and improve the customer journey beyond the first purchase across Post-Purchase, CRM, Email and Lifecycle. Build stronger customer relationships, increase repeat purchases and grow customer lifetime value.

What success looks like: Within your first 12 months, you’ll aim to increase webshop conversion by 30%, help deliver our 2027 E-commerce revenue target of 40M in new business, and establish clear ownership and priorities for Loyalty. Longer term, you’ll drive improvements in repeat purchase rate, CLV and lifecycle revenue, including increasing first-to-second-purchase retention from 40% to 50%.

👉 Who you are

• You think commercially: You naturally look for the opportunities that will have the biggest impact on revenue and customer value, rather than simply working through a list of tasks.

• You are analytical and curious: You enjoy digging into data, understanding what customers are doing, and using those insights to decide what to improve next.

• You make things happen: You take ownership from opportunity to execution, create structure around projects, and follow through until the result is delivered.

• You are always looking for a better way: You enjoy improving customer journeys, processes and systems and think about how solutions can be scaled rather than solving the same problem repeatedly.

• You are strong across teams: You’re comfortable driving projects through people you don’t directly manage, aligning different stakeholders, and creating clarity around priorities and ownership.

🎓 Your experience

To succeed in this role, you should bring a strong combination of E-commerce experience, commercial thinking, analytical skills and project ownership.

• You have 3–5 years of relevant experience, ideally in E-commerce, digital growth, CRO, CRM, lifecycle marketing, or a similar commercially focused role.

• You have owned E-commerce performance and can point to measurable commercial results you personally helped create.

• You have hands-on experience with CRO and customer journey optimisation and know how to turn insights into improvements.

• You are strong with data, prioritization and project management, and are comfortable coordinating initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholders.

• Experience with CRM, lifecycle, retention or multi-market E-commerce is a strong advantage.

🚀 Who We Are

Limepack is a profitable Copenhagen-based European scale-up making custom-branded takeaway packaging accessible to businesses of all sizes. Since 2018, we’ve expanded across 14 countries by partnering with European manufacturers to offer faster, more affordable, and more sustainable packaging solutions.

We’re growing fast: we’ve been named a Børsen Gazelle four years in a row for exceptional revenue growth (Limepack.com/growth), and our ambition is to triple revenue over the next three years.

Today, we’re a team of 33 people, including 14 remote colleagues. We put a lot of emphasis on building a great place to work, and we’re proud to be a certified Happy Workplace (Limepack.com/happy). 🚀

💚 We offer:

• A full-time position based in Copenhagen with flexibility to work from home.

• A competitive salary based on experience.

• 6 weeks of paid time off, pay during sick days, and generous paid parental leave.

• The opportunity to take ownership of an important commercial area and grow from E-commerce ownership into leading Limepack’s Loyalty, CRM & Lifecycle agenda.

Meaningful impact: Your work will help improve the uptime of commercial hydrogen refueling stations and keep zero-emission fleets operating.

Modern facilities in Lind: You will work in modern facilities with advanced test bays, a high-quality lunch canteen, an active staff association, and health insurance.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The product and the direction

Today we sell chat. Email is rolling out now, and phone and social follow. On top of that we are building the brain: a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers, understands why people buy, and why they do not, and acts on it while the buyer is still on the page. The effect is measured against a control group, so the shop can see what it means for revenue.

That moves the sale from a customer service tool to a conversation about growth, and revenue per customer can become several times what it is today.

The role

Ownership of new business, partners and existing customers in one place. You run the process from first contact to signature, find out what works and write the sales process the rest of the company will follow.

The partner channel has to be built. Agencies and platform partners need to be found, judged realistically and sold alongside until they can do it on their own.

Growth in the existing customer base is part of it, especially as email, phone and the brain roll out, measured against clear monthly and quarterly targets.

Price, pitch, customer profile and process are yours. They change when they do not work, and the team is built as the numbers allow. Denmark is home turf, but we already have customers and partners in DACH and the Netherlands, and those markets grow from here.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

You do not step into a finished sales organisation. You build the commercial side together with the founder, and what you decide on price, pitch, process and the first hires is what Userlink will sell on for years.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The brain

The agents are the arms. The next layer is a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers: conversations on chat, email, phone and social, on-site behaviour, orders, returns and reviews.

The system identifies the moments where a sale is won or lost and intervenes while the session is still live. It scores answer coverage per product and closes the gaps, quantifies objections and unmet demand, and traces returns back to the expectation that broke.

Learning happens across all webshops, more than six million visits a month, where patterns become visible that no single shop has the traffic to see. Every intervention is measured against a control group. The patterns are shared, the data stays with each shop.

The hard problems are retrieval and evaluation of LLM output at scale, data isolation when patterns are shared across customers, latency in real-time flows, and attribution that holds up under scrutiny.

The stack

Java with Spring Boot, React and MongoDB, with language models and vector search on top. Moving the backend to C# and .NET is under consideration.

The role

Technical ownership of the platform: architecture, code quality, operations, security and prioritisation, combined with hands-on development every day. Standards for review, testing, monitoring and releases, and recruiting the next developers.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

jobs.occupation: PhD in In-Operando Diagnostics of Li-ion and Post-Li-ion Batteries Using Acoustic Technology
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a PhD stipend position is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 15 November 2026 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks
Battery performance assessment and diagnostics rely today on standardised electrical measurements complemented by post-mortem analysis. None of these methods is suited for in-operando diagnostics, as they are either destructive or require the battery to be taken out of its daily operation. Acoustic techniques, based either on passive listening to acoustic emissions or on active ultrasound signal injection, have recently been proposed as an alternative; however, further research is needed to establish the relationship between materials degradation and the sensed acoustic signals. The aim of this PhD project is to establish a mechanistic understanding of the coupling between battery ageing mechanisms and measured acoustic signals, and to translate this understanding into a diagnostic method applicable to both Li-ion and post-Li-ion chemistries.

You will start by reviewing the state of the art in acoustic-based battery diagnostics, and you will then design and build a set-up for sensing acoustic emissions in coin cells. Using this set-up, you will carry out degradation tests over a wide range of operating conditions with simultaneous acoustic and electrical measurements, and you will analyse how the acoustic signatures relate to the electrical ones and to the underlying degradation mechanisms. On this basis, you will develop an acoustic-based, physics-validated model for battery diagnostics; the resulting algorithm is targeted to be at least 25% more accurate than conventional impedance-based estimation and at least 50% less energy demanding than traditional diagnostic approaches. While most of the experimental work will be carried out at coin-cell level, a proof of concept at single-layer pouch-cell level is expected, which will facilitate further demonstration towards innovation.

The work will be supported by critical analysis of the results, benchmarking against the state of the art, and high-quality publications and conference presentations. In addition to the research activities, you will contribute to teaching and to the supervision of student projects, as well as to broader dissemination activities within the department.

The position is offered in relation to the research group Batteries, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials.

Your competencies 
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate who is eager to work at the intersection of battery testing, sensing instrumentation and signal processing, and who enjoys combining fundamental understanding with hands-on experimental work. The ideal candidate is curious and persistent in the laboratory, excels at troubleshooting, can plan and execute experiments independently, and motivated to collaborate closely with colleagues in an international and interdisciplinary environment.

Applicants must hold an M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering, energy engineering or mechatronics. Experience with one or more of the following will be considered an advantage: electrical characterisation of batteries, acoustic or ultrasonic sensing and laboratory instrumentation, and signal processing and data-driven modelling (e.g., in MATLAB or Python). Experience with Problem Based Learning (PBL) is required, as the PhD student will be involved in the supervision of BSc and MSc student projects. Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken, are required, as the project will be carried out in an international research environment. Danish language skills are highly desirable and will support co-supervision of BSc student projects; however, they are not a formal requirement.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are    
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges.

Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk.

How to apply

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Other relevant documents

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

Your work will include formulating representative power system analysis and optimization problems, developing and implementing quantum and hybrid quantum–classical solution methods, and comparing their performance with relevant classical approaches. jobs.occupation: Project Planning Specialist, Medium Voltage Products
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

**Product Marketing Manager

__

**At ABB, we are dedicated to addressing global challenges head-on. Our core values: care, courage, curiosity, and collaboration - combined with a focus on diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities - are important drivers in our goal to enable everyone to create sustainable solutions. This is our story. Make it your story.

**Role and tasks

**As Project Planning Specialist, you will combine project planning and control with operational sales administration support within ABB’s Medium Voltage Products business. Working closely with project managers and colleagues across sales administration, engineering, finance, procurement and operations, you will create reliable schedules, maintain accurate SAP data and provide clear insights into project costs, revenue, cash flow, risks and opportunities.

The role is designed with a broad scope. Alongside project planning responsibilities, you will support the sales administration team during peak workload periods and planned absences and help administer project-related financial guarantees. Your work will contribute to reliable project delivery, accurate commercial data and continuity in day-to-day operations. The position is based at our office in Middelfart and follows a hybrid work model.

• Maintaining and improving SAP master data, including material creation, sales item maintenance, product group structures and customer segmentation.

• Developing and maintaining integrated project schedules, including baselines, forecasts, milestones, resources and critical-path activities.

• Monitoring project progress, costs, revenue and cash flow, and providing regular reports and forecasts to the project team and relevant stakeholders.

• Identifying scheduling or cost deviations and working with project managers to define practical corrective actions.

• Creating, administering and maintaining advance payment guarantees, warranty guarantees and other project-related financial securities.

• Providing operational support and backup during peak workload periods and planned absences within the sales administration team.

• Supporting project risk, change, contract and claims management by assessing potential schedule and cost impacts and contributing to mitigation plans.

• Coordinating planning activities with engineering, procurement, finance, customers, contractors and other stakeholders while contributing to improvements in local tools and processes.

**Qualifications For The Role

**

• Hands-on experience using SAP for master data maintenance, material creation, sales item maintenance or related sales administration tasks.

• Experience with project planning, project control, project coordination or a related area.

• Experience monitoring project costs, forecasts, cash flow or other financial project information.

• Experience with financial guarantees, commercial administration or similar project-related documentation is helpful.

• Familiarity with project risks, changes, contracts or claims is helpful.

• A relevant educational background in engineering, finance, business, project management or another applicable field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Ability to organize information, manage parallel activities and communicate clearly in English; Danish proficiency is an advantage.

Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization that emphasizes employee well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability

You will be based at our office in Middelfart, alongside team members and colleagues. In addition, we offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also sign up to receive notifications on other opportunities within ABB. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Morten Hellesøe at +4540278387.

Project Director, Healthcare – Aarhus

Do you want to take ownership of one of the most strategic and visible programmes in Danish digital health? As Project Director, you will lead a comprehensive, product-strategic initiative for our electronic patient record (EPR) product, which has the potential to become the foundation for international growth. Sounds exciting? Then seize the chance now!

Systematic Healthcare – a coherent healthcare system

Systematics’ healthcare solutions are used by more than 200,000 users in, among others, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK and New Zealand. Our EPR solution is the core system in a hospital and has been developed in close collaboration with our customers.

Experienced Project Director with ownership, impact and business understanding

As Project Director, you will have overall responsibility for one of Systematics’ most strategic initiatives: an extensive, long-term, product-strategic programme for our EPR product. The programme is closely linked to the EPR solution used in Western Denmark today and is characterised by high complexity, both internally and externally, with many stakeholders including our customers.

The role is not only about delivering on time, price, scope and quality - as our new Project Director, you help create the framework for the program and ensure that both our customers and Systematic realise the expected benefits.

You are the programme’s single point of accountability towards both the steering committee, our customers management and the management in Systematic.

The programme is run as a virtual organisation across tracks such as development, product management, customer projects, implementation and operations. You have no direct reports and therefore create results through influence, trust, clear direction and strong governance. You report to the Vice President for the area and work closely with our customers, Product Management and the leadership of the EPR area.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Owning the programme plan, budget and business case, and ensuring a coherent solution and the expected benefits over the programme’s lifetime.

• Establishing and driving the programme’s governance and acting as the programme’s primary representative towards customer and Systematic management, including preparing and presenting decision papers.

• Actively owning and protecting the scope: challenging new requirements, driving priorities and ensuring an effective change management process.

• Owning the roadmap, schedule, milestones, budget and resource plan, and ensuring proactive risk management with timely escalation to the steering committee.

• Ensuring delivery in accordance with the agreements and leading changes and negotiations together with our Sales and Legal teams and the Vice President.

• Managing a complex stakeholder landscape, internally and externally, including customers and their regional top management, political decision-makers, clinical leadership, partners and internal units, and ensuring that the product roadmap is aligned with the programme’s commitments.

• Building and leading the virtual programme organisation across tracks and departments by setting direction, removing obstacles and being an ambassador for culture and collaboration. At the same time, you support the organisational change that the programme entails

You will be based at our office in Aarhus and can expect customer meetings around Denmark. Your success is measured by whether the programme delivers within the agreed time, price, scope and quality, and whether the benefits of the business case are realised. An important success criterion is the trust of customers and management in the programme.

Your competencies and qualifications

We envision that you have 10–15 years of experience in programme and project management, several of them with large, complex IT programmes of similar complexity: multi-year, with several parallel tracks, many stakeholders and organisational interfaces. You hold a master’s degree, for example in engineering, IT or economics, and ideally a certification in programme management, such as PMI PgMP or Axelos MSP.

In addition, we expect that you:

• Have experience from the IT industry and with public customers, large public contracts and politically governed organisations. Experience from the healthcare sector is a significant advantage.

• Have been responsible for budget, business case and contractual commitments, including negotiating changes with customers.

• Have experience reporting to executive management and steering committees, leading in matrix or virtual organisations without formal line authority, and taking part in organisational change.

• Have a strong understanding of business and finance, as well as experience in contract and risk management.

• Speak Danish as your native language and are fluent in English.

As a person, you:

Take ownership: You act as the owner of the programme, not as an administrator of plans and reports, and you have the courage to say no and make difficult prioritisations.

Lead through influence: You create commitment and results without formal authority.

Have executive presence and political awareness: You are credible at executive level and communicate complex topics clearly and in a balanced way.

Are commercial and customer-minded: You balance customer value with Systematic’s interests and understand the importance of our customers’ work for patients and clinicians.

Are structured, proactive and resilient: You create overview, make decisions on an incomplete basis, and keep your energy and calm throughout a long, high-paced programme.

Are demanding and inclusive: You create an open and honest environment where people are heard and their work is recognised.

jobs.description:
Do you want to help Arla shape the future of milk planning? Working with advanced forecasting, AI, and optimization, you'll assist in developing innovative solutions that predict future milk supply and optimize how milk is allocated across our global production network.

“In Supporting & Cross Functions within IT & Digital, we partner with Global Trading & Planning, Arla International, and Arla Foods Ingredients. You will become part of a strong and collaborative team working closely with business stakeholders to drive value creation, co-create digital roadmaps and ensure we realize the full value of our digital investments across Arla.__”, says IT Value Partner, Mikkel Nissen.

About the job

You will work with two central solutions supporting Global Planning One Milk Balance and One Intake. One Milk Balance is Arla’s internally developed planning system for balancing raw milk supply with the needs of our dairies. It ensures that incoming milk, fat, and by-products are allocated according to site capacities and business priorities. The solution runs on Azure and integrates with SAP IBP, One Intake, and Power BI.

One Intake is Arla’s next-generation milk intake forecasting solution. Built on Databricks, it uses modern time-series models to improve visibility into future milk supply by combining data science, farmer insights, and supply chain planning. More specifically, you will

• Develop forecasting and optimisation solutions using Python, SQL, Databricks, Azure, and MLOps.

• Support the operational performance of One Milk Balance and One Intake.

• Turn analytical insights into actionable Power BI reporting.

• Work closely with global planners to improve forecasting, planning, and decision-making.

Who are you?

You are curious about how data can solve real business challenges and are motivated by continuously improving forecasting and planning solutions through data and technology. We imagine that you bring most of the following

• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics or a related field.

• At least two years of experience as a Data Scientist or in a similar technical role.

• Hands-on experience with Python, SQL, Databricks and Azure-based data solutions, including data pipelines, analytics and modelling.

• A strong analytical mindset and business curiosity, with the ability to translate complex data into practical solutions.

• A proactive and collaborative approach, with a motivation to work closely with business stakeholders.

What do we offer?

You will have the opportunity to work at the intersection of data science, technology and global milk planning, contributing to solutions that help Arla forecast, balance and allocate milk across its global network. We offer a flexible hybrid working model, competitive salary and benefits, and opportunities for professional development.

We’re looking for an analytically sharp Student Assistant to join our Risk Management function, working directly with our Chief Risk Officer (CRO). You’ll help with analysis, reports, and projects that management and directors use to keep track of the bank’s risks. Along the way, you’ll see up close how a fast-growing, fully licensed neobank makes decisions at the very top.

What you will be doing

The role is project-driven, and no two weeks will look the same. That said, you’ll primarily work across these areas:

• Supporting the CRO: Helping to carry out risk reviews, checking how well the bank identifies and handles its risks. You will also help keep our overview of the bank’s key risks up to date, along with our model inventory – the list of models the bank uses and how each one is controlled.

• Ad-hoc financial analysis and risk reporting: Collecting and analysing data, researching specific questions and helping to assess risks. For example, you might look at how our risk models are set up and whether they work as intended.

• Reports and dashboards for management and the Board: Helping to turn your analysis into clear reports and dashboards. Examples include the monthly risk appetite report, which shows whether the bank stays within the limits for how much risk it’s willing to take, the annual CRO report, and the dashboards presented to the Board of Directors.

And don’t worry. You’ll have experienced colleagues backing you, helping you find your way in both risk management and banking.

Who we are looking for

Ideally, you:

• Are currently enrolled as a 3rd-year Bachelor’s or 1st-year Master’s student in Finance, Economics, Business, Data Analytics, or a related quantitative field.

• Have strong analytical problem-solving skills.

• Demonstrate a keen interest in the modern FinTech ecosystemAre already familiar with or want to learn and apply advanced GenAI tools to optimise analytical workflows, automate data synthesis, and assist in complex financial research.

• Communicate fluently in English. Spoken Danish is an advantage but not a prerequisite.

What we offer

We offer a high-energy, collaborative fintech environment built on trust, humour, ambition, and innovation.

• High-level exposure: You report directly to the CRO and get a front-row view of executive decision-making in a licensed EU bank, with a steep learning curve.

• Competitive student pay: Hourly rate from 165 DKK (BA) / 180 DKK (Master).

• Flexibility: Typically 15–20 hours per week, with full flexibility around exams and study commitments.

• A vibrant student community: 10+ fellow students from CBS, DTU, KU, and CPH Business in our Student Forum.

• Perks: Free lunch, cake on Thursdays, a free fitness studio on site, and a strong health insurance package with broad coverage.

About kompasbank

With the latest technology and an outside-the-box mindset, we are building the future role model for business banking. As a neobank, we’ve built our platform from scratch – completely independent of existing structures and processes – and we aim to deliver services and products that make life much easier for small and medium-sized businesses across Europe.

Since opening our doors in August 2021, we have grown by leaps and bounds. With traction in Denmark, Germany, and Spain, we are now considered one of the leading fintechs in the Nordics. In 2024, kompasbank was ranked #2 on the Sifted 250, a leaderboard highlighting the fastest-growing companies in Europe based on revenue growth.

jobs.occupation: Senior Infrastructure and Cloud Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. You will own the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across infrastructure, network, and workforce identity security, and rolling out the first paved roads for a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen), workforce identity and access, and drift checks for cloud configuration and network rules. You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers, and every Veo employee, work securely across our offices and clouds.

**What You Will Do

**You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network

• Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work

• Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation

• Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it

• Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation

• Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path

• Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

**What You Could Bring

**This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

• Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale

• Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC

• Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows

• A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist

• Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain

• Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact

• Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done

• Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.

Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for a position in which you can set direction and help shape our company? If so, then you could be the newest addition to our team as

**Senior Frontend Engineer – Tracking.

****Be part of the movement - and play your part.

****About The Role

This is a role for someone who enjoys both hands-on implementation and seeing the bigger picture: how platforms, tracking, data flows, consent, and customer experiences connect to create better and more personalised journeys.

Working at DFDS At DFDS, you will be part of an environment where technology, collaboration, and business impact go hand in hand. This role offers the opportunity to work on meaningful digital initiatives that influence how we engage with customers across channels and platforms.

• Meaningful scope: Help shape the Martech and customer data foundation behind important digital journeys.

While you’re with us, we want you to develop. At DFDS, we believe that development happens first and foremost through activities in the workplace. We will also offer training courses that can support you in your role, if needed.

Are we a match? Then what are you waiting for? Apply Now. If you think your personality, skills, experience, and desire match this role, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your CV as soon as possible, as we’re keen to meet potential candidates on an ongoing basis.

For questions regarding the technical scope or team culture, feel free to reach out to Frontend Chapter Lead, Noman Ahmed Khan at nkhan@dfds.com. Please note that we only consider applications submitted directly through our official recruitment system.

We look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.    

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is November 22, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk  

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**About The Job

**Flatpay has become one of the fastest-growing payment companies by helping merchants accept payments in-store. Now we're taking the next step.

Online is one of Flatpay's newest and most strategic engineering domains. We're building the products and platforms that enable merchants to accept payments online and grow their businesses in the digital economy.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll play a key role in defining the technical direction of Flatpay's online platform and helping establish the technical and architectural foundations that will support the next phase of Flatpay's growth.

**Why Flatpay?

Operating in Denmark, Finland, Germany, Italy, France, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, we're more than just a service provider; we are your trusted business partner.

We continuously strive to stay ahead of the curve, adapting our solutions to meet our clients' evolving needs. Ready to be part of something extraordinary?

_Join Pandora’s Global Strategy & Business Development Team as Senior Manager, Strategy Delivery Office

_Are you a delivery leader who will help Pandora’s most important strategic initiatives realise their full potential? Do you want to work at the heart of our strategic agenda, partner with senior leaders and help mobilise a global organisation around its ambition? Join us at Pandora’s Global Office in Copenhagen and play a central role in turning strategy into sustained business impact for the world’s leading jewellery brand.

**About The Team

**Pandora’s Strategy Delivery Office is part of our Global Strategy & Business Development team, which reports directly to Pandora’s CEO. We connect Pandora’s ambition, portfolio choices and organisational mobilisation to create confidence that our most important initiatives are focused on the right outcomes, progressing with sufficient pace and realising the value behind our strategy. We partner closely with senior leaders across functions and markets to strengthen delivery and resolve risks and dependencies that cut across the organisation. We combine a collaborative spirit with sharp problem-solving skills and offer a supportive and fun team environment.

**What You’ll Do

**We are looking for a delivery leader who is motivated by helping strategic ambitions become reality. You know how to build momentum and outcomes while keeping accountability with the leaders responsible for delivery.

**

• Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from initial scope through execution and impact.

• A track record of constructively challenging senior leaders on plan quality, pace, value and organisational readiness.

**

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe’s Best Workplaces and ranked #1 among Danish companies, Pandora is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace. We are dedicated to nurturing a culture where everyone feels respected, valued.

jobs.occupation: Dedicated Team Leader for Mechanical Engineering Team
jobs.description:
Polyteknik AS is expanding, and we are therefore searching for an excellent leader for our competent mechanical engineering team. The mechanical engineering team designs highly advanced production systems for the semicon/mems/sensor and ICT industries primarily in Europe.

Tasks

Our team of mechanical engineers takes Polyteknik’s advanced production systems from initial concept through detailed design to the production-ready BOM. The team currently consists of 7 people. Polyteknik AS is a Danish PVD systems manufacturer with an innovative and best service approach. With more than 30 years in business, an international reference list, and an excellent platform of technology, Polyteknik AS has proved to be an appreciated partner in the thin film industry.

jobs.occupation: Lead Integration Developer (.NET / APIs / Cloud) for Emply
jobs.description:

As a senior team member, you will be involved in hands-on coding, design, development, customization, configuration, testing, and deployment of enterprise software solutions. Emply People is a flexible HR solution for small and medium-sized businesses, supporting the full employee journey, from recruitment and onboarding to performance, time and absence management, and offboarding.

We're transitioning to modern technologies including microservices, containerisation and serverless architectures. You'll play a key role in this transformation from an integration perspective, helping build a more scalable, efficient and agile platform.

We're looking for a Lead Developer with strong hands-on experience building enterprise-grade integrations using the .NET stack.

**

• Defining integration architecture in collaboration with the Architect.

• Owning integration patterns and standards.

• Designing scalable APIs and integration services.

• Improving technical implementations, simplifying the codebase, and promoting coding best practices.

• Improving reliability, performance, and observability.

• Guiding the migration towards cloud-native services.

• Mentoring developers and raising engineering standards.

• 10+ years of proven experience designing and developing enterprise applications.

• Experience modernising legacy codebases and working with non-functional requirements such as security, performance, and scalability.

• Strong ownership of architecture and the ability to drive critical technical decisions.

• Hands-on experience with C#/.NET, MS SQL, Hangfire, REST, and GraphQL.

• Experience with API/interface modelling using OpenAPI.

• Strong understanding of integration, including enterprise integration patterns, synchronous vs. asynchronous integration, and related trade-offs.

• Experience with Domain-Driven Design (DDD).

• Experience with Git and development tools such as Azure DevOps and Jira.

• A proactive approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in clear business terms and act as a technical sparring partner and mentor to other developers.

You will work in our Østerbro office, in a team that cares about its members and enjoys a good laugh. Emply is part of Paychex Europe, a leading provider of HCM solutions. Paychex Europe is growing rapidly and expanding into the European market, constantly seeking passionate talent to join them on this exciting journey. Find out more at www.emply.com.

We value different perspectives and believe diverse teams make better decisions. If this role interests you and you can see yourself contributing to our team, we encourage you to apply!

For questions about the role, please do not hesitate to contact Jacob Borella jborella@paychex.eu. Applications are reviewed continuously, and we look forward to meeting candidates who are excited about this opportunity.

Respect and partnership are at the heart of how we work together. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of age, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, religion or background. At Paychex Europe, we strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and thrive. Our hiring decisions are based on skills, experience and potential.

Start date: As soon as possible

Location: Østerbro (Hybrid)

**Full time

****PAYCHEX EUROPE

**Paychex Europe delivers Payroll, HR, and Workforce Management solutions that simplify processes, save time, and provide insights that help businesses support their people and drive success. Built on over 50 years of expertise, our solutions adapt to changing needs — helping businesses run more efficiently, today and tomorrow.

jobs.occupation: Senior Data & Process Specialist at Skærbæk Power Station

In this role regular physical visits to our locations at Avedøre Power Station and in the Gentofte office should be expected.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of Data & Application where you, together with your colleagues, will be responsible of environmental and non-financial calculations for regulatory reporting, customer settlement and internal ESG reporting for Ørsted’s Danish combined heat and power plants. We have workplaces in Skærbæk, Gentofte, and at Avedøre Power Station, and we visit our energy assets on site when needed. Data & Application is part of Digitalisation & Technology, offering a collaborative environment with passionate and skilled colleagues. **

• utilizing technical insight to ensure complete, correct & validated data

• managing flue gas emissions data and reporting, including follow-up on emission limits, permit conditions and regulatory documentation

jobs.description:
System Architect (senior specialist) – Drive the architecture of next-generation medical device platforms

This is not a software architecture role.

At Coloplast, we develop and manufacture physical medical devices used by millions of people worldwide. As a Senior System Architect, you will help define the architectural foundations of future product families and platforms, enabling innovation, scalability, and efficient product development across generations of products.

You will shape how platforms are structured to support reuse, new technology, portfolio growth, manufacturability, and long-term business value together with other R&D disciplines.

Working at the intersection of product development, manufacturing, quality, and systems engineering, you will balance user needs, product performance, regulatory requirements, risk, and platform strategy to create robust and scalable architectural solutions. Your work will ensure that future products are built on well-defined architectural foundations that enable both innovation and efficient execution.

Join a team shaping the future of R&D

You will become part of our Requirements Engineering Team within the Centre of Excellence in R&D.

The team consists of highly skilled specialists within Requirements Engineering and Systems Architecture, working with our processes and platforms.

We support development projects across the organization and continuously strengthen how systems development is conducted in a regulated medical device environment.

Design architecture that enable innovation

As our new Senior System Architect, you will be responsible for defining and maintaining system architectures related to the products and product families for one of our Chronic Care business areas, serving as the architectural lead.

Working closely with product teams and stakeholders across R&D, you will transform business needs, user needs, stakeholder requirements, and technical opportunities into architecture decisions that balance innovation, manufacturability, regulatory compliance, risk, cost, and long-term scalability.

Specifically, you will:

• 
Define and drive the platform strategy for a dedicated business area, enabling scalable product families, reusable platform assets, and accelerated delivery of future products.

• 
Drive architectural decomposition into system capabilities, subsystems, interfaces, and architectural building blocks.

• 
Establish and maintain architecture documentation and system structures.

• 
Define system boundaries, interfaces, and allocation of functionality across the system.

• 
Identify opportunities for platform reuse, standardization, modularization, and scalability.

• 
Facilitate architectural trade-offs across business, technical, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and user perspectives.

• 
Provide architectural guidance that ensures alignment between product architecture, platform strategy, manufacturing, quality, and development activities.

• 
Support the understanding of the systems architecture discipline and the synergies to other development disciplines through close collaboration with key stakeholders across R&D and beyond

Strong architecture experience within complex product development

You combine strong systems thinking with the ability to navigate complexity and create practical solutions.

You enjoy collaborating across disciplines and are comfortable influencing decisions without having formal management responsibility. You are motivated by solving real development challenges and helping teams make sound architecture decisions. You take initiative and focus on opportunities and solutions rather than constraints.

What we expect from you:

• 5+ years of experience working with Systems Architecture, Systems Engineering, or development of complex multidisciplinary products.

• Experience defining system architecture and driving technical decisions in product development programs.

• Strong understanding of systems thinking and Systems Engineering principles.

• Experience working across multiple engineering disciplines.

• You thrive both when driving tasks independently and when working closely with colleagues to achieve shared goals

• Proven ability to influence stakeholders and create alignment across functions.

• Experience from regulated industries such as medical devices, life science, aerospace, defence, industrial automation, robotics, or similar.

• Understanding of requirements engineering, risk management, verification, and validation.

• Experience with modular architectures, platform development, and reusable solutions.

• Strong communication skills and ability to explain complex topics to a broad stakeholder audience.

• Experience defining system boundaries, interfaces, and reusable architectural building blocks that support platform-based product development.

• Motivated by both shaping long-term architectural direction and contributing to successful day-to-day product delivery.

You might also bring

• Experience from medical device development.

• Knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62304, IEC 62366, or similar standards.

• Experience with technology roadmaps and long-term architecture planning.

• Experience working with external development partners.

• Experience with architecture modelling approaches and tools.

Please note: Seniority level will be determined based on your experience (specialist or senior specialist)

Why join us?

This is a unique opportunity to influence some of Coloplast's most important development programs while helping establish platform-based development as a key capability across R&D.

You will work with highly skilled colleagues, contribute directly to products that improve people's lives, and play a vital role in enabling future innovation through strong system architecture.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about this position, please contact Head of Requirement Engineering, Centre of Excellence, R&D, Stine Renberg at +45 49113320. We continuously review applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. You will work closely with technical leaders, product leaders, and other managers across Dalux Development.

At Dalux, Development Managers typically contribute across four areas:

People leadership

You will lead and support your team members in their professional growth, motivation, and performance. You will help create clarity, direction, and engagement in a specialist environment, and you will play an active part in attracting and hiring new colleagues.

Team and engineering enablement

You will help your teams succeed by improving ways of working, removing obstacles, and strengthening collaboration. In a specialist department, that also means creating the right conditions for deep technical work, knowledge sharing, and high engineering quality.

Product and cross-functional collaboration

You will work closely with Product Management, Design, and technical leaders to ensure that our Computer Vision and Machine Learning capabilities are translated into intuitive product features that allow users to navigate, understand, and act on real-world site data. You will help balance technical possibilities, product value, quality, and long-term sustainability.

Organizational development and change

As Dalux continues to grow, many of our leaders contribute beyond their own teams. You may take part in or drive initiatives related to tooling, engineering processes, quality, innovation, technical maturity, or organizational development.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a leader with a background in software development and relevant experience from Computer Vision or similar domains working with visual or spatial data .

Most importantly, you have the technical understanding and leadership maturity to lead highly skilled specialists and help them perform at a high level.

We expect that you have:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related field

• Experience with development of Computer Vision systems

• Experience taking responsibility in either technical leadership , people leadership , or both

• A passion for helping other people grow and succeed

• Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical roles

It is an advantage if you also have:

• Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or applied fields of Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Robotics, Autonomous systems, or similar

• Experience leading specialist teams or senior engineers

• Experience working with spatial data, mapping, or geometry-heavy problems in a product development context

• Experience hiring technical talent in highly specialized fields

• Experience working in empowered product teams or similar collaborative product development setups

What Success Looks Like In The Role

In this role, you will succeed by building a strong and healthy specialist engineering environment. That means:

• Your teams are motivated, growing, and delivering high-quality work

• Collaboration across engineering, product, and design is strong

• The department is able to attract and hire great specialist talent

• Technical depth and product impact reinforce each other

• You help scale both people and practices as Dalux grows

Why join Dalux?

Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005. We create digital tools for the construction industry, and our products are used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

We are proud to develop our products entirely in-house , and we care deeply about engineering quality, modern technology, and building strong teams. At Dalux, you will join an environment with ambitious colleagues, real product impact, and a strong belief that great software is built by empowered people working closely together.
