A position as associate professor (10% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Radiology (Odense), the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology, Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), in collaboration with University College Lillebælt (UCL) and Odense Universitetshospital (OUH), invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in Radiography, with 10% research time at the Department of Radiology, OUH. The position is offered for a five-year period with the possibility of extension. The starting date is subject to agreement.

About the research unit

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology conducts high-quality research across all radiological specialties and contributes significantly to the education and development of highly qualified staff for both clinical and academic work.

The unit values researchers with diverse professional backgrounds and has approximately 20 affiliated members, including a professor, associate professors, PhD students, adjunct professors and others.

The unit has a well-established research environment and organises a number of regular activities and meetings throughout the year, including research retreats combining academic and social activities.

Research and Teaching Responsibilities
The position involves research, academic development, research training, teaching, including examinations, supervision and assessment activities.

Qualifications and Expectations
The Associate Professor must hold a primary position at UCL.

The successful applicant must have documented research and teaching experience within radiography and a particular interest in ultrasound.

Furthermore, strong collaborative skills are required in order to further develop research in radiography, both across disciplines and at national and international level. Having international research collaborators is considered an advantage but is not a requirement.

Joint Research Strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and OUH

The joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and OUH sets the direction for our shared research activities in the coming years.

Based on the vision, “We conduct research together to create the patient care of the future,” particular emphasis is placed on:

• 
Research across disciplines, with people at the centre

• 
Strong research environments as a driving force for development

• 
The research pathway from idea to impact

Further information about the joint research strategy is available on the SDU website.

Applicants Must Document

• 
A PhD degree or equivalent postgraduate research qualifications

• 
Relevant research experience documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals

• 
Relevant clinical experience

• 
Relevant experience in educational administration

• 
A successful track record in obtaining research funding

Applicants must meet the qualifications required at Associate Professor level in accordance with the applicable Danish Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Reporting

The Associate Professor will report to Head of Research Bo Mussmann on matters relating to the associate professorship.

Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Research Bo Mussmann, Department of Clinical Research/OUH: Email: bo.mussmann@rsyd.dk, Telephone: +45 20 59 88 56

Application deadline

01.11.2026 at 23:59 CET

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Associate Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed associate professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Kløvervænget 10, 2nd floor, 5000 Odense C, Denmark.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below. 

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. 

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation. 

Your application must include the following as PDF files:

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total).

• 
a motivation letter 

• 
a detailed CV 

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
6 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file. 

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan

• 
a detailed description of research experience 

• 
an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

• Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
• Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
• Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
• Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
• Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
• Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
• Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
• Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.
The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

• Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
• Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
• Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
• Strong written and spoken English skills.
• Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.
What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.

Are you passionate about end-to-end Supply Chain? Do you want to take Global Product Launch to the next level, coordinating with stakeholders throughout the entire value chain? Do you have an optimization mindset and can effectively manage multiple projects?

Then this might be your defining moment. Ambu is currently looking for a Global Product Launch Manager to be based at HQ in Ballerup to join our growing Global Supply Chain team!

**A role with global impact

**In the role, you will both support and take lead on assigned NPI Projects during all project phases, incorporating Global Supply Chain resources, whilst managing all critical aspect of taking new products to the market.

You will oversee execution across regions and markets, support risk‑buy management, and collaborate closely with global production sites on ramp‑up activities, capacity planning, and overall launch readiness.

Working closely with stakeholders across the entire value chain- including Global Product Management, R&D, Procurement, Production, Quality, and Commercial teams - you will act as the Supply Chain lead who drives alignment and momentum throughout the project.

Furthermore, you will be encouraged to challenge existing processes and proactively identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• New Product Introductions (NPI) – during all project phases.

• Close collaboration with stakeholders globally within Ambu, as well as external suppliers.

• Support Development of the NPI / Launch process across the Ambu organization.

• Reporting to GSC Management / Relevant stakeholders.

**Suggested candidate profile

**Skills and experiences can be earned in many ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be prescribed on paper. You are however likely to succeed in this position if you have a proven track record within project management, production and risk buy handling – and can deep dive into details whilst having the overview to keep it all on track. Moreover, you’re recognized by your energetic drive, strong motivation, and accountability in everything you do.

**Furthermore, You Have

**

• Around 5 years of experience within Supply Chain and Operations Management, preferably within a production set-up.

• A Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Engineering, Production or similar

• Strong, global end-to-end Supply Chain understanding across Value Chain.

• Experience in Business Intelligence.

• Strong communication skills and collaborative team-oriented mindset.

• Experience with ERP system.

• Fluency in English, both oral and written.

**About The Department

**You will join a fast-growing Global Supply Chain department, where high level of competence, humor and execution is part of everyday life. You will be reporting into the Head of Global Product Launch, Thomas Bigum. The team consists of dedicated and skilled colleagues, where you will have the opportunity for personal and professional growth. You will work from Ambu's headquarters in Ballerup, Denmark. You will, however, be working in a global context, where your stakeholders are located across the world.

**Apply for a career #ForeverForward

**The Talent Attraction team will engage with candidates on an ongoing basis; hence we encourage you to not hesitate, and apply!

If you have questions regarding the position, don’t hesitate to reach out to Head of Global Product Launch, Thomas Bigum, at tbig@ambu.com

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for a highly driven Team Manager to join Boozt Media Partnership (BMP), our in-house retail media business that helps brands grow through data-driven media solutions, creative concepts and tailored activations.

This is a player-coach role for someone who is an exceptional salesperson who knows how to drive results both individually and through a team. You will lead and develop our BMP sales team while owning your own portfolio of key clients.

Beyond hitting targets, we are looking for a strategic and commercially minded person who brings new ideas and challenges the status quo. You know how to build strong partner relationships, identify opportunities and turn them into sales and growth. Internally, you are a strong stakeholder who knows how to get people on board, drive initiatives forward and ensure our sales efforts are aligned with the wider business.

**What You Will Do

**

• Lead, coach, and challenge the sales team to deliver against ambitious targets.

• Own and grow a portfolio of key clients, building trust and acting as a strategic partner to drive larger, long-term investments.

• Drive sales performance across both your own portfolio and the wider team

• Navigate and manage internal stakeholders, collaborating cross-functionally to ensure our retail media offerings align with broader business goals.

• Identify and drive upselling and new revenue opportunities

• Use pipeline, CRM, and performance data to forecast, prioritize, and grow the business.

**YOUR PROFILE

**

• 5+ years of sales experience within media, digital advertising or a similar commercial environment

• Leadership experience or a strong track record of coaching and developing others

• A true salesperson with a strong performance and target-driven mindset

• Experience working with KPIs, CRM, pipeline management and forecasting

• Strong commercial understanding and experience with upselling

• High energy, strong communication skills and the ability to motivate others

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Remote Sensing of Ecosystem Resilience across Danish Landscapes
jobs.description:
We are seeking applications for a 2 year postdoc position in the field of remote sensing of ecosystem resilience in the Section of Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity at the Department of Biology, Aarhus, University, Denmark.

Biodiversity loss, landscape management and other global change drivers might influence how vegetation reacts to extreme events such as droughts or floods. Climate change is expected to increase the frequency and intensity of extreme events, which is why it is important to monitor the resilience of vegetation to such events. Remote sensing offers the opportunity to study resistance and recovery of vegetation greenness and productivity across entire landscapes, including natural, semi-natural and agricultural vegetation.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 28 February 2029.

Job description
This Postdoc position broadly aims at analyzing satellite time series to understand ecosystem responses to environmental stressors and disturbances, including extreme events like droughts and floods that might become more frequent under accelerating climate change. The main overarching research question is:

How do natural and managed ecosystems react to extreme events or disturbances, and how resilient are they?
The goal is to develop satellite-based indicators of ecosystem resilience across land-use types.

To this purpose, the Postdoc will be expected to combine multiple remote sensing techniques across scales, including Sentinel-2, Landsat or Sentinel-1. Compared to many land surface phenology studies at broad spatial scales (e.g. kilometers), the aim of this postdoc is to explore patterns at the level of individual fields, forests or grasslands in a fragmented landscape. By analysing responses across fine spatial scales, we will generate locally relevant metrics of ecosystem resilience and assess how different land-use types respond to climate anomalies.

This Postdoc position will focus on natural and agricultural landscapes, and mainly contribute to the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT) with the vision to provide a novel framework that tests and assesses the sustainability of agricultural production, both within Denmark and globally. The candidate will be part of the Section for Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity (ECOINF), Department of Biology.

The Postdoc will work directly with Prof. Fabian D. Schneider and collaborate with Prof. Signe Normand.
Applicants are encouraged to submit an individual, short project proposal of 1 to 2 pages maximum, showing how the applicant’s methodological competences can be used for the research and demonstrating the applicant’s understanding of related research, including referenced literature.

Your profile
We are seeking highly motivated Postdoc candidates interested in a scientific career. The applicant should hold an internal fascination for the topic, be independent, have excellent writing skills, and should be enthusiastic about working in an interdisciplinary and international academic environment.

Applicants are expected to have a PhD degree within ecology, Earth system science, geography, biology or similar, and have experience with: 

• Geospatial and statistical analyses of remote sensing and ecological data,
• Good programming skills, ideally using R, Python, or similar,
• Land cover and land use change,
• Multispectral remote sensing, and ideally multi-scale remote sensing tools,
• Biogeography, ecosystem or biodiversity science, including an understanding of the concept of ecosystem resilience and remote sensing of vegetation stress.
We expect the candidate to have strong knowledge and/or strong interest in remote sensing, sustainability and biodiversity, data science and agricultural and natural systems in Danish or European landscapes.

Important personal qualities are to be creative, good at problem-solving, a team-worker, independent, well structured, and keen to work across disciplines and societal sectors. Very good oral and written communication skills in English (fluent English) are expected.
Holding a B driver’s license is an advantage.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (http://bio.au.dk/) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department is especially known for its research contribution in biodiversity, global change and conservation biology, aquatic biology and ecology, arctic environment and ecosystems, genetics and evolution, microbiology and zoophysiology. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the institute. 
The department offers a vibrant and informal research environment with a long-standing tradition of collaboration with international university partners. Much of the internal communication is in English and we welcome international applicants.

What we offer 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators 
• a work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion 
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of employment is Aarhus University, Department of Biology, Section for Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity (ECOINF), Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with affiliated institutions. 
The work involves some periods of field work away from Aarhus.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Fabian Daniel Schneider, +4520906289, fabian.schneider@bio.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 3 November 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University, Roskilde, Denmark, invites applications for a permanent position as Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry. We seek a motivated and collaborative researcher who will contribute to improving and expanding our internationally recognised research and research-based advisory and teaching activities within environmental chemistry and related disciplines. The position is available from April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a permanent position starting April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University aims to expand and diversify its research, teaching, and advisory activities addressing current and future environmental challenges. We are therefore seeking an Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry to contribute to the continued development of the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology.

The candidate is expected to establish and maintain a research profile while contributing to collaborative research activities across the department and with external partners. The position offers considerable freedom to develop new research directions within environmental chemistry and related disciplines under the responsibility to keep your group including yourself mainly externally funded.

The Associate Professor will contribute to:
 * Development of an internationally strong and externally funded research programme. 
 * Research addressing the occurrence, fate, transport, transformation, exposure, and impacts of chemical contaminants in natural and engineered systems. 
 * Research-based advisory activities for Danish ministries, public authorities, and other stakeholders. 
 * Teaching and course development at Life Long education, MSc, and PhD levels. 
 * Supervision of MSc students, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other junior researchers. 
 * Development of interdisciplinary collaborations across environmental chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, modelling, and data science. 
 * Knowledge exchange and collaboration with governmental agencies, industry partners, and international research networks.

The selected candidate is expected to contribute directly to both basic and applied research and to support the department's longstanding tradition of combining scientific excellence with societal impact through research-based advisory services

Your profile
Applicants hold a PhD in Environmental Chemistry or a closely related discipline.

The selected candidate should have documented research experience within at least one area of environmental chemistry and demonstrate the ability to develop an internationally visible research profile.

Particular emphasis will be placed on:
 * Scientific productivity documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals. 
 * Ability to develop and maintain national and international research collaborations. 
 * Experience in obtaining external research funding, or clear potential to do so. 
 * Experience with university teaching and supervision. 
 * Effective communication and collaboration skills. 
 * Commitment to contributing to an inclusive and collegial research environment.

In addition, experience within the following areas will be considered:
 * Development and application of analytical methods for trace analysis of organic contaminants in environmental and biological matrices.
 * High-resolution mass spectrometry, including target, suspect screening, or non-target workflows.
 * Environmental fate, transport, and transformation of organic contaminants.
 * Environmental monitoring programmes and environmental assessment.
 * Exposure assessment and chemical risk assessment.
 * Environmental data analysis, chemometrics, or environmental data science.
 * Research-based advisory activities, including experience supporting governmental authorities or regulatory agencies.
 * Experience with the Danish environmental advisory system or similar national or international regulatory frameworks.
 * Interdisciplinary research bridging environmental chemistry with toxicology, ecotoxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, engineering, or computational sciences.

Qualifications at the Associate Professor level will be assessed in accordance with the criteria specified in the Danish university job structure and Aarhus University's assessment criteria for permanent academic positions.

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. The knowledge base encompasses fields such as social science, geography, economics, and policy analysis, in addition to mathematical modeling, physics, chemistry, toxicology, and microbiology. Both pure and applied research is conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services and climate change. Research based advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders and central to the Department economy. Currently, about 150 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology. The section conducts research and research-based advisory work targeting a better understanding of the transport and fate of organic pollutants in the environment, as well as a better understanding of the links between environmental chemistry, toxicology and human exposure. This includes tools to identify and quantify impacts, which can act as indicators of emerging problems. The aim is to provide the highest capability in Denmark for assessing risks associated with the distribution and fate of organic pollutants in the environment.

What we offer 
The department and section offer:
● An active, internationally recognised research environment
● a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories with high-end analytical equipment
● an interdisciplinary environment with both national and international collaborators as well as authorities and private companies
● a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
● a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
● a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work will be at Aarhus University, RISØ Campus, in Roskilde, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located close to Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits.

You will be working using several methods to study RNA, protein-interactions and epigenetics, often including high through-put methods. jobs.occupation: Postdoc Positions in Natural Language Processing (CPH)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for two or more postdoc positions in the area of Natural Language Processing (NLP). The positions are open for appointments from January 1, 2027 or soon thereafter. The duration of the positions is one or two years, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and preferences. The positions are at AAU’s Copenhagen campus, located at the waterfront in Sydhavnen.

The application deadline is Monday, November 9, 2026. Interviews are tentatively planned for December 10, 2026.

The positions are hosted within the Natural Language Processing (NLP) research group https://aaunlp.github.io/ at AAU Copenhagen, and postdocs will work under the academic leadership of Professor Johannes Bjerva https://bjerva.github.io/. The NLP group is a rapidly expanding research environment with strong activities in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed approaches to NLP, factuality in LLMs, and socially sustainable AI. The group is supported by several major national and international research grants – in 2026, we have grown to 20 researchers, including a full professor, four assistant professors, one postdoc, two research assistants, and 12 PhD students.

As a postdoc, you will join a highly collaborative, international, and ambitious research community, with access to state-of-the-art computational resources. In your role, you will have the opportunity to develop an independent research profile and compete for individual fellowships and faculty positions. The positions include the opportunity to undertake one or more research stays abroad to facilitate knowledge exchange with top research environments worldwide. The positions are in part funded by a DFF: Sapere Aude project (“Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection”) Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection - Aalborg University's Research Portal, an NNF: Ascending Data Science Investigator project (“LM2-SEC: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Security”)  https://vbn.aau.dk/en/projects/linguistically-motivated-language-model-security/, and an Erasmus+ project on AI-based Personal Language Learning Assistants in collaboration with VSKDansk  https://www.brondby.dk/om-kommunen/nyheder/2025/08/vskdansk-far-eu-stotte-til-udvikling-af-ai-baseret-sprogtutor.

Your work tasks

As a postdoc, you will conduct research within the area of multilingual NLP. We are seeking postdocs with two distinct profiles within this area:

• Postdoc 1: Security, Safety, and Privacy in Natural Language Processing and AI, with a focus on Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-based systems, and Agentic AI

• Postdoc 2: AI-based personal language learning assistants (1 year) and AI security (1 year).

Furthermore, there will be the possibility to gain experience as a co-supervisor for PhD students associated with these projects, and to supervise students on BSc. and MSc. levels.

The positions are embedded in an active and rapidly growing research environment, including ongoing projects on, e.g., AI security, epistemic diversity, linguistically motivated NLP, and knowledge-graph grounded factuality in LLMs. The postdocs will work both independently and collaboratively within the group and will have opportunities to engage with national and international partners. As a part of the projects funding these positions, we will host internationally recognised researchers at AAU, creating additional opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Your competencies

We are looking for candidates motivated to make fundamental scientific contributions to multilingual NLP and AI security. Candidates should have the ambition of reaching an internationally leading level of research excellence by building their own research profile, while contributing to the research environment.

Applicants must have:

• A relevant PhD degree (e.g., NLP, AI, ML, Security, Cryptography, or a related field) and a relevant MSc degree (e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computational Linguistics, or a related field)

• Strong skills in machine learning and deep learning

• Extensive experience with modern ML and NLP methods, including experience with experimentation, and with publishing in top-tier venues (e.g. ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, ACL, EMNLP, TACL)

• Excellent communication skills in English

Applicants with documented experience in security, privacy, safety, or robustness will be preferred.

**Qualification requirements

**Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

Who we are

According to the most recent US News and World Ranking, Aalborg University ranks 4th in Europe and 27th in the world within Best Universities for Engineering. According to a 2018 MIT report, Aalborg University is considered to have the 4th best engineering program in the world. According to the recent Times Higher Education Impact ranking, Aalborg University ranks 9th in the World for UN SDG Impact.

The Department of Computer Science at Aalborg University is highly regarded among researchers, students, and external partners because of our leading research, education, and collaboration. The department currently has more than 170 scientific staff, 20 administrative staff, and 1,100 students. Education and research are built around AAU's problem-based learning model.

The Section for Copenhagen at the department is a highly collaborative research environment, currently expanding from around 40 employees to approximately 60 over the next few years. The section includes members from research groups within NLP, AI, ML, Databases, Formal Methods, Human-Centred Computing, and others, and is uniquely characterised by an open, friendly, and supportive atmosphere. Daily life in the section is marked by informal interactions, knowledge sharing, and a strong sense of community. We also host a bi-weekly SemiBar (a combined seminar and Friday bar), where staff are challenged to present their research in a manner that provokes discussion across our diverse scientific backgrounds, along with regular social events, reading groups, cross-group research activities, and a newly established local PhD organisation promoting an active social and scientific life among our most junior researchers. Together, these initiatives create a dynamic and welcoming environment for early-career researchers and senior staff alike.

The Natural Language Processing (NLP) group, led by Professor Johannes Bjerva, is a rapidly expanding research environment specialising in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed AI, and trustworthy language technologies. The group hosts several major research projects funded by, e.g., the Carlsberg Foundation, Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (DFF), the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and AAU’s AI:X initiative. The group collaborates broadly across Europe and globally, and offers an inclusive, ambitious, and supportive research culture.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Cover letter, stating your motivations for applying and your qualifications in relation to the position – at most one page.

- Please indicate your preferred starting date, and your preferred duration of employment (at least 1 year, and at most 2 years).

- We ask applicants not to use generative AI or writing assistant tools in the preparation of their cover letter, except for basic grammatical and spelling correction.

• Curriculum Vitae (CV) - at most two pages

• A full list of publications.

- For three of these publications, include a single brief paragraph detailing your contributions to the work.

• Diplomas (bachelor, master's, and PhD degree diplomas)

• Project description – at most two pages.

• Please describe your research vision for the position in relation to the project topics outlined above.

• Other relevant document

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

**Do you have any questions?

**If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

**Salary and terms of employment

Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

VP of Quantum - Diasense ApS

Reports to: Marvin Holten, Founder and CTO

Team: Quantum Lead, Quantum Engineers, and part-time specialists in quantum information science and quantum optics, growing through 2027

Location: Quantum Denmark, Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site.

Start: January 2027

Company Overview

Diasense is a deep-tech company turning fundamental quantum physics into world-class scientific instruments. We are building the world's most sensitive magnetic microscope, using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond to measure magnetic fields at a sensitivity that no other technique can reach.

We are applying that instrument to one of the hardest measurement problems in semiconductor manufacturing: seeing what is actually happening inside a finished chip, electrically and non-destructively. It is a market where the physics has to be exceptional and the engineering has to be industrial, and very few companies in the world are attempting both.

We are a spin-out of DTU Physics, based in the quantum center of Copenhagen, and we are about to move from a working prototype to instruments installed at customers’ sites. The team today is eight full-time and six part-time people. Over 2027 and 2028, we are building that to around thirty. By joining now, you will be one of the people who decide what this company becomes, not someone who inherits it.

Position Overview

Job Description

We are looking for the person who will own the quantum side of our instrument, outright.

You will lead our quantum function: a Quantum Lead, quantum engineers, and part-time specialists, growing over the next eighteen months. You are an experimentalist at heart. We are not looking for someone who manages a lab from a desk. We are looking for the person other physicists go to when something does not work, and nobody can say why. Today that person is our CTO, and your role is to change that. When the quantum work gets stuck, it should stop with you.

You will be joining at the transition point where the instrument moves from lab to customer sites. The physics has to keep improving, and it now also has to withstand contact with the real world. Both halves of that are yours.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Ownership of the Quantum Platform

• 
Own the performance of the NV-diamond measurement chain end to end: optical read-out, microwave control, sensitivity, noise floor and measurement protocols.

• 
Set the technical direction for how we push sensitivity and measurement speed over the next two years.

• 
Make the calls on where the physics effort goes, and be accountable for them.

Hands-on Experimental Work

• 
Spend the majority of your week in the lab, on the instrument, with your hands on it.

• 
Diagnose and fix the problems that have no procedure attached - the ones where the measurement is wrong and nobody yet knows why.

• 
Develop and prove new experimental protocols, rather than reviewing someone else's.

Leading and Building the Quantum Team

• 
Lead the quantum function: our Quantum Lead, quantum engineers and part-time academic specialists, with further hires planned through 2027.

• 
Raise what the team can do unaided. Success looks like fewer problems reaching you over time, not more.

• 
Own hiring for the quantum team as it grows, together with the CTO.

Instruments in the Field

• 
Take technical responsibility for the quantum performance of instruments installed at customer sites.

• 
Support and eventually supervise measurement campaigns at customer locations, so that deployment does not depend on the founders.

• 
Work closely with instrumentation, software and applications colleagues - this instrument only works when all four disciplines agree.

Qualifications & Experience

• 
A PhD in Physics, Quantum Optics, Atomic Physics or a closely related field, followed by substantial further experimental experience in academia or industry.

• 
Deep, sustained, hands-on experimental physics. Years at the bench, building and debugging experiments yourself. This is the single most important qualification and we will test for it.

• 
A demonstrable record of solving unfamiliar, hard experimental problems without supervision. We are interested in what you did when the standard approach failed.

• 
Experience guiding, mentoring or leading other researchers or engineers - formally or informally. You do not need to have held a management title, but you do need to want this half of the job.

• 
An inquisitive and stubborn mindset: willing to question assumptions, including your own, and to keep going after a problem that has already resisted three attempts.

• 
Fluency in Python or MATLAB for research-grade data analysis.

Experience with one or more of the following is a significant advantage:

• 
Cold atoms or trapped ions. Our techniques originate in cold-atom physics rather than in quantum sensing, and we have found that people trained in that tradition tend to carry exactly the debugging instinct this role needs.

• 
Magnetometry, especially with NV centres, and precision measurements.

• 
Microwave electronics and real-time control systems.

• 
Building complex free-space optical systems from components.

• 
Taking a laboratory technique out of the laboratory.

Compensation & Benefits

• 
A competitive salary package.

• 
An attractive warrant package. You will share directly in what you build, and at this stage the share is meaningful.

• 
Relocation support for you and your family, and assistance with the Danish researcher tax scheme, which for qualifying international hires taxes salary at a flat 32.84 percent for up to seven years.

• 
Denmark's quantum ecosystem at your door: DTU Physics, the Niels Bohr Institute and one of Europe's densest concentrations of quantum research.

• 
A small, senior team where decisions are made in a conversation rather than in a process.

USP's for this job

• 
You are the ceiling, not waiting for one. In most companies, the deepest technical authority sits above you, and you work within it. Here you are being hired to become it. The quantum direction of this instrument will be yours.

• 
Lead a team without leaving the lab. Almost every physicist who moves into leadership loses the bench. This role is explicitly designed so that you do not - the leadership comes from being the best experimentalist, not from stopping being one.

• 
Build the Unprecedented: You will be a leading the development and rollout of the most powerful magnetic microscope in the world, directly pushing the boundaries of scientific measurement.

• 
It leaves the building. Our instruments are going into customer laboratories. You will see your work measured by whether it survives in somebody else's fab, which is a rarer and more satisfying test than a paper.

• 
Early enough to matter. Fourteen people today, around thirty by the end of 2028. The people joining now set how this company works.

Company Description

With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit & Assurance, Tax & Legal, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About the team

In Organization and Work Transformation, we help clients achieve their transformation goals through their most valuable asset: their people. Successful transformation relies on defining the right organization, operations, and behaviours, and anchoring changes with employees' collaboration. Our consultants translate transformation agendas into new operating, capability, and governance models. We design and implement strategic change initiatives based on data-driven insights, enhancing organizational performance, productivity, and profitability. If you are passionate about this work and value collaboration, challenging the status quo, and personal development, this position is for you!

Job Description

Join Deloitte's Organization and Work Transformation team as a Consultant and contribute to meaningful change for our clients. We are looking for motivated professionals with experience supporting change management and organizational readiness in ERP and technology implementation programs. As a Consultant, you will work alongside industry experts, utilize advanced methodologies, and help shape the future of organizations. If you are driven by making an impact and excel in a dynamic environment, we encourage you to apply and become a valuable member of our innovative team.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Designing and implementing strategic change initiatives that support successful ERP and other technology transformation programs.

• Conducting stakeholder assessments, change impact assessments, and organizational readiness activities to help clients prepare for and adopt new processes and technologies.

• Developing and delivering communication, engagement, and training initiatives that drive employee adoption and business readiness throughout the transformation lifecycle.

• Supporting program leaders and business stakeholders in navigating organizational change and realizing the expected benefits of ERP implementations.

• Leveraging data-driven insights and adoption metrics to identify risks, inform decision-making, and drive successful change outcomes.

Qualifications

Whether you studied business, psychology, human resource management, political science, strategy, or something completely different, is not the most important factor to us. We are more interested in your strong analytical skills combined with an engaged, structured, and curious personality, as well as your interest in our area of expertise in Organization and Work Transformation.

We expect that you have experience delivering change management activities such as stakeholder engagement, change impact assessments, communications, training, and business readiness within complex transformation programs. In addition, you possess excellent project management and communication skills, both verbal and written, and are motivated by creating lasting value for clients and colleagues. As many of our projects are delivered in Danish organizations and involve close collaboration with local stakeholders, fluency in both Danish and English is required.

What you bring to the team:

• 1-3 years of consulting or change management experience, with experience supporting large-scale business or technology transformation programs.

• SAP change management experience preferred, with an understanding of organizational change and transformation methodologies.

• Experience in stakeholder management, communication planning, training, and user adoption activities.

• Strong presentation, facilitation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work effectively in client-facing environments and collaborate with diverse stakeholder groups.

• Fluency in both Danish and English is required.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, and grade transcript by 01.11.2026. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: 04.01.2027

Please do not hesitate to contact Karoline Gillespy, Senior Consultant at kagillespy@deloitte.dk or Anne Bach-Kristensen, Senior Consultant at annebach@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Opslag 170259 Professor or Associate Professor and Research Group Leader with special focus on molecular mechanisms of diabetes
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen

   

  BRIC wishes to recruit a strongly motivated scientist at Associate Professor or Professor level for an independent research group leader position. We are seeking excellent candidates with ambitious research visions within translational diabetes type 1 or 2 research and a drive to contribute to a diverse and inspiring research environment. The research group leader position is combined with a senior researcher position at the Bartholin Institute, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics, Rigshospitalet, Capital Region. The start date is 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  It is a requirement for the appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the research group leader position and the senior researcher position. In order to be considered, the applicant must send two applications: one to the faculty (the research group leader position) and one to the hospital (the senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the senior researcher position. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at the Hospital. The advertisement for the senior researcher position is available here

  The workplace
 BRIC is an international center of excellence with the mission to perform cutting-edge basic and translational biomedical research in an open environment that fosters interdisciplinarity and collaboration. Active research areas include many aspects of cancer biology, stem cell biology and neurobiology. The center is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. 

  Job description
 As a group leader, you will establish an independent research program within translational diabetes research. Your capacity to integrate research and clinical perspectives is emphasized. In the job, you will be expected to:

   	
• Conduct, publish, and communicate high-quality research that moves the field forward 	
• Engage in outreach and knowledge-sharing with society 	
• Develop your research group through attraction of competitive funding and talent development of team members 	
• Conduct research-based teaching and examination 	
• Be involved in academic assessments 	
• Be involved in local as well as international collaborative and multidisciplinary research projects and engage in core center activities such as talent or technology development to advance BRIC’s research environment and culture   You are also expected to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills and to contribute to developing the research environment and culture at BRIC.

  50 % of the working time is employment at Copenhagen University and will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Director at the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The remaining time will be allocated for other tasks at the Bartholin Institute and the Department of Pathology (e.g. research administration, personnel responsibility, methods establishment and development, grant writing and the establishment of a competitive research group) in agreement with the Head of the Bartholin Institute.

  Candidate profile
 Your background includes a PhD degree, postdoctoral training, and a track record documenting your research experience as reflected in a strong publication record matching your career stage. Also desired is a successful record of attraction of funds, leadership and educational experiences, collaboration experiences and additional capabilities within areas such as outreach or technology transfer activities, again reflecting your career stage.  

  We offer

   	
• Access to cutting edge technologies through core facilities, including high-content screening, flow cytometry, next-gen sequencing, bioinformatics, microscopy, single cell genomics, histology and access to spatial transcriptomics and pathology services. Additional core facilities are available at faculty level. 	
• A vibrant and open scientific community with focus on collegiality, collaboration and creativity.  	
• A focus on talent training and development at all career stages, including strong PhD and postdoc programs. 	
• Strategic support for funding strategizing, grant writing and implementation of larger grants and collaborations and for research communication and outreach. 	
• A package covering the salary of 1-2 group members and technical support equivalent to 50 % of a full-time technical position from the Bartholin Institute. 	
• Administrative support with regards to laboratory services and safety, purchase, economy, HR, and IT. 	
• Additional start support may be obtained from private foundations (obtained at individual or center level).   Terms of employment
 Initial appointment as group leader (Associate Professor) is for 6 years.

  BRIC wants to offer a further career path pending a positive evaluation following transparent guidelines, which include the UCPH criteria for recognizing merit

  This can happen in form of employment in a permanent position based on public advertisement, or the group leader may enter the University of Copenhagen Promotion Program towards a position as full professor (permanent position). Experienced research leaders may be recruited at the level of full professor. 

  The average weekly working hours in the combined position are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Additional information about BRIC can be found on www.bric.ku.dk

  Inquiries are welcome to Director Anders H. Lund bric-director@bric.ku.dk

  Recruitment process
 The recruitment process will contain four evaluation steps: 

   	
• After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager will shortlist applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointment Committee after an evaluation of the written application material. Evaluation criteria can be seen here. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. Due to differences in career stage or institutional background, not all candidates are required to fulfil all requirements in full. 	
• The Vice Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. The selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. 	
• Selected candidates will be evaluated in an online interview with the Appointment committee. The online interviews is expected to be carried out between late January and early February  	
• Selected candidates will be invited for an on-site visit and final evaluation in late February    

  To be qualified for a Professor or Associate Professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion..

  You can read about the recruitment process here: Recruitment process  – University of Copenhagen.

  Application material

   	
• Cover letter outlining the applicant’s motivation to apply to BRIC and brief summaries of research visions (1 page). 	
• Application dossier (10 pages) 	 		
• Research vision/goal and synergy with BRIC 		
• Current and future research plan 		
• Description of five most significant contributions (e.g., scientific, clinical, commercial achievements, honours/awards) 		
• List of funding and commercial income raised incl. information about grant donor, type of grant, amount, and period 		
• Description of leadership experience and development. 		
• Description of organizational activities, including initiatives, responsibilities, and participation in committees and platforms 		
• Teaching portfolio including reflection on teaching and supervision, see guidelines. Selected candidates that do not have the required teaching experience will be given the opportunity to qualify within the first two years of employment. 	 	    	
• CV (2 pages use provided sub-sections) 	
• Diplomas 	
• Complete list of publications/ORCID – please indicate contribution in collaborative papers. Highlight selected publications relevant for research plan and for these include a short description (10 lines) of outcome/impact of the work and your contribution.  	
• Reprints of up to five selected papers (Associate Professor) or ten (Professor) (only published or in press)    

  Please note the level of appointment sought.

  Please note that selected applicants who have applied for either both positions or just the professor position will be assessed for the associate professor position if they are found not-qualified for the professor position.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the Assessment Committee requires further documentation. The Assessment Committee is comprised of employees from both BRIC and Rigshospitalet.
 
 The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 
 
 The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position (see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric)
 
 Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Thursday, 19 November 2026

  BRIC highly values diversity and encourages people of all backgrounds to apply see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric

  The University of Copenhagen International Staff Mobility Office offers assistance and guidance regarding relocation, e.g., housing, spouse program, pension and taxes, as well as on general information on the Danish society, e.g. child-care, healthcare etc. For more information, visit the ISM website:  https://ism.ku.dk/.

Consultant Interventional Cardiologist – PCI On-Call Service

Department of Cardiology, Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

The opportunity
Are you an experienced interventional cardiologist looking to join a highly specialised university hospital with a strong clinical, academic and collaborative environment?

The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is seeking one or more Consultant Interventional Cardiologists from the EU/EØS to join our team. We welcome applications from candidates who are already qualified to participate in a PCI on-call service, as well as experienced PCI operators who are motivated to develop the additional competencies required for on-call duties.

The position is available as soon as possible or by mutual agreement.

This is an opportunity to work in a busy interventional cardiology environment, contribute to the development of specialised cardiac care and collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across cardiology, cardiac surgery and other disciplines.

The position
Your primary clinical responsibilities will be within interventional cardiology, particularly percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary team providing specialised care for patients with ischaemic heart disease, including patients requiring urgent and complex coronary interventions.
Depending on your experience, qualifications and the department's clinical needs, there may also be opportunities to contribute to the development of other specialised interventional services, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.

Alongside your clinical responsibilities, you will contribute to the department's research, teaching and professional development activities, as well as relevant administrative and organisational tasks.

What we offer

• The opportunity to work in a busy university hospital with an established PCI service and a broad range of specialised cardiology services.
• Professional development: Opportunities to further develop your interventional skills and, where appropriate, expand your expertise into complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A strong multidisciplinary team: Close collaboration with cardiologists across subspecialties, cardiothoracic anaesthetists and cardiac surgeons.
• An academic environment: Opportunities to participate in clinical research, teaching and the development of new treatment pathways.
• Supportive colleagues and leadership: We value professional respect, constructive collaboration and a positive working environment.
• Flexible working arrangements: Working hours and duty schedules are organised within the applicable employment framework.
• An international perspective: The opportunity to join a university hospital committed to clinical excellence, research, education and continuous improvement.
Qualifications and experience
Essential requirements

• You hold specialist certification in cardiology.
• You have or are able to obtain a Danish Authorization to practice medicine
• You are fluent in or command a professional working proficiency in Danish. Norwegian or Swedish (B2/C1 level)
• Or are willing to learn Danish
• You can perform PCI procedures independently.
• You have the clinical judgement and professional skills required to manage patients with ischaemic heart disease.
• You communicate effectively and work constructively with colleagues across clinical disciplines.
• You can maintain an overview and make sound clinical decisions in a demanding and sometimes unpredictable environment.
• You are committed to high standards of patient care, patient safety and continuous professional development.
• You are willing to contribute to the department's clinical, organisational and educational activities and to take on the leadership and supervisory responsibilities associated with a consultant position.
Desirable qualifications

• Experience participating in a PCI on-call service.
• Experience from a university hospital or another highly specialised cardiac centre.
• Experience in complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A PhD, or other research qualifications or a strong record of scientific publications.
• Experience in clinical research, teaching or quality improvement.
• Experience in a PCI on-call service is an advantage but is not essential, provided you are an independent PCI operator and are motivated to acquire the necessary competencies following an appropriate period of training and induction.
About the Department
The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is a large, specialised and research-active department providing advanced care across a broad range of cardiovascular conditions, including ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, valvular heart disease, thoracic aortic aneurysms, pericardial diseases, thromboembolic disorders and dyslipidaemia.

Our department performs approximately:

• 6,000 invasive procedures annually
• 8,000 inpatient admissions annually
• More than 30,000 outpatient consultations annually
• Approximately 14,000 echocardiographic examinations annually
Our medical team comprises doctors at different stages of postgraduate training and 32 consultant cardiologists, including two professors.
We provide inpatient and outpatient services, operate a cardiac catheterisation laboratory and maintain a dedicated cardiology research unit.
Our work is guided by a shared commitment to clinical excellence, patient safety and involving patients and their families in shared decision-making. We also have a strong responsibility for undergraduate medical education and postgraduate specialist training.
The department operates across three hospital sites in Aalborg, Thisted and Hobro, with the vast majority of clinical activity based at the newly built Aalborg University Hospital.

Salary and terms of employment
This is a full-time position. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement.
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.
Further details regarding the on-call arrangement and employment conditions can be discussed with the Head of Department or Lead Senior Physician Bent Raungaard tlf. 27201096, e-mail: b.raungaard@rn.dk
 
Application
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and interviews will be arranged continuously. The advertisement will be withdrawn once the position has been filled.
Please submit your application by email to:
Ljubica Vukelic Andersen
Head of Department of Cardiology
Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark
Email: ljubica.andersen@rn.dk
Telephone: +45 30 38 25 10

Please include:

• Curriculum Vitae (CV).
• Letter of motivation
• Proof of specialist certification in cardiology.
• List of publications, if applicable.
The assessment process will follow the applicable Danish requirements for consultant appointments, including assessment of competencies across the seven physician roles.

_Are you technically curious, service-minded, and motivated by helping customers resolve critical technical issues? Do you enjoy combining troubleshooting with coordination and clear communication? If so, this could be your next career opportunity.

**Your position

**As our new Senior Support Specialist, Telecom, you will support the daily operation of our customers communication Systems. You will take ownership of incoming requests, gather the necessary technical information, assess urgency and operational impact, and perform structured troubleshooting. When specialist assistance is required, you will coordinate the correct escalation and ensure that customers remain informed throughout the process.

You are not expected to be the specialist for every system. Your role is to establish a clear overview, perform the agreed initial checks, document findings and decisions, and ensure that each case is resolved.

Your place of work will be at our Global HQ located in Esbjerg in a full-time position. You must be willing and able to participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation according to an agreed schedule.

**Your Tasks & Responsibilities

**Your work will include receiving customer calls and service requests, monitoring tickets and alarms, carrying out remote troubleshooting, and coordinating technical responses. You will maintain technical records, contribute to service reporting and preventive-maintenance activities, and help improve service procedures and documentation.

**Your Tasks Will Include But Are Not Limited To

**

• Manage service tickets from initial request through resolution.

• Perform troubleshooting and monitor systems through Zabbix or comparable platforms

• Keep customers informed and ensure that technical findings, communication, and agreed actions are documented accurately

**Your Profile & Qualifications
