jobs.occupation: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
jobs.description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (copy of original and an official English translation).  

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is 31 December, 2026, at 11:59 PM / 23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process. 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is 1 March 2026 (may be adjusted by mutual agreement) or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Tax Professional, Customer Handling, Securities Tax Services (Copenhagen)
jobs.description:
**Job Description

**Are you customer-focused, structured and motivated by working in an operational area where quality, documentation and service delivery are key? Do you enjoy supporting customers and advisers, coordinating with internal stakeholders and ensuring that processes run efficiently from start to finish?

We are looking for a detail-oriented colleague to join our Customer Handling Team/Tax Services team in Copenhagen. The team serves as a primary point of contact for advisers and customers and plays an important role in onboarding, documentation management, customer support and service delivery related to securities tax services.

On clients’ behalf, Danske Bank applies for a reduction in foreign tax on returns from securities held in customers’ custody accounts. This includes relief of foreign dividend and interest tax, either at source or through tax reclaim processes. The service is complementary to Danske Bank’s custody service and is particularly relevant for clients earning income on foreign financial instruments, where a tax reduction may be available under applicable double taxation agreements.

**About Securities Tax Services

**Securities Tax Services is part of Danske Bank’s tax area and is responsible for handling services related to withholding tax on securities. The area consists of several teams located in Denmark and Lithuania, working closely together across locations, functions and customer segments.

You will join a team of skilled specialists who support corporate, institutional and other customer segments. We value collaboration, curiosity, continuous learning and a strong focus on delivering high-quality service in a well-controlled environment.

**Your role

**As a team member in Customer Handling, you will support customers and advisers with inquiries, documentation and service-related matters. You will help ensure that customer agreements, onboarding, offboarding and service changes are handled correctly and efficiently.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Acting as a first point of contact for customer and adviser inquiries

• Handling customer onboarding and offboarding activities

• Ensuring customer agreements and service documentation are sent, received and registered correctly

• Collecting, reviewing and maintaining required customer documentation

• Supporting changes to customer preferences and service setups

• Following up with customers and advisers on outstanding documentation and requests

• Coordinating with internal stakeholders to ensure efficient service delivery

• Participating in client meetings and supporting customer relationship management

• Maintaining and updating information in internal systems

• Supporting controls to ensure accurate and compliant processing

• Contributing to continuous improvement of customer processes and service quality

The role combines recurring operational tasks with customer interaction and collaboration across teams. You will get exposure to securities services, withholding tax processes, custody-related services and post-trade operations.

**About You

**We are looking for a structured and service-minded colleague who enjoys working with customers, documentation and operational processes. You take ownership of tasks, communicate clearly and can manage several activities while maintaining attention to detail.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience from customer service, client support, operations, financial services or a similar area

• Have a customer-centric mindset and strong communication skills

• Are comfortable working with documentation, regulations and operational processes

• Can manage multiple tasks while maintaining high accuracy

• Collaborate well with colleagues and stakeholders across teams and locations

• Are proactive, curious and willing to learn in a complex environment

• Have strong English skills, both written and spoken

Experience from Asset Services, post-trade operations, custody services or withholding tax is considered an advantage.

**What We Offer You

**You will join a supportive team environment where you can develop your expertise through varied work and mentorship opportunities. We operate a hybrid working model with 3 to 4 days per week in the office to promote collaboration and knowledge sharing. Your career will progress through exposure to diverse tax challenges and continuous learning opportunities.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**We would be delighted to hear from you if this opportunity aligns with your career aspirations. Please reach out to our hiring manager Nicolai William Schou Hansen at nicoh@danskebank.dk for any questions about the role. We look forward to hearing from you!

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

**Founders Associate (Part-Time, min. 24 h/week)

Company: Levitate Technology ApS

Location: Copenhagen/Herlev

Start: As soon as possible

****About Us

**Levitate Technology is a fast-growing Danish startup that makes sports and everyday prosthetics for amputees. Our mission is to give amputees better lives through innovative, affordable products. We're growing internationally, and we're looking for a Founders Associate to work closely with our Founder & CEO and keep the company running smoothly.

**The Role

**Your job is to keep things moving. You'll be the link between management, our team, and a wide range of external partners. You will take part in Management meetings, own key business processes and administer the systems the company runs on. You'll also support the CEO on strategic topics that shape where Levitate goes next. The role is broad and varied, with real responsibility from day one.

**What You'll Be Part Of

**

• Company building: helping build the processes and structures that support Levitate's growth.

• Board meetings: helping prepare board materials and following decisions through, with a close view of strategic decision-making.

• Funding and investor relations: supporting funding rounds and investor communication.

**Responsibilities

**

• Stakeholder communication: Be the main point of contact for a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. This includes our external finance team, our bank, our insurance provider, and other partners.

• Strategic projects: Support the CEO on strategic initiatives. This means preparing analyses, following up on company KPIs, and turning information into clear input for management and board decisions.

• Systems administration: Act as admin for our company tools, including Shopify, Google Workspace, Slack, Claude and the rest of our stack. You'll manage users, access and permissions, and keep things organised.

• HR and people operations: Support hiring, payroll, onboarding and offboarding, and day-to-day people operations. You'll work closely with management and external partners.

• Meeting support: Organise and prepare internal and board meetings. This covers agendas, slides, minutes and follow-ups.

• Documentation: Prepare documents, reports and presentations.

• Confidentiality: Handle sensitive company, financial and employee information with discretion.

**Who You Are

**

• Enrolled in a relevant degree with at least one year of studies remaining, preferably a master's programme at Copenhagen Business School.

• Relevant experience from a similar role, a startup, or a management support function.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

• Structured and reliable, with strong attention to detail.

• Analytical, with an interest in strategy and how a company grows.

• Comfortable juggling many topics and stakeholders at once, and able to take ownership without being told every step.

• Confident with digital tools and quick to learn new systems.

**Practical Information

**

• Start date: As soon as possible.

• Hours: minimum of 24 hours per week, flexible around your studies.

• Location: Our office in Herlev, with the option to work from home. You'll be at the office at least 3 days a week.

**What We Offer

**

• A competitive part-time salary.

• Direct collaboration with the Founder & CEO, with insight into strategy, board work and fundraising.

• Real responsibility and a broad view across finance, HR, operations and systems.

• A mission-driven, international team.

• Flexibility to balance work with your studies.

**How To Apply

**Apply through The Hub with your CV and a short motivation statement explaining why this role suits you. We review applications on a rolling basis.

Levitate Technology ApS is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to an inclusive workplace.

**Job Description

**SOUNDBOKS is an innovative tech company and aspiring lifestyle brand. You may have seen us at a music festival, street party, or your friend’s celebration (think: private events combining festival-grade sound with beat-enhancing lights) where special moments are turned into memories. We create the loudest, most durable, and arguably coolest Bluetooth speakers and audio reactive lights on the market.

At SOUNDBOKS, trust and community go hand in hand. People are encouraged to take ownership of their work while knowing they have the support of the team behind them. Voices are heard, ideas are welcomed, and collaboration is what pushes us forward.

This is more than a job - it’s a community where people care about each other, celebrate together, and share the energy of creating something meaningful. Life at SOUNDBOKS is bold, fast, and full of passion - for the product, for the mission, and for showing up as your true self. With 70 team members, this is a place where you can do your best work and truly belong.

ROLE AUDIO ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

HOURS FULL TIME

LOCATION COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

START DATE OCTOBER 2026 or ASAP

The Product Development team at SOUNDBOKS is the group responsible for the exciting product journey, taking every step of the development process toward and into mass production. In it’s heartbeat you’ll find collaborative and self-driven team members with a large cross-discipline understanding tied to ownership. They are there to make a difference - for the products, the team and the SOUNDBOKS customers as a whole.

As our Audio Engineer, you'll explore new ways to improve the audio experience across SOUNDBOKS products by combining signal processing, system simulation, and engineering insight. Working closely with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams, you'll help shape the technologies behind our next generation of speakers.

Okay, let’s make things a little more concrete. Here’s what we expect your daily life to look like:

**Audio System Development

**

• Develop audio concepts and proof-of-concepts at a system level.

• Explore new approaches to improve audio performance across products.

• Collaborate with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams during concept development.

**Signal Processing & Simulation

**

• Perform advanced signal processing simulations with a focus on sound pressure level (SPL), sound quality, and system efficiency.

• Simulate the interaction between acoustics, amplifiers, electronics, and battery performance.

• Evaluate and develop signal processing algorithms to improve overall product audio performance.

**System Performance & Collaboration

**

• Work closely across the entire Product Development team in order to evolve and improve the audio performance across our future product portfolio.

• Apply signal processing methodologies to improve sound pressure, sound quality, and battery performance.

**Job Requirements

****In order to become a success in this role, we believe that your profile should be aligned with the bullets listed below. However, we acknowledge that success can take many forms, so please do apply even if you don’t tick all the boxes.

**

• You hold a BSc or higher in Audio Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Acoustics, or a related engineering field.

• You've designed and simulated audio systems, ideally loudspeakers, and know your way around signal processing for audio.

• You're comfortable using simulations and measurements to test ideas, challenge assumptions, and make better engineering decisions.

• It’ll be considered a plus if you have experience working with loudspeaker design, transducers, enclosure design, or audio electronics.

• You get excited by solving difficult audio problems and finding smarter ways to improve performance.

• You're naturally curious, love experimenting, and enjoy digging into the details until things sound and work better.

• You take ownership of your work and enjoy bouncing ideas around with people who know more than you in their field.

• You're drawn to what SOUNDBOKS is building and are excited to be a part of the journey!

Intrigued? At SOUNDBOKS you’ll find yourself a part of a community. We realize that growth is a process and we don’t expect you to go through it alone. Actually, we guarantee that you won’t have to. We work together in order to work smarter, we inspire each other to be better, and we never forget that every member of the team is responsible for our success.

So, if you’re tired of all of the noise in the job market, we’d love to hear from you. This may be the coolest job you ever have.

jobs.description:
HSO International – Project Manager

Position: Project Manager

Department: Program Services

Visa Sponsorship: You must have legal working rights in your country of residence within the EMEA region. Sponsorship and relocation only available within the Netherlands

Type of work: Remote or Hybrid, depending on location

International travel is required depending on program needs. **Minimun 35% travelling

****About The Role

**The Project Manager at HSO is accountable for the successful delivery of a defined project or major workstream within a broader transformation program. This role owns delivery outcomes within clear boundaries: scope, schedule, quality, readiness, and customer adoption for their project.

In this role, your primary focus is on driving execution excellence. You spend most of your time on detailed planning, sequencing, dependency management, readiness control (testing, data, cutover), issue resolution, and day-to-day delivery leadership. You optimize outcomes within given constraints and ensure that delivery reality is visible early.

If you want a role where you own the execution layer of large or complex global programs and make a direct impact on delivery success, this is it.

**Leading Microsoft Partner

**HSO belongs to the elite Microsoft Dynamics Inner Circle for 21 years, within the top 1% of all Microsoft partners worldwide. With over 2,800 professionals and a worldwide presence, we deliver successful implementations across industries globally.

**HSO International

**At HSO International, you’ll join a diverse team of 300+ colleagues from 50+ nationalities, working on cross-border projects that make a global impact.

Learn more about Life at HSO International: https://www.hso.com/en/campaigns/life-at-hso-international/

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own day-to-day delivery of assigned projects or complex program workstreams, ensuring scope, plan, dependencies, and customer readiness remain aligned

• Participate in pre-sales and mobilization by shaping delivery plans, budgets, governance models, and risk assumptions that are executable in practice

• Contribute to and co-author Statements of Work (SOW), with specific accountability for assumptions, risks, delivery economics, team structures, phase entry/exit criteria, and change control

• Build and maintain integrated delivery plans that align architecture, build, testing, integrations, and customer activities

• Coordinate cross-functional delivery across architects, developers, functional consultants, testers, integration teams, and customer SMEs

• Monitor requirements gathering and setting acceptance criteria, ensure backlog items are sized, prioritized, and ready for build

• Drive testing readiness, including test planning, data availability, environment coordination, defect management, and go-live preparation

• Maintain strong RAID discipline, proactively identifying risks, issues, dependencies, and downstream impacts

• Identify scope gaps early and initiate structured change-control discussions when required

• Run governance forums that drive real decisions, including steering committees, risk reviews, and change control boards

• Communicate clear, factual status and risk updates to customers, senior project managers, and program leadership

• Partner with customers to strengthen their ability to participate effectively in requirements, testing, data readiness, and decision-making

• Contribute to continuous improvement of HSO’s Standard Working Practices (SWP) and delivery quality culture

• Depending on seniority and complexity of an assigned project, you will work under the guidance and direction of a Senior Project Manager or Program Manager.

**Requirements

**

• 3–5+ year’s experience delivering ERP. Data, or digital transformation projects experience is preferable into ERP Implementation experience

• Must exposure to Dynamics 365 ERP experience or comparable enterprise platforms

• Experience in complex, multi-team or multi-stakeholder environments

• Strong grounding in planning, backlog management, requirements clarification, testing preparation, and RAID (Risks, Actions, Issues, and Decisions)

• Experience working within structured delivery frameworks and governance models

• Ability to see and manage task-level delays and manage their downstream impacts

• Ability to simplify complexity and drive clarity in pressured environments

• Experience using DevOps or similar delivery management tools.

• Hands-on, structured, and proactive approach to execution and problem solving.

• Confidence to escalate issues factually and early

• Influence without authority; create clarity and accountability through facts, options, and trade-offs

• Structured approach to risk management, ambiguity, and scenario-based decision-making

• Awareness of delivery economics and commercial impact

• Ability to balance scope, quality, time, and cost without false certainty

• International travel required depending on program needs. Minimun 35% travelling

**Benefits

**Career Path for this role

**Project Coordinator / PMO → Project Manager → Senior Project Manager → Program Manager.

Project Managers grow by mastering execution discipline, customer leadership, and cross-team coordination within global transformation programs.

**_Fun and success

_**You work in a collaborative and professional environment where success is built on teamwork and with colleagues who are ready to help each other.

**_International project exposure

_**Joining our team offers an exciting opportunity to engage in international projects, providing invaluable exposure to diverse cultures, markets, and perspectives. Through your involvement in these projects, you will broaden your global network, enhance your cross-cultural communication skills, and gain firsthand experience in navigating the complexities of international collaboration.

**_Freedom and responsibility

_**You have the freedom and flexibility to organize your workdays, but especially to shape your own career.

**Take the next step!

**Does the combination of business processes and Microsoft technology appeal to you? Take the next step in your career path with HSO International!

Drive business development and secure major EPC projects in the global energy sector.

BWSC – Ever better energy!

Join us in our mission to power the world with reliable, efficient energy, and help shape the future of power generation. 

BWSC is re-establishing our footprint in the EPC market for engine-based power plants, building on a long track record as a turnkey EPC contractor for customers around the world. jobs.occupation: Senior Hardware Productization Engineer / Mechatronics Lead
jobs.description:
The role

We are looking for a senior hardware/product development engineer with strong experience taking physical products from prototype through engineering validation and into manufacturing.

You will work directly with the founder and take ownership of the physical architecture of Dreamspire.

This is not primarily a firmware role and it is not a pure industrial-design role.

We need someone who can look at a prototype and systematically turn it into a product.

You should be comfortable moving between:

• mechanical engineering

• electronics integration

• manufacturing

• prototyping

• reliability

• assembly

• suppliers

• cost

• compliance

• user experience

A large part of the work will initially be hands-on.

Your first mission

Your first objective will be to create a clear Dreamspire Product Architecture V1.

You will examine the existing prototype, identify its weaknesses and determine how we should build the next generation of the system.

This includes answering questions such as:

• Which prototype mechanisms are suitable for a real product?

• What needs to be redesigned?

• Which components should be custom versus off-the-shelf?

• How should cameras, lighting, electronics and mechanical systems be integrated?

• How do we make assembly simple and repeatable?

• What are the major reliability risks?

• What manufacturing processes should we use?

• What should the production BOM look like?

• What needs tooling?

• What can initially be produced in low volume?

• What compliance and certification work will be required?

• How do we move from one prototype to 10, 100 and eventually thousands of units?

The objective is not to rush into manufacturing.

The objective is to progressively remove technical and manufacturing risk until the product is ready.

Responsibilities

You will:

• Audit the existing Dreamspire hardware and mechanical architecture.

• Design and build improved prototype generations.

• Own mechanical design and product engineering.

• Integrate cameras, PCBs, lighting, power, cabling, connectors and sensors into the physical product.

• Design enclosures, mounts, mechanisms and structural components.

• Define tolerances and mechanical interfaces.

• Design for manufacturing and assembly — DFM/DFA.

• Reduce part count, assembly complexity and manufacturing cost.

• Select appropriate materials and production methods.

• Decide when to use CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding or other processes.

• Work with PCB/electronics engineers where specialist electrical work is required.

• Develop production BOMs and cost estimates.

• Source and evaluate components and suppliers.

• Communicate directly with prototype houses and manufacturers.

• Design test fixtures and production test procedures.

• Establish reliability and lifecycle testing.

• Help define EVT, DVT and PVT stages.

• Identify CE, EMC, electrical safety and other relevant compliance requirements.

• Help design the system for serviceability and repair.

• Help prepare Dreamspire for small pilot production and eventually mass production.

What we are looking for

The most important requirement is:

You have personally helped ship real physical products.

Ideally, you have taken products through several stages of:

prototype → engineering validation → manufacturing → production → customer

You should have strong practical experience with several of the following:

• Mechanical engineering

• Mechatronics

• Consumer electronics

• Product development

• DFM / DFA

• CAD

• Injection-molded plastic parts

• CNC and rapid prototyping

• Electronics packaging

• PCB integration

• Cameras / optical systems

• Sensors

• Motors or electromechanical systems

• Tolerance analysis

• Supplier management

• BOM optimization

• Production testing

• Reliability testing

• Manufacturing ramp-up

You should be comfortable physically building, modifying and debugging prototypes rather than only designing them.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

Experience from products such as these would be especially relevant:

• Consumer electronics

• Robotics

• Smart-home products

• Interactive toys

• Gaming hardware

• IoT products

• Camera systems

• Medical or laboratory devices

• Small electromechanical products

Experience working in a startup or small product-development team is a major advantage.

What we are not looking for

This is probably not the right role if your experience is primarily:

• Arduino hobby projects

• Pure firmware development

• PCB design without product/mechanical ownership

• Industrial design without engineering responsibility

• CAD work without manufacturing experience

• Large-company engineering where manufacturing and suppliers were handled entirely by other teams

We are looking for someone who understands the whole physical product.

How you work

You should enjoy environments where the product is still evolving.

You should be able to say:

“This prototype mechanism works, but it will not survive production.”

or:

“We can remove these five components if we redesign this assembly.”

or:

“Don’t spend money tooling this yet — we need to validate this part first.”

We want someone who challenges assumptions and prevents expensive mistakes rather than simply implementing specifications.

Working with the founder

You will work closely with the founder, who currently develops the software, computer-vision systems, embedded systems and game concepts.

You will therefore have considerable influence over the architecture of the product.

The expectation is that you become the technical owner of the physical Dreamspire platform, while working closely with software and game development.

If the collaboration works well, the role could evolve into something resembling:

Head of Hardware / Head of Product Engineering

as Dreamspire grows.

Location

The role is based around Copenhagen.

Much of the work can be done remotely, but during prototype development we expect regular hands-on work with the physical Dreamspire system.

Candidates elsewhere in Denmark or the Øresund region are welcome if they can work regularly in Copenhagen.

Employment

We are open to:

• Full-time employment

• 3–4 days/week

• An initial senior consulting/fractional arrangement that can develop into a permanent role

For a strong permanent candidate, expected salary is approximately:

65,000–75,000 DKK/month + pension, depending on experience.

Exceptional candidates with significant consumer-product leadership experience may be above this range.

Why this role is interesting

Dreamspire is not another incremental electronics product.

The aim is to create an entirely new category of tabletop gaming platform and then build multiple games on top of it.

The fundamental question is:

Can we create something with the physical presence and social experience of a board game, but with systems and mechanics that were previously only practical in video games?

A large part of whether that succeeds depends on making the hardware disappear into the experience.

That is the problem we want you to help solve.

How to apply

Email jobs@dreamspire.dk with your CV and a few lines about the physical products you have helped ship. We read every application and use it only to assess it; see how we handle your data.

SOUNDBOKS is an innovative tech company and aspiring lifestyle brand. You may have seen us at a music festival, street party, or your friend’s celebration (think: private events combining festival-grade sound with beat-enhancing lights) where special moments are turned into memories. We create the loudest, most durable, and arguably coolest Bluetooth speakers and audio reactive lights on the market.

At SOUNDBOKS, trust and community go hand in hand. People are encouraged to take ownership of their work while knowing they have the support of the team behind them. Voices are heard, ideas are welcomed, and collaboration is what pushes us forward.

This is more than a job - it’s a community where people care about each other, celebrate together, and share the energy of creating something meaningful. Life at SOUNDBOKS is bold, fast, and full of passion - for the product, for the mission, and for showing up as your true self. With 70 team members, this is a place where you can do your best work and truly belong.

ROLE ACOUSTIC ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

HOURS FULL TIME

LOCATION COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

START DATE OCTOBER 2026 or ASAP

The Product Development team at SOUNDBOKS is the group responsible for the exciting product journey, taking every step of the development process toward and into mass production. In it’s heartbeat you’ll find collaborative and self-driven team members with a large cross-discipline understanding tied to ownership. They are there to make a difference - for the products, the team and the SOUNDBOKS customers as a whole.

Every SOUNDBOKS starts with a great idea - but turning it into a speaker that can survive a festival, run for hours, and sound incredible takes a lot of engineering. As the Acoustic Engineer, you'll be taking charge of the acoustic development that helps bring those products to life.

Okay, let’s make things a little more concrete. Here’s what we expect your daily life to look like:

**Concept & Prototype Development

**

• You'll select and design acoustic components based on product and market requirements.

• You'll define initial enclosure concepts.

• You'll build and evaluate proof-of-concept prototypes to validate acoustic concepts.

• You'll collaborate with Mechanical Engineering during the early product development phase to mature acoustic concepts.

**Simulation & Validation

**

• You'll perform acoustic simulations with a focus on sound pressure level (SPL), sound quality, and system efficiency.

• You'll validate simulation results through physical testing.

• You'll collaborate with suppliers to refine acoustic components based on simulation and test results.

**Driver Specification & Verification

**

• You'll own the technical specification of loudspeaker drivers towards suppliers.

• You'll define driver specifications and tolerances.

• You'll support manufacturing verification with suppliers.

• You'll participate in the acoustic verification of the final product towards mass production.

• You'll collaborate with the Audio team on audio signal handling, including crossovers, compressors, and limiters.

**In order to become a success in this role, we believe that your profile should be aligned with the bullets listed below. However, we acknowledge that success can take many forms, so please do apply even if you don’t tick all the boxes.

**

• You have proven experience designing and simulating loudspeakers, including transducer design and specification, enclosure design, and acoustic measurements.

• You hold a BSc or higher in Audio, Acoustics, Mechanical, or a related engineering discipline.

• You've done loudspeaker simulation and measurements, and use both to validate and refine your designs.

• You've worked with loudspeaker development from concept through verification and ideally have experience collaborating with external manufacturing partners.

• Familiarity with crossover design, FEM simulations, or failure analysis is an advantage.

• Ideally you also have experience building physical speaker mock-ups or collaborating with large-scale loudspeaker manufacturing partners.

• You work independently, take ownership of your area, and enjoy collaborating closely with engineers across disciplines.

• You're curious, creative, and constantly looking for ways to improve acoustic performance.

• You're drawn to what SOUNDBOKS is building and are excited to be a part of the journey!

Intrigued? At SOUNDBOKS you’ll find yourself a part of a community. We realize that growth is a process and we don’t expect you to go through it alone. Actually, we guarantee that you won’t have to. We work together in order to work smarter, we inspire each other to be better, and we never forget that every member of the team is responsible for our success.

So, if you’re tired of all of the noise in the job market, we’d love to hear from you. This may be the coolest job you ever have!

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Reality Capture for Digital Twinning of Built Structures - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
The aim of this project is to develop technologies for creating building information models of existing built structures. This is part of a larger goal of using digital techniques to support sustainability in construction - specifically by making it easier to repurpose buildings.

Responsibilities
You will work within the area of visual computing. Much of the work will be based on machine learning and in particular vision language models. The use of generative methods will be central to your research whose overarching goal is to study how it is possible to extract information about a construction from photographs and other data sources and generate a precise building information model with little or no user input.

You will be affiliated with CEBE (Civil Engineering and the green transition in the Built Environment) which is a Danish cross-university research programme focusing on the sustainable development of the built environment. CEBE’s vision is to promote science-based circular, low-carbon and resilient built environment within planetary boundaries. CEBE is supported by the Villum Foundation.

You will be matriculated at the DTU Compute PhD School, employed at DTU Compute, and embedded in the Section for Visual Computing. The Section for Visual Computing is focused on medical image analysis, geometry and appearance modelling, computer vision, multivariate statistics for images and analysis of 3D microstructures. Within these areas, our overarching research aim is to make methodological contributions of broad applicability but motivated by applications.

Qualifications
To qualify for this position, you must have a background in visual computing (computer graphics and computer vision), a good understanding of the basics of computer-aided design and machine learning. These qualifications must be underpinned by a strong background in applied mathematics. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Andreas Bærentzen, janba@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 3 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• 
A letter motivating the application (cover letter)

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute
DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Moiré and Patterned 2D Materials for Bandgap Engineering - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
If you want to design the electronic properties of a material rather than simply measure them, this PhD puts the tools in your hands. When two-dimensional crystals are stacked with a controlled twist, or when a periodic pattern is imprinted into them, an artificial superlattice emerges in which the band structure can be reshaped and bandgaps opened by design, using a novel combination of 2D materials and freestanding oxide membranes. 

You will create such materials yourself in a group that has worked with 2D materials for two decades and with full access to the cleanroom and microscopy infrastructure at DTU Nanolab. The project is part of METRIQS and is carried out together with national and international partners.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to create and control superlattices in graphene and other 2D materials, and to establish how the engineered structure translates into an engineered electronic band structure. You will pursue two complementary routes: assembling hybrid van der Waals heterostructures in which the moiré periodicity is set by twist angle and lattice mismatch and imprinting periodic patterns directly into the 2D material or its supporting layers by nanofabrication. Both routes call for careful design, reproducible processing and close comparison between intended and realised structure. You will work with colleagues at DTU Physics and DTU Nanolab and with partners in the METRIQS collaboration. 

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Design superlattice geometries and device layouts, using modelling and simulation to decide what is worth fabricating.
• Assemble hybrid van der Waals heterostructures from graphene, hBN, transition metal dichalcogenides and related materials with controlled twist and alignment, using a newly developed semi-automatic stacking system, and collect data on stacking recipes and results to obtain and document optimal parameters through datamining and statistics. 
• Imprint periodic patterns into 2D materials and their supporting layers using electron beam lithography, etching, thin film deposition and related nanofabrication.
• Fabricate devices in which the engineered materials can be contacted, gated and measured.
• Characterise structure and electronic properties by scanning probe microscopies, electron microscopies, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy and electrical transport at cryogenic temperatures. 
• Connect the measured electronic response back to the intended superlattice design, and iterate on the design.
• Establish reproducible fabrication and measurement protocols, analyse your data and present the results in publications and at conferences.
We are looking for a candidate with a background in physics, nanotechnology, materials science, electrical engineering or a related field. You should have hands-on experience with micro- or nanofabrication or comparable experimental laboratory work, and be comfortable with systematic work, data analysis and programming for design, automation or modelling. Experience with 2D materials, layout and CAD design, electron microscopy or electronic transport is an advantage, but the project spans several techniques, and we do not expect you to bring all of them with you. We value curiosity, persistence and the ambition to take ownership of your own project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Peter Bøggild and Timothy John Booth. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is 1 January 2027, or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Professor Peter Bøggild, pbog@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Physics and DTU Nanolab at https://physics.dtu.dk/ and www.nanolab.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 1 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Physics conducts research across a broad range of fundamental and applied physics. The position will be based in the department's 2D Materials Physics and Engineering section (2DPHYS), where we study the synthesis, fabrication and physical properties of atomically thin materials and heterostructures, including also hybrid heterostructures. The project makes extensive use of the nanofabrication and characterisation facilities at DTU Nanolab and involves close collaboration with national and international research partners in METRIQS.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced financial-crime leader to be our registered MLRO / Hvidvaskansvarlig (HVL § 7, stk. 2) for Monta Pay ApS under our EMI license and to lead Financial Crime Prevention (FCP) across Monta, group-wide for the Danish/EEA EMI plus UK and US compliance as those markets scale. The role is registered with Finanstilsynet, so the appointment is subject to a fit & proper assessment as a change of key function holder.

Monta Pay ApS holds an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license, granted by Finanstilsynet in April 2026. We are now migrating our financial services from Monta ApS to Monta Pay ApS, with go-live planned for Q2 2027. This is the moment the AML/FCP framework moves from build to live operation, and you will own it.

This is a high-profile, senior role. You sit at the centre of our financial-services compliance strategy as we scale, "directly exposed to the fire." You must balance obligations against resources with a risk-based approach, communicate complex issues clearly to senior leaders and the Board, and run your work-streams with strong, solution-oriented project management. In return, you have an outsized impact on how Monta builds and operates financial services compliance, and direct exposure to decision-making at a fast-growing scale-up.

You report day to day to Nick Skovsen, COO of Monta Pay ApS, with direct, independent access to the CEO and executive management of Monta Pay ApS and to its Board and Governance, Risk & Compliance Committee.

Key responsibilities

• 
Registered MLRO / Hvidvaskansvarlig: Act as the statutory AML-responsible person for Monta Pay under the EMI license. Approve AML/CTF policies and high-risk customer relationships escalated by the first line (PEPs, and business involving high-risk third countries). Receive internal escalations, decide on and file SARs/STRs with the FIU, and be the primary AML contact for Finanstilsynet.

• 
Own the Financial Crime Prevention framework: Steward Monta's FCP model (our nine-pillar "FC9" framework) covering AML/CFT, sanctions, fraud, and anti-bribery & corruption. Propose the risk appetite and risk-based approach for Board approval and monitor against it, and keep the framework effective and proportionate to our activities, customer types (B2B & B2C), and transaction flows.

• 
Fraud, transaction monitoring & customer due diligence: Own the frameworks for fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, and KYC/KYB (CDD/EDD, PEP and sanctions screening) across onboarding and the lifecycle (EU and US). Set the rules, thresholds and procedures the Financial Operations team runs in the first line, and assure their quality and effectiveness.

• 
Sanctions & screening: Set the screening standards (lists, thresholds, re-screening frequency) and assure the quality of first-line alert handling.

• 
Policy suite, risk assessment & governance: Maintain the AML/CFT policy suite in the Centralised Policy Register (with version control and Board-approval tracking), and own the Business-Wide Risk Assessment (BWRA) and the AML risk assessment underpinning the framework.

• 
Regulatory reporting: Deliver AML and payments regulatory reporting (for example Section 99 Payment Act, KPSD, AML/CTF returns) and ensure CESOP readiness.

• 
Technology, controls & assurance: Work with Product and Engineering on case management, screening and monitoring tooling and AI/automation, oversee AML-relevant third parties, and run the internal-controls framework (monitoring, QA, remediation).

• 
Training, culture & Board liaison: Build AML/FCP training and a strong compliance culture, and advise Senior Management and the Board GRC Committee on financial-crime risk, regulatory change, and performance.

• 
Build and lead the team: Build out and lead the second-line FCP/AML team as volumes grow post go-live.

What You’ll Walk Into (first 6 to 12 months)

• 
The foundations are in place; the job is to make them operational for go-live.

• 
On AML: everything required to obtain the EMI license has been submitted and approved. The remaining gap is operational readiness, and that is the focus: embedding the framework in day-to-day operations and rolling it out with our customers and with colleagues across Monta.

• 
On FCP: This role brings centralised ownership and direction, consolidating what already exists, formalising it into clear Standard Operating Procedures, and training the relevant teams on them ahead of go-live.

• 
Concrete early priorities include standing up transaction monitoring and fraud detection, locking v1.0 of the policy suite (Sanctions, PEP, EDD, Outsourcing, and the Sanction-Screening and SAR/STR filing SOPs) into the Centralised Policy Register, building the regulatory-reporting data structure and CESOP readiness, finalising KYC/KYB (EU + US), and securing your Finanstilsynet fit & proper approval ahead of go-live. A structured focus-areas plan accompanies this role.

Requirements

• 
Minimum 3 years (ideally 5+, given this is a registered key-function role) of relevant experience in the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, ideally in a licensed EMI, payment institution, bank, or regulated fintech. Comparable experience in public authorities, AML consulting, or other AML-regulated sectors (for example gaming/gambling) will also be considered.

• 
Strong, current understanding of Danish AML law (Hvidvaskloven) and the EU framework (AMLD/AMLR, EBA guidelines), plus sanctions regimes. Awareness of the incoming EU AML package (AMLR + AMLD6, applying July 2027) is a plus.

• 
Eligibility to pass a Finanstilsynet fit & proper assessment. Prior approval in a fit & proper / key-function role at an EU financial institution is a strong advantage.

• 
Hands-on experience with fraud prevention and transaction monitoring, and with the underlying tooling (KYC/KYB, screening, monitoring, case management). Data literacy and comfort with AI/automation are a plus.

• 
Experience across risk controls, compliance, the payments area, credit management, or lines-of-defence leadership. Fintech/scale-up experience is a plus.

• 
Strong communication skills, autonomy, and sound decision-making, with the ability to build from a blank page and then scale a function and team.

Analytical and investigative skills to detect patterns and anomalies in financial transactions and to investigate suspicious activity.

• 
Danish speaking, or willing to learn (the role is regulator-facing).

• 
Relevant education (economics, mathematics, law, or financial-sector training) is a plus.

• 
No prior convictions or legal issues that would make the candidate unfit for the role, particularly offences related to financial crime, fraud, money laundering, or other criminal activities undermining trust and integrity.

If this sounds like you, we look forward to receiving your application.

Why Monta

• 
Impact, not easy mode — your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

Ownership from day one — we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

The grind is real — priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

Our core product is a unique, cutting-edge technology born from years of university research called Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD). This technology enables post-quantum secure key exchange for protecting sensitive data across critical infrastructure.

Celare partners with local and international governments, telecom operators, data centers, banks, defense ministries, and leading academic institutions. Over the past year our team has successfully launched commercial pilot deployments of our technology.

The Celare Team

Based in Copenhagen, we combine deep academic expertise with hands-on experience in launching complex, high-impact technology products.

You will be part of a small team of optical engineers responsible for optical development and test activities in the company. As part of a small and agile organization, you will contribute across the full product lifecycle — from early architectural decisions and prototyping to production and large-scale deployment. You will work both in collaboration with our team and independently as a specialist, sharing knowledge across disciplines.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in theoretical chemistry, “Towards quantum-enhanced computational algorithms for discovering sustainable energy materials” - DTU Chemistry
jobs.description:
The project focuses on the development of next-generation quantum-enhanced algorithms for predicting the electronic excited-state properties of organic molecules. By integrating quantum chemistry, quantum computing, and computational materials design, the project aims to enable the efficient screening and discovery of sustainable materials for solar energy conversion and other clean-energy technologies. The PhD project is a collaborative effort between Sonia Coriani (DTU Chemistry, principal supervisor), Piotr de Silva (DTU Energy Conversion and Storage, co-supervisor), and Achintya Kumar Dutta (IIT Bombay, co-supervisor), and is cofinanced through a DTU Alliance PhD fellowship and the Novo Nordisk Foundation-funded Hybrid Quantum Chemistry on Hybrid Quantum Computers (HQC)² project.

As part of the Alliance partnership, the PhD student is expected to spend two research stays of approximately three months each (or one stay of 6 months) at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, working under the supervision of Achintya Kumar Dutta and collaborating closely with a PhD student based at IIT Bombay. The project will also involve close interaction with the research teams associated with the (HQC)² project, providing access to a broad international network and expertise at the interface of quantum chemistry and quantum computing. 

Responsibilities and qualifications

• Design computational methods for predicting excited-state properties, in particular algorithms suitable for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) and Early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
• Generate high-quality benchmark datasets
• Implement computational software and workflows
• Use developed algorithms to: screen candidate organic molecules, support inverse molecular design, discover sustainable energy materials for next-generation solar-energy technologies 
• Disseminate the results of the research in scientific articles and at conferences 
• Participate in the group meetings and activities
• Teaching-related activities at the Department of Chemistry, Technical University of Denmark, including (co)supervision of BSc and MSc student projects
The following additional qualifications are considered as a boon:

• Solid mathematical background and experience within quantum chemistry, computational spectroscopy and programming in Fortran and/or C/C++ and/or Python
• Experience in the development and implementation of correlated wavefunction methods of quantum chemistry, for instance Coupled Cluster or multireference methods.
• Experience on the development of quantum computing algorithms for NISQ and/or (early) Fault Tolerant quantum computers
• Experience with quantum computing software libraries like IBM’s Qiskit or Pennylane
Equally important, you are highly motivated, able to work independently and confident in both written and spoken English. You strive towards scientific excellence, are ambitious and hard working. You enjoy collaborating with others from diverse backgrounds as well as supporting more junior group members. Only applicants, who seek to be among the brightest in their field and do science at the highest international level, will be considered

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree, in either Chemistry (preferably with a focus on theoretical and computational chemistry), Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or Quantum Information Science.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by a panel composed by Prof. Coriani, Prof. De Silva and Assoc. Prof. Kumar Dutta.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position.

The position is available with start on January 1, 2027 or as soon as possible after 01/01/2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Enquires about the position may be made to Professor Sonia Coriani, soco@kemi.dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Chemistry at www.kemi.dtu.dk, and about Coriani’s group at https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Physical-Chemistry/sonia-coriani-group

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications (if any), including the master and bachelor theses
• List of up to three scientists with whom you have closely worked in your past research, whom we may contact for references
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Chemistry is an internationally leading institute with research and teaching in the main areas of chemistry: physical (incl. theoretical/computational), biophysical, organic and inorganic chemistry. Academic excellence, innovation and entrepreneurship are core to its research activities, and drivers of academic and industrial collaborations, spinouts, and high impact publications. The Department has a long-standing tradition of training PhD students and Postdoc fellows who move on to successful careers within academia and industry.

The department actively contributes to both basic chemical research and applied research in energy, pharmaceuticals, catalysis and materials. Strong relationships exist with neighbouring areas such as physics, nanotechnology, biochemistry, including collaboration with industry and universities at home and abroad. Many research projects are also closely linked to applications. The institute has approx. 180 employees.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

**Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and we’re looking for a Product Manager to help shape the future of BIM and make complex building information accessible and useful to everyone in construction.

You’ll play a key role in evolving how our users view, navigate, understand, and collaborate around building models. Combining an understanding of BIM, UI/UX, and computer graphics, you’ll help turn complex technical capabilities into tools that work effortlessly for our users.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Product Discovery: Evaluate and prioritize new product opportunities, balancing user value, technical feasibility, and business impact.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users to understand their BIM workflows, uncover pain points, and translate feedback into meaningful product improvements.

• User Experience: Collaborate with Product Design to make complex BIM interactions intuitive, from navigating 3D models to finding and understanding building information.

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Align with engineers, designers, and fellow product managers to deliver cohesive experiences across Dalux products.

• Feature Ownership: Lead new features from discovery and definition through development, delivery, and validation with users.

• Product Strategy: Help define the direction of BIM at Dalux, identifying opportunities and deciding where we should invest to deliver the greatest value.

**What To Expect As a Daluxian

**At Dalux, we offer a creative, collaborative, and supportive environment where your ideas make an impact. Here’s what you can look forward to as part of our team:

• A central location in Copenhagen, a focus on work/life balance, and no dress code.

• An active social environment with monthly events and social clubs.

• A flat organization with open communication, a short path from idea to product, and the creative freedom and trust to create tangible value for our users.

• A highly specialized, international team with room for creativity and professional growth.

• A strong focus on diversity and inclusion, where your ideas are heard and opportunities are available to all.

• Attractive employee benefits, including health insurance, a lunch plan, coffee and fruit, free fitness facilities, and free parking.

• Support for your professional development and personal well-being.

**About You

**We believe you have a solid background in product management and experience working closely with software development teams, preferably on SaaS platforms. You’re curious about how technology works and motivated by making sophisticated tools easy to use.

We also believe you:

• Have 5+ years of experience in product management, taking products or features from discovery to delivery.

• Have a background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Understand BIM workflows and how building models and their data are used across design, construction, and operations.

• Have a strong understanding of UI/UX principles and can work with designers to evaluate interaction flows, challenge unnecessary complexity, and validate solutions with users.

• Have a working understanding of computer graphics concepts such as 3D geometry, rendering, and model interaction, enabling you to discuss technical trade-offs with engineers.

• Can balance strategic thinking with attention to detail, particularly where usability, model complexity, and performance meet.

• Are comfortable working in agile development environments and prioritizing based on user insights and product outcomes.

• Communicate clearly and fluently in English, both written and spoken.

Experience with IFC, BIM viewers, or other software for working with 3D models would be an advantage.

**Ready for the next step?

**If we have managed to pique your interest, we would love to hear from you. Send us your motivated CV and an application.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your application today.

**About Dalux

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics. Despite being the world’s second-largest industry, construction remains one of the least digitalized, with only 30% of onsite time spent on actual building tasks. At Dalux, we’re changing this by providing end-to-end solutions that streamline the entire lifecycle of a building—from design and construction to maintenance and eventual demolition—reducing waste, time, and costs.

We stay ahead by using cutting-edge technology, including cloud solutions, drones, computer vision, and AI, to transform how the construction industry works. Over the last five years, we’ve grown by 60% annually and now have over 700 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.
