jobs.occupation: Carbon flux and particle export along the land-ocean continuum in Greenland’s coastal ocean
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 01 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Research area and project description:

Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship within the Center for Ice-Free Arctic Research (CIFAR) and the Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University.

Rapid warming is increasing freshwater inputs to the Arctic Ocean from melting glaciers, ice sheets, and altered precipitation patterns. Additionally, sea ice cover is rapidly declining. These changes are transforming the structure and functioning of the Arctic coastal ocean. CIFAR aims to understand how the complex interplay between ice melt, terrestrial runoff, and changing ocean conditions affects Arctic coastal ecosystems and their functioning across spatial and temporal scales.

Fjord systems are a critical interface between the cryosphere, the terrestrial environment and the coastal ocean. They act as important sites of carbon transformation, burial and export, yet we still have a limited understanding of how ongoing freshening will influence these processes. Increasing terrestrial runoff delivers large quantities of particles, minerals and organic carbon to coastal waters, while simultaneously altering water-column structure, particle synamics, and marine primary production.

The overall aim of this PhD project will be to determine how carbon is transformed and transported along the land-ocean continuum in Greenland fjords, and how changes in freshwater inputs influence carbon fluxes and particle export in coastal waters.

The project will investigate interactions between terrestrial organic carbon, marine-produced carbon and mineral particles, with a particular focus on understanding which components of the carbon pool are retained, transformed or exported from the water column. Although much of the terrestrial carbon entering Greenland's coastal systems is transported in particulate form, freshwater runoff also supplies dissolved organic carbon that can be highly bioavailable and rapidly processed within coastal ecosystems. Understanding the fate of these different carbon pools is therefore essential for predicting how Greenland's coastal carbon cycle may respond to continued freshening.

The student will have the opportunity to combine field observations from Greenland with laboratory and analytical approaches to investigate the sources, composition, transformation and export of carbon and particles. The precise scientific focus will be developed together with the student and the wider CIFAR research team.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants to the PhD position must hold a master’s degree and have demonstrated interest and background in biogeochemistry, for example through a bachelor’s or master’s thesis, research project, internship, or other relevant research experience.

• Skills in data analysis and programming, using R, Python, or other relevant programming languages and analytical tools.

• Ability and willingness to work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary and international research environment.

• Good written and oral communication skills in English.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage, but is not required:

• Marine or aquatic biogeochemistry

• Organic carbon analyses

• Particle dynamics, sedimentation or particle export

• Geochemical or stable-isotope approaches

• Processing and analysis of environmental or oceanographic datasets

• Fieldwork in marine, coastal or Arctic environments

We particularly encourage applications from candidates who are scientifically curious and interested in developing their own ideas within the broader aims of the project.

Place of employment and place of work:

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is C.F. Møllers Alle 3, 8000 Aarhus and Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde; Denmark.

Turn user behaviour into funnels that convert

**About Good Tape

**At Good Tape, we’re building tools that make working with voice and audio effortless. We help journalists, researchers, and organisations capture, transcribe, and analyse conversations at scale. Our team is small, ambitious, and deeply technical, and we care about reliability and craft.

**The role

**At Good Tape we are ready to level up. We've built up tons of data, a large user base, and a team that's eager to move fast.

We have a world class product, shipping speed and roadmap that warrants our ambition level.

We're looking for someone excited to own the path our users actually take through the product; from signup to activation to conversion, and to turn our data into a steady stream of experiments that move the numbers. You'll report directly to our CCO and work closely with our data scientist, on spotting opportunities and blind spots in the funnel, and Growth Marketing Manager, who owns everything that brings people to the door.

It's a rare opportunity; endless data, a real user base and a world class product.

**What You'll Do

**Your responsibilities will include

• Own funnel optimisation and CRO across signup, onboarding, pricing page, and in-product conversion points.

• Design, run, and analyse structured growth experiments end to end.

• Work closely with our data scientist to spot opportunities and blind spots across the conversion path.

• Partner with Product and Engineering to translate product launches into growth experiments and user value.

• Own the conversion funnels of our website; signup flow, pricing page and checkout.

• Feed funnel and experiment data into the pricing and positioning conversations led by our CCO.

**What We’re Looking For

**

• A-can-do-mindset who are curious, humble and tech-savvy enough to build manual processes that we can later scale.

• An AI-first approach to problem solving

• An eye for UX and conversion-focused design is a plus

• Proactive, high-ownership mindset with strong cross-functional communication skills.

• Experience in product-led growth, CRO, or growth product management, and comfort with core SaaS metrics.

• Strong analytical instincts and comfort designing and reading experiments.

• Thrives in a fast-paced startup environment with a proven ability to learn quickly.

**Why join Good Tape?

**

• Work in a small, focused, and highly skilled team where your impact is visible every day.

• Play a key role in shaping our product funnels and conversion strategy.

• Help define how Good Tape turns interest into activation and activation into revenue.

• Bring passion and proactivity, and see it directly converted into user value.

**Apply for the job

**We’re excited to see how you can help us make Good Tape even better for our users.

Are you passionate about building software that powers real-world manufacturing and drives the digital transformation of global production? Then join our mission to pioneer smarter water solutions that reduce energy use and improve lives.

As our new Full-Stack Software Developer, you'll be designing, developing, and maintaining full-stack applications for Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) that support critical production processes across Grundfos's global manufacturing sites. You'll be part of a diverse, supportive and inclusive culture, that celebrates our differences and puts people first by fostering growth, well-being, and a sense of belonging.

What you will be doing

As a key part of the Manufacturing IT team, you'll create impact by building scalable, integrated software solutions that connect enterprise systems with shop-floor operations, enabling smarter and more efficient production worldwide.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Design, develop, and deploy full-stack applications using .NET, C#, React, and MS SQL on local servers or Azure Cloud services

• Build APIs and backend services for system integration, including SAP and shop-floor automation equipment using industrial protocols such as OPC UA

• Collaborate with production engineering, IT, and infrastructure stakeholders to translate business needs into reliable, maintainable software solutions

• Maintain and enhance CI/CD pipelines and automation scripts for build, test, and deployment workflows

• Ensure code quality through peer reviews, unit/integration testing, and adherence to coding standards within an agile SCRUM team

• Provide mentorship and technical guidance to associate developers while contributing to architectural discussions and continuous improvement

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you're a skilled full-stack developer with strong .NET and React experience, a solid grasp of system integration patterns, and the ability to communicate effectively with both technical peers and domain experts in a fast-paced agile environment.

We'd also imagine that you are/have:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field

• 3+ years of full-stack development experience with .NET, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, React, and MS SQL

• Solid understanding of software engineering principles and patterns (e.g., SOLID), RESTful APIs, and web application frameworks

• Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and scripting (e.g., PowerShell)

It's a plus if you also:

• Experience with Siemens Opcenter Discrete MES platform development and configuration

• Familiarity with ERP systems (especially SAP) and/or shop-floor integration using industrial protocols (OPC UA, MQTT)

• Experience with Azure Cloud services and containerized deployments

Why you'll love working here

Day to day, you can look forward to:

• A working environment built around your needs, with flexible hours, home working opportunities and parental support.

• Annual bonuses, health insurance and a strong focus on well-being activities.

• Three days' additional paid leave for volunteering.

• On-demand training and structured development programmes to support your growth.

Valuing our differences helps us see possibilities where others can't. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all abilities, experiences, and backgrounds. As part of our commitment to a safe and compliant hiring process, final candidates may be required to undergo a background check, subject to applicable local laws and regulations.

Join Grundfos, apply today!

About Grundfos

Grundfos is one of the world’s leading water technology companies with more than 19.000 employees in 60+ countries all over the world. Our skills commit us to pioneering solutions to the world’s water and climate challenges and improve the quality of life for people. We dare to do things that others cannot or dare not do, as we believe innovation is not only a business opportunity, but an obligation. And what really matters to us is not short term profit, but the impact we make. By becoming part of our united powerful team, you too can drive this change no matter your role.

An inclusive team

We believe that the key to a work environment, where employees thrive and grow, is our ability to celebrate and value our differences in background, experiences and perspectives. In our recruitment process we welcome all professional people without consideration of age, colour, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental disability, ethnicity or religion.

What Makes Us, Us  Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**Our Accounting team is growing and we are looking for more team members to join. If you are curious, collaborative and enjoy taking initiative this could be a great place to work. You do not need to have all answers from day one. What matters to us is that you are open to learning, willing to try and comfortable to step into new challenges.

At SimCorp, we support some of the largest financial institutions in the world to be successful by simplifying their investments, accounting and operations.

Accounting is a unit within SimCorp’s Product Division which delivers all rules and calculation methods in order to provide our clients with a legally binding subledger for all supported asset classes.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Develop and maintain features in the Accounting product areas.

• Contribute across the entire development lifecycle - from requirements analysis and design to implementation, test automation, documentation, and ongoing support.

• Collaborate closely with teammates, Product Managers, and Architects to deliver high-quality and secure solutions.

• Create, document and maintain test cases and automated tests to cover the features’ acceptance criteria (system, integration, unit etc.)

• Uphold engineering best practices and contribute to continuous improvement.

• Learn deeply about our Accounting domain and understand how our products support customer outcomes.

• Be open to feedback, mentorship, and knowledge sharing in your team.

**Your Skills

**Most importantly, you can see yourself contributing and thriving in the position described above. How you gained the skills needed for doing that is less important. We expect you to be good at several of the following and be able to - and interested in - learn the rest.

• Confident in software engineering fundamentals, including algorithms and data structures.

• Willingness to learn and work with in-house tools and frameworks, especially the APL programming language.

• Proficiency in at least one object-oriented or functional programming language (C# is a benefit).

• Familiarity with modern engineering tools and practices, including CI/CD and trunk-based development.

• Experience working with relational databases and SQL.

• Readiness to work in a complex accounting domain, dealing with financial and investment-related instruments.

• Good English skills (upper-intermediate or higher), both written and spoken.

• Experience with cloud technologies and fintech domain is a plus.

**What Is It Like To Work Here

**SimCorp plans work in an agile manner, using 4 planning intervals (PI’s) per year, each consisting of 5 sprints of 2 weeks each, followed by a 3-week Innovation and Planning sprint, which can be used for mastering skills in various areas, or more freely investigating ideas with prototypes. It is important that our people learn and grow constantly, and SimCorp invests a lot to foster the continuous learning environment to support people on their journeys.

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

**Benefits

**An attractive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential components of any employment package. At SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. In addition to the traditional benefits, we promote an effective work-life balance, including flexible work hours and a hybrid workplace model. As a large organization, we offer a wide range of career opportunities, with an individualized approach to professional development to support the career path you wish to pursue.

**NEXT STEPS

Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible. We process incoming applications continually. Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.** At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**WHO WE ARE?

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

jobs.occupation: Launch your career as a Business Tech Consultant - join our Discovery Day!
jobs.description:
Company Description

Are you a tech-minded graduate ready to make an impact within technology and transformation? Do you want to explore different career paths within consulting – and find the right match for you?

On 18-19 November 2026, we invite ambitious soon-to-be or recent Graduates to Deloitte’s Talent Discovery Days - your opportunity to get to know the different career paths and work with cases in Deloitte Technology & Transformation leading to a potential position in one of our offerings.

Technology & Transformation

In Deloitte Denmark, our Technology & Transformation teams work with the intersection of business and technology to help organizations navigate change and turn technology into practical, impactful solutions.

You will join a collaborative environment with ambitious colleagues, where learning, development, and teamwork are key – and where you get the opportunity to grow both professionally and personally.

Job Description

What can you expect?

During the Talent Discovery Days, not two moments will be alike. You will collaborate with peers on case challenges, meet our consultants, and explore the different opportunities within Technology & Transformation. Among other things you will:

• Work on case exercises and tackle real-life client challenges with peers

• Meet our consultants and hear their career stories first-hand

• Explore our tech teams and discover where your skills and interests fit in

• Get the chance to move forward: based on the days, selected participants will be invited to individual interviews with the possibility of a job offer in the following period

Please note: Discovery Day takes place over two full days, and participants are expected to be able to attend both days. In addition, selected participants must be available for potential follow-up calls after both day 1 and day 2 as part of the assessment process.

Qualifications

Who are we looking for?

At Deloitte, we look for curiosity, drive, and passion for combining business and technology to create impact. A candidate who is:

A soon-to-be or recent graduate (up to 2 years of experience) within Computer Science, Engineering, IT or Business IT

• In possession of a valid Danish work and residence permit

• An interest in the balance and intersection between technology and business

• A problem solver who enjoys tackling complex challenges

• A passionate learner eager to grow your skills and career

• A team player who thrives in collaborative environments

• A candidate with a passion for collaborating with customers to solve their problems

Here you can read more about our offerings and what type of candidates they specifically are looking for:

AI & Data

In AI & Data, we help organizations solve their complex challenges by turning data into a strategic asset. This means you'll be hands-on with projects that span the entire data journey – from shaping AI strategy and building modern data platforms to developing and implementing agentic and generative AI, machine learning, analytics and automation solutions. You will collaborate with a team of advisors and deep-tech specialists to deliver tangible results for clients across all industries. We practice what we preach, applying AI-powered tools in our own work to enhance quality and accelerate delivery.

We are looking for curious and ambitious problem-solvers with a genuine interest in the connection between data, technology, and business. You don't need to be an expert yet, but an understanding of data engineering, data science, or AI concepts is essential, along with a strong desire to learn and grow.

ServiceNow

We combine consulting with hands-on implementation of ServiceNow solutions to help organizations streamline and future-proof their operations. Our work spans process automation, performance tracking, and digital workflow optimization across functions such as IT, HR, Finance, Risk and Compliance.

We are looking for curious and motivated candidates who thrive at the intersection of business and technology. You may lean more towards technical development or towards project and process work, but you should be interested in understanding how digital solutions support business outcomes.

You are not expected to have ServiceNow expertise before joining - competencies will be developed through training and project experience. What matters most is your ability to think abstractly and translate ideas into tangible solutions. For example, you should be able to interpret a written process description and visualize or structure it into a clear process flow.

Customer

At Deloitte Digital, we help organizations transform their front-office by designing and implementing CRM solutions across sales, marketing, and service. We are looking for talented colleagues who understand how technology supports customer-facing processes and are eager to work hands-on with CRM platforms.

The ideal candidate thrives at the intersection of business and technology, can translate client requirements into practical solutions and is motivated to develop both functional expertise and technical skills in a dynamic, team-oriented environment.

Finance Transformation

In Finance Transformation, we help organizations modernize and improve the entire CFO area, from invoicing and reporting to finance strategy and financial planning. By combining business insight, technology, data, and process excellence, we help finance functions become more efficient and better equipped to support strategic decision-making.

As a junior consultant, you will gain exposure to a variety of projects across the CFO agenda and work closely with both colleagues and clients. This gives you the opportunity to build a broad understanding of finance transformation before gradually developing deeper expertise within a specific area that matches your interests and strengths.

We are looking for curious and analytical candidates with an interest in the intersection of business, finance, and technology. You enjoy solving complex problems, working with data, and collaborating with stakeholders to create practical solutions that deliver measurable impact.

Supply Chain & Network Operations

In Supply Chain & Network Operations (SCNO), we help organizations transform how they plan, optimize, and execute their supply chains. You'll work hands-on configuring platforms like Kinaxis Maestro and SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), implementing decision intelligence solutions, and enabling resilient supply chains. You will collaborate with supply chain strategists, technical and industry experts to deliver transformational outcomes across complex, global supply networks.

You will translate supply chain requirements into technical solutions, work directly with client teams on implementation, and develop expertise in planning, logistics, procurement, manufacturing, and product lifecycle management. You'll gain exposure to digital thread designs connecting product design, manufacturing, and supply chain execution. You'll grow both technical skills in platform implementation and consulting skills in translating client challenges into designs.

We seek curious and ambitious candidates who thrive at the intersection of business and technology. You should be a collaborative team player who genuinely cares about client impact and learning from colleagues. You don't need platform expertise - competencies develop through training and project experience. What matters most is your ability to think systematically about interconnected processes, translate business requirements into technical specifications, and collaborate across teams.

Additional Information

Whats next?

Expected start: January 2027 & September 2027

Location: Deloitte, Weidekampsgade 6, 2300 Copenhagen S

We only have a limited number of seats available, so do not hesitate to send your application before 8th November.

To apply, please upload your CV, you transcript of grades, and answer our three short questions. Please note that Talent Discovery Day is an invitation-only event. Once you have submitted your application and all required documents, we will review your profile.

You may attend the event only if you are selected and receive an official invitation email from Deloitte; submitting an application does not itself grant access to the event.

We will look at applications on an ongoing basis and you will receive answer no later than  11 November.

If you have any questions, please contact Sarah Manniche (Manager, People & Purpose).

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Kickstart your Career with Deloitte’s Finance Consultancy Programme
jobs.description:
Company Description

Are you interested in working in an exciting and challenging consulting role, where you can deploy and develop your skills and competencies within the CFO domain of companies? Do you hold a business-related Master’s degree by the summer of 2027, and are you ready to embark on a life-long learning journey in a leading global consulting firm? If yes, then we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Who we are

Joining our Finance Consultancy Programme, you will get to collaborate with experienced consultants on a wide variety of assignments and development opportunities. At Deloitte, we work with different project sizes across finance disciplines and industries, but the foundation is always the same: Our genuine passion for the CFO area and creating value together with our clients.

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte Technology & Transformation (former Consulting) consisting of more than 350 consultants in Denmark who work across all areas of the CFO function. We engage with clients to operate, advise, optimize, and transform their finance functions. Our clients range from domestic to international, from private to public, across various industries, sizes, and time horizons.

You will join a team that emphasizes collaboration, collegiality, coaching, and talent development. At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, encouraging an inclusive and collaborative environment.

Job Description

Exciting tasks await you

As an Analyst in Deloitte Finance Transformation, you will experience that no workdays are the same. You will face a wide range of tasks, both in the form of interim-based roles and project-based assignments. Projects and tasks will vary across finance disciplines (e.g., operational finance or business finance) and industries (e.g., private or public), and within the first years of your career, you will be assigned to as many different projects and tasks as possible to expand your toolbox and build on your financial craftmanship.

Based on the specific client's needs and your interests, experiences, and competencies, typical assignments and projects could be within the scope of:

• Finance operations optimization and transformation, e.g., controlling, month-end closing, and reporting

• Transformation and digitalization of finance functions, e.g., process optimization, closing excellence, internal controls advisory, and leveraging technology solutions

• Enterprise performance management, e.g., analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting

• ERP-enabled finance transformations and finance systems implementation, e.g., outlining the ERP-strategy, defining business requirements and ensuring consistent data migration

• Finance strategy and operating model, e.g., designing service delivery models, outlining roles and responsibilities and conducting assessments

• M&A readiness and finance post-merger integration

• Global business services transformations, e.g., assessing, developing and implementing shared service functions and aligning service delivery with corporate strategy

• Internal business development and leadership support, e.g., assisting on client proposals, facilitating events and developing material to strengthen our market offerings.

Onboarding and learning

When joining us, you will participate in our onboarding programme designed with the purpose of giving you the best foundation for kickstarting your career in Deloitte. During your first two weeks, you and your peers will attend our Finance Transformation Nordic Bootcamp and our Consultant Academy, where the content is tailored to match your competencies as recent graduates. The Finance Transformation Bootcamp helps you in building your finance craftmanship and toolbox, while the Consultant Academy prepares you for your consulting role in Deloitte Technology & Transformation. Also heavily focused on social activities and team-building, the onboarding programme provides a smooth transition from university as it offers a unique opportunity to connect and build strong relations with your fellow new joiners from day one.

At Deloitte, we believe in life-long learning, and we are committed to investing in your individual development, both professionally and personally, throughout your career. You will experience this with our Finance Consultancy Programme, which is a highly structured learning programme, aimed at equipping you with the appropriate skillset and the right level of competencies needed to succeed in your role.

Leadership and culture

To support your learning, you will also be assigned a People Leader as your closest leader and go-to sparring partner. Your People Leader will help you set the overall direction of your journey in Deloitte and provide guidance across projects to make sure that your individual aspirations and professional development goals are met. Every career path is unique, and together with your People Leader you get the chance to shape your own.

We believe in leadership at all levels, and we have committed ourselves to creating and maintaining an inclusive and psychologically safe culture, where you are encouraged and empowered to take responsibility while leading both yourself and others. We combine this with a substantial focus on continuously staying relevant and being a meaningful social community to our people. We are a people’s business, and therefore we strongly believe that this is an essential prerequisite for making an impact that truly matters – for ourselves and for our clients**.

Qualifications

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for you, who are passionate about consulting and the CFO-area and who are willing to go the extra mile to deliver sustainable impact that truly matters to our clients. You show an eagerness to make a difference for both clients and colleagues and you are able to see the opportunities and potential in all types of assignments. As our business can be highly changeable, it is important that you are curious by nature, and that you face challenges with an open-minded and solution-oriented approach.

In addition to this, you:

• Have completed a master’s degree within the fields of finance, economics, business, accounting, social sciences, IT, or similar areas in the summer of 2027 or before

• Have achieved academic results from your bachelor’s and master’s degree that you are proud of

• Demonstrate a flair for both oral and written communication and are fluent in English

• Have a legal working permit in Denmark

Although relevant job experience might be an advantage, this is not a requirement.

Additional Information

Want to know more?

Click the "I'm interested"-button above and upload your CV and grade transcripts from your bachelor’s and master’s degree if you are interested and ready to join our team**. Instead of an application letter, we would like you to answer the questions you will be presented with on the next pages** (please only consider the required (*) fields). As we process applications and arrange interviews on an ongoing basis, we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Application deadline: Hiring on an ongoing basis.

Please do not hesitate to contact Giulio Marano (gimarano@deloitte.dk / +45 30 93 64 11) or Maria Banke (mbanke@deloitte.dk / +45 20 97 64 15) if you have any questions about the position.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Company Description

Are you curious about modern software development and looking for the next step in your career? At Deloitte Engineering, we are looking for recent graduates and early-career software developers who want to strengthen their technical and problem-solving capabilities while helping us grow our Engineering practice. You will have the opportunity to work hands-on with software development while applying your skills in a consulting environment, working with clients to solve complex business and technology challenges.

With more than 2.700 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Technology & Transformation.

About the team

We, the Engineering offering of Deloitte Technology & Transformation Denmark, are on the lookout for additional team-players for our quickly growing practice of software engineers, architects, cloud consultants, and IT management consultants. We assist our clients, some of the largest companies, agencies, and organizations in Denmark and the Nordics, on the implementation of new cloud-native systems as part of their digital transformation – and we need you to help build their opportunities and meet their challenges!

Together, we will accelerate your career towards becoming a proficient software developer. At Deloitte, we are committed to empowering you throughout your career development. As a new employee, you are assigned a talent manager to support your career aspirations and development. You will also be part of a tech community with monthly meetings in which we share knowledge, investigate new topics, and upskill within relevant technologies and methodologies.

Job Description

As a software developer at the Engineering offering, you will work with many different aspects of development, from writing code to testing it. You will work closely with both clients and internal stakeholders to ensure that our solutions meet their business needs and technical requirements. Our client assignments can vary greatly, but common for all of them are that we strive to work with the technologies that the client prefers. Regardless of the technology, we provide you with the opportunity and tools needed to learn and grow within all of them.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Developing applications and solutions of all sizes, frequently in Agile settings (SAFE/Scrum). This includes both backend and frontend development.

• Assisting in the implementation of CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code (IaC), and adopting DevOps practices to streamline development workflows.

• Building internal capabilities through community tasks, maybe within new business areas.

• Joining in on workshops and sales pitches and contributing to proposals for new client projects.

Qualifications

You hold a Master’s degree, preferably within Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Software Development, or another relevant technical field. You are either a recent graduate or have up to 4 years of full-time professional experience, preferably within software development. Experience from student positions, internships, or part-time software development roles is also considered an advantage. You enjoy applying your analytical and problem-solving skills to technical challenges and are motivated by working both hands-on with software and in a client-facing consulting environment. About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Clinical Sciences, you'll help turn Hemab's science into well-designed clinical studies and clear evidence about how our treatments perform in patients. You'll take scientific ownership across protocol development, study execution and data interpretation, working closely with Medical Directors and colleagues across clinical development, regulatory and other functions.

What you'll do

• Lead the clinical science contribution to study strategy, design and execution, keeping the scientific questions and patient needs at the centre of decisions.

• Drive protocol development with the Medical Director, including amendments as emerging data or study needs require.

• Own the scientific review of clinical study data, identify discrepancies and trends, and turn emerging safety and efficacy data into clear questions and actions for the team.

• Shape study documents and plans, including informed consent forms, eCRFs, medical monitoring plans and data review plans.

• Guide sites and vendors on protocol requirements, eligibility criteria and participant management so studies are executed consistently and to the intended design.

• Partner across clinical development to analyse and interpret study results and build a clear understanding of what the data mean.

• Translate study findings for internal and external audiences alongside the Medical Director.

• Develop clinical content for regulatory documents, including investigator brochures, annual safety reports, clinical study reports and registration submissions.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Substantial clinical science or clinical research experience in drug development, with direct responsibility for clinical studies.

• Experience developing clinical protocols and interpreting safety and efficacy data from interventional studies.

• A strong working knowledge of ICH-GCP, clinical study design and drug development in a regulated environment.

• The scientific judgement to interpret clinical information, literature and changing treatment approaches and apply it to study and development decisions.

• Experience working effectively with investigators, vendors and cross-functional clinical, medical and regulatory colleagues.

Nice to have

• Experience in haematology, rare disease or bleeding disorders.

• Experience contributing to development programmes through later-stage studies and registration.

• An advanced scientific or clinical degree.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This is the actual shape of working somewhere at this stage: It's genuinely energising for the right person and genuinely frustrating for the wrong one. If you want a place where the operating manual is already written, this might not be it – but if you want to help write it, this might be exactly it.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

jobs.occupation: Prototype Engineering Specialist (12 months cover position)
jobs.description:
Coordinate complex prototype activities that enable better medical devices.

At Coloplast, we develop products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. In this role, you help our development projects turn product concepts into prototypes: for design iterations, usability studies, clinical trials, and design verification.

You bring structure to technically complex work. You connect engineers, manufacturing specialists and project teams around one plan. Your job is to build the integrated overview, maintain appropriate traceability and make the complete prototype flow work across the relevant stages of product development

Make complex prototype flows work

You coordinate prototype activities in complex development projects. That can mean multiple prototype variants, several manufacturing steps or sites, shifting levels of design maturity, demanding traceability requirements, or a wide stakeholder group.

This is an engineering-based coordination role: you will not be expected to manufacture the prototypes yourself or replace the technical specialists who define the prototype needs and requirements. The technical specialists remain responsible for defining their prototype needs, while the manufacturing teams remain responsible for production execution and manufacturing documentation. You bring these contributions together into one coherent and executable prototype plan. You build plans, spot dependencies and missing information, keep things visible, and push unresolved issues to a decision.

Join a growing engineering capability

You'll join our Test Development Engineering team: Test Development Engineers and Prototype Engineering Specialists, supporting product-development projects across Coloplast.

In this role you’ll have a broad footprint across the whole organization. You'll work closely with Product Development Project Managers, Test Engineers, Mechanical Design Engineers, Clinical and Usability colleagues, Quality Assurance, manufacturing sites, and external partners. You'll also work with the other Prototype Engineering Specialists to build consistent, practical ways of managing prototype activities across the team.

Your key responsibilities are:

• Coordinate complex prototype activities from early project planning through the final samples the project needs.

• Establish and maintain appropriate project-level prototype traceability, including references to the relevant manufacturing documentation.

• Build and maintain one overview of prototype purpose, quantities, variants, maturity, timing, manufacturing flow.

• Align prototype requesters with internal or external manufacturers.

• Challenge unclear, conflicting, or incomplete requirements before they cause delays.

• Coordinate dependencies across components, prototype versions, manufacturing processes, sites, and project activities.

• Keep prototype status, decisions, risks, and open actions visible to everyone who needs them.

• Spot planning, capacity, documentation, and delivery risks early, and work with the right people to fix them.

• Help improve the processes, templates, and working methods for prototype management.

What you bring

Your engineering background lets you challenge weak assumptions, identify gaps, and bring in the right specialist at the right time. You need technical understanding to see how requirements, product variants, materials, manufacturing processes, documentation, and timelines affect each other.

Your real contribution is keeping the complexity manageable, so the team delivers.

We expect that you:

• Hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in engineering, life science, pharmaceutics, or another relevant technical discipline.

• Have experience coordinating technical activities in product development, manufacturing, engineering, or a similar environment.

• Can turn input from several disciplines into a structured plan people can execute.

• Thrive in a central role, with multiple stakeholder interactions.

• Understand manufacturing flows and how product design, materials, processes, and documentation connect.

• Work confidently with requirements, dependencies, risks, traceability, and shifting priorities.

• Communicate clearly across functions and professional disciplines.

• Take a proactive, practical, accountable approach to commitments and deadlines.

• Are comfortable working in English in an international organization.

Experience in medical devices, life science, or another regulated environment is a plus. So is familiarity with prototype production, design verification, configuration management, quality systems, or coordination across multiple manufacturing sites.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Scott Jonas Hansen, Head of Test Development Engineering, dkschan@coloplast.com

jobs.occupation: Specialist/Consultant in Neurology looking for job opportunities in Denmark?
jobs.description:
Specialist/Consultant in Neurology looking for job opportunities in Denmark?

Newly Created Position at Mid- and West Zealand Hospital for an Emergency Neurology Profile in Partnership with Rigshospitalet, The University Hospital of Copenhagen.

We are expanding our team of specialists at Mid- and West Zealand Hospital, Denmark as we develop a new emergency neurology profile. You will have a direct professional influence on our future emergency services and become part of a new, close partnership with Rigshospitalet.

Why choose us?

• Help shape the emergency services of the future: You will play a central role in developing and launching our upcoming emergency neurology profile (without a thrombolysis service).

• New partnership with Rigshospitalet: The collaboration will open opportunities for professional exchange, knowledge sharing and research. For those interested, there will also be opportunities for attractive split appointments (e.g. one day per week at Rigshospitalet).

• New professional opportunities from 1 January 2027: As a result of the healthcare reform in Denmark, we will take over specialised rehabilitation from the municipalities, creating exciting opportunities for professional development.

• Scope for your subspecialty: Whether your interests lie in MS, movement disorders, headache, dementia, epilepsy or rehabilitation, we will adapt the framework to allow you to pursue your area of expertise.

• A strong research environment: We focus on patients with multimorbidity and have our own Professor of Neurology. Research is primarily focused on multiple sclerosis.

Your profile

You are a specialist/consultant in neurology, whether you are newly qualified and eager to develop your skills or an experienced colleague looking for a new professional setting.

We imagine that you:

• Are passionate about multidisciplinary collaboration and want to help shape the quality of the new emergency setup.

• Value a strong professional network across hospitals.

• Appreciate the opportunity to provide clinical guidance and supervision to our junior doctors.

• Are decisive, flexible and actively contribute to our positive working environment and pioneering spirit.

Your working day and responsibilities

Our department provides primary-level neurological services in the hospital at Slagelse (inpatient ward for phase II rehabilitation, primarily for apoplexy cases, as well as specialist clinics), and in the hospital of Naestved, where we run the Centre for Neurorehabilitation (CNN), which provides services at regional level.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Working in our outpatient department, specialist clinics or the interdisciplinary Memory Clinic, in collaboration with geriatricians, psychiatrists and neuropsychologists.

• Supervising junior doctors and participating in the multidisciplinary environment across our hospital sites.

• On-call duties: Our consultants currently cover the senior on-call function on site until 9.00 pm, followed by an on-call-from-home arrangement (there is junior on-call doctor is present on site around the clock).

About the department

Neurology is part of a combined department (Medicine 3 and Department of Physio- and Occupational Therapy) that works closely and efficiently alongside the Department of Geriatrics. We place a strong emphasis on professional dialogue and peer support within a group of doctors characterised by strong collegial relationships and a shared desire to develop the specialty.

Mid- and West Zealand Hospital is located around 60 min. by car from central Copenhagen.

Practical information and application

• The seven medical roles: Your application should address the seven medical competencies specifically, supported by the best possible documentation.

• Interests: If you have specific wishes regarding subspecialisation or are interested in a split appointment with Rigshospitalet, we would be pleased if you mention this in your application.

Relocation Assistance and Danish Language Tutoring

When you relocate to Denmark in connection with your employment, we offer free, professional assistance with relocation and settling in, either close to the hospital or anywhere on Zealand you might prefer. You will receive help with everything from finding accommodation to registration and arrangements for any accompanying family members.

An important part of working as a doctor in Denmark is communication between you and your patients and colleagues. For patient safety reasons, Region Zealand therefore requires our doctors to have a satisfactory level of Danish language proficiency. We therefore provide a language teacher for one-to-one tuition, enabling you to communicate with your patients as quickly as possible at a level where you can understand one another.

This means, that we expect you to be prepared to devote time to learning Danish, both spoken and written as part of your employment.

Find out more about what kind of assistance we offer, as well as watch interviews with other doctors that have relocated to Region Zealand at www.medicaljobsdenmark.com.

Would you like to know more?

You are very welcome to contact Chief Physician Benedikte Wanscher on mobile +45 93 57 62 51 or by email at bewa@regionsjaelland.dk for an informal and confidential conversation about the position.

Please upload your application and CV as soon as possible. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Startløn for overenskomstansatte

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.

Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbejder vi hver dag for at fremme det sunde liv ved at forebygge og behandle i en sammenhængende sundhedsindsats. Som hospital forener vi psykiatri og somatik. Vores mål er, at patienter og borgere oplever gode og trygge forløb af høj kvalitet.

Som medarbejder bliver du en del af et nytænkende, fagligt og organisatorisk robust hospital, hvor vi gør en forskel for de mennesker, der har brug for os. Læring og udvikling er en del af hverdagen og sker i fagligt forpligtende fællesskaber. Også på tværs af afdelinger.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital dækker et opland på ca. 230.000 borgere. Vi har 766 sengepladser og er omkring 5.000 ansatte fordelt på 20 afdelinger, herunder 16 somatiske og psykiatriske specialer.

Vi tilbyder et solidt forskningsmiljø med 13 professorer og et stærkt fagligt uddannelsesmiljø, hvor vi hvert år byder cirka 2.700 studerende, elever og læger i videreuddannelsesforløb velkommen.

jobs.occupation: Associate Project Director, Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about translating strategic priorities into disciplined execution? Do you have extensive experience leading complex, cross-functional projects in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry? If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Associate Project Director, GRAPS.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking an experienced and highly structured Associate Project Director to join our GRAPS Enablement & Insights function within Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety.

In this role, you will translate GRAPS priorities into integrated plans and disciplined execution across Global Regulatory Affairs, Global Patient Safety, and key enterprise functions. You will lead strategic and operational initiatives involving multiple functions, geographies, vendors, and systems, while establishing clear governance, decision pathways, performance reporting, and risk management.

This is an exciting opportunity to combine strategic perspective with hands-on project leadership in a global and highly regulated environment. You will work closely with the GRAPS Leadership Team, functional leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen quality, compliance, predictability, and organizational scalability.

You will join the GRAPS team (Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety) and report directly to Jethro Ekuta, Chief Regulatory & Safety Officer, who is based in US.

The position may be based in US or DK, with travel to Ascendis Pharma locations and other business-critical meetings as required.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Lead assigned GRAPS projects and programs from initiation through closeout, establishing clear scope, objectives, governance, integrated plans, milestones, accountabilities, dependencies, budgets, risk controls, and measurable outcomes

• Partner with GRAPS leaders to translate strategic priorities into roadmaps and sequenced execution plans, while maintaining a consolidated view of the GRAPS project portfolio, including capacity constraints, interdependencies, risks, and decisions requiring leadership attention

• Establish and facilitate fit-for-purpose governance, steering forums, workshops, stage reviews, and decision-making processes, and prepare concise executive dashboards, status reports, decision materials, and recommendations

• Coordinate stakeholders across Regulatory Affairs, Patient Safety, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Quality, IT, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, and external partners, creating clarity around roles, responsibilities, interfaces, and handoffs

• Drive operational excellence and sustainable change by identifying opportunities to standardize, simplify, and scale processes, tools, and ways of working while supporting applicable GxP, regulatory, pharmacovigilance, documentation, training, inspection-readiness, and records-management requirements

You will also provide project-methodology guidance and coaching to workstream leads and more junior project-management colleagues and may coordinate contractors or matrixed team members.

Qualifications and skills

You hold a relevant academic degree, preferably a bachelor's or master's degree in life sciences, business, project management, engineering, or a related discipline, and have at least 8 years of relevant experience from the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or another highly regulated industry.

Furthermore, you have:

• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, programs, or major workstreams involving senior stakeholders, multiple functions, geographies, vendors, or systems

• Strong command of project and program management disciplines, including scope, schedule, governance, resources, budgets, dependencies, risks, issues, change control, and benefits realization

• Working knowledge of drug development and commercialization, preferably combined with experience in Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Patient Safety, Quality, Regulatory Operations, or a closely related function

• Experience creating executive-ready dashboards, status reports, decision materials, and presentations using Microsoft 365 and relevant project-management or reporting tools

• A project-management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent is preferred. Agile or change-management training would be considered an advantage

Key competencies

You have an enterprise mindset and a strong patient focus, combined with sound judgment regarding business, quality, compliance, and reputational risk.

You are highly structured, analytical, and detail-oriented while maintaining a clear focus on strategic objectives and outcomes. You can simplify complexity, frame options, recommend a path forward, and communicate decisions clearly to executive, technical, and operational audiences.

You are an experienced stakeholder manager who can build alignment, create accountability, and influence without formal authority. You are comfortable working with ambiguity, managing competing priorities, and adapting plans when business needs change.

As a person, you are collaborative, inclusive, culturally aware, and effective in a global matrix organization. You demonstrate high integrity, discretion, ownership, and a strong commitment to transparent communication and follow-through.

Travel: 15-25 days a year.

Office: Ascendis Pharma, Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform. Applications sent by email or through other channels will not be evaluated.

You can learn more about Ascendis Pharma by visiting our website.

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team, specifically from a Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director, is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.occupation: The Danish School of Education (DPU) at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University, invites applications for a position as an associate professor in educational and developmental psychology, commencing on 1 March 2027.
jobs.description:
Associate Professor in Educational and Developmental Psychology  

This is a full-time position commencing on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position is based at DPU, at either the Aarhus campus or the Emdrup campus in Copenhagen. The selected applicant will be expected to participate in day-to-day activities at the school, including teaching and supervision. Some travel should be expected between the school’s campuses in Aarhus and Copenhagen. 

The position  

The position involves research and university teaching in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will help further develop the existing research and teaching environment within the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, with a particular focus on developmental psychology in early childhood. 

The position involves teaching at Master’s level and conducting research in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will become part of a well-established academic environment within the Department 

The selected applicant should be able to document experience conducting empirical research, both independently and in collaboration with others, including studies within childhood developmental psychology, using qualitative, quantitative and/or mixed methods. 

Preference will be given to applicants who can document an interest in one or more of the following research areas: Transitions between institutions and families; family life, children’s psychological, emotional and relational development in and across different settings. 

Preference will be given to applicants able to teach and supervise in psychological and educational assessments and psychometrics. 

Research  

The selected applicant will be expected to: 

• develop new research projects relevant to the field of educational and developmental psychology 
• contribute to collaborative research initiatives at DPU, both nationally and internationally 
• pursue external research funding 
• contribute to theoretical, methodological and empirical developments in the fields of early childhood and/or childhood studies and/or family studies. 
• Applicants must outline their vision and plans for contributing to the suggested research fields. 
Teaching  

The selected applicant will teach and supervise students at all levels across relevant degree programmes at DPU, particularly the Master’s degree programme in educational psychology, including the specialisation in educational psychological counselling (PPR) and related electives, as well as in the field of early childhood. Teaching may also be expected on the professional Master’s degree programme in well-being. 

Talent development  

Associate professors at DPU/AU are expected to continuously develop their competences in supervising students at the Master’s and PhD levels, including the development and teaching of PhD courses focusing on theory, methodology and/or specific methods in collaboration with colleagues. Applicants are invited to describe their experiences of and plans or ideas for talent development. 

Knowledge exchange  

The selected applicant will be expected to engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy of the Faculty of Arts, for instance through collaboration on research with external partners, public dissemination activities, consultancy work or collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Applicants should document any prior experience of knowledge exchange activities and outline their plans for maximising the impact of their research within educational and developmental psychology and its implications for practice. 

Qualifications  

Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent qualifications in a relevant field and be able to document: 

• a research profile within developmental psychology in the fields of daycare/reception class and/or family life, as well as children’s psychological and relational development in early childhood 
• an international publication profile, including experience of participation in international networks 
• experience applying for and obtaining external research funding 
• knowledge of and interest in psychodynamic–relational theories of personality, identity and selfhood from a developmental perspective, whether from a supportive and/or a critical position. 
• experience conducting empirical research, preferably using a range of methodologies relevant to the field of developmental psychology 
• knowledge of psychological tests and assessment tools relevant to early childhood and developmental psychology. 
Further information  
For further information about the position, please contact the head of the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, Charlotte Mathiassen, email: cham@edu.au.dk, tel.: +45 6186 3645. 

The application must be submitted in English. 

About the Danish School of Education  

The Danish School of Education (DPU) is one of the three schools at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University. 

Across its two locations at Campus Emdrup in Copenhagen and Nobel Park in Aarhus, DPU is home to approximately 200 academic and administrative staff, as well as approximately 80 PhD students. 

Our degree programmes  

The Danish School of Education currently offers a Bachelor’s degree programme in educational studies and ten Master’s degree programmes in a range of educational and pedagogical disciplines, as well as six professional Master’s degree programmes that can also be studied as single-subject courses. 

Approximately 2,000 students are enrolled in the school’s Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes, with approximately 250 students enrolled in professional Master’s degree programmes. 

Many of these programmes are offered at DPU’s locations in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, with students fairly evenly divided between the two campuses. 

Our research  

The Danish School of Education is Denmark's largest university environment for basic and applied research in pedagogy and education. 

The school is home to strong research environments within educational studies, educational theory and curriculum studies, general education, educational psychology, educational anthropology, educational sociology and educational philosophy, 

In addition, we conduct interdisciplinary research focused on specific educational fields of inquiry, particularly schools and early childhood education and care. 

DPU promotes public awareness of research in education and pedagogy through extensive dissemination activities with the aim of providing society with a rich and robust knowledge base. 

International applicants  

International applicants are encouraged to read about family and work-life balance as well as the attractive working conditions and other benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a relocation service and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see the taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here: http://international.au.dk/research/ 

An appointee who does not speak Danish will be required to acquire proficiency in Danish to handle tasks, including administrative and managerial responsibilities, and to participate fully in the activities of the Danish School of Education within approximately two years of commencing the appointment. These activities include, but are not limited to, teaching and examining students, reading work-related texts and participating in meetings and collegial gatherings in Danish. 

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and no more than five examples of academic production (mandatory).
Please upload this material electronically along with your application.

If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts: shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
• Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as (xxx) at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).
The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About ArtsThe Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts | Aarhus University

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.
