Your focus will be to ensure:

• Clear ownership of and accountability for master data

• Consistent, high-quality data across systems and countries

• Responsible, value-creating use of AI solutions built on a solid data foundation

The role is closely connected to IT, to the business and to senior management, and requires you to move confidently between strategy and practice. You will report to the Head of Digital & IT and become part of the IT department.

Your key responsibilities

• Coordinate and support master data governance across NDI Group

• Work closely with relevant key stakeholders and business areas on the structure, quality and maintenance of master data

• Ensure robust and effective governance for the use of AI within NDI Group

• Help ensure that AI solutions are built on accurate, consistent and documented data

• Coordinate AI-related initiatives across the organisation in collaboration with IT and the business

• Support common methods, principles and guidelines - without creating a burdensome layer of control

• Communicate complex data and AI topics in language that both the business and IT can understand

Your profile

We imagine that you:

• Have experience with master data, data governance, BI, ERP systems (such as D365FO) or related areas

• Have an interest in - or experience with - the application of AI in a business context

• Thrive in a coordinating and communicative role involving many stakeholders

• Work in a structured manner and are able to create clarity and drive progress

• Have strong communication skills and can bridge the gap between IT and the business

• Understand that master data and AI are not solely IT matters, but also management and business disciplines

• Experience with a range of AI tools would be a clear advantage

What we offer

• A central and visible role in a group with ambitious digital goals

• The opportunity to shape how NDI works with data and AI going forward

• Close collaboration with IT, the business and senior management

• An organisation where ideas can quickly be turned into action

• An informal working environment with a high level of professional expertise and strong engagement

Why you should choose NDI Group

You will become part of an ambitious IT team focused on development, digitalisation and continuous improvement. At NDI Group, you will have the opportunity to influence both processes and decisions while building a strong network across the Group.

We believe that the best solutions are created in close collaboration with the business. We are therefore looking for a colleague who is eager to engage, challenge the status quo and make a real difference.

NDI Group consists of, among others, the companies NDI A/S, Super Dæk Service, TyreTrust, Flex1One and J.A.K., and we employ more than 1,100 people across the Nordic countries and Germany.

Interested in learning more about the position?

jobs.occupation: AI Solution Architect to Shape the Future of Retail Technology
jobs.description:
Join Salling Group Tech Innovation as an AI Solution Architect and help turn AI opportunities into reliable solutions that create measurable value across retail operations, decision-making, and customer experiences.

As Denmark’s largest retail group, Salling Group operates at a scale where AI can make a practical difference in everyday work for customers, colleagues, stores, supply chains, and support functions. That gives our ML&AI team a broad and concrete playground for building solutions that move beyond prototypes and into real business impact.

The job

As AI Solution Architect, you will bridge business needs, AI development, data, platforms, and enterprise architecture. You will translate opportunities and sometimes ambiguous requirements into practical solution designs and help guide technical decisions from initial idea through implementation and operation.

You will join our ML&AI team, which develops AI/ML initiatives across brands and departments in Salling Group. You will work closely with business stakeholders, Product Owners, AI Developers, platform teams, security specialists, data specialists, and Enterprise Architects.

The role covers both established machine learning solutions and newer areas such as generative AI, AI agents, and AI-enabled process automation. You will be involved throughout the process, helping to ensure that solutions work not only in theory, but also in practice.

Primary tasks and responsibilities

• Translate business needs and opportunities into clear, actionable AI solution designs covering data, models, applications, integrations, deployment, and lifecycle.

• Evaluate solution options and communicate architectural choices and trade-offs, ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, cost-conscious, maintainable, and compliant with data protection, responsible AI, governance, and regulatory requirements from the start.

• Guide implementation together with AI Developers and other technical specialists through architectural direction, practical sparring, and timely decision-making.

• Stay hands-on where it matters by building prototypes, proof-of-concept code, and architecture-critical components to validate designs, reduce risk, and set the technical direction.

• Define reusable patterns, guardrails, interfaces, and documentation, and support reliable operation through evaluation, observability, monitoring, and lifecycle management.

• Create alignment across business areas, development, data and platform teams, security, and enterprise architecture, and share knowledge that strengthens architectural thinking across the team.

**

We are looking for someone with...**

• A relevant technical degree within Computer Science, Engineering, AI, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Experience designing, developing, integrating, and operating software, data, AI, and machine learning solutions.

• The ability to understand business problems and translate them into coherent technical solutions while considering value, complexity, risk, cost, security, and maintainability.

• An understanding of modern software architecture, APIs, integrations, data flows, and cloud-based platforms, as well as the AI/ML lifecycle from development and deployment to evaluation, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and clearly document solution designs and technical decisions.

• A structured approach to problems that may initially be ambiguous or insufficiently defined.

**

Areas where experience is an advantage**

• Applied AI and generative AI: You have built agent-based, RAG, or AI-enabled workflow solutions and know how to evaluate whether they work in practice. Experience with platforms such as Azure AI Foundry, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, LiteLLM, or similar is an advantage.

• Production and MLOps: You have taken AI/ML solutions from development into production using Python, FastAPI, Scikit-learn, or similar frameworks. You are familiar with CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes, Terraform, ArgoCD, observability, monitoring, logging, and model lifecycle management.

• Data and integration architecture: You have designed data and integration foundations for AI solutions using platforms such as Snowflake, SAP Datasphere, PostgreSQL, and API-based integrations. Experience with semantic models, knowledge graphs, vector search, and identity and access control is an advantage.

• Responsible and governed AI: You have built solutions where security, data protection, AI governance, regulatory requirements, explainability, risk management, and operational guardrails are part of the design from the start.

**

Please note:** You do not need experience across all areas. We are especially interested in candidates who have helped move AI solutions beyond prototypes into reliable, integrated, observable, and maintainable systems.

While the position is targeted towards an AI Solution Architect profile, we recognise that strong candidates come from different backgrounds and career stages. For the right candidate, we may also consider matching the role at Associate AI Solution Architect level.

It will be a strong match if you...

• Are pragmatic and passionate about AI and focus on problems worth solving rather than technology for its own sake. You also like staying close enough to delivery to see whether a design works in practice.

• Ask constructive questions and are comfortable challenging assumptions, including your own, when a direction no longer holds.

• Take ownership while actively seeking input from colleagues and domain experts. You enjoy supporting others through mentoring, knowledge sharing, best practices, and informal leadership.

**

What we offer you

**You will join an experienced and collaborative ML&AI team with room to shape solutions, influence technical direction, and continue developing your expertise across AI architecture, engineering, governance, and real-world retail use cases.

The role gives you the opportunity to influence how AI solutions are designed and implemented while staying close to both business needs and technical delivery.Your daily workplace will be at the Salling Group headquarters in Brabrand, Aarhus.**

Interested?

**At Salling Group, we value diversity and encourage everyone to apply regardless of background. We believe that different perspectives strengthen our team and contribute to innovative solutions.

To apply, please submit your resume and application outlining your relevant experience and why you are a strong fit for the role.

We assess applications on an ongoing basis and reserve the right to close the position when we have found the right candidate. For any inquiries, feel free to contact Miklas Strøm Kristoffersen, Senior Manager, AI, at miklas.stroem.kristoffersen@sallinggroup.com.

Picture your typical week: on Monday you’re on-site at a pharmaceutical client, leading a cross-functional team through a critical MES go-live. By Wednesday you’re working with the IT leadership to turn your delivery results into a business case for the next phase. Friday, you’re back at Emendo’s Nordhavn office sharing what you learned and sharpening the methods your colleagues will use on their projects. If that sounds like work you’d love, keep reading.

Why We’re Hiring Now

We paused hiring over the past year to be deliberate about the team we build next. The consulting market in Denmark has tightened, and our clients have changed how they buy: they want fewer consultants with more experience, people who can walk into a complex situation and show measurable progress within weeks, not months. We are now making a small number of senior hires — each one matters, and we are taking the time to find the right people.

About Emendo

Emendo is a 200-person consultancy built by people who used to sit on the client side — running transformation programmes inside pharma before deciding to do it for a living. We understand the pressure a site director feels before a go-live, we know what an inspector looks for, and we speak the language of the people who operate the systems we implement. We work across the full pharmaceutical value chain from R&D through shipping, with offices in Copenhagen, Kalundborg, Odense, Silkeborg, Munich, and Raleigh (USA). Our strategy is simple: deliver faster, prove value in hard numbers, and use our methods and AI tools to do what we do well — only quicker.

We are a methods-driven firm rooted in operational excellence and Lean. Our motto, Observe, Think, Improve, is itself a method: go to the floor, understand what is actually happening, analyse it rigorously, then design and implement a concrete improvement. That simplicity is what makes it reliable when the project gets complicated and the usual playbooks stop working.

The Role

You will lead IT/OT transformation engagements for clients in pharma and regulated industries — operating at the intersection of technology, business process, and organisational change. You are expected to create measurable impact from the outset, build trusted relationships with client stakeholders, and identify opportunities to expand Emendo’s footprint within your accounts. At Emendo, seniority means more than years served: it means sound judgement in ambiguity, credibility with demanding stakeholders, and the willingness to raise the standard of the whole team.

What You Will Do

• Lead client engagements on-site, owning delivery of IT/OT implementations across enterprise, operations management, process control, and process equipment layers

• Drive measurable progress in short cycles — the kind your client’s leadership can point to in a steering committee: cost reduced, lead time shortened, risk closed out

• Manage project governance, solution architecture alignment, and validation concepts within complex, multi-stakeholder environments

• Shape how Emendo works — contribute to our methods, package what you learn into repeatable offerings and case studies, and use AI tools to deliver faster without cutting corners

• Build lasting client relationships — become a trusted partner to your stakeholders, spot opportunities for follow-on work, and contribute to Emendo’s business development by turning strong delivery into new engagements

• Apply Observe, Think, Improve as your foundation — and mentor junior colleagues to do the same

What It Takes

Must-Have Qualifications

• Master’s degree in engineering, IT, or a related discipline

• 6–10+ years of hands-on delivery experience in IT/OT project management, product ownership, or solution implementation — ideally within pharma or other regulated industries, though strong candidates from adjacent sectors are welcome

• Track record of delivering quantifiable business outcomes (cost reduction, lead-time improvement, risk mitigation) — not just on-time/on-budget projects

• Strong command of project governance, stakeholder management, and the ability to engage credibly with C-suite and senior client leadership

• Deep understanding of at least one area: enterprise systems (ERP/MES), process control, IT–OT convergence, or value chain technology

• Fluent English, both written and spoken; Danish skills are strongly preferred, or a commitment to learn

• Willingness to work on-site at client locations in Denmark and occasionally internationally

Nice to have — but not required

None of the following are dealbreakers. If you tick even one or two, it tells us you will ramp up faster — but we have seen great consultants arrive without any of them and build the expertise here.

• Experience with GxP compliance, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), or regulatory frameworks in life sciences

• Familiarity with AI/automation tools applied to enterprise transformation or operational settings

• Background in operational excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies

• Experience working across multiple sites or geographies in global transformation programmes

• Comfort with outcome-based or fixed-price engagement models

What Makes Emendo Different

• Measured on outcomes, not utilisation — you work directly with industry leaders on engagements that matter

• One integrated firm with deep methods: cross-unit collaboration across Implementation, Engineering, Digital, and R&D, backed by a Lean toolbox and AI accelerators

• Freedom under responsibility — challenging projects with room to shape the solution and your own career

• A flat culture where your input matters and your wins are celebrated

• Competitive compensation reflecting the seniority and impact expected in this role

This role is probably not for you if:

• You prefer purely advisory work with limited implementation responsibility.

• You work best with narrow ownership and very clear boundaries.

• You have strong technical exposure but limited experience leading cross-functional change.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We are hiring two to three Senior Consultants this year. Each one joins a team that has led some of the largest IT/OT programmes in US and European pharma — people who chose Emendo because they wanted senior-level impact in a firm that still feels personal. If that resonates, we’d like to hear from you.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We will be in touch promptly.

For further information, reach out to Mikael Elley (me@emendo.com or +45 24 83 62 01).

jobs.occupation: Are you our new GTM Engineer?
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this cross-functional, individual-contributor role, you will build, operate, and iterate Accutics' GTM revenue system across the entire sales lifecycle: Accounts → contacts → signals → outreach → meetings → pipeline → revenue → expansion.

You will not only be responsible for filling the funnel; you will own the systems, data, routing, and operational efficiency to ensure a seamless handoff, maximum conversion velocity, and a reliable path from activity to revenue using a modern GTM stack (Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...).

You will work side-by-side with our AEs, Product Marketer, and CPO, and report directly to the CEO. This is a hands-on role for a technical self-starter who builds things themselves, takes ownership, experiments quickly, and turns successful tests into production systems.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead Generation & Demand Capture: Build, operate, and iterate targeted, multi-channel campaigns across outbound, ABM, and account expansion to generate qualified meetings, pipeline, and revenue. Build account/contact lists, enrich prospects, identify signals, and activate contacts through appropriate channels.

• Sales Enablement & Alignment: Act as a GTM systems partner to the sales team. Deliver well-qualified accounts and contacts equipped with deep contextual data, signals, and account intelligence. Onboard sales reps into workflows and ensure system transparency so it saves them time rather than becoming a black box.

• AI-Supported Revenue Operations: Build and operate the GTM technology and data stack. Build robust enrichment, scoring, routing, synchronization, and automation workflows.

• Market & Persona Strategy: Translate ICP, enterprise account, and persona strategies into repeatable GTM workflows and continuously iterate based on performance.

• Flawless Tracking: “Drink our own champagne.” Utilize the Accutics platform internally to guarantee that our own campaign tracking, naming conventions, and metadata are perfectly structured from the point of creation. Maintain high-quality GTM and CRM data so pipeline and revenue can be reliably measured.

• Full-Funnel Analytics: Monitor the GTM system and its commercial performance from initial account targeting through closed-won revenue and account expansion. Identify bottlenecks and build solutions to fix them.

What We Are Looking For

Required:

· Enterprise GTM Execution: 1–3 years of hands-on experience in GTM Engineering, GTM Operations, or RevOps, preferably in GTM agency or B2B SaaS. Proven track record taking outbound, ABM, and expansion campaigns from concept to production.

· GTM Engineering & Data: Hands-on experience with Clay (including Function and Workflow capabilities), bidirectional CRM sync with Salesforce, APIs, webhooks, and automation workflow logic.

· AI / Agentic GTM: Experience experimenting with and deploying production multi-agent GTM systems built with Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools.

· Working Style: Highly autonomous, operationally disciplined, and commercially minded, measuring success by quality pipeline and revenue, not top-of-funnel metrics.

A Plus:

· Experience with GTM tools such as email and LinkedIn sequencers, unified inboxes, email infrastructure, enrichment, intent/signal, LinkedIn social warming, call dialer.

· Experience building other GTM workflows: account expansion/ churn/ partner sales/ inbound flywheel.

· Experience building Salesforce CRM data foundation, CRM data cleaning routines for modern GTM.

· Comfortable handling SQL, Agent loops.

What We Offer

· Ownership: Build, operate, and iterate Accutics' new GTM revenue system across the sales lifecycle.

· Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...

· Commercial Impact: Direct impact on pipeline generation, deal velocity, and revenue while returning time to sales teams.

· Agile Environment: Small, international SaaS team with high autonomy, short decision paths, and direct leadership access.

· Copenhagen Office: Central Copenhagen location, Nordic work-life balance, flexible hours, and regular social events.

· Package: Permanent full-time position, competitive salary, pension, and benefits.

Requirements

• You have a valid work permit to work in Europe (Denmark).

• You are fluent in English, both verbally and in writing.

• You are located in the Greater Copenhagen Area (Denmark) or will be relocating here.

Hiring Process

1. GTM Builder Interview: Meet a GTM builder and demonstrate systems you have built and deployed.

2. CEO Interview: Discuss Accutics, the role, and how you will shape the GTM engine.

3. Build Together Session: Collaboratively solve a real GTM challenge to demonstrate your build and testing approach.

What Success Looks Like (3-6 Months)

· Take full build and iteration responsibility for Accutics' GTM revenue system.

· Establish and run daily operational routines, onboarding sales reps to maintain workflow transparency.

· Bring the Salesforce data foundation up to the standard of your new GTM system.

· Continuously test new tools, workflows, and solutions to eliminate sales friction and deliver quality pipeline and revenue.

About Accutics

Accutics is a Copenhagen-based B2B SaaS company providing the ultimate data foundation for global enterprise marketing. We work with the world’s leading brands. Our platform standardizes campaign tracking, governs taxonomy, and ensures data is AI-ready, eliminating manual QA loops for confident, data-informed decisions.

Proud of our Nordic roots, we combine deep domain expertise with close collaboration. We are a small, international team looking for a GTM Engineer to build, operate, and continuously improve a modern, AI-native revenue system across the entire funnel.

How to Apply

Think you’re the right fit? Apply today by submitting your resume and a brief cover letter. You can email it to careers@accutics.com.

Would you like to help build and develop the platform that makes it easier for Whiteaway’s software Engineers to develop, deploy and run their solutions?

Whiteaway Group is looking for a skilled Platform Engineer to join their Platform Squad in Aarhus.

As a Platform Engineer, you will become part of a strong technical environment focused on building and continuously improving the platform used by Whiteaway’s development teams in their daily work.

This is not traditional IT operations. Instead, the focus is on creating automated, stable and scalable solutions that make it easier for Engineers to develop, deploy and run their software.

Whiteaway is a digital-first company where technology plays a central role in the business. The company operates some of the largest online stores in the Nordics within electronics and home appliances, and its technical platforms are an important part of the continued development of the business.

Your role

You will play a central role in developing and improving Whiteaway’sinternal platform and will work closely with software Engineers and the other members of the Platform Squad.

A key part of the role is the close collaboration with Engineers. You will be curious about how they work, understand their needs and challenges, and use their feedback to identify how workflows, processes and platform tooling can be made simpler, faster and better.

Over the coming years, Whiteaway will be taking the platform to a significantly higher level. A key focus will be reducing and removing legacy and building a more modern, scalable and developer-friendly platform. AI will also play an increasingly important role in how the platform develops and how Whiteaway’s Engineers work.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Developing and continuously improving the cloud platform

• Automating deployment and development processes

• Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD pipelines

• Containerisation and Kubernetes

• Cloud infrastructure – primarily AWS

• Monitoring, observability and reliability

• Engineering tooling and self-service solutions

• Security and access management

• Troubleshooting and optimising platform performance and stability

The role offers a high degree of freedom, and you will have the opportunity to take ownership and influence both the technology and the way the team works.

Whiteaway believes in freedom under responsibility. You will have the opportunity to take ownership, influence technical decisions and help shape both the platform and the way the team works.

We imagine that you…

You have a strong technical background and experience within software development, cloud, DevOps or platform engineering. Perhaps you are already working as a Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer or Senior Software Engineer with strong cloud and infrastructure experience.

Your title is less important than your motivation to work hands-on with platform engineering and your ability to thrive at the intersection of software development, cloud and operations. Experience with general software development is an advantage, particularly Node.js and/or Go.

We would like you to have experience with several of the following technologies and tools:

• AWS

• Kubernetes

• Docker

• Terraform / Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD

• Git/GitHub

• Linux

• Node.js and/or Go

• Datadog

• ArgoCD

• Spacelift

• Cloudflare

• Monitoring and observability

• Networking and cloud infrastructure

Experience with GitOps is an advantage, but not a requirement. Experience with security or with the intersection between operations and software development is also considered an advantage.

You do not need to know everything. What matters most is that you have strong technical curiosity, can understand complex problems and are motivated to continuously improve the way things are done.

Your professional development is important to Whiteaway.

You will have the opportunity to work with development plans, strengthen your technical skills and take your expertise to the next level. At the same time, knowledge sharing is an important part of the culture – you are expected not only to develop yourself, but also to help lift others around you.

On a personal level, drive, determination and humility are highly valued. You take ownership and get things done, while remaining curious, collaborative and motivated to find the best solutions together with others.

What Whiteaway offers

At Whiteaway, you will be part of an informal, inclusive and supportive leadership culture where Engineers have real ownership and the opportunity to influence their work. The culture is built around experimentation, knowledge sharing and continuous learning, with opportunities to take part in hackathons, pair programming and MOB programming, as well as access to learning resources.

The social side of working together is also important. People at Whiteaway genuinely enjoy working together, and there is a strong focus on building good relationships across the team. Through activities such as hackathons, Improvement Mondays and other social initiatives, there are plenty of opportunities to come together, share knowledge, experiment and have fun.

Whiteaway also values a healthy work-life balance, a great lunch and good colleagues. The office is located in Skejby, with free parking.

About Whiteaway Group

Whiteaway Group is a tribe of 300+ passionate people working across Scandinavia, selling and shipping appliances through e-commerce, franchise stores and B2B channels.

Around 250 employees are based at the headquarters in Aarhus, covering the group’s central functions. Around 45 people work within Tech across IT, Engineering and Product. The Platform Squad currently consists of four Platform Engineers, and the team is expected to grow in the coming years as the demands on and use of the platform continue to increase – including with the growing use of AI.

With brands like Skousen, Tretti and Whiteaway, the group is grounded in innovation and honesty, always pushing for better customer experiences through technology.

Interested in joining Whiteaway Group?

Bloom is handling the recruitment process on behalf of Whiteaway Group and is actively reviewing applications. We look forward to receiving your application and CV in Danish or English as soon as possible.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact IT Recruitment Manager Dorte Pape at Bloom at dp@bloom.dk or on +45 3160 9365.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. As the most senior engineer on the team, you will own the technical direction of the platform security, identity, and network security slice, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across platform security, identity, and network security, and rolling out the first paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, CVE response, CI/CD identity, and a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen). You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers write, review and ship secure systems.

What You Will Do

You will join a focused platform security team and operate as its most senior engineer. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities, and we expect this role to set the bar.

• Design and build the paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, and CVE response, running inside the pipelines teams already use, with findings routed to the owners who can fix them under tracked SLAs

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for a unified internal network and VPN across GCP, AWS, and our Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen offices, while the team that owns the network keeps running it

• Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own

• Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves

• Build audit logging as a shared capability that teams plug into rather than reinvent

• Turn GRC controls into technical implementations, with evidence pipelines that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Own the contracting cycle for external penetration tests and build the intake, classification, and tracking system that routes findings to named owners, while the owning teams remediate

• Hand each capability off cleanly, with a runbook, a named owner, and an escalation path, and run office hours where product and platform teams can get a security review or a paved-road question answered

• Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

What You Could Bring

This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

• Platform security: you have run vulnerability scanning, CVE management, and image scanning at scale, and you know the operational reality of getting CVEs fixed, beyond standing up the tooling

• Identity and auth: you have worked hands-on inside an auth codebase, rolled out MFA on live systems, and managed token lifecycles in CI/CD with OIDC and workload identity

• Network security at scale: you have designed and run a unified internal network across multiple cloud providers and offices, with a VPN approach that holds up

• Platform-as-product mindset: you have built internal security tooling that other teams chose to adopt, with guard rails built into the tools developers already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured the impact

• Infrastructure as Code: strong experience with Terraform, Crossplane, or similar

Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

How We Work

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. This role sets the technical direction for the team's quarterly missions. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on three or four items but not all of them, apply anyway. The "deep in one, ready to grow into the other" framing above is not a hedge, it is how we actually hire at this level. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy, and Environmental Medicine at the Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health, University of Southern Denmark, is offering a new 5-year (20%) position for an Associate Professor within clinical pharmacy. The position is to be filled from February 1st, 2027.

The academic position

The research areas of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM) span from pharmacological epidemiology to clinical studies and cell-based basic pharmacology. CPPEM has a strong background in investigations of exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. The academic position is affiliated with the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, that utilizes the Danish registries to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. 

The area of research is flexible within the area of pharmacoepidemiologic and clinical research and could be (but is not limited to) drug use patterns and rational pharmacotherapy. The department has a strong focus on interdisciplinary collaboration both in-house and with external researchers and the new person is expected to continue this tradition.
 

Areas of responsibility

The applicant will be expected to establish their own research area within the pharmacoepidemiologic research group at the department. Thus, the applicant should be able to attract external research funding to support research and employ scientific and technical staff. The applicant may have a background within pharmacy or medicine.

The research unit teaches in four educations: Medicine, Pharmacy, Chiropractor, and Biomedicine, and the position comes with teaching obligations within these subjects at the University as well as supervision of bachelor and master projects. Additionally, we expect that you will contribute to administrative duties, e.g., participating in Study Board or other similar activities. 

Fluent English (both written and spoken) is required. You are expected to have qualifications that renders it probable that you will be able to establish your own research area within the research unit. Further, you are required to have a PhD degree or similar research experience. 
 

Employers

Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine today has approximately 50 employees. It consists of three separate research groups: pharmacoepidemiology, translational pharmacology, and environmental medicine. Additionally, it collaborates closely with the Department of Pharmacology at OUH. Collectively, this constitutes Denmark’s largest center for research, teaching and clinical service in pharmacology.

It produces approximately 100 international peer-reviewed publications per year. 

Professor Tore B. Stage heads the unit and Professor Pernille Tanggaard Andersen heads the Department.

Management

The Associate Professor answers to the research leader for the unit of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine.
 

Contact information

Further information can be obtained from the leader for the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, Professor Anton Pottegård (apottegaard@health.sdu.dk).
 

Application deadline and interviews

November 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CET
 

Salary and terms of employment

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Applications will be assessed by an expert committee. Applicants will be informed of their assessment by the university.

Applications – including the required attachments – must be sent via the below-mentioned link “Apply online". Only online applications will be accepted. Attached files must be Adobe PDF or Word format. Each field in the application form can contain up to max. 10 MB.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.
 

Application (as pdf- or Word/docx- files):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (inclusive of PhD diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please notice that one pdf- or docx- file must be attached for each publication

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

References will be obtained for the applicant who is the first choice for the position – from the applicant’s most recent employer and previous employers as required.

Further particulars concerning the application – please see the link below.

********Job Description Summary

********The International Clinical Education & Strategy CVUS manager is responsible for defining and executing the clinical education and alignment strategy across regions in close collaboration with internal stakeholders and external partners. The role ensures strong clinical differentiation of the product portfolio through effective education programs, third‑party partnerships, and close alignment with Marketing on competitive positioning to maximize sales effectiveness and win rate. the clinical education manager reports to the CVUS GM International.

**

Le/La Responsable International(e) de la Formation Clinique et de la Stratégie CVUS est chargé(e) de définir et de déployer la stratégie internationale de formation clinique et d’alignement, en étroite collaboration avec les parties prenantes internes et les partenaires externes.

Ce rôle garantit une forte différenciation clinique du portefeuille produits grâce à des programmes de formation efficaces, des partenariats avec des tiers et un alignement étroit avec le Marketing sur le positionnement concurrentiel, afin de maximiser l’efficacité commerciale et le taux de concrétisation des ventes.

Le/La Responsable de la formation clinique reporte au Directeur Général CVUS International.

****Job Description

******Key Responsibilities

****Clinical Education & International Clinical Management

**

• Define and lead the international clinical education strategy across regions, ensuring consistency, quality, and alignment with business priorities.

• Develop, deploy, and continuously optimize clinical education programs addressing customer needs, care pathways, and evolving clinical practices.

• Coordinate and align regional clinical leaders to ensure consistent execution of clinical education initiatives at international level.

• Monitor clinical education outcomes and leverage insights to improve adoption, customer engagement, and clinical confidence.

**Third‑Party & Industry Partnerships

**

• Establish and manage strategic partnerships with third‑party organizations, including medical device companies, education providers, and clinical institutions.

• Co‑develop joint educational initiatives, clinical programs, and content to enhance clinical credibility and market impact.

• Ensure all partnerships comply with regulatory, ethical, and company standards while delivering measurable value.

**Clinical Alignment with Marketing & Competitive Strategy

**

• Act as the clinical partner to the Marketing Director and Marketing teams to ensure strong clinical alignment in go‑to‑market strategies.

• Lead clinical input into competitive analysis, translating market and competitor insights into clear clinical value propositions.

• Adapt and validate battle cards and competitive tools by integrating clinical arguments aligned to competitive products and customer decision drivers.

• Support the optimization of win rate by ensuring sales teams are equipped with clinically relevant, differentiated, and credible competitive messaging.

**Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Strategy Execution

**

• Work closely with Sales, Marketing, Product Management, and R&D to ensure clinical insights are integrated into product positioning, roadmap discussions, and launch strategies.

• Communicate and monitor the execution and alignment of clinical strategies across international regions and zones.

• Provide regular feedback to senior leadership on clinical priorities, competitive landscape, and education performance.

****Qualifications

• Senior profile with an experience in the medical industry

• Experience in ultrasound & Cardiology

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Excellent organizational skills

• Willingness and ability to travel 50% of time

• Valid motor vehicle license

• Experience with interfacing with both internal team members, external customers and industrial group

• Working level English

• Ability to develop and execute multiple priorities and approaches to meet objectives

• Direct customer relationship experience

• Proven ability to effectively communicate across a distributed workforce

**Responsabilités clés

****Formation clinique et management clinique international

**

• Définir et piloter la stratégie internationale de formation clinique à travers les régions, en garantissant la cohérence, la qualité et l’alignement avec les priorités business.

• Développer, déployer et optimiser en continu des programmes de formation clinique répondant aux besoins des clients, aux parcours de soins et à l’évolution des pratiques cliniques.

• Coordonner et aligner les responsables cliniques régionaux afin d’assurer une exécution cohérente des initiatives de formation clinique au niveau international.

• Suivre les résultats des actions de formation clinique et exploiter les retours pour améliorer l’adoption, l’engagement des clients et la confiance clinique.

**Partenariats tiers et partenariats industriels

**

• Établir et gérer des partenariats stratégiques avec des organisations tierces, notamment des fabricants de dispositifs médicaux, des organismes de formation et des institutions cliniques.

• Co‑développer des initiatives éducatives conjointes, des programmes cliniques et des contenus visant à renforcer la crédibilité clinique et l’impact marché.

• S’assurer que tous les partenariats respectent les exigences réglementaires, éthiques et les standards de l’entreprise, tout en générant une valeur mesurable.

**Alignement clinique avec le marketing et la stratégie concurrentielle

**

• Agir en tant que partenaire clinique du/de la Directeur(trice) Marketing et des équipes marketing afin d’assurer un fort alignement clinique des stratégies de mise sur le marché.

• Piloter l’apport clinique aux analyses concurrentielles et traduire les informations marché et concurrentielles en propositions de valeur clinique claires.

• Adapter et valider les battle cards et outils concurrentiels en intégrant des arguments cliniques alignés sur les produits concurrents et les critères de décision des clients.

• Contribuer à l’optimisation du taux de gain en dotant les équipes commerciales de messages concurrentiels cliniquement pertinents, différenciants et crédibles.

**Collaboration transverse et exécution de la stratégie

**

• Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Ventes, Marketing, Gestion de Produits et R&D afin d’intégrer les retours cliniques dans le positionnement produit, les discussions de roadmap et les stratégies de lancement.

• Communiquer et suivre l’exécution et l’alignement des stratégies cliniques à travers les régions et zones internationales.

• Fournir régulièrement à la direction des retours sur les priorités cliniques, le paysage concurrentiel et la performance des actions de formation.

****Qualifications Requises

• Une certaine séniorité dans l’industrie du médical

• Expérience en échographie et en cardiologie

• Excellentes compétences de communication écrites et orales

• Excellentes compétences organisationnelles

• Disponibilité et capacité à voyager jusqu’à 50 % du temps

• Permis de conduire valide

• Expérience d’interaction avec des équipes internes, des clients externes et des groupes industriels

• Anglais professionnel courant

• Capacité à développer et exécuter plusieurs priorités et approches pour atteindre les objectifs

• Expérience avérée de relation directe avec les clients

• Capacité démontrée à communiquer efficacement au sein d’une organisation distribuée

At Trustpilot, we're on an incredible journey. We're a profitable, high-growth FTSE-250 company with a big vision: to become the universal symbol of trust. We run the world's largest open customer review platform, and while we've come a long way, there's still so much exciting work to do. Come join us at the heart of trust!

Join our Identity and Access Management (IAM) team within our broader technology department. In this role, you will work cross-functionally across Security, HR Ops, Privacy, and IT to manage critical access and secure resources enterprise-wide. We foster a healthy, transparent, and highly collaborative environment where you can work with state-of-the-art tech and leverage our AI investments to innovate in the IAM space.

As an Identity & Access Management Analyst, you will take ownership of the day-to-day disciplines that govern how colleagues access the systems they need. Working directly within the wider IT Operations and Identity & Access Management function, you will run the joiner, mover and leaver processes, handle incoming access requests, administer privileged access, and run and improve our access review programme, working with system owners to confirm who should have access, and with auditors to evidence that it is right. Your efforts will directly shape how quickly and securely our team members get the access required to do their best work.

This role needs both sides. You will configure access, troubleshoot sign-in issues and grow into application onboarding with Single Sign-On (SSO) and automated user provisioning (SCIM). Just as much of your week will be spent working with people: walking system owners through access reviews, agreeing who should have access to what, answering auditors' questions, and keeping HR Ops in step on starters and leavers. We are looking for someone who is as comfortable leading a conversation with a system owner or auditor. You will have support from senior team members on more complex work.

What You'll Be Doing

• Access Administration & Ticketing: Serve as the operational contact for IAM ticketing, managing end-to-end user access lifecycles, including ticketing queues, approvals and access provisioning, while driving process improvements through automation.

• Identity Lifecycle & Provisioning Management: Partner with HR Operations to oversee end-to-end Joiner, Mover, and Leaver (JML) workflows for employees and contractors—ensuring precision day-one access, timely deprovisioning, and swift operational pivot capabilities during last-minute schedule and scope shifts.

• Access Reviews & Certification: Run and continuously improve our access review programme. Set up new review cycles as applications come into scope, walk reviewers through what they are being asked to confirm, chase completion, and make sure revocations are carried out.

• System Ownership & Access Coordination: Connect regularly with system owners to help clarify access roles, coordinate baseline permission levels, and maintain clear, straightforward review guidelines for teams.

• Audit & Compliance Partnership: Be the point of contact on access controls for internal audit, external auditors (SOC 2) and financial systems audits. Walk auditors through how our controls work, provide evidence, and follow findings through to closure with the relevant teams.

• Manage Elevated Permissions: Administer privileged and administrative access, ensuring elevated permissions are time-bound, justified, and regularly reviewed.

• Maintain Reliable Identity Data: Govern group memberships, access roles, and HR system integrations to ensure identity data remains accurate across systems.

• Application Onboarding: Integrate new SaaS tools with our Identity Management (IdP) using SSO (SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect) and SCIM where supported, defining access groups and initial permission levels. Where SCIM is not supported, follow a documented manual process with proper checks.

• Stakeholder & Vendor Liaison: Support internal system owners and external software providers by helping troubleshoot user access requests and ensuring platform permissions stay accurate and up to date.

• Solve Access Challenges: Support colleagues when access issues arise, looking into root causes to build lasting, friendly solutions rather than short-term fixes.

• Automate & Streamline: Look for repetitive tasks that can be simplified or automated, and work with the team to improve them.

Who You Are

• Identity Experience: Background in an IT or Identity & Access Management role using a modern identity provider. Experience with IdP is a plus, but experience with a comparable platform is welcome.

• Confident with Stakeholders: Confident in proactively reaching out to new colleagues, facilitating structured discussions, and serving as a trusted advisor to help leaders at any level navigate and understand access policies.

• Governance Experience: Has run or supported access reviews, and is comfortable walking an auditor through how a control works. Experience with SOC 2 or financial systems audits (IT general controls) is a strong plus.

• Hands-on Lifecycle Experience: Practical experience handling joiner, mover and leaver work, access requests, or user administration, with an appreciation for why accurate access matters to people's day-to-day work.

• Influences Without Authority: Partner thoughtfully with busy system owners and leadership to complete routine access reviews and remove unnecessary permissions, using clear communication, proactive follow-ups, and genuine professional relationships to keep security hygiene on track.

• Single Sign-On & Provisioning: Practical experience configuring enterprise SSO alongside vendors or app owners, backed by an understanding of SAML, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Exposure to SCIM, or a solid grasp of the concepts. Comfortable with scripting or keen to learn.

• Familiar with Modern Security: Comfortable with access controls like multi-factor authentication and conditional access, as well as modern sign-in options, from one-time codes to authenticator apps, passkeys and certificates, and why some offer stronger protection.

• Ownership & Follow-Through: Chases the open review, closes the loop on the finding, and doesn't let a ticket go quiet. Juggles requests, review deadlines and last-minute HR changes without dropping things.

• Curious & Methodical Problem-Solver: Able to troubleshoot sign-in flows independently and find the root cause rather than the quick fix, recognising that identity work carries a low tolerance for mistakes.

• Clear Communicator: Explains things clearly in person and in writing, including documentation and evidence that an auditor can follow without a walkthrough.

What's in it for you:

• A range of flexible working options to dedicate time to what matters to you

• Competitive compensation package + bonus

• 25 days holiday per year, with an extra 5 days holiday allocated after your 1 year anniversary (prorated)

• Two (paid) volunteering days a year to spend your time giving back to the causes that matter to you and your community

• Rich learning and development opportunities are supported through the Trustpilot Academy and Blinkist

• Comprehensive health package, pension, and full access to Headspace, a popular mindfulness app to promote positive mental health

• Paid parental leave

• Central office with  a laid-back vibe and constant buzz of different languages being spoken everywhere you go It’s complete with a coffee bar, canteen, and table tennis and has a wide variety of refreshments available - you can opt-in for breakfast and lunch at an affordable price

• Regular opportunities to connect and get to know your fellow Trusties, including company-wide celebrations and events, ERG activities, and team socials

• Opportunity to join the Trustpilot Social Club for a small monthly fee and attend regular social and leisure activities like go-karting, cooking classes, and escape rooms

• Employee discounts to restaurants and shops

Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• 
Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• 
Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• 
Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• 
Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• 
Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• 
Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• 
Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• 
Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• 
Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

A brief overview of our tech stack:

• 
Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• 
PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• 
OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• 
Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• 
Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• 
AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 
1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• 
Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• 
You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• 
A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• 
Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• 
Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

AI Competency

• 
You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• 
GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• 
ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• 
Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• 
Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• 
AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• 
We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• 
Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• 
Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• 
The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• 
The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• 
A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• 
A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• 
Free lunch every day.

• 
Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• 
Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• 
Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• 
Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

Please send us your application in English.

To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Nanostructured 2D Materials and van der Waals Heterostructures for Advanced Optoelectronics - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in engineering materials at the atomic scale and exploring how nanoscale structures can enable new optoelectronic functionalities? 

 At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to break new ground in 2D materials and create artificial material architectures with properties that go beyond those of naturally occurring materials.

 We are seeking a candidate for a PhD Scholarship in Nanostructured 2D Materials and van der Waals Heterostructures for Advanced Optoelectronics. 

 The position is offered within the framework of the Novo Nordisk Foundation NERD program “Quantum Interfaces”, which explores how interfaces and interactions between low-dimensional materials can be engineered to create new optoelectronic functionalities. You will be part of an ambitious research team comprising two PhD students and three postdoctoral researchers, working closely together on the synthesis, engineering, characterization, and fundamental understanding of 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures. The project will provide a highly collaborative environment combining complementary expertise in materials growth, nanoscale fabrication, advanced spectroscopy, optoelectronic characterization, and device physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
 The primary responsibilities of the PhD student include:
 
• Fabricate 2D and van der Waals heterostructures using mechanical exfoliation, deterministic transfer, and controlled stacking of atomically thin crystals. 
• Develop nanofabrication strategies for patterning materials into nanoribbons. 
• Perform structural, optical, and optoelectronic characterization using techniques such as AFM, conductive-AFM, Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and photocurrent mapping. 
• Fabricate and characterize optoelectronic devices to investigate how material structure and device geometry influence their photoresponse. 
• Supervise and contribute to MSc/BSc student projects. 
• Document and disseminate research through scientific publications and international conference contributions.
The ideal candidate should have a strong academic background in physics, nanotechnology, materials science, electrical engineering, photonics, or a related field.

 Experience with 2D materials, nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy, deterministic transfer, electron-beam lithography, or cleanroom fabrication is an advantage.

 You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
 The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
 The assessment of the application will be made by Stela Canulescu and Ganesh Ghimire. 

We offer
 DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
 The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

 The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is full-time position.

 You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
 Further information may be obtained from Stela Canulescu, email: stec@dtu.dk. 

 You can read more about the Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering at www.electro.dtu.dk.

 If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
 Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 October (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:
 
• A letter motivating the application (cover letter) 
• Curriculum vitae  
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale 
• List of publications (if applicable) 
• A brief letter of interest describing your motivation for the PhD project and highlighting relevant skills and experience.
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

 Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

 All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

_Most machine learning never makes it to production. Your job is to make sure ours does. We are looking for an ML Engineer who turns models into reliable, maintained systems that construction companies actually use to make better decisions about their equipment and operations. Shape how we build and run ML. Influence the tools, engineering practices, and deployment patterns that take solutions from an initial idea through to production and continuous improvement.

**

• You bring strong Python skills and solid software engineering practices, including testing, version control, code reviews, and CI/CD.

• Databricks expertise is a significant advantage.

jobs.description:
Ambu A/S is currently looking for a Global Process Owner, Order to Cash to be based in Denmark

In this role, you will own Ambu’s global end-to-end Order to Cash process within our ERP transformation, covering sales planning, order management, distribution, invoicing, customer service and collections. You will report to the Global Operations Program Director, with dual reporting to the Director, Supply Chain Transformation, and work closely with Global Business Owners, other Global Process Owners, Commercial, IT, Finance, Quality and site leadership.

This is a unique opportunity to create a globally aligned Order to Cash capability and set the standard for how it operates across Ambu. It will suit an experienced leader who combines strategic thinking with the ability to deliver transformation at scale.

**Key Responsibilities

**Your main responsibilities will include:

• Owning the global Order to Cash process vision, standards, governance and roadmap

• Acting as Business Workstream Lead and driving fit-to-standard design

• Leading process decisions that balance service, cash, compliance and customer experience

• Establishing process KPIs and driving readiness and adoption across countries

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

**Lead customer software implementation from onboarding to go-live

**_At UNEEG Medical, we are on a clear mission: improve epilepsy care and enhance patients' quality of life through objective, real-world EEG data. UNEEG EpiSight Solution, our sub-cutaneous EEG monitoring solution enables remote monitoring of brain activity in people with uncontrolled epilepsy and is already making an impact across Europe and the US. We combine the agility of a small company with the high standards of the medical device industry.

You will be part of Customer Enablement and Governance and act as the primary program interface between customers and UNEEG. The role coordinates commercial, technical, clinical, legal/data privacy, cybersecurity and quality stakeholders, while the relevant specialists remain accountable for their evidence and decisions. You will work closely together with colleagues across the entire organization.

**Your main responsibilities will be:

**

• Lead customer onboarding and implementation plans, including milestones, risks, decisions and escalations

• Drive infrastructure readiness, installation, validation, go-live and hypercare activities

• Maintain implementation playbooks, templates, status reporting, evidence requests and knowledge repositories

• Coordinate operational handover to support and drive continuous improvement through implementation KPIs and lessons learned

• Create scalable software implementation processes that support growth in our focus markets

**You will thrive in this role if you:

**

• Are customer-focused, collaborative and pragmatic, with the ability to build trust across technical and non-technical groups

• Create structure and momentum without waiting for perfect processes

• Are highly structured, accountable and proactive, with strong planning, documentation and follow-through

• Are comfortable with ambiguity, changing priorities and leading through influence

• Can balance customer requirements, patient impact, compliance and internal priorities without cutting corners

• Have sound judgement and a hands-on, solution-oriented mindset

**Your background:

**

• A bachelor's degree or higher in engineering, computer science, health technology, life sciences, business, project management or a related discipline

• At least 3 years of program or project management experience in customer-facing software implementations

• Experience from healthcare technology, SaaS, enterprise software or medical devices

• Proven cross-functional stakeholder leadership and confident customer communication

• Experience managing multiple complex implementations in an evolving environment

• Fluent professional English, both written and spoken, and willingness to travel

**It will be an advantage if you have experience with:

**

• Hospital IT deployment, clinical engineering or digital health implementation

• Regulated software, validation and medical device quality systems

• Privacy, cybersecurity and assurance reviews, including GDPR, HIPAA, DPIA, HECVAT, SIG, MDS2, DTAC or DSPT

• Relevant standards such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, ISO 13485 or IEC 81001-5-1

• Healthcare systems in both the US and Europe

Applicants must be eligible to work in Denmark and possess a valid work and residence permit if applicable. At this time, we are unable to support work permit applications or sponsorships.

**

• Close collaboration with skilled colleagues and international hospital stakeholders

• A workplace with great energy, social activities and a culture of togetherness

• A role based at our modern HQ in Allerød with good facilities and easy access

At UNEEG, your ideas matter, your work makes a difference, and your colleagues have your back.

**For more details about the job, please contact VP Commercial, Kristian Lykke Fick, at +45 53 39 80 18.

All applications must be in English and are treated confidentially. We screen applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

We collaborate with leading institutions across Europe and the US to help patients regain control of their life. At UNEEG Medical, we are currently 40 dedicated people with diverse backgrounds.
