jobs.occupation: Computational and Data Staff Scientist Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design
jobs.description:
We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent computational and data scientist to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD), University of Copenhagen (UCPH). The post suits someone with experience in computational chemistry, biology, and/or structural biology, as well as managing big data. This is a full-time position, starting 1 February 2027 and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research
 The CPD is a new initiative at UCPH. It is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, that is, designing proteins that are fit for purpose such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Data science at CPD: Increasingly, modern protein science is about data: collecting it, organising it, analysing it, and learning from it to build a deeper understanding of how proteins fold and function. Protein design is no different. Indeed, through the application of generative AI, it is at the leading edge of the confluence of data science and protein science. To coordinate this in the CPD, we are looking for someone experienced in and excited about working at this interface.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/

  Your job
 Specifically, we seek a talented computational and data scientist and team player to help develop research infrastructure, including hardware and computational tools, to advance the CPD’s research and mission. The successful candidate will join a growing multidisciplinary team to help collect, organise, analyse, and exploit data from computationally designed protein sequences and structural models, through protein expression levels, and onto a wide range of experimental structure-function studies. A key part of the role will be integrating into the wider team and working collaboratively with CPD researchers, rather than simply providing a data-management service. For example, we anticipate that the successful candidate would assist with and lead on various projects with CPD researchers to develop robust, reliable, and scalable data and computational tools to enable the very best protein design.

  Key responsibilities will include

   	
• Helping establish CPD's computational infrastructure to provide computing and data management for its researchers 	
• Developing automated pipelines that convert raw instrument output files directly into data plots suitable for analysis, saving time and resources across the research pipeline 	
• Collecting data and generating databases of designed proteins, e.g., constructs, sequences, models, and biophysical data (LIMS) 	
• Assisting in the development of new predictive models based on the gathered experimental and computational data using machine learning methods 	
• Being responsible for data management plans at the CPD and coordinating these plans with the host departments 	
• Related to the above, managing (i.e., best practice in collecting, organising, accessing) data generated by computational protein design workflows and by the CPD’s Protein Biophysics Facility 	
• Advising and training CPD scientists in creating and analysing large computational datasets, linking their experimental data and computational data to extract key information, and managing their computational protein design pipelines 	
• Contributing to, and where appropriate leading, grant applications for and publications from CPD research projects 	
• Teaching appropriate aspects of the above on CPD Master’s and PhD courses 	
• Serving as the primary technical bridge between the CPD and central KU IT to set up CPD’s computing systems in close collaboration with KU IT and establish internal data processing environments   Qualifications and expectations
 To succeed in this role, we anticipate that your areas of expertise could include one or more of the following:

   	
• Computational protein modelling and, ideally, design 	
• Protein or biomolecular sequence data and analysis 	
• Collection, manipulation and use of data from protein biophysics and structural biology 	
• Use and understanding of modern biomolecular statistical data analysis, including ML and AI methods, and generative AI for protein modelling and design 	
• Experience of establishing computational infrastructures for the above   Essential experience and skills

   	
• A PhD in bioinformatics, data science or a related domain, e.g. computational/structural biology 	
• Excellent knowledge of scientific computing and coding languages, e.g., Python 	
• Documented experience (e.g., scientific publications) in machine learning, scientific computing, and similar 	
• An active interest in protein design, engineering, and structure  	
• A proven ability to work with others on challenging multidisciplinary problems 	
• A team player keen on collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds and who is service-minded with clear organisational, communication, and networking skills. 	
• Excellent skills in written and spoken English   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Knowledge of experimental protein science, for example, biophysical methods and/or structural biology 	
• Experience in computational molecular/structural biology   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Salary and terms of employment
 The employment is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with a fixed-term until 31 July 2032. The starting date will be 1 February 2027.

  Depending on qualifications the position will take place as Special Consultant or Senior Consultant in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority), with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Center Manager Gretchen Repasky, Gretchen.repasky@bio.ku.dk.

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page). 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two referees) (max. two pages)  	
• List of publications including preprints (no limit, but do not include copies of the papers) 	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below.

  Application deadline: 8 November 2026

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.
 The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration. 

  As part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching to the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Sustainable Indoor Solar Cells for Ambient Light Energy Harvesting in IoT Applications - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing thin-film solar cells designed to operate efficiently under indoor lighting and thereby contributing to the green transition? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to break new ground by harvesting energy from ambient light and help pave the way towards sustainable technologies.

The Thin-Film Photovoltaics Group at DTU Electro is seeking candidates for a PhD Scholarship focused on the development and characterization of highly efficient Sb₂S₃ solar cells. You will investigate materials, interfaces, and device architectures to understand and overcome the fundamental limitations of photovoltaic performance under low-light conditions.

The position is offered within the framework of DTU’s Alliances and Strategic Partnerships with Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Estonia. You will be part of an international research collaboration combining thin-film synthesis, solar-cell fabrication, advanced optoelectronic and defect characterization, and device testing under realistic illumination conditions. As part of the PhD project, you will undertake a research stay at TalTech and work closely with researchers from both universities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project focuses on developing high-efficiency Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells for indoor energy harvesting. The project will investigate how material properties, interfaces, and device architecture influence charge transport, recombination, and voltage losses under low-intensity illumination. The overall objective is to develop solar cells optimized for indoor light and demonstrate series-connected mini-modules capable of powering battery-free IoT devices.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Develop and optimize Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells by engineering device architectures and interfaces to enhance charge collection while minimizing recombination and voltage losses under indoor illumination.
• Characterize solar cells under different LED spectra, light intensities, and illumination conditions relevant to realistic indoor environments.
• Investigate defect states, interface recombination, and open-circuit voltage losses, including advanced electrical characterization during a research stay at TalTech.
• Develop and characterize series-connected indoor photovoltaic mini-modules for battery-free IoT applications.
• Supervise and contribute to MSc/BSc student projects.
• Document and disseminate the research through scientific publications and international conference contributions
You should have a strong academic background in physics, chemistry, materials science, nanotechnology, or a related field. Prior knowledge of semiconductor physics and photovoltaics, and experience with thin-film materials, solar-cell fabrication, optoelectronic characterization, or indoor photovoltaics, would be particularly valuable.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be made by Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms. 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is the 1 February 2027. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from the Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu, email stec@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Are you a talented hacker with a passion for data engineering and building things that actually run in production? Do you enjoy working close to the metal, solving real problems, and seeing your code go live within hours?

Then you might be the next Quant Infrastructure Student joining our team at Alipes!

About Alipes

At Alipes Capital, we have been a market leader in automating financial markets since our inception in 2008, pioneering fully automated natural language processing systems to read and interpret financial news.

To accomplish our goal of being the best at what we do, we are focused on building a world-class ML engineering workflow, ensuring seamless training, deployment and monitoring of our predictive models.

What you’ll do

• You’ll help us build and improve the ML infrastructure powering our fully automated trading systems. Expect hands‑on work with:

• Python tooling for data processing and rapid model experimentation.

• Scalable pipelines for dataset generation, feature engineering and model training.

• Distributed computing technologies (e.g., Ray, Kubernetes).

• Internal utilities that make it easier for researchers to prototype, validate and deploy models.

• Improving latency, reproducibility and monitoring in our deployment workflows.

You’ll work closely with quantitative researchers and ML engineers, contributing directly to production‑grade systems.

About the team

You’ll join an informal, highly technical Quant team where ownership matters and good ideas move fast. We’re a tight-knit group of researchers across 9 nationalities, all with strong backgrounds in math, modeling, and machine learning - and everyone writes code. We collaborate closely with our software developers and traders, working together on models end‑to‑end and engaging deeply in the technical details that make them work.

About you

• You don’t need years of experience, but you do need curiosity, strong fundamentals, and a willingness to build things that work. You are currently studying either a Bachelor's or Master's in Denmark. We’re looking for someone with:

• A scientific and inquisitive mindset.

• Solid understanding of computer science fundamentals (data structures & algorithms).

• Strong Python skills, especially around data preprocessing or pipeline building.

• Interest in distributed systems or ML Ops.

• Experience working with datasets that don’t fit in memory.

• Familiarity with at least one strongly typed language (C#, C/C++, Rust, etc.).

• Currently enrolled in a technical BSc/MSc program (CS, engineering, math, physics, etc.).

Nice to have

• Hands-on experience with ML workflows (dataset generation → training → evaluation).

• Exposure to distributed computing frameworks (Ray, Spark, Dask).

jobs.description:
A three-year position as a Postdoctoral researcher is now available at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The Postdoc’s employment is expected to start on 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  About the Center

  You will be employed at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, which aims to build a strong scientific foundation for understanding and acting on complex public-health challenges. The Center leverages multi-layered nationwide social and health data combined with an interdisciplinary fusion of methods spanning data science, epidemiology, ethnography, econometrics, and systems science. Our research focuses on the complex interplay of health, social, and environmental factors that shape individuals, families, and networks over time. We emphasise interdisciplinary collaboration, offering you an opportunity to actively engage as a collaborative partner in different projects depending on your interests and expertise. Learn more about the Center and our research, vision, and values here.

  About the Department 

  The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

  About the position 

  The position will be nested within the Child Health group at the Center, where we advance knowledge through a combination of research activities that leverage the Center’s data infrastructures and methodological expertise, and engagement with policymakers and practitioners. The Center has developed a strategic partnership with a Danish municipality – the Thriving Communities Lab – which offers a platform for connecting the scientific activities at the Center with real-world health promotion efforts. The focus of this partnership is to enhance the conditions for adolescents to thrive through a dynamic learning process that involves professionals across sectors in the municipality, the local government, and researchers, over a period of several years. One question we will explore is whether computational modelling can usefully bring together local knowledge, scientific evidence, the Center’s data resources, and insights emerging from practical interventions, and so strengthen this learning process. Your work as a postdoc will be anchored around this question. Our vision at the Center is to build on this experience to engage with more municipalities over time, addressing a variety of complex health challenges.

  As a Postdoc, your responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• Spearheading the development of a decision-support/scenario exploration tool that offers policymakers a way to visualize and simulate systemic effects of social investments and programmes, in close collaboration with our partners in the Thriving Communities Lab. 	
• Engaging with municipal collaborators within the Thriving Communities Lab to ensure a dynamic interplay between research activities and local efforts. 	
• Exploring multi-layered life-course data from the Danish Life Course Cohort (DANLIFE), augmented with local data from the municipal partner, to map the interrelated landscape of well-being among adolescents. 	
• Contributing to scientific publications and engage in the dissemination of research results related to these topics. 	
• Collaborating with researchers in the Center on interdisciplinary projects. 	
• Participating in research-based teaching at the Department of Public Health. 	
• Actively contributing to the development of organisational elements within the Center, such as network activities, website, outreach initiatives, social engagements, scientific meetings, and more.   Profile 

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with the following competences and experience:

   	
• You have a PhD degree in social science, economics, epidemiology, data science, complexity science, computational science, or other related sciences. 	
• You have experience with system dynamics modelling. Experience with agent-based modelling, social return on investment analysis or other analytical frameworks to model social and systemic impacts of social policies and programmes would also be an advantage. 	
• Experience working with Danish register data is an advantage. 	
• You are motivated to engage in participatory processes with practitioners and policymakers, and to collaborate with a variety of stakeholders to foster change. 	
• You have an active interest in complex-systems science applied to public health and epidemiology. 	
• You have proficient communication skills and a proven ability to work in interdisciplinary teams. 	
• You have excellent English skills, both written and spoken. 	
• Danish language skills are an advantage but not essential.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, next to the Lakes in Central Copenhagen.

  Terms of employment 
 The average working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is February 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark for the past 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Further information

  For specific information about the position, please contact the Associate professor Christopher Jamil de Montgomery: cmon@sund.ku.dk

  Applicants may find the following links useful:

   	
• Copenhagen Health Complexity Center: https://healthcomplex.dk/ 	
• University of Copenhagen: http://ku.dk/english/ 	
• Department of Public Health: http://publichealth.ku.dk/ 	
• International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/   Application process

  Your application should be written in English and must include the following documents – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter of motivation (max 1 page). Please briefly describe your previous research experience and interests as well as what attracts you to the position. 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 	
• Certified/signed copies of
 	a) PhD certificate (if the PhD has not been completed, a written statement from the applicant’s supervisor will suffice)
 	b) Master of Science certificate. 	
• A research plan (max 2 pages) outlining your ideas for how a decision-support/scenario exploration tool could be developed, drawing on system dynamics modelling or other analytical frameworks suitable for modelling dynamic effects of social policies and programmes.   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be considered.

  After the expiration of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been advanced for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each applicant is given an opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves.

  You can read more about the recruitment process here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Application deadline 

  Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 47-48.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

Do you take pride in working in the early morning? If so, you are a good match as a forklift driver for our goods receiving department. When IKEA opens at 10 AM, it is important we have replenished the shelves so we are ready for our customers.

As a forklift driver you play an important part for IKEA’s customers and sales, because you and your team make sure our home furnishing solutions and accessories are always accessible for our customers. Every day is fast paced because we work with a sharp deadline at 10 AM, when the store opens.

Do you want to turn complex information security risks into decisions and actions that protect the business and enable its strategic ambitions? At COWI, you will work at the intersection of cybersecurity, enterprise risk management, business operations, technology, and digital transformation. You will play a central role in identifying the information security risks that matter most and ensuring they lead to clear ownership, informed decisions, and effective risk reduction.

At COWI, we create sustainable solutions that improve the quality of life for people today and generations to come. Our experts work across infrastructure, energy, water, environment, architecture, and buildings, delivering projects that shape societies and support critical services around the world.

As a trusted advisor to clients and partners, information security is an essential part of how we deliver projects, protect information, manage risk, and maintain trust. Our increasing use of digital platforms, data, artificial intelligence, and software-based delivery models creates new opportunities, but also increases our exposure to cybersecurity, regulatory, supply-chain, and delivery risks.

Your role, responsibilities, and team

COWI is strengthening its approach to information security risk management as part of a broader development of Information Security and Enterprise Risk Management across the Group.

Our ambition is to identify and understand the most important information security risks facing COWI, enable informed management decisions, drive effective risk treatment, and provide transparency and assurance to Executive Management and the Board.

This role has been established to help turn that ambition into practice.

As Senior Information Security Risk Specialist, you will be responsible for driving the information security risk management process across COWI. You will develop a consolidated and business-relevant risk picture, facilitate complex risk assessments, challenge assumptions, and translate material risks into decision-ready treatment options.

An important part of the role is ensuring that significant risks are not simply recorded in a risk register. You will help transform prioritized risks into clearly defined initiatives and projects, with accountable business owners, realistic delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and transparent reporting.

You will be part of the Group CISO and the ERM function, and you will work closely with IT, Legal, Procurement, Process & Quality, Transformation Office, and Business Lines, incl. operational risk owners across all of these.

Your primary responsibilities will include

• Leading the identification, analysis, evaluation and prioritization of information security risks across COWI’s business operations, projects, digital solutions, information assets, and third-party dependencies.

• Translating technical, regulatory and operational security issues into clear business-risk scenarios, including credible causes, consequences, existing controls, risk exposure and treatment options.

• Facilitating strategic risk assessments and cross-functional risk workshops with senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, and accountable risk owners.

• Preparing decision-ready risk analysis and reporting for the Group CISO, Executive Management, the ERM Committee, the Audit Committee, and the Board of Directors.

• Developing risk treatment proposals and project charters for prioritized risks, including proposed scope, ownership, governance, outcomes, dependencies, resource requirements, milestones and measures of risk reduction.

• Supporting risk owners in defining practical key risk indicators, treatment progress measures and evidence that demonstrate whether risk exposure is being reduced.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

• Doing hands-on development and engineering work across the team's core technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and internal tooling (around 80% of the role)

• Making the final technical decisions within the team's decision domain, and helping define where that domain's boundaries sit versus where the team needs external alignment

• Securing technical quality in the team – code and infrastructure-as-code review, best practices, testing and automation standards

• Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team

• Participating in refinement, securing that features, stories and tasks describe architectural dependencies, feasibility, quality requirements and operational aspects such as reliability, security, cost and developer experience

• Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation

• Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

• Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers

• Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback

• Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines

• Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally

• Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments

• Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team

• Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

• Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling

• Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain

• Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform

• Has a collaborative mindset – comfortable gathering feedback from stakeholders across teams and using it to design clean, well-reasoned solutions

Joining the EIVA crew

ROLE DESCRIPTION

INVISIO is looking for a commercially minded and pragmatic Corporate Legal Counsel to support its global business. This is a broad legal generalist role with a strong commercial focus, where you will work closely with the business and provide legal support across a wide range of matters, with particular emphasis on international contracts, tenders, customer projects and other commercial legal matters.

As Corporate Legal Counsel, you will become part of a small legal team together with Signe Karstoft, Legal Director, to whom you will report. The role is based at INVISIO’s headquarters in Hvidovre, and the legal function is organisationally anchored within INVISIO’s Sales & Program function, which consists of approximately 50 employees globally, including around 25-30 in Denmark. You will primarily support the global sales organisation and work closely with colleagues across the business. Much of your work will involve large and complex customer contracts, tenders and projects.

You will provide legal support across INVISIO’s international business, including in relation to US contracts, such as contracts within the defence sector, and support sales teams across Europe and other markets. You will also support INVISIO in connection with major public tenders, including tenders involving ministries and defence organisations, providing legal support on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

As a technology company, intellectual property is an important part of INVISIO’s business. While dedicated specialists handle areas such as patents, you may also advise on IP-related matters as part of the broader commercial legal support. Experience with IP or from a technology or other IP-intensive business would therefore be an advantage.

In addition to the day-to-day legal support, you will contribute to developing and improving the way Legal supports the business. This includes driving legal improvement initiatives, maintaining and developing contract templates and legal guidelines, and conducting workshops and awareness activities for the business.

The role is highly international and outward-facing, with significant interaction with customers and stakeholders at all levels. You will have opportunities to join customer visits and negotiate contracts abroad, as well as participate in trade fairs in Denmark, Europe and the US.

The role is expected to involve approximately 25 travel days per year.

As INVISIO continues to grow rapidly, you will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and no two days are the same.

AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

INVISIO is looking for an independent and commercially minded lawyer who takes ownership and enjoys working closely with customers and colleagues across the organisation. Your key responsibilities will include:

Commercial contracts and negotiations:

• 
Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial contracts, including large international sales contracts, non-disclosure agreements, letters of intent, consulting agreements, tender-related contracts and distribution agreements.

• 
Take an active role in customer dialogue and contract negotiations and provide commercially focused legal advice, working closely with relevant stakeholders to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives.

• 
Provide pragmatic legal advice on contractual and other commercial matters arising in the day-to-day business.

**

Tenders and customer projects:**

• 
Provide legal support in connection with major public tenders, including reviewing tender documentation and advising on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

• 
Advise on legal and contractual aspects of tender structures, including which INVISIO entity should participate and any related intercompany arrangements.

• 
Support and, where relevant, take a coordinating role in customer projects and other commercial initiatives, including advising on contractual set-ups, priorities and how existing solutions can be applied in different markets etc.

**

IP and export control:**

• Ad hoc Advise on IP and export control matters, including IP considerations in commercial agreements and questions relating to export restrictions and requirements in connection with international sales and customer projects.

**

Legal development and business support:**

• 
Develop, maintain and improve contract templates, legal guidelines and other tools.

• 
Drive legal improvement initiatives and conduct workshops and legal awareness activities for the business, for example in relation to NDA’s.

• 
Provide ad hoc legal advice and support across INVISIO as required.

REPORTING AND TITLE

Reporting to: Signe Karstoft, Legal Director.

Title: Corporate Legal Counsel.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Education: You hold a master’s degree in law (cand.jur. or cand.merc.jur.).

Work experience: You have approximately 3-6 years of relevant legal experience from an in-house role, for example in a technology or software company or another larger international industrial company.

Legal areas of specialisation: You have strong experience in drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements and are comfortable handling contractual matters independently. You also have experience supporting tender processes and advising on the legal and contractual matters that arise in this context.

In addition, you have a broad legal profile and are able to navigate a varied range of legal matters. Experience with IP-related matters, particularly from a technology or other IP-intensive business, would be an advantage. Knowledge of export control would also be beneficial.

Commercial: You have a strong commercial mindset and understand how legal advice fits into the broader business context.

You have experience working directly with customers and are comfortable collaborating with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. You are able to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives and provide pragmatic, solution-oriented advice.

Language skills: You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and verbal.

PERSONAL CAPABILITIES

Independent & proactive: You work independently, take ownership of your responsibilities and proactively drive matters forward.

Outgoing & interpersonal: You are outgoing and enjoy interacting with people with different backgrounds and at all levels, both internally and externally. You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable engaging with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Analytical & pragmatic: You have strong analytical skills and are able to understand complex legal and commercial matters while maintaining a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach.

Structured & able to prioritise: You work in a structured manner, maintain a good overview of your responsibilities and are able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment where new and urgent matters frequently arise. You remain calm and focused when priorities change or deadlines are tight.

Stakeholder management & collaboration: You build strong relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and organisational levels. You are a team-oriented colleague who contributes to a strong sense of teamwork across the organisation and is able to influence stakeholders in a constructive manner.

Positive & constructive: You have a professional approach to your work and interact with others with maturity and integrity. You bring positive energy, are resilient when challenges arise and remain constructive in a busy environment.

INVISIO’S VALUE PROPOSITION TO YOU

INVISIO is a rapidly growing company with ambitious growth targets. The company achieves these ambitions through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts will be important to INVISIO’s continued success, and by joining the company, you will become part of an international headquarter with an informal working environment.

INVISIO offers a wide range of professional and social employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

ABOUT INVISIO

INVISIO is a global leader in communications technology for professionals working in mission-critical environments. Established in Denmark in 1999, the company develops and markets advanced, integrated communication systems for defence and public safety professionals, helping users communicate clearly and safely in demanding environments.

INVISIO’s modular and scalable portfolio includes headsets, control units, intercom systems, hubs and software designed to work together across dismounted, vehicle-based and command operations. The solutions are marketed under the INVISIO and Racal Acoustics brands.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, INVISIO has an international presence across Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 330 employees globally, including around 215 in Denmark, and is growing rapidly. INVISIO is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (Large Cap).

INVISIO is characterised by a strong focus on innovation, close customer collaboration and an international working environment. Its core values are Passion, Innovation, Teamwork and Customer First.

You can learn more about INVISIO here: www.invisio.com.

APPLICATION AND CONTACT

If you believe this position is a good fit for you, we look forward to receiving your application. Please attach your CV and any relevant documentation. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please don’t hesitate to contact Camilla Krogh at (+45 51261264) or Mikkel Falkenberg at (+45 29993065) from the team at RESOLVA.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  The application deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.

We require a physical presence in our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. We believe this enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles to build an impactful product that users love to use.

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

• 
Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

• 
OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

• 
Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

• 
Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

• 
Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

• 
Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

• 
Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

• 
Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

• 
Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

• 
Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

• 
Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

• 
Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

• 
Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

• 
Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

• 
Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

• 
Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

• 
Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.

What We Offer

• 
Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

• 
Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field.

• 
A vibrant, learning-focused work environment.

• 
A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

Do you want to influence how one of Europe's leading pharmaceutical companies leverages technology to create competitive advantage? About the job

You will work closely with senior leaders and key stakeholders across Pharma Trade to understand business strategy, commercial priorities, operational challenges, and digital opportunities. You will shape demand and identify how technology can improve decision-making, gross margin, operational scalability, process efficiency, and execution across the Pharma Trade value chain.

You will play a central role in developing and maintaining the technology roadmap for Pharma Trade. This includes connecting needs and opportunities across Business Development, Product Supply, Portfolio Management, Hospital and Tender Management, Regulatory, Sales, and other relevant functions.

Working closely with the Head of Pharma Trade Solutions, Product Owner, delivery teams, and shared IT functions, you will ensure that demand is clearly understood, prioritized, qualified, and prepared for successful delivery. You will help move Pharma Trade towards a coherent, scalable, and value-driven digital landscape.

Your focus will not only be on identifying new initiatives, but also on ensuring that technology investments lead to measurable business outcomes and support the long-term transformation of Pharma Trade.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Act as the primary strategic IT partner and point of contact for new technology demand across Pharma Trade

• Build and maintain a consolidated, value-based technology roadmap for Pharma Trade in close collaboration with business leadership and the Pharma Trade Solutions team

• Develop a deep understanding of Pharma Trade’s end-to-end value chain, business processes, decision points, data needs, and application landscape

• Identify, assess, and develop digital opportunities that can improve gross margin, commercial decision-making, scalability, time-to-market, supply visibility, and operational efficiency

• Ensure that initiatives are prioritized across the entire Pharma Trade domain rather than optimized for individual functions or markets

• Challenge business demand constructively and distinguish between underlying business problems, requested features, and appropriate technology solutions

• Secure clear business ownership of business cases, benefits, process decisions, data, adoption, and value realization

Who are you?

You are a senior, business-oriented IT professional who combines strong stakeholder management with a structured and analytical approach to technology demand and business value.

You understand both business priorities and IT delivery realities. You are comfortable engaging with senior leaders, but you also have enough technology understanding to challenge, shape, and qualify ideas before they become projects.

You bring:

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of bringing better deals of medicine to millions.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

jobs.occupation: Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for byggeri og Bygni
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling

Research area and project description
Predictive control can reduce energy costs and CO2 emissions of heating and cooling homes. However, its performance depends on knowing when residents are home and what they find comfortable.

You will develop a natural-language interface, based on a large language model, between residents and a predictive controller. Residents can then tell the controller, when they are away, report how the rooms feel, or ask for a warmer bathroom etc. In return, the controller explains what it did and why, shows what the next hours cost in money and CO2, and suggests alternatives that residents can accept or decline. The comfort limits are thus set by the residents; with the information they need.

This dialogue can save energy in three ways. Knowing when people are home and which rooms they use enables occupancy-based control, heating only where and when needed. Reports on how the rooms feel train personal comfort models, so setpoints match each household. The third, and least explored, is energy sufficiency: residents knowingly accept less heating or cooling, for example 20 °C instead of 21.5 °C on an expensive evening, while remaining free to say no. A central question is whether explaining alternative control actions and their cost changes how residents judge the same indoor conditions (their thermal acceptability), and whether the change lasts. All three look the same on the energy meter, so the project must separate them.

Few people want a system that talks all the time. Residents differ in how much information they want, in what form, and whether the system should take the initiative or only respond when asked (proactive versus on-demand interaction). Engagement may also fade as the novelty wears off. The project will study these differences and design for them.

You will:
• couple the language model to the controller, so that residents' requests become control actions within safe limits
• run a climate chamber experiment on whether explanations change thermal acceptability
• carry out a field study in occupied Danish homes through a winter and a summer, covering heating and overheating
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a M.Sc. in engineering, computer science, building science or a related technical field. Applicants with a B.Sc. and at least one year of master's studies can apply through the 4+4 programme.

You should be able to program, preferably in Python, and be comfortable analysing data. Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: model predictive control or optimisation, large language models, statistics and the design of experiments with people, and field measurements in buildings. Nobody will have all of these, and you should be willing to learn what you lack.

The field study involves installing equipment in people's homes and talking with the residents, so you should be comfortable working with people. Danish is an advantage for the field work but not a requirement.

Applicants from neighbouring fields with relevant technical skills and a clear motivation for the topic are encouraged to apply.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Arhus C., Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Michael Dahl Knudsen, mdk@cae.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Massimo Fiorentini, massimo@cae.au.dk (co-supervisor)

jobs.description:

Energinet is seeking a highly skilled cyber security professional to join our Attack Surface Management team within the Group Cyber and Information Security unit. You will be the link between the department's technical specialists and the rest of Energinet and ensure that security requirements are both understood, prioritised and complied with.

You combine solid technical insight with clear communication and business understanding. You present innovative ideas with confidence, along with the presence and authority to guide decisions. 

Key Responsibilities

• Oversee the operation and continual improvement of enterprise vulnerability management capabilities across IT, cloud, and hybrid environments.
• Build, maintain, and optimize vulnerability scanning infrastructure, configurations, policies, and workflows.
• Develop scalable vulnerability assessment processes covering infrastructure, endpoints, servers, applications, cloud workloads, containers, and identities.
• Ensure accurate asset discovery, coverage validation, and vulnerability visibility across the enterprise.
• Manage lifecycle vulnerability processes from detection through validation, prioritization, remediation, and closure.
• Establish metrics and performance indicators to measure remediation effectiveness and risk reduction outcomes.
• Analyze attack paths, exposure chains, and security control weaknesses that could contribute to organizational risk.
• Develop risk-based methodologies for prioritizing exposures based on exploitability, business criticality, threat intelligence, and operational impact.
• Support continuous assessment of the organization's security posture through exposure analytics and attack surface monitoring.
• Serve as the technical owner and subject matter expert for vulnerability and exposure management platforms.

• Be fluent in English at a high level in writing and speech. Danish proficiency is an advantage but not mandatory.

At our office in Ballerup or Fredericia, you will be part of Attack Surface Management - a new department under the Group Cyber and Information Security unit. The department is responsible for the technical protection layers that reduce Energinet's attack surface. 

Together with the other departments in Cyber and Information Security, we are responsible for developing and operating the organizational processes and technologies within cyber and information security in Energinet and for coordinating the IT preparedness in the electricity, gas and hydrogen sectors.

If you have any questions about the job, you are very welcome to contact Arpan Roy at arroy@energinet.dk or on tel. +45 5161 2898. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send us your motivated cv as soon as possible.

By leading the way in the green transition, we can help to solve the global climate challenge. New solutions require us to be able to see problems from many different angles, and diversity is therefore a keyword in our culture. We strive to listen to, involve and share our knowledge. From its headquarters in Kolding, Vetaphone develops advanced, reliable systems that ensure optimal adhesion, print quality and production efficiency for customers in the print, packaging, converting and extrusion industries – and today the company is represented in more than 60 countries around the world. To strengthen the international sales organisation, we are now looking for a technically strong and commercially minded:

Technical and commercial sales support with close customer dialogue

As Technical Sales Manager, you become one of the key technical and commercial support behind Vetaphone’s global sales team, working closely with Area Sales Managers and agents to solve real production challenges where surface treatment performance impacts efficiency, quality and compliance. You get a broad and technically demanding role, where you guide projects from the very first customer dialogue and solution design through to quotation, negotiation and handover to the internal project department.

It is natural for you to drive technically complex, project-based sales to OEMs and end customers, and to step in as technical sales lead on selected projects in close cooperation with Area Sales Managers, agents and internal specialists. You analyse customer applications, production processes and requirements to define the optimal surface treatment solution, and you prepare and present technical and commercial proposals that communicate value, performance and compliance in a way customers understand and trust.

You support OEM customers with system integration, specification and application know-how, and build long-term customer relationships based on trust, expertise and results. At the same time, you contribute to knowledge sharing and capability building across the sales organisation and agent network, and you stay on top of market trends, customer needs and competitive developments – with regular international travel to customers, OEM partners and key industry events.

In the selection process, we will particularly emphasise:

• A solid technical background, preferably within mechanical and/or electrical engineering

• Proven experience with consultative, project-based B2B sales of technical systems or solutions

• The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear customer value propositions

• A structured and self-driven approach, combined with strong stakeholder management skills

• Comfort working independently in an international, matrix-based organisation

• Fluent in Danish and excellent communication skills in English

• Willingness to travel internationally approx. 50-70 days per year

The ideal candidate has a solid technical foundation combined with a genuine sales flair, and thrives in a role where every project brings a new technical puzzle to solve. Maybe you already work in a similar technical sales role today, or you come from an engineering or application background and are ready to take the step into a more commercial, customer-facing career.

In return, you become part of a global technology leader with a strong market position, working closely with experienced technical and commercial colleagues on high-value international projects – with good opportunities for professional development within a specialised, knowledge-driven organisation.

The role is based at Vetaphone’s headquarters in Kolding, Denmark, combined with the international travel the role calls for.
