Requisition ID: 1706128

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

As you write your next chapter, what shape will it take?

Are you ready to take the next step in your M&A career and work on some of the most exciting deals in the market? We are looking for a Senior Consultant to join our Transaction Strategy and Execution team in Copenhagen.

In this role, you will be part of a high-performing team that supports clients across the full deal lifecycle: from M&A strategy to execution. You will work closely with clients on complex, high-impact engagements, where your insights and capabilities will drive real results. At the same time, you will play an active role in shaping our team, contributing to a strong culture and supporting the development of future leaders.

Shape your future with confidence.

Skills and attributes for success

You are analytically strong and comfortable working with complex data and problem-solving, using AI-enabled tools to enhance analysis and insight generation. You bring a structured and pragmatic approach, combined with strong business understanding and attention to detail.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and can manage ambiguity while maintaining focus on delivering high-quality outcomes. At the same time, you communicate clearly and confidently, translating complexity into actionable insights for both clients and colleagues.

You bring experience from client-facing or in-house roles across M&A execution (pre- and/or post-deal) and operational delivery, for example:

• Product and technology diligence

• Assessment of the product portfolio and roadmap, together with the underlying technology and R&D setup to evaluate commercial attractiveness/value creation potential

• IT diligence

• Evaluating the IT environments, from strategy to costs, to identify risks and opportunities, and to inform the investment case

• Technology integration and separation

• Leading technology workstreams, from strategy to execution/operationalization

• Digital value creation

• Assessing digital and AI-driven value creation opportunities, and implications for the deal theses and post-deal value capture

As a Senior Consultant, you will work across a range of M&A engagements spanning M&A strategy, operational diligence, as well as value creation and deal management. You are passionate about the operational aspects of M&A, thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments, and build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Conducting operational due diligence/value creation analysis

• Managing and driving workstreams across pre- and post-deal engagements

• Supporting business development through pitch content, proposals and client conversations

What we look for

As our new colleague you bring 3-6 years of experience from strategy and M&A consulting or industry experience. You bring an inclusive approach, building strong relationships with both clients and colleagues and are a strong communicator who can translate complex ideas into clear and actionable insights. You take ownership of your work with a consistent focus on quality and impact.

What’s in it for you

• Work on complex, high-profile M&A and divestment engagements

• Collaborate with integrated teams across geographies and disciplines

• Continuous coaching, feedback and formal learning to support your development

• A purpose-led culture focused on creating long-term value for clients and society

Full-Stack Software Engineer (Mid/Senior)

Location: Central Copenhagen; primarily in office

Language: English

Highlights:

• Full-Stack Python/TS engineer needed for a B2B SaaS startup in Copenhagen (with plenty of traction!)

• We have a lean, get-stuff-done team. No annoying extra management layers or unnecessary bureaucratic rituals. And we are "AI-forward" in our own development practices.

• You will own features end to end, from the data model through to the screen, on a platform that manufacturers rely on to keep production lines running.

• You will work in a small engineering team, directly with the person who decides what we build, and the problems you spend your time on are hard because the domain is hard, not because the organization is.

• We're building legitimately useful tools for the industries and companies that make the world go around.... manufacturers. Both AI-tools and just "plain-old-good-software" tools.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality, all in a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth.

The platform now covers more ground than the team that built it. We are hiring engineers to keep that pace sustainable, and to go deeper on the parts of the product our customers are pushing hardest.

The role

You will join a small engineering team and work across the whole stack: Python on the backend, TypeScript on the frontend and in the AI layers. There is no split between people who design and people who implement. You will take a problem from a customer conversation or a product decision through to something running in production for real manufacturers.

You will work directly with our co-founder and CEO, who is a hands-on product builder himself. That means short conversations instead of tickets thrown over a wall, and it means your questions about why something should work a certain way get answered by the person who decided it.

The domain is genuinely complicated, and that is the interesting part. Supplier relationships in automotive involve deep hierarchies, long-running approval processes, strict audit requirements and a lot of state that has to be exactly right. Modeling that well is most of the job.

Title and level flex with experience. We are open to strong mid-level engineers and to senior engineers who want more scope than their current company gives them.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and on a codebase with this much implicit context, working through problems with the rest of the team in person is much faster than doing it in writing. Sensible flexibility when you need it is a given; full-time remote is not what we are offering.

Our current stack:

• Backend: Python / Django

• Frontend: Vue (but no specific Vue experience is needed)

• Infrastructure: AWS (mostly)

• Agents: Cloudflare (TypeScript) + Claude & OpenAI platform

What you will do

• Build features end to end, from data model and backend logic through to the TypeScript frontend our customers actually click on.

• Build end-to-end / front-to-back AI features (in-app AI assistants, background worker agents, email-routing agents, customer-configurable agent framework components)

• Design and evolve the relational data model that sits under supplier relationships, approvals and quality records.

• Take vaguely defined customer problems and turn them into something specific enough to build, then build it.

• Work on integrations between Supplios and customer systems (ERP and adjacent tooling), where failures have visible consequences for a production line.

• Improve the parts of the codebase that need it, rather than routing around them.

• Review other people's code and have yours reviewed; we keep the loop tight and unbureaucratic.

• Help keep the platform healthy in production across our regions: errors, performance and the boring things that keep customers trusting us.

• Take part in product decisions. Engineers here are expected to have opinions about what we build, not just how.

What we are looking for

Essential

• Professional experience with Python. This is not negotiable; the backend is Python and you need to be effective in it.

• Solid TypeScript experience and genuine comfort working on the frontend.

• Experience building and running SaaS products, including the part after launch where real users depend on them.

• AI-forward development techniques. (This does not mean you no longer write code.)

• A track record of owning work end to end without waiting to be told what to do next.

• The temperament for a small, senior company: high ownership, low ceremony.

• You want to work primarily from an office in central Copenhagen, with a small team.

Nice to have

Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. Nobody has all of these.

• Experience with B2B enterprise SaaS, especially where customers are large and demanding and implementations are not self-serve. This is a significant plus.

• Experience with complex relational data modeling, and with large, long-lived codebases that you did not write yourself. A big plus.

• Experience building AI-based products, using the latest frameworks/harnesses and infrastructure components (including RAG) is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with any of: domain-driven design, the actor model, finite state machines, CQRS, event-driven architecture. We use these ideas where they earn their place, and it helps if the vocabulary is already yours.

• Startup experience, particularly early stage. A significant plus.

• Knowledge of manufacturing, automotive or supply chain. Useful, but we can teach you the domain; we cannot teach you the craft, so do not rule yourself out on this.

Language

English is the only important language for this position; we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• The scope is unusually large for the stage. You are one of a small number of engineers on a platform that serves demanding customers globally. What you build ships, and it ships soon.

• No layers between you and the decisions. You work directly with the co-founder and CEO, who runs product. There is no committee to navigate and nobody to translate your work for you.

• Hard problems that are not artificially hard. The complexity comes from the domain (hierarchies, state, audit trails, integrations that must not fail), not from organisational overhead.

• Real customers already, and real gaps. The product has paying customers in automotive and clear places where it needs to get better. Both halves of that are true, and both are why this is a good job.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

Scientific Software Engineer for Research Software Engineering Group

The European Spallation Source (ESS) is one of Europe’s largest research infrastructure projects and is building the world’s most powerful neutron source. Through cutting-edge science and technology, ESS will enable discoveries that advance our understanding of materials, energy, health, and the environment.

About the role

The Research Software Engineering (RSE) group develops and maintains critical software systems that make neutron scattering experiments at ESS possible and successful.

As a Scientific Software Engineer, you will contribute to the development of key platforms supporting the scientific user journey, including the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information systems. You will work closely with scientists, software engineers, and stakeholders across ESS to gather requirements, understand user needs, and develop robust software solutions that integrate seamlessly with the wider ESS ecosystem.

The RSE group uses modern web technologies and software engineering practices to deliver high-quality software with a long operational lifetime. In addition, the group is expanding its focus on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning solutions that can enhance the scientific user experience. As part of this effort, you will contribute to new AI-related initiatives and help establish RSE as a centre of expertise and development for AI applications within the Science Directorate.

This position is well suited for an experienced software engineer with a strong technical foundation, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for building software that enables world-class scientific research.

Key responsibilities

• Design, develop, test, and maintain software systems supporting the scientific user journey at ESS.

• Contribute to the development of the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information management systems.

• Gather, analyse, and refine requirements from scientific and technical stakeholders across ESS.

• Design and implement integrations between RSE applications and other ESS services and platforms.

• Apply modern software engineering practices to deliver reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions.

• Contribute to technical and process improvements within the SIMS group.

• Participate in AI and Machine Learning initiatives supporting the Science Directorate.

• Collaborate with scientists, software engineers, and international partners to develop innovative solutions for scientific computing and data management.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing within the team when appropriate.

• Contribute to software architecture discussions and technology decisions within the group.

Required qualifications

• Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Typically 4-7 years of relevant professional experience in software development.

• Experience developing modern web applications and services.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern software development practices.

• Experience gathering requirements and working directly with stakeholders and end users.

• Experience designing and implementing integrations between complex software systems.

• Ability to work independently and manage technical tasks and projects with limited supervision.

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

Desirable qualifications

• Experience working with scientific software, research infrastructures, or data-intensive environments.

• Experience with cloud-based services and distributed systems.

• Experience with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning technologies and their practical application.

• Experience with user-facing platforms, portals, or information management systems.

• Familiarity with modern DevOps practices, CI/CD, automated testing, and container technologies.

• Experience working in international and multidisciplinary environments.

• Experience contributing to open-source software projects.

What we offer

DMSC is located on the DTU campus in Kongens Lyngby, north of Copenhagen, while the ESS neutron facility is based in Lund, Sweden. Together, they form a unique cross-border scientific environment in the Øresund region.

You will join a dynamic and highly collaborative international workplace with colleagues representing nearly 60 nationalities across ESS and DMSC. This is a full-time, permanent position based in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, and we need someone who can start as soon as practically possible.

Senior Data Analyst – SAP Reporting & Stakeholder Alignment

• Location: Copenhagen, Denmark or Lisbon, Portugal

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: Hybrid

• Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about turning business questions into meaningful data solutions? Do you enjoy working with stakeholders, solving complex data challenges, and transforming data into insights that drive better decisions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Senior Data Analyst, you will join the Data & Insights team and report directly to the Head of Data & Insights. In this role, you will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and SAP data, ensuring reporting requirements are clearly defined, translated into actionable data solutions, and delivered with accuracy and impact.

You will work closely with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Operations, and Data Engineering teams to support data-driven decision-making while improving reporting processes and data quality across the organization. This is a great opportunity to influence business decisions, collaborate across functions, and help shape the future of data and analytics at STG.

What your day will look like

In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Partner directly with business stakeholders — Finance leadership, Sales/Commercial, Supply Chain/Operations — to understand their reporting and data needs, and translate them into concrete data requirements.

• Work closely with data engineers to scope, request, and validate data pulled from SAP, acting as the translation layer between business language and technical/data specifications.

• Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, validate, and consolidate data for recurring and ad hoc reporting.

• Build and maintain Excel-based models, trackers, and reports that stakeholders rely on for decision-making.

• Consolidate data into stakeholder-ready reporting, and supporting data checks.

• Act as the go-to person for scoping ambiguous stakeholder requests — clarifying what's actually needed, managing expectations, and pushing back constructively when a request isn't well-defined or feasible.

• Identify data quality issues at the source and work with SAP module owners and data engineers to resolve them.

• Document data definitions, sources, and logic so reporting stays consistent and auditable month over month.

• Continuously look for ways to streamline the process rather than repeating manual work each cycle.

What you'll bring

• 5+ years of experience in a data analyst, business analyst, or similar data-facing role, ideally in a retail or consumer business.

• Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing and troubleshooting complex queries independently.

• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, data modeling; Power Query is a plus).

• Familiarity with SAP data structures, particularly FI (Finance) and SD (Sales & Distribution).

• Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), or willingness to learn it, is a plus.

The Role

To support the growth of Genmab, we are looking for a Manager, Reverse logistics to join the team in Copenhagen.

As Manager, Reverse Logistics & Compliance you will develop and manage global reverse logistics processes across Genmab’s distribution network in the US, EU and APAC.

The role covers product returns, recall logistics, expired and damaged inventory, and product destruction, ensuring traceability, inventory accuracy and effective coordination with Quality, Finance and relevant compliance functions.

You will also coordinate compliance across global supply chain activities, working closely with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal and Finance to embed applicable regulatory requirements and internal controls into operational processes. This includes supporting compliance risk assessments, audit readiness, corrective actions and training, while promoting clear accountability and continuous improvement across supply chain teams and external partners.

The role reports to Director, Head of Corporate Logistics & Distribution, Commercial Supply Chain

Responsibilities

• Global reverse logistics: Establish and manage processes for return authorization, collection, transportation, receipt, segregation, inventory reconciliation and final disposition, including associated documentation and financial closure.

• Returns management: Coordinate commercial returns with 3PLs, distributors and regional teams, ensuring product eligibility, batch details, quantities, condition and supporting documentation are verified.

• Recall and withdrawal support: Lead supply chain execution of recalls and market withdrawals under the relevant governance, including collection, shipment tracking, reconciliation and operational support for mock recalls.

• Product disposition and destruction: Coordinate the execution of Quality-approved disposition decisions, including return to saleable inventory where permitted, continued quarantine or destruction. Ensure destruction is documented and reconciled with inventory and financial records.

• Traceability and systems: Maintain accurate physical and system inventory records throughout the returns lifecycle. Coordinate with IT and serialization teams on applicable product verification, serialization and traceability activities.

• Financial and trade coordination: Work with Finance, Commercial/Trade and Trade Compliance to align returns with credit processing, inventory write-offs, SOX controls and applicable customs, VAT and duty requirements.

• Performance and improvement: Develop a global scorecard covering return cycle time, reconciliation accuracy, destruction completion, supplier performance, compliance issues and cost. Lead improvements that reduce waste and strengthen process control.

• Supply chain compliance governance: Establish and maintain a global supply chain compliance framework across the US, EU and APAC, coordinating with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal and Finance to embed applicable requirements into supply chain processes.

• Compliance monitoring and remediation: Coordinate supply chain compliance risk assessments, monitor adherence to approved procedures and internal controls, and drive timely closure of, Quality events, assigned audit findings and corrective actions with accountable functions.

• Change assessment and training: Partner with Quality and compliance functions to assess the supply chain impact of regulatory and operational changes, translate agreed requirements into procedures and controls, and coordinate training for internal teams and external partners.

• Management of stakeholders: Corporate and Regional Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Commercial/Trade, Procurement, IT and serialization teams, alongside 3PLs, distributors, transportation providers and authorized destruction partners.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related discipline.

• Typically five or more years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology logistics, distribution or supply chain operations.

• Experience managing product returns, recalls, inventory reconciliation and destruction within a regulated environment.

• Working knowledge of GDP/GxP principles, temperature-controlled distribution and pharmaceutical product traceability.

• Familiarity with ERP and warehouse management systems, preferably SAP, and operational reporting tools.

• Experience supporting supplier oversight, deviations, corrective actions, audits and controlled documentation.

• Experience in supply chain compliance within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including working knowledge of GxP/GDP, trade compliance and SOX/internal controls.

• Demonstrated ability to conduct compliance risk assessments, support audits and inspections, and coordinate corrective and preventive actions across supply chain functions.

Skills and capabilities

• Strong cross-functional coordination and the ability to influence without direct authority.

• Structured approach to problem-solving, documentation and follow-through.

• Ability to establish global standards and adapt execution to regional requirements.

• Sound judgment when escalating quality, compliance or business risks.

• Clear communication skills and confidence working with internal stakeholders and external partners across time zones.

Design for the people in the tiny chairs

At Famly, we build software that takes admin off the plates of early-years educators, so they can spend their time where it matters - with the children. And we make it easier for over a million parents to stay close to their child's day, even while they're at work.

We're looking for a design system builder to join the design team - responsible for the design system, prototyping tools and all other infrastructure with the goal of driving consistency and coherence across the entire product.

About Famly

We’re on a mission to stop admin stealing the joy of working with young children. We do that with our platform, the world’s first proactive assistant for educators and staff that handles admin for them so they can get back to what they love. And we do it with our content (like The Tiny Chair Podcast), reminding educators of the joy and meaning that got them into working with children in the first place.

About the role

You live where design and code meet. With a small team, you'll own Famly's design system: the components, patterns, and documentation that product teams (and increasingly, AI agents) build on every day.

The team's job is coherence. Every feature and every domain should feel like it came from the same place. You'll give builders what they need to design and build to our standards, and keep the conversation going so the system keeps getting better.

You'll bring deep technical knowledge of design systems, and you'll care just as much about how the product feels to the people using it.

The team is based in our Copenhagen office, but we are open to you being based somewhere else.

What you'll be doing

• 
Build production-quality React and TypeScript components for Famly's design system.

• 
Design component APIs that are hard to misuse, and version them so upgrades don't break product teams.

• 
Write the documentation that makes those components self-serve, so a new engineer or an AI agent can pick one up and use it correctly without asking anyone.

• 
Keep the system trustworthy: tests, visual regression, and a release process people don't dread.

• 
Learn Famly's frontend deeply enough to know where a pattern lives, who depends on it, and what breaks if it changes.

• 
Audit and evolve the components we already have, for consistency, accessibility, and reuse across the product.

• 
Own the code side of the design standard with a small team, so design intent survives the trip into production.

• 
Push back when a design won't hold up in code - too many states, no empty case, a pattern that already exists - and say what you'd do instead.

• 
Work with PMs, designers, and engineers across product teams, and bring them ideas before they ask.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

• 
You have 5+ years of frontend experience in B2B SaaS, including design system work.

• 
You're strong in React, TypeScript, and CSS.

• 
You have taste for craft: spacing, motion, states, and the details that make a component feel finished.

• 
You think in systems: reusable, documented, maintainable components over one-off fixes.

• 
You get from a rough idea to a working prototype fast.

• 
You own your work end to end, from discovery through testing to shipping.

• 
You care about the difference between "works" and "is right," and you'll say so and set the direction.

• 
Short meet and greet with Lead People Partner

• 
A logical test

• 
1st interview: Meet and greet with our Senior Director of Product Design

• 
Take-home assignment

• 
2nd interview: Assignment presentation with Senior Director of Product Design and Lead Designer

And who are Famly?

You’re probably wondering at this stage, and Famly are...? Well, it all began when our co-founder Henrik’s daughter was ready to start at daycare. He couldn’t believe the amount of work being done on paper - and how distant he felt from his first child during the day. The paper ‘parent’ books they exchanged once a month just weren’t cutting it. Together with his friend, our co-founder and CEO Anders, they set about solving that.

These days, about 180 of us build Famly for more than 10,000 institutions and over 1 million parents.

We handle admin stress so they can get back to what matters, and we make it easier than ever to connect home, and nursery so parents can play a part in their child’s day. If you join us, you’ll be building, selling, or support customers with everything from staff rotas and invoices, to child development and parent communication.

How we work

Famly prides itself on a few principles; we choose simplicity, we believe friendliness is a superpower, we set the pace, and we want everyone to be surrounded by talent.

It all adds up to a culture that refuses to make employees choose between a place that is ambitious and sets the pace for what good looks like - and one that is a nice place to work. We think you can be ambitious and kind and when you get to meet our team, we hope you’ll agree.

What we expect of you, is that you make others shine, that you believe in being better than yesterday, and you are not afraid to just ‘get it done’. Finally, we want you to value ‘sitting in the tiny chair’ - which means you look at your work through the impact it has on our customers: the people sitting in tiny chairs in childcare settings all over the world.

Competitive pension, private health insurance, and paid maternity/paternity leave.

We’re all about hiring clever people who are good humans too. It means Famly is full of top thinkers and generous teammates waiting to help you shine.

We like to give a lot of ownership both in terms of responsibility and freedom to try new, challenging tasks.

We believe collaboration happens best in person, so we have the default of four days a week in office - but with plenty of flexibility for when life happens outside the office too.

jobs.occupation: Accessing orbitronics and twistronics with microscopic and ultrafast angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, invites applications for a PhD position, starting February 1st, 2027, offering applicants an exciting opportunity to join a new research project on orbitronics and metastable states in two-dimensional quantum materials.

The project involves fabrication of devices and their integration with the existing angle-resolved photoemission (ARPES) infrastructure at the ASTRID2 light source to discover quantum geometric effects and their link to new forms of transport phenomena.

The aim of the project is to develop new types of 2D material devices that can realize orbital, spin and valley Hall effects that form the basis for prototypical memory devices. A series of novel infrastructures will be applied to achieve these goals, including semi-automated fabrication systems in inert environments, clean-room facilities for device production, micro-focused synchrotron light for ARPES characterization at ASTRID2 as well as ultrafast femtosecond laser pulses for optical control of the materials.

The major activities include:

• Design and manufacturing of advanced 2D devices that are compatible with the microARPES experiment at ASTRID2 with the specific aim to uncover orbital-driven phenomena in materials.

• Combining synchrotron and ultrafast laser sources to visualize, excite and control electronic states with distinct orbital and spin textures in quantum materials.

• Isolation, twisting and stacking of monolayer metallic and semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenide, including materials that are sensitive to ambient conditions.

• Development of new techniques to isolate and integrate such air-sensitive materials with devices for photoemission experiments carried out in UHV conditions.

• Applying a state-of-the-art laser beamline integrated with the ASTRID2 synchrotron light source for femtosecond control of electronic structure of 2D materials.

Microbe–electrode interactions are central to the performance of bioelectrochemical anaerobic digestion systems, yet the organisation, activity and stability of these interfaces remain poorly understood.

The project is part of PROMETHEUS (Microbial Electrochemical Methanation Initiative, www.linkedin.com/company/prometheusbiotech/posts/, a large interdisciplinary research initiative funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. jobs.occupation: Quantum Control of Emission in Valleytronic Materials
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a candidate for a fully funded 3-year PhD project at the Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, in the new group of Asst. Prof. Christian Frydendahl, as part of a DFF Sapere Aude research grant.

Compact, integrable sources of circularly polarized light (CPL) are a key enabling technology for chip-scale quantum technologies, but electrically driven sources of pure CPL do not yet exist. Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) emit left- or right-handed CPL depending on which band structure valley, K or K', an electron-hole pair recombines in. Ordinarily, this occurs with an equal 50/50 split between the two valleys.

This project aims to build a new light-emitting diode geometry in which the Valley Hall effect, another intrinsic property of these materials, filters the valley index of the charge carriers during transport, enabling a purely electrically pumped source of CPL. Inducing valley polarization electrically rather than optically is one of the key open challenges in the emerging field of device-based valleytronics.

The project also includes a planned 6-month external research stay at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), where you will develop and fabricate nanophotonic cavities for integration with the new diode design, enhancing its emission and CPL purity further via the Purcell effect.

Your general working tasks would be:

• van der Waals stacking of hBN-encapsulated TMDC monolayers

• Nanofabrication in the AU/SUTD cleanroom facilities (EBL, RIE, metal deposition)

• Opto-electronic characterization: probe station, polarization- and time-resolved spectroscopy at room- and cryogenic temperatures

• Publishing results and presenting at international conferences

• Participating in general dissemination and teaching activities

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

Desirable

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) is pleased to announce an exclusive fellowship opportunity for a researcher who holds a position at a Swedish research institution. The fellowship is made possible through a collaboration with Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in Sweden.The purpose of the AIAS-RJ fellowship is to strengthen the ties and expand collaborations between the Swedish and Danish research communities.

Why apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

AIAS is a haven for intellectual exploration, hosting excellent researchers eager to develop their work in an interdisciplinary, international and collaborative environment. AIAS nurtures an innovative atmosphere where breakthroughs emerge through transparent, inclusive and reflective discussions, offering a space for engagement and creativity.

The AIAS-RJ fellowship gives the selected fellow the opportunity to concentrate on their own research interests while also being an active member of the AIAS research community and participating in and contributing to seminars and activities beyond their own field of expertise. The fellow must be eager to engage in the interdisciplinary community at AIAS and expand research collaborations with colleagues at Aarhus University.

Who can apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

The call is open to curiosity-driven researchers who:

• are of any nationality who hold a tenured position at a Swedish research institution

• work within the humanities and social sciences

• have a research experience of minimum 4 years after completion of the PhD

A unique interdisciplinary platform at AIAS

AIAS fosters connections, sparks ideas and dissolves boundaries as fellows engage with researchers from different disciplines within the Institute and across departments and research hubs at Aarhus University. Therefore, the call welcomes applications from all research areas and themes.

With a location within the unique campus of Aarhus University, AIAS functions as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University and international scholars. AIAS has fellows who work in thematic groups or in individual fellowships, and hosts events and activities, which AIAS-RJ fellows are welcome to join and contribute to.

AIAS and Aarhus University strive to create a multidisciplinary, inclusive academic environment and to be an inspiring workplace for all by fostering a culture in which the individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The fellowship includes

The AIAS-RJ Fellow is offered:

• a salary based on seniority (employment conditions and wages are regulated through the Danish collective union agreements)

• travel costs to and from Aarhus

• relocation assistance

• a moderate budget for research-related costs

The AIAS-RJ Fellow will have office space at AIAS and can participate in academic training activities, conferences and workshops at AIAS. They will also be affiliated with the relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

How to apply: Application process and deadline

Applications must be submitted online via the system: GrantOne.

In the ‘Guide for Applicants,’ you can find the detailed application requirements and more information on the structure of the application system, the selection criteria and the selection process.

Timeline of the application process

• Opening of call: August 2026.

• Deadline for applications: 24 November 2026 at 12.00 (noon) CET.

• Evaluation and selection period: December 2026 - March 2027.

• Applicants will receive answers: Ultimo March 2027.

• Fellowship begins: 1 September 2027.

About AIAS

As an 'Institute for Advanced Study,' AIAS brings researchers together across disciplines, seniority and nationality. AIAS offers fellowships for excellent researchers from all academic disciplines to pursue cutting-edge research projects for the benefit of society and humankind in optimal research conditions.

The daily encounter with colleagues from diverse research disciplines at AIAS provides fellows with fresh and different insights, methods and perspectives on their own research, leading to new and unexpected research questions and ideas.

jobs.occupation: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Real-Time Vision - Simulator Technology
jobs.description:
Shape the future of real-time vision in sports technology

Join Trackman’s new Simulator Technology team and help build next-generation camera systems for the world’s leading golf simulators. We are looking for an experienced engineer with expertise in real-time video pipelines, camera integration, and low-latency systems.

About the team

Trackman is the global leader in indoor golf technology, delivering advanced simulator experiences through precision tracking, virtual golf software, and in-bay technology.

Our new Simulator Technology´s (SimTech) mission is to drive innovation across the entire in-bay customer experience: cameras, projectors, kiosks, moving floors, and the software that ties them together. The team works in close collaboration with Trackman's hardware, tracking, ML, and Virtual Golf teams to deliver seamless, world-class experiences. This is a unique opportunity to become one of the first engineers shaping the future of Trackman’s simulator technology used by elite athletes and golfers around the world.

The role

You will help build a Windows-based real-time vision platform that captures camera streams, runs AI-based image analysis, and outputs video overlays. The role focuses on low-latency camera integration and high-performance video pipelines. This work sits at the heart of SimTech's camera platform the low-level foundation that everything from swing capture to AI coaching will be built on. Our current team is strong in vision/ML, and we need an engineer who specializes in camera integration and real-time video pipelines.

What you will do

• 
Design and implement low-latency camera capture pipelines on Windows.

• 
Integrate with 3rd party cameras using vendor SDKs as well as our own custom camera modules

• 
Build reliable frame pipelines from capture to inference handoff to overlay output.

• 
Optimize for stable FPS, low jitter, and deterministic end-to-end latency.

• 
Implement robust camera lifecycle handling: hot-plug, disconnect/reconnect, error recovery.

• 
Work closely with ML engineers to define frame formats, metadata, and timing contracts.

• 
Build diagnostics: dropped-frame counters, latency telemetry, and health logging.

• 
Support production readiness across different camera models and hardware configurations.

Success in this role means delivering stable, low-latency dual-camera pipelines with reliable recovery mechanisms, robust telemetry, and a well-documented architecture that enables the broader SimTech team to confidently build on the platform.

Job requirements

• 
5+ years in real-time video, machine vision, or camera systems engineering.

• 
Strong C++ (C++17 or newer) - preferably on Windows.

• 
Hands-on with Media Foundation and/or DirectShow capture stacks.

• 
Proven integration experience with industrial camera SDKs (IDS peak / uEye SDK strongly preferred).

• 
Deep understanding of pixel formats, color conversion, timestamps, and buffering.

• 
Solid grasp of USB3 Vision / GenICam concepts and camera controls (exposure, gain, trigger modes).

• 
Experience with multithreaded/parallel pipelines and performance profiling.

• 
Practical OpenCV experience for image handling and overlay operations.

• 
Experience designing fault-tolerant long-running services/applications.

Preferred qualifications: Experience with GStreamer or FFmpeg, GPU acceleration, multi-camera synchronization, inference runtimes, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and GenICam / USB3 Vision standards is considered a plus.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

Desirable

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

Did we get your attention?

We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Mentor Programme 2027 | Deloitte’s Consulting Practice | Aarhus
jobs.description:
Calling all ambitious and curious students to join Deloitte’s Mentor Programme 2027 – a unique programme for finance and economics students interested in consulting.

Are you excited about Finance Operations and Transformation? Do you wish to gain insights into the life of a consultant within the CFO area? Would you like to advance your personal and professional growth journey through exclusive sparring sessions with a mentor from Deloitte?

Then apply now for a spot in our Mentor Programme 2027!

The Mentor Programme 2027

Deloitte’s Finance Transformation (FT) department is at the heart of the Mentor Programme, offering engagement opportunities for students with an interest in Finance Transformation. Our FT team, consisting of +350 consultants based in Copenhagen and Aarhus, supports clients by operating, advising, optimising, and managing finance functions. The work spans all areas under the CFO, including operational finance, finance optimisation, ERP implementation, performance management, and finance strategy. We collaborate with a broad range of private and public clients, including C25 companies and key public institutions, both nationally and internationally.

As part of the Mentor Programme, you will be invited to educational workshops and social events that will provide you with deep insights into our toolbox and life as a consultant. These events provide great opportunities to network with Deloitte professionals and fellow peers.

Throughout the programme, you will receive personalised guidance through 1:1 sessions with a mentor from Deloitte. These sessions are aimed at guiding you towards your personal and professional ambitions and goals. Topics touched upon with your assigned mentor can cover everything from student life, courses, and bachelor/thesis topics to career sparring and dialogues around CV and applications. The mentor-mentee relation is centred around your development, whereas you will be the one to choose the topics that are most relevant for you to discuss.

The Mentor Programme runs from January to September 2027. Throughout the course of the programme, we have arranged four main events that we expect you to commit to attending*:

• Event 1, ultimo January: The Beginning | Introducing the Programme & Deloitte

• Event 2, primo March: Opening our Toolbox | Strengthening Your Skills

• Event 3, ultimo April: Unique Insights | Explore & Engage

• Event 4, ultimo August: Festive Culmination | Celebrating the Finalization of Your Journey**

In addition to the main events, we will arrange smaller group sessions with 3-4 mentees and mentors. These sessions will allow you to network in a more personal setting and gain deeper insights into areas such as client projects and tools.

* The event dates are subject to change, and the final dates will be provided later.

** All events are held in the evening and start at 16:00 earliest.

We embrace students on their bachelor’s and 1st year master’s degree with interest in all aspects under the CFO’s responsibilities.

The Mentor Programme 2027 is centred around Finance Transformation. However, a few mentors from two other departments are represented and involved in the programme. This involves the following:

• Strategy & Performance (Monitor) is Deloitte’s strategy practice that combines deep industry insights with cutting-edge methods to help leaders resolve their most critical decisions, drive value, and achieve transformational success. We specialise in end-to-end strategy consulting, helping chief executives and their teams solve their most complex problems by advising on everything from growth and corporate strategies to operating models and cost and capital optimisation. We deliver tailored solutions that ensure long-term success and efficiency for our clients.

• Corporate Finance Advisory is part of Deloitte’s dedicated M&A practice, guiding clients through every stage of the transaction lifecycle – from identifying targets and buyers to structuring deals and realising post-close value. We support a diverse range of clients, including corporates, private equity firms, financial investors, and family-owned businesses. Our integrated service offering span sell- and buy-side advisory, debt capital advisory, and complex financial modelling. By combining deep industry expertise with rigorous financial analysis, we enable leaders to navigate complexity, structure optimal deals, and unlock sustainable value - creating an impact that matters.

In case you are interested in joining the Mentor Programme with a mentor from one of the abovementioned departments, please select this in the application form. Please note that Finance Transformation is the main department represented, hence the largest proportion of mentors and mentees will be within Finance Transformation.

Be aware that Strategy & Performance (Monitor) is only represented in Aarhus, while Corporate Finance Advisory is represented in both Aarhus and Copenhagen Mentor Programme 2027.

How to apply

To ensure that all participants obtain maximum value from the Mentor Programme 2027, we have limited number of seats. To apply for the programme, you must attach your CV and grade transcript, as well as answer the following screening questions in the sign-up form:

• Why do you wish to participate in the Mentor Programme?

• Which experiences and competences do you bring into the network?

• What are your career ambitions and key strengths for your future career?

We expect to get back to you shortly after the application deadline. If you are selected to proceed in the application process, you will receive an invitation to a short online interview about your motivation.

Apply now to seize the opportunity to unleash your potential and expand your network.

Deadline: Sunday November 1, 2026.

Contact

If you have any questions, you are welcome to reach out to our mentor coordinators:

Katrine Hjenner Rasmussen (Copenhagen)

ahjenner@deloitte.dk

Phone: + 45 3093 6297

Ditte Marie Jørgensen (Aarhus)

dittemariej@deloitte.dk

Phone: + 45 2970 6613

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.
