jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Mathematical Modeling for Health Policy - DTU Management
jobs.description:
Are you interested in research in cutting edge modeling techniques addressing urgent questions in health? Are you interested in quantitative methods that can be applied to relevant policy questions? 

This position involves a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of policy relevant questions and mathematical modeling methods to answer some of the following questions: How can we develop multi-disease models to quantify overall health outcomes? What interventions in and out of the healthcare system improve outcomes for multiple diseases?

The Department of Technology, Management and Economics at Technical University of Denmark invites applications for a 3-year PhD position in disease modeling and Cost-Effectiveness Analysis starting in February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The PhD student will be part of the Management Science Division and affiliated with the Operations & Supply Chain Management Section.

The project will include:

• Developing multiple models for cardiovascular disease, Type 2 diabetes, and stroke and integrating them into one model 
• Estimating the health effects and costs of non-healthcare interventions that prevent metabolic disease over the next 20 years in Denmark
• Conduct a cost-effectiveness analysis
• Develop methods to improve modeling of multiple diseases
Copenhagen — ranked the world's most livable city — offers a safe, sustainable urban environment, a rich cultural scene, and an enviable work-life balance. As part of DTU Management, you'll combine this quality of life with a dynamic, interdisciplinary research setting at one of Europe's leading technical universities."

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will work with academics and healthcare professionals to develop modelling methods to improve health policy modeling and assessment. As a PhD student, you will: 

• Be responsible for conducting your own research project
• Contribute to new knowledge about health policy modeling
• Strive to publish your work worldwide in recognised journals
• Collaborate with researchers from the Management Science Division
• Present your work at international conferences and seminars
• Assist in teaching and co-supervise engineering students with their thesis work
• Take classes equivalent to 30 ECTS over the PhD project period
The PhD scholarship is a full-time position allowing you to become a research scientist and benefit from the academic activities at the department. The yearly salary is internationally highly competitive. Department duty work (teaching) is very limited, allowing you to focus on your PhD project. 

The PhD project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Anneke Claypool and co-supervised by Professor Martin Utley and the candidates for the PhD position will be assessed on the following criteria:

• Profound knowledge in Operations Research and Management Science and/or disease modeling
• Knowledge in and practical experiences with programming (e.g., Python, Java, Julia, R, etc.)
• Knowledge in healthcare operations management, health policy modeling, cost-effectiveness analysis, health economic assessment, and related fields
We seek to recruit a PhD student with experience in simulation modeling, an interest in health policy, and a background in management science, operations research, computer science, applied mathematics, quantitative health policy, epidemiology, or a related field.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained by contacting Assistant Professor Anneke Claypool, e-mail: alacl@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Management at www.man.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A 1-page research statement describing how you would formulate a research project based on the given information
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Who are we?
DTU Management conducts excellent research in the intersection between management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability within society. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master and PhD level across DTU’s study programs. The department has around 200 employees, approximately 50% coming from abroad. In the Management Science Division, the research ranges from mathematical-based optimization models to process-oriented management models and is used in basically every sector, such as transport, energy infrastructure, the education sector, as well as the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Natural Language Processing
jobs.description:
PhD Project in Cultural Reasoning with Language Models

The AI Section at the Department of Computer Science invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational modelling and evaluation of cultural interpretation with language models. The position is part of the research project “CuRe: Cultural Reasoning for Responsible Language Model Development” (DFF project 5334-00088B), funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark.

The expected start date is February 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Language models can produce fluent interpretations of texts while obscuring the cultural assumptions, uncertainty and alternative readings underlying their answers. CuRe investigates how language models understand and reason about culture, ambiguity and interpretation, and how these capabilities can be evaluated and improved to support responsible language model development. Literary texts provide a demanding testbed: their interpretation depends on historical and cultural knowledge, close attention to textual evidence and the ability to accommodate several plausible readings.

The PhD candidate will develop computational methods and evaluation resources for culturally grounded interpretation. Working closely with researchers in natural language processing and literary studies, the candidate is expected to:

• 
construct datasets and benchmarks linking literary passages, relevant cultural and historical context, textual evidence and expert or reader interpretations;

• 
analyse what cultural knowledge and interpretive strategies language models use, where their interpretations fail and how confidently they present uncertain conclusions;

• 
develop methods for grounding interpretations in evidence and for representing uncertainty, ambiguity and multiple plausible interpretations;

• 
evaluate the resulting methods through automatic experiments and studies with literary scholars and other readers; and

• 
publish the results in leading venues in natural language processing, artificial intelligence and computational humanities.

 The exact research questions will be refined together with the successful candidate. Relevant methodological directions include language model evaluation and probing, retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation, explicit representations of interpretive evidence and uncertainty, data annotation, human-centred evaluation and multilingual or cross-cultural analysis. The empirical work will primarily use modern Scandinavian literary texts, while aiming to develop methods and findings that generalise beyond literature. The project includes a planned research stay at McGill University.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates with a strong computational background and an interest in how language, culture and interpretation can be studied rigorously. Applicants may have a background in natural language processing, computational linguistics, computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, data science, digital humanities or a closely related field. Formal training in literary studies is not required, but the successful candidate must be motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries and to engage seriously with humanities research questions.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD fellow will join the CoAStaL research group and the AI Section at the Department of Computer Science. The research environment brings together faculty, postdoctoral researchers and PhD students working on multilingual and cross-cultural NLP, multimodality, language model training and evaluation, responsible AI and computational humanities. The section collaborates broadly with leading research groups in Denmark and abroad.

CuRe is an interdisciplinary collaboration with the Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics at the University of Copenhagen. The project builds on established joint work in computational literary studies and provides access to large literary corpora, domain expertise and relevant annotation resources. The PhD fellow will therefore be part of both a technically strong NLP environment and a close collaboration with literary scholars.

The group is part of the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern GPU computing resources, shared data and annotation infrastructure and access to relevant text corpora.

Principal supervisor: Associate Professor Desmond Elliott, Department of Computer Science, de@di.ku.dk.

Co-supervisor: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Daniel Hershcovich, Department of Computer Science, dh@di.ku.dk.

Co-supervisor: Associate Professor Jens Bjerring-Hansen, Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, jbh@hum.ku.dk.

The PhD programme

The position is offered as a three-year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme).

Qualifications needed
To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment 

The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 31,800 DKK/approx. 4,200 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

Responsibilities and tasks

• 
Carry through an independent research project under supervision

• 
Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE

• 
Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• 
Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities

• 
Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals

• 
Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project

We are looking for the following qualifications:

• 
A master’s degree or equivalent qualification relevant to the PhD project.

• 
Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with machine learning or natural language processing tools.

• 
Knowledge of modern NLP and language models and an ability to design, implement and evaluate computational experiments.

• 
Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: language model evaluation, retrieval or retrieval-augmented generation, data annotation, interpretability, multilingual NLP or computational humanities.

• 
Relevant research experience, publications, thesis work or professional activities.

• 
Ability to work independently, formulate research questions and collaborate across computer science and the humanities.

• 
A curious and critical mindset with a strong interest in culture, interpretation and responsible AI.

• 
Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of a Scandinavian language or experience with literary analysis is an advantage but not a requirement.

Application and Assessment Procedure

Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

Please include: 

• 
Motivated letter of application (maximum one page) explaining your motivation for the project, your relevant qualifications and the research directions that particularly interest you.

• 
Curriculum vitae including information about your education, research or work experience, language skills and other skills relevant to the position.

• 
Original diplomas for bachelor’s and master’s degrees and transcripts of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If the master’s degree has not yet been completed, a certified or signed recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

• 
Publication list, if applicable.

• 
Reference letters, if available.

Application deadline: 

The deadline for applications is November 8th, 2026, 23:59 CET

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process 
After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 49.

Questions
For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the project supervisor Daniel Hershcovich at dh@di.ku.dk or +45 53 33 88 04.

[General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/].

The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Your Role

As an experienced Engineer in “Manufacturing Engineering” which is a part of the “Hardware Development & Supply” organization, you will act as a key technical contributor across R&D and Production. Your responsibilities will be to ensure that Trackman’s new and existing hardware platforms can be produced reliably, at scale and volume.

You will be expected to ensure design for manufacturing (DFM). This role suits an experienced engineer who enjoys combining hands-on engineering with technical expertise and ownership.

• Design, build and validate production- and test solutions for all relevant technologies. This includes fixtures for assemblies, automation, “bed of nails” setups, and other supporting electronics.

• Drive collaboration with EMS suppliers, including transfer, ramp-up, and continuous improvement of test and production processes

• Analyze production and test data to improve yield, quality, and robustness, and to support data-driven decision-making

• Strengthen the ability to plan and execute according to plan, i.e. spending part of your time doing project coordination work supporting the whole team.

Job requirements

What You Bring

We imagine that you:

• Hold a degree in Electronics Engineering and have extensive experience (5+ years) within electronics development, production, or test engineering

• Advanced user of relevant lab test equipment (e.g., oscilloscope, signal generators, spectrum analyzers etc.)

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology  Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Pandora sells more jewellery than any brand in the world, at a gross margin of around 80 percent, among the strongest in consumer goods. That strength is what lets the brand keep creating, designing, crafting and showing up for the people who wear it, and what earns the trust of the investors who back it. Guarding it, piece by piece and collection by collection, is what this newly created role is for. We deliver on our promises, and precious metals at multi-year highs are testing every jewellery maker's discipline right now. The brands that keep their craft and their strength through it will set the pace. That is the work, and it starts immediately.

Pandora's success is built on product: design that powers both the love for the brand and the profit that sustains it, and an assortment where every piece earns its place, in the stores and in people's hearts. You will build product profitability governance with our Product organization: what enters the assortment and on what threshold, what leaves it and when, and how design, cost, price and mix add up to a portfolio that earns steady love from millions.

You lead through mandate and the forums you chair, not headcount: the team is deliberately senior and flat, and your counterparts are the CPO leadership team, Merchandising, Revenue Growth Management, Craft & Supply finance and the CFO office. Your work is in front of the Executive Leadership Team every cycle, at the center of the company's strategic agenda.

What you will do

• Own the numbers behind what every product costs and earns, hands-on in the cost and BI systems, and build the story behind them, told at Executive Leadership and investor standard.

• Partner Product Strategy, Merchandising, pricing and Craft & Supply finance on how design choices become cost, how whole product families keep earning as they grow, and the link between what we choose to sell and what we charge.

• Hold the finance position with senior product stakeholders on thresholds and lifecycle decisions, and keep the partnership strong while you do it.

• Direct a product finance analyst on content and draw on a shared analytics bench built for exactly this work. Contribute to building agentic capabilities to expand the value you deliver.

What is needed to succeed

• 10+ years in product or gross margin finance from vertically integrated retail or consumer goods; you have run a costing or product-profitability function, not only analyzed one.

• Hands-on analytical depth that has stayed recent: you build and defend margin baselines yourself, and master data is familiar ground.

• A track record of building governance that held: gates or lifecycle forums with thresholds that survived contested, sponsored proposals.

• Credibility in front of a CFO and a CPO in the same meeting.

Who you are

• A self-starter: you break the ice on work nobody has owned before and bring structure where there was none.

• You develop and defend your own point of view, and you change it when the evidence says so.

• Consumer-centric: you know growth comes from products people love and a brand they think of first, and you read margin through that lens. Multipliers, not mechanical levers.

• You believe finance is a strategic copilot to the business, in the room when plans are made, not after they are priced. And you see it as the essential guardrail that keeps a company strong enough to be trusted, by the people who wear the jewellery and the investors who back it.

• You can have difficult conversations respectfully: holding strategic financial realities against a proposal someone loves, and keeping the relationship.

• People-centric and a collaborator: you build capability in others and win as a team across functions.

Reporting into the Sr Director, Global Product & Marketing Finance, you will join a small, senior team at the center of a chapter Pandora is building on design, brand and the discipline underneath them, with a mandate sponsored from the top of the company, the room to build, and a market that will not wait.

Additional information:

Global Career Band 4A - Senior Manager.

Hybrid Working Flexibility – 3 days in office per week

Location Copenhagen; Global scope.

English is our working language; Danish is not required.

Did we get your attention?

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics
jobs.description:
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at the Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Roskilde Campus, Denmark, within the Environmental Science and Toxicology department. The position is available from February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Title
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics

Research area and project description
Spatial metabolomics enables the study of biochemical processes and human–environment interactions at micrometer to cellular resolution (single cell metabolomics). Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is increasingly used to investigate how environmental stressors and micropollutants affect biological systems across space and time. However, data processing, image segmentation, multimodal image registration, reproducible computational workflows and biological interpretation remain major challenges.

This project will develop computational methods and open-source tools for processing, analyzing and interpreting MSI and spatial metabolomics data. The methods will be applied to microbial communities, environmental samples and tissues to uncover spatially resolved biotransformation processes and metabolic responses to environmental stressors.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational science, biochemistry, microbiology and analytical chemistry. The project will combine computational method development with experimental spatial metabolomics including signal preprocessing, machine learning, spatial statistics, image registration and interactive software development. The PhD student will join an interdisciplinary team of chemists, microbiologists, biologists and computational scientists and contribute to both methodological development and biological applications.

The position includes:
• Developing batch-processing workflows for MSI and metabolomics data, including normalization, quantification and feature alignment.
• Developing spatial segmentation methods, including uncertainty-aware and spatially regularized clustering.
• Collaborating with experimental scientists, mass spectrometrists and biologists to validate methods against experimental and biological datasets. Ensure reliable implementation of automated quality control, testing, documentation and reproducibility reporting.
• Communicating computational results clearly to interdisciplinary and non-computational re-searchers. Processing and analyzing imaging datasets and presenting results at internal and international scientific meetings.
• Publishing methodological and application studies and releasing well-documented open-source software.
• Close supervision and collaboration with dedicated researchers and senior investigators.
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
We are seeking highly motivated candidates with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research. Applicants should hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, bioinformatics/ cheminformatics, AI/ML, data science, chemistry, computational biology, chemometrics, analytical chemistry or a related discipline.

Essential qualifications:
• Solid background in computational chemistry, image processing, omics data analysis and/or mass spectrometry
• Strong interest in spatial metabolomics and its applicationsDesirable qualifications:
• Experience with mass spectrometry, microscopy, microbial systems, or analytical chemistry
• Ability to work independently as well as in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams
Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Roskilde Campus, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Optical Design Engineers for our High Power Beam Combining team
jobs.description:
Optical Design Engineers for our High Power Beam Combining team

Location: Farum, Denmark | Level: PhD / Postdoc / Experienced Engineer

The Mission: Build the Next Generation of SBC Systems

At Ibsen Photonics, we are developing Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures. We are looking for creative, hands-on Optical Design Engineers to take full ownership of designing, building, and optimising our SBC platform.

This role bridges the gap between theoretical physics and industrial reality. You won’t just design on a screen; you will spend significant time in the lab, iterating rapidly from proof-of-concept to robust, production-ready, scalable systems.

Key responsibilities:

• Design & Assemble: Develop compact, efficient SBC modules using Ibsen’s world-class transmission gratings, while considering optical beam paths, thermal effects and mechanical constraints.

• System Optimisation: Drive performance by refining optical alignment, mechanical stability, and complex thermal management for high-power loads in a reiterative process: design – experiment – optimise.

• Characterisation: Use advanced diagnostics to maintain beam quality (low M²) during power scaling, including wavefront sensing and spectral analysis.

• Full Lifecycle Ownership: Source optical/mechanical components and manage the transition from experimental prototypes to scalable, volume-ready designs.

• Global Collaboration: Work closely with an internal team and international partners, including potential overseas visits for joint prototyping and testing.

What you bring

You are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a “build-test-learn” environment. Ideally, you possess:

• Education: A PhD or Postdoc in Optics, Photonics, Laser Physics, or a related field.

• Expertise:

• Hands on experience with (high-power) fibre and free-space optical systems, precise alignment, and experimental troubleshooting.

• Understanding of (and ideally experience with) SBC and CBC beam combining techniques.

• Beam quality measurement and analysis.

• Mechanical design of low-tolerance devices

• Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of Gaussian optics, beam propagation, and high-power laser effects (thermal lensing, runaway-effects, mitigation strategies).

• Software Skills: Proficiency in optical simulation tools (e.g., Zemax) and familiarity with mechanical CAD.

• Mindset: Independent enough to drive a project and work on your own, but collaborative enough to thrive in a flat-hierarchy, cross-functional team, sharing insights and discussing projects/next steps. The role is highly experimental and hands-on, requiring independence and a strong drive to make systems work in practice, not just on paper.

• Security Clearance: You are a European citizen with no family ties to Russia or Russian allied territories, and you have a clean criminal record.

Why join Ibsen Photonics?

• High Impact: Your designs will directly shape the future of high-brightness laser systems for manufacturing, defence, telecommunications, and science.

• Freedom to Innovate: We value experimental drive—if you have a better way to align or stabilise a system, we want to see it.

• Danish Engineering Culture: Enjoy a supportive environment with fast decision-making, real ownership, and a healthy work-life balance.

jobs.description:
Om du är på jakt för nya utmaningar på jobbet och funderar på att jobba i Danmark är kardiologen på Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital i Slagelse ett självklart val.

Här kan du vara med och påverka framtidens hjärtmedicin och samtidigt få möjlighet att utveckla och leda ditt eget specialområde.

På hjärtmedicinska avdelningen (Medicin 2) kommer du som specialistläkare att spela en central roll för den kliniska verksamheten och yrkesområdets utveckling. Du kommer att arbeta i nära samarbete med avdelningens övriga specialistläkare, chefer och andra professioner för att skapa smidiga och sammanhängande patientförlopp.

Yrkesmässiga utmaningar och ett flexibelt arbetsliv

Som specialistläkare hos oss får du inte bara en tjänst. Du får möjlighet att styra inriktningen inom ett eller flera specialområden, om du har ambitionen och intresset för det.

Du får

• möjlighet att ta ansvar för och utveckla ett helt eget specialområde inom exempelvis ischemi, arytmi, hjärtklaffssjukdomar eller bilddiagnostik i form av ekokardiografi, hjärt-CT och hjärt-MR

• möjlighet att delta i forskningen vid avdelningen

• möjlighet att ingå i en högspecialiserad miljö med engagerade kollegor

• ett nära samarbete med övriga professioner och en hög grad av kollegialt utbyte.

Dessutom kan vi anpassa tjänsten så att den passar dina behov. På Medicin 2 lägger vi stor vikt vid att skapa balans mellan arbete och fritid, och vi prioriterar stort inflytande och ansvar.

Om dig

Vi tror att du

• är specialistläkare i kardiologi, eller är på väg att bli det

• fokuserar på att utveckla vårdkvaliteten och förbättra patientförloppet

• trivs i en miljö där man både för ett nära samarbete och arbetar självständigt

• bidrar till en aktiv och god arbetsmiljö

• har ett intresse för kvalitet, utbildning och eventuellt forskning

• kommunicerar öppet och konstruktivt.

Om oss

Vår avdelning bedriver verksamhet i två olika lokaler i Næstved respektive Slagelse, som ligger 30 km från varandra.

I Slagelse består avdelningen av två vårdavdelningar med 24 respektive 20 sängplatser. Därutöver har vi en hjärtmottagning samt det vårdmässiga ansvaret för en hormonmottagning.

I Næstved består avdelningen av ett trombos- och koagulationscentrum, en hjärtmottagning samt det vårdmässiga ansvaret för en hormonmottagning. Utöver detta rymmer lokalerna även ett diagnostiskt centrum.

Vi är för närvarande 12 specialistläkare inom kardiologi samt specialistläkare inom avdelningens övriga specialistfunktioner.

Vi ansvarar för undervisningen av medicinstudenter från Köpenhamns universitet.

Därför ska du välja Midt- och Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- och Vestsjællands Hospital fokuserar vi på yrkeskompetens, samarbete mellan professioner, kvalitet, utbildning och forskning.

Specialister spelar en central roll både för den kliniska verksamheten och för den ämnesspecifika utvecklingen, och du blir en del av en miljö med hög grad av specialisering, tydliga ambitioner och goda möjligheter att påverka utvecklingen inom ditt specialistområde.

Vi erbjuder en arbetsplats där fokus ligger på vårdkvalitet, kontinuitet i patientförloppet och förutsättningar som främjar såväl kliniskt arbete som utbildning och forskning.

Din huvudsakliga arbetsplats kommer att vara i Slagelse som har goda transportförbindelser med bland annat Odense, Köpenhamn och övriga Själland.

Är du redo för nästa steg?

Vill du vara med och utveckla kardiologin på Midt- og Vestsjælland? Då ser vi gärna att du hör av dig.

Mer information

Om du vill ha mer information om tjänsten är du välkommen att kontakta tillförordnad chefsläkare Roman Sykulski på tel. +45 56 51 41 34 eller chefsjuksköterska Camilla Vest på tel. +45 93 56 84 89.

Villkor, lön och anställning

Du kommer att ingå i ett jourteam med bakjoursansvar från ditt eget hem i egenskap av överläkare och ha jour utanför arbetsplatsen i egenskap av specialistläkare.

Vi har omfattande erfarenhet av att hitta flexibla lösningar som möjliggör ett hållbart arbetsliv, så kontakta oss gärna för ett förutsättningslöst samtal om vilka möjligheter som finns.

Den professionella bedömningen av sökanden kommer att baseras på sökandens uppgifter om sina egna kompetenser i förhållande till de sju läkartjänsterna. Om du söker en tjänst som överläkare kommer en professionell bedömning att genomföras som kommer att vara avgörande för din kvalifikation som överläkare.

Anställningen sker enligt avtalet mellan Danske Regioner och YL/Overlægeforeningen, beroende på vilken tjänst som söks, och är villkorad med att det finns en tillfredsställande børneattest (utdrag ur belastningsregistret som visar om en person dömts för sexualbrott mot barn under 15 år).

Vi önskar tillsätta tjänsten senast eller enligt överenskommelse.

Hjälp med flytt och undervisning i danska

Om du vill flytta till Danmark i samband med anställningen erbjuder vi kostnadsfri, professionell hjälp med flytt och bosättning nära sjukhuset eller eventuellt i Köpenhamn. Du får hjälp med allt från att hitta boende till registrering och eventuella medföljande familjemedlemmar.

En viktig del av arbetet som specialistläkare är kommunikationen mellan läkare och patient. För patientsäkerhetens skull kräver därför Region Sjælland att våra specialistläkare ska ha kunskaper i danska språket på en tillfredsställande nivå. Vi tillhandahåller därför en språklärare för privatundervisning så att du så snabbt som möjligt kan kommunicera med dina patienter på en nivå där ni förstår varandra.

Det innebär att vi förväntar oss att du är inställd på att lägga tid på att lära dig danska, både i tal och skrift.

Se mer om vad vi erbjuder i form av hjälp här

Rekryteringsprocessen

När vi har mottagit din ansökan kommer vi att bedöma om dina kvalifikationer matchar det vi söker, och du kommer initialt att bjudas in till en intervju via Teams. Om båda parter är intresserade av att fortsätta dialogen kommer du att bjudas in till ett rekryteringssamtal på sjukhuset, där du får träffa avdelningens ledning och personal samt vår HR- och språkkonsult.

Ansökningstid

Vi kommer att granska ansökningarna till tjänsten löpande, så vänta inte för länge med att ansöka.

Verksamhetsområde

Den 1 januari 2027 slås Region Själland och Region Hovedstaden samman och bildar Region Østdanmark till följd av sjukvårdsreformen. Ditt verksamhetsområde kommer att vara Region Østdanmark, inklusive alla tillhörande organisatoriska enheter.

Läs mer om vad verksamhetsområdet innebär på Region Østdanmarks webbplats.

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbetar vi varje dag för att främja ett hälsosamt liv genom förebyggande åtgärder och behandling inom ramen för en samordnad hälso- och sjukvårdsinsats. Som sjukhus förenar vi psykiatri och somatik. Vårt mål är att patienter och medborgare ska få bra och trygg vård av hög kvalitet.

Som medarbetare blir du en del av ett innovativt, kompetent och organisatoriskt stabilt sjukhus där vi gör skillnad för de människor som behöver oss. Lärande och utveckling är en del av vardagen och sker i professionella sammanhang med ett gemensamt ansvar. Det sker även mellan olika avdelningar.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital betjänar ett upptagningsområde med cirka 230 000 invånare. Vi har 766 vårdplatser och cirka 5 000 anställda fördelade på 20 avdelningar, däribland 16 somatiska och psykiatriska avdelningar.

Vi erbjuder en gedigen forskningsmiljö med 13 professorer och en stark yrkesmässig utbildningsmiljö, där vi varje år välkomnar cirka 2 700 studenter, elever och läkare som deltar i vidareutbildning.

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Startløn for overenskomstansatte

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.

Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbejder vi hver dag for at fremme det sunde liv ved at forebygge og behandle i en sammenhængende sundhedsindsats. Som hospital forener vi psykiatri og somatik. Vores mål er, at patienter og borgere oplever gode og trygge forløb af høj kvalitet.

Som medarbejder bliver du en del af et nytænkende, fagligt og organisatorisk robust hospital, hvor vi gør en forskel for de mennesker, der har brug for os. Læring og udvikling er en del af hverdagen og sker i fagligt forpligtende fællesskaber. Også på tværs af afdelinger.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital dækker et opland på ca. 230.000 borgere. Vi har 766 sengepladser og er omkring 5.000 ansatte fordelt på 20 afdelinger, herunder 16 somatiske og psykiatriske specialer.

Vi tilbyder et solidt forskningsmiljø med 13 professorer og et stærkt fagligt uddannelsesmiljø, hvor vi hvert år byder cirka 2.700 studerende, elever og læger i videreuddannelsesforløb velkommen.

Are you an experienced bookkeeper who enjoys working independently and taking full responsibility for the day-to-day finances? Do you like having the full overview and making sure everything is in order – even when things get busy? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

You know what good bookkeeping requires, and you have experience taking responsibility for the full financial function. Even when things get busy.

We develop technical solutions that make a real difference for our customers – and we need you to make sure our finances are in order, so the rest of the organisation can focus on what they do best.

What will you be doing?

You will be a key part of our team, working closely with management and external partners.

In practice, this means:

• Payroll processing and payroll administration for all employees.

• Accounts payable and accounts receivable, as well as day-to-day bookkeeping.

• Budget follow-up and reporting to management.

• Preparing the annual accounts and ensuring everything is ready for the audit on time.

Who are you?

You have at least 5 years of experience as a bookkeeper and are an experienced SAP user. You know your way around financial accounts, and you are comfortable taking responsibility for the company’s overall financial operations. You communicate clearly in Danish and English – and if you also speak German, that is a plus.

Most importantly, you take responsibility, work in a structured way and find practical solutions rather than waiting for them to appear.

What do we offer?

Based in Aalborg with limited travel. An informal culture with short decision-making processes and a strong sense of professional pride. The opportunity to shape your own responsibilities and develop your skills as part of a team of talented colleagues across different disciplines. Salary based on qualifications.

Application

If you would like to hear more about the position or have any questions, please feel free to contact COO Klaus Knudsen on +45 31 43 40 60 or at klaus.knudsen@aalborg-hcs.com

The position starts in November – preferably sooner.

Please send your application to job@aalborg-hcs.com

The application deadline is as soon as possible. We will conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and hire once we have found the right candidate.

We look forward to receiving your application.

About aalborg hc systems

At aalborg hc systems, we design and deliver thermal systems for district heating networks in the Nordics, Germany and the rest of Europe. We help utilities and municipalities electrify and transform their heat supply – without compromising on security of supply or economy. It’s a specialised discipline that only a few companies in Europe master – and we’re proud of that.

We were formerly the low temperature division of Aalborg CSP and continue from 2026 as an independent company within the German Alois Müller Group. In Aalborg we are around 25 employees – and around 1,100 across the group.

Project Manager for strategic property projects

Would you like to use your project management expertise to deliver property projects that make a difference?

Copenhagen Contractors A/S is a Danish company operating internationally. We value agility, teamwork and a flat organisational structure in which employees take initiative and adopt a hands-on approach. We are looking for a Project Manager to support the planning, management and delivery of projects across national and international markets.

Copenhagen Contractors A/S is a subsidiary of Copenhagen Group A/S. The company operates within the defense sector and delivers complex projects and turnkey solutions for major national and international clients, including the United Nations and the Danish Armed Forces.

We are currently working on several property development projects, with further projects in the pipeline. You will primarily be involved in national projects, with occasional international assignments, while being based at our headquarters in Nordhavn, Copenhagen.**

About the role**

You will become a key member of a newly established Real Estate department within a well-established company. The department will consist of approximately four colleagues: you, the Head of Real Estate, an Architect and a Project Developer.

You will work on a diverse range of projects, ranging in size from approximately 300 to 15,000 m². These include defense-related developments, offices, residential projects and water-related construction projects. We work with temporary, semi-permanent and permanent structures, although the majority of our projects involve permanent construction.

As Project Manager, you will be responsible for driving projects from initial ideas and concepts through planning, pricing, design and construction to final delivery. You will coordinate internal and external stakeholders and help ensure that projects are delivered in accordance with agreed objectives, timelines, budgets and quality requirements.

We believe in short decision-making processes. You will therefore experience a high degree of autonomy and minimal unnecessary administration. In return, we expect you to take initiative, demonstrate ownership, and have the confidence and ability to make decisions and drive projects forward.**

Your profile**

We imagine that you:

• Have +5 years of experience within project and construction management.

• Have a practical understanding of the construction process and appreciate the relationship between functionality, buildability, quality and cost.

• Are structured, pragmatic and solution-oriented and are comfortable coordinating consultants, contractors and other project stakeholders.

• Have a strong network among consultants and main contactors in the Danish market.

• Are motivated by autonomy, responsibility and the opportunity to influence projects rather than by rigid processes and traditional management structures.

• Have an entrepreneurial approach and enjoy taking initiative, making decisions and assuming responsibility for new areas.

• Are fluent in both Danish and English, in writing and in speech. English is the company’s official working language.

Could this be your next opportunity?

You can submit your application through our website, and if you would like to learn more about the role, you are always welcome to contact:

**Head of Real Estate

Lars Bramsen

**Phone: +45 2116 8959

Email: labr@cphgroup.com

Job Description

Would you like to be part of exciting and challenging projects within the IT world? Do you dream of having the opportunity to contribute to some of Denmark’s most business-critical IT solutions? Then we have the ideal student job for you.

At Netcompany, we are looking for a student who wants to take part in our innovative projects. Here, you will have the chance to influence our solutions while working alongside some of the industry’s most skilled colleagues, who will inspire you and support your learning.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a student assistant with us, you will be given responsibility from day one and become an important part of one of our teams. You will experience how your work directly contributes and creates value in the solutions we deliver to our clients. A student position with us gives you the opportunity to take on challenging tasks on equal footing with our full-time consultants.

We follow a well-established methodology from identifying client needs to implementing and rolling out solutions. You will therefore gain hands-on experience with developing IT systems from start to finish. You will primarily work on IT solutions and service-oriented architectures based on .NET and Java technologies, typically within maintenance, development and testing. The role provides the opportunity to put many of the skills gained during your studies into practice.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing functional and technical designs for system components.

• Programming tasks across all layers of the system.

• Configuration and development of extensions for standard platforms.

• Automation of business processes.

About you

We are looking for a student who can work approximately 16 hours per week. We are flexible during exam periods, but availability is expected in the lead-up to project deadlines and other key milestones. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are in the final year of your bachelor’s degree or have started a master’s degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field.

• Have some experience with object-oriented programming and familiarity with languages such as C# .NET and/or Java.

• Are highly motivated and eager to develop your skills.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

Retire the ERP

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

About the Role

You'll sit at the heart of our Customer function and work with our most important customers. You’ll make sure they understand the value Light brings them and drive renewals and upsell.

Your customers are Financial Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs at fast-growing multinational SaaS and tech companies. Senior, technical, time-poor. They expect you to keep up, to tell them straight when something won't work, and to make their team the hero.

We’re a young company, and we’re just starting to renew contracts. In parallel, we’re deploying Agentic Customer Engineers who help our customers make the most of Light. While they re-design customer workflows and deploy agents, you’ll own the stakeholders, the adoption, and the commercial in this motion. There's no set playbook yet. You'll write it, and we'll help.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Own existing customer relationships and drive adoption, renewal and upsell

• 
Ensure that Controllers, Finance Directors, and CFOs see the value Light brings

• 
Make finance the hero - help them do their best work and get recognition for it

• 
Partner two-in-a-box with Agentic Customer Engineers to help customers make the most of Light and our suite of AI agents

• 
Spot an engagement going sideways before the customer does, and fix it

• 
Feed what you learn back into the playbook the team is building

Experience & Qualifications

• 
5+ years owning customers in account management, customer success, consulting, or a commercial delivery role - with outcomes you can point to

• 
You hold your own with a CFO. You can talk multi-entity finance, ROI, and adoption without flinching, and you know when to push back

• 
You've driven adoption and expansion, not just kept accounts warm and sent QBRs

• 
You bring structure to messy, ambiguous engagements - clear plans, sharp prioritisation, and the judgement to know which details matter

• 
You've owned accounts and driven outcomes

• 
You use AI tools daily and have specific opinions on where they help and where they don't

• 
Fluent English; additional European languages a plus

• 
Bonus #1: Finance or accounting background

• 
Bonus #2: Experience in a forward-deployed, solutions-led, or professional-services model focused on renewals and upsell, ideally in the context of AI

You'll probably struggle here if

• 
You need a big support team, a mature playbook, and a manager on call to operate - this is a founding role with limited scaffolding

• 
You can't give a concrete example of telling a senior customer "no" and making it stick

• 
You love the status quo - this job is about change more than maintenance

• 
You've used ChatGPT once and weren't impressed - we go all in on AI at Light

The good stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a really fun and innovative environment, we offer:

💸 A competitive salary + potential stock options

🏝 Generous package of paid annual leave + public holidays

🥳 Regular socials and company off-sites (last time was in Piemonte, next time is in Provence)

🚀 A huge opportunity for career growth as you'll help shape a market-defining motion

The famous last words

Working at Light means you're embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat-code is that we've built something like this before - and are now doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it's taking off 🚀

Light is the new way to run multinational finances for modern technology companies. Run AR, AP, expenses, bookkeeping, and financial reporting automatically across all your entities — without the chaos of multiple systems. Crafted and built by the designers and engineers behind world-class companies like Spotify, X, AWS, Klarna, Google and Shopify, we empower multinational finances with a joyful user experience like no other.

About the job

Chainalysis is the cryptocurrency ghostbusters, pioneering in the blockchain analysis space. Identifying high-risk activities on the blockchain, playing a central role in ensuring cryptocurrencies are used for a legitimate purpose. Ultimately, Chainalysis is building trust in blockchains.

The Chainalysis engineering team solves large scale, technically complex data problems by ingesting, transforming and supporting nearly 1TB of data per day across multiple blockchains serving public and private sectors internationally. Our industry is evolving at a rapid pace and our job is to build a flexible platform that will allow us to adapt accordingly.

Software Engineers are at the epicenter of that mission by building and scaling the data pipelines, infrastructure and applications our customers rely on every day to stop crime, reduce financial risk and prevent financial loss.

In This Role You Will

• Be part of an Student Developer cohort from September 2026 - February 2027, working with a specific team and benefiting from local mentors

• Collaborate with experienced engineers, product managers, and designers to solve real-world problems, features that demystify crypto data, facilitate collaboration between customers in their investigations, improve our data pipelines and workflows, and more

• Develop and deploy high quality code using modern frameworks and technologies within AWS and GCP such as lambdas, Kafka, S3, Java, Typescript, Databricks, etc.

• Debug production issues and participated in a blameless post-mortem process to make our systems stronger

To Achieve Success In This Role You Have

• Customer-centric mindset to ship performant, scalable and well-tested code to production

• A strong sense of urgency and solid working engine

• Computer Science degree (or similar technical degree) in progress with an expected graduation date during 2027

• Demonstrated applications development or data engineering experience from previous internships, work experience, coding/startup competitions, open source contributions or publications

• Participated in code and architecture reviews at internships or open source projects

• Used or been exposed to React/Angular, Kafka, Spring boot and Postgres

• Strong interest in learning about cryptocurrencies from some of the most knowledgeable people in the field

About Chainalysis

Blockchain technology is powering a growing wave of innovation. Businesses and governments around the world are using blockchains to make banking more efficient, connect with their customers, and investigate criminal cases. As adoption of blockchain technology grows, more and more organizations seek access to all this ecosystem has to offer. That’s where Chainalysis comes in. We provide complete knowledge of what’s happening on blockchains through our data, services, and solutions. With Chainalysis, organizations can navigate blockchains safely and with confidence.

You belong here.

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

About the company

Do you want to take a central role in shaping how a high‑tech defense company secures reliability, compliance and world‑class product integrity on a global scale? As the new QHSE Director at Sky Watch, you will own and continuously evolve the company’s Quality and HSE foundation, ensuring that our products, processes and teams operate at a consistently high and predictable standard across the entire value chain.

You will be responsible for safeguarding Sky-Watch’s Quality Management System, driving compliance with AS9100, ISO 9001 and AQAP, and enabling stable, scalable execution in an increasingly demanding international defense environment. Through strong cross functional leadership and data driven governance, you will strengthen decision making, reduce operational risk, accelerate execution stability and help deliver a dependable customer experience built on safety, performance and traceability.

Joining Sky‑Watch means stepping into a fast‑growing scale‑up where reliability is a strategic differentiator — and where your expertise will directly influence both day‑to‑day operations and the company’s ongoing global growth journey.

You will report directly to the CEO, including direct leadership responsibility for the QA Manager and dotted line leadership of the QC Manager.

In this role, you act as a trusted advisor to the Executive Management Team, providing clear, fact based recommendations on quality, risk and compliance, and contributing actively to strategic decision‑making at enterprise level.

Your key responsibilities include:

• QHSE Strategy & Policy

• Sky‑Watch QMS (AS9100 / ISO 9001 / AQAP)

• Quality Governance & Risk Management

• Digital QHSE & Data Governance

• Continuous Improvement & NCR / CAPA

• Supplier Quality Requirements & APQP / PPAP

• Manufacturing Quality & QC oversight

• Audits & Compliance

• Health, Safety & Environment (in collaboration with the Health & Safety

• Organization / AMO)

• People Leadership & Cross‑functional Collaboration

To succeed in this role, you hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing or a related technical field, combined with at least 10 years of experience in global Quality/QHSE leadership within regulated, high‑tech industries with full value chain such as defense, aerospace or equivalent.

You have demonstrated strong results in defect reduction, execution stability and QMS maturity, and you bring hands on experience with MRB, concessions, PPAP and supplier audits. You possess deep knowledge of AS9100, AQAP and ISO 9001 requirements and are comfortable working with lifecycle product safety in a regulated environment.

You work confidently with structured problem‑solving and quality methodologies such as RCA, FMEA, Control Plans and capability analysis, and you are experienced in configuration and document control to ensure consistency and traceability. In addition, you bring strong digital QHSE literacy, using data governance, dashboards and digital adoption to create transparency, support sound decision making and drive continuous improvement across the organisation.

You are based within approximately one hour’s driving distance from Støvring and are willing to travel around 20–30 days per year.

As a person, you take ownership of your responsibilities and bring energy and commitment to your work. You are proactive and structured, balance strategic thinking with hands‑on execution, and remain calm and focused in a fast‑changing environment. With a strong analytical and curious mindset, you are able to translate complex quality, risk and compliance topics into clear, actionable messages that create understanding, alignment and strong buy‑in across senior leadership and the wider organization. You work collaboratively across functions, build trust with key stakeholders, and act as a credible role model for quality, integrity and professional judgement.

Are you the new QHSE Director at Sky‑Watch in Støvring? If so, please submit your application and CV as soon as possible. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity or religion.

For further information about the position, please contact consultant Martin Tveit, Sensu A/S, by phone at +45 26 83 38 42.

For more information about Sky‑Watch, please visit www.sky-watch.com.

Please note that applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and no application deadline is set.

Turn complexity into clear insights and recommendations

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Reversible Programming for Energy Efficient Cyber-Physical Systems (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC12)
jobs.description:
The SDU Drone Center, part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on reversible programming languages and their use for energy efficient cyber-physical systems. The position is doctoral candidate DC12, "Energy Efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

 

The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. MSCA eligibility rules apply, see the section "What we expect" below. Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.

 

What we offer

E-CoRe is a European doctoral network on reversible computing. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. As one of the E-CoRe doctoral candidates you join a cohort at partner universities across Europe, take part in joint training schools and network events, and spend secondments at partner institutions, currently planned at the University of Bologna and the University of Manchester.

The main supervisor is Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz, whose research spans programming languages, software engineering, robotics, and drones. You will be co-supervised by researchers from the Software Engineering section, and you will collaborate closely with the reversible computing group at the University of Copenhagen, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position connects to other ongoing projects at the Drone Center, including WildBotics (a newly started Marie Skłodowska-Curie doctoral network) and Robotic Intercropping, and to local companies such as Spaceline.

The position addresses a programming languages question with an applied setting: how do we write software in reversible programming languages for systems where energy matters, and how much energy does this save? The setting is low-energy computations for cyber-physical systems such as perching aerial robots and IoT devices. The work belongs to the E-CoRe work package on applications and builds on the languages and tools developed elsewhere in the network. Concretely, the work includes the following:

• 
Implementing algorithms in reversible programming languages and extending these languages where the application domain requires new constructs or idioms.

• 
Integrating the resulting software into simulated cyber-physical systems, such as perching drones and IoT sensing scenarios.

• 
Estimating energy consumption through combined hardware-level and system-level analysis, using the modelling framework developed in the network.

• 
Answering the central research question of the position: how do the energy savings from reversible computation correlate with the I/O characteristics of the system?

• 
Publishing the results at international conferences and in journals in programming languages, software engineering, and cyber-physical systems.

The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. You are expected to participate in the Drone Center's project portfolio and outreach activities and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.

 

What we expect

We expect you to hold an MSc in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field, or to complete one before the start date. The core of the work is programming languages and software. You do not need experience with drones or embedded hardware, and you do not need prior knowledge of reversible computing. You should have experience with, and an interest in, some of the following:

• 
Programming language design and implementation.

• 
Functional or declarative programming, or other work with languages beyond the mainstream.

• 
Software design and development in languages such as C, C++, Rust, Python, or Haskell.

• 
Algorithms and their analysis.

• 
Simulation, modelling, or energy estimation of computing systems.

• 
Embedded, real-time, or robotic software.

We expect you to write and speak English fluently, to work independently and with an international team, and to travel for the secondments and network events described above. We furthermore expect you to publish findings at recognised international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.

The position follows the rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and you must meet all of the following conditions at the recruitment date:

• 
You do not hold a doctoral degree. Applicants who have defended a doctoral thesis but not yet been awarded the degree are not eligible.

• 
Mobility rule: you have not resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays such as holidays are disregarded, as is compulsory national service and time covered by the 1951 Refugee Convention.

• 
You are eligible regardless of nationality.

Recruitment follows the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. The process is open, transparent, merit-based, and equitable. The position is also announced on the Euraxess portal.

 

Workplace description

The SDU Drone Center is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the Faculty of Engineering, located on the main SDU campus in Odense. At the center we research civilian drone technologies and their applications in agriculture, inspection, energy, healthcare, and nature conservation. We collaborate closely with companies in the robotics community around Odense and with research partners in Denmark and abroad. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, engineers, and faculty working on autonomous systems and the software behind them.

 

Further information

For further information, please contact Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz (ups@mmmi.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
A statement of where you have resided and carried out your main activity in the 36 months before the expected recruitment date, to document the MSCA mobility rule.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
Master's and Bachelor's degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation).

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish).

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under 'Cover letter' (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under 'Resume' (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under 'Miscellaneous documents' (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position. The position follows the MSCA Doctoral Networks funding rules. The MSCA contribution consists of a monthly living allowance of EUR 5,325.28, a monthly mobility allowance of EUR 710, and, where applicable, a monthly family allowance of EUR 660. These amounts are gross contributions to the employer. The salary paid to you is derived from these amounts after employer costs and is subject to Danish income tax and social contributions. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, this may be reflected in the salary placement within the Danish collective agreement.

The preferred start date is from 1 January 2027.

Applicants must hold a master's degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants' previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a "self-organizer".

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

This project has received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No 101120187.
