About the role and company:

I'm using AI to write the job posting, and I asked Codex to use the Slack connector to collect some "cultural proof points" about what it's like working at Templafy. This is what it came up with:

Templafy engineering culture comes across as pragmatic, product-close, technically opinionated, and unusually open about trade-offs.

· Engineers are expected to think like product builders, not just implementers. Threads often connect technical work to customer demos, pilots, product quality, adoption, and user feedback

· Pragmatism is a real value. There’s repeated language around simple/explicit code, logical PR chunks, avoiding feature creep, solving the 80% case first, building MVPs, and getting something testable into users’ hands quickly

· Quality matters, but in a practical way. Tests, E2E coverage, evals, pipeline health, flaky tests, feature-flag cleanup, and technical health all show up as shared concerns

· Engineers are candid and trusted to challenge scope. I saw people questioning whether work should be bugs vs feature requests, whether backlog items are clutter, when to pause work, and when a “quick fix” is acceptable

· Cross-functional collaboration is very present. PMs, design, solutions, support, security, platform, and product engineering are all in the same threads negotiating quality bars, customer urgency, UX, risk, and ownership

· AI/tooling curiosity is strong, but not naive. The AI guild and engineering channels show people experimenting with code review agents, AGENTS.md, evals, Codex/Claude workflows, guardrails, and agentic SDLC, while also worrying about learning, friction, false positives, security, and long-term maintainability

· There’s a bias toward async feedback and shared learning. Moving sprint review-style updates into short videos and Slack feedback is a good culture signal: fewer meetings, more continuous visibility

· Ownership is distributed. People jump in to unblock, sanity-check, investigate, create PRs, clean up flags, or hand over work when someone is away. The tone is informal but accountable

Small caution: I would avoid selling the culture as “perfectly polished.” The honest version is stronger: Templafy looks like a place where engineers have real agency, real product context, and real technical messes to improve.

The rest of this job posting is probably more like what you'd expect.

What You’ll Do

In Product Engineering, you will help build and improve product experiences used by Templafy customers. You will work with product managers, designers, and other engineers to understand customer problems, shape solutions, and deliver features from idea through production.

You will:

• 
Build, improve, and maintain customer-facing product features

• 
Collaborate with Product and Design to turn ambiguous problems into usable solutions

• 
Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully as part of your everyday engineering workflow

• 
Make technical decisions within your area and contribute to broader architecture discussions

• 
Write reliable, maintainable code that fits existing patterns and systems

• 
Use tests and fast feedback loops to support confident delivery

• 
Build early versions of ideas to evaluate real behavior instead of debating hypotheticals

• 
Help simplify product paths, remove complexity, and make features easier to test and maintain

• 
Debug issues, improve performance, and support production systems

• 
Help the team balance delivery speed, technical quality, and customer impact

• 
Contribute to engineering practices, code reviews, and technical discussions

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who enjoys product context and wants to be part of shaping what gets built, not only how it gets built.

You probably have:

• 
Strong experience building production software in a product engineering team

• 
Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools in real development work

• 
The judgment to use AI tools without outsourcing your understanding of the system

• 
Good technical judgment and the ability to make pragmatic trade-offs

• 
Experience with modern web application development

• 
A solid understanding of software design, testing, and maintainability

• 
Comfort working across frontend, backend, or full-stack

• 
Strong communication skills, especially in async and cross-functional settings

• 
A bias toward making discussions concrete through prototypes, tests, and working software

• 
A sense of ownership over outcomes, not just assigned tasks

• 
The ability to challenge scope constructively and keep work focused

Nice To Have

• 
Experience with SaaS or B2B software

• 
Experience with cloud platforms, CI/CD, observability, distributed systems

• 
Experience building AI-enabled products, agentic workflows, evals, or prompt/tooling systems

• 
Interest in improving developer experience, technical health, and team practices

What You’ll Join

You’ll join a product engineering team that cares about building useful software, learning quickly, and keeping the systems healthy enough that we can keep moving. We value people who can ask good questions, make things simpler, and help the team find the right trade-off when there is no perfect answer.

This is a good role for someone who wants meaningful product ownership, close collaboration with non-engineering colleagues, and enough technical complexity to make simplification genuinely valuable. We are looking for someone who can move fast, but who also knows that the fastest teams are usually the ones that keep their systems understandable.

Frontend: TypeScript, React, HTML/CSS/SCSS

AI: LLM integration & agentic AI (tool-calling, multi-agent)

Cloud/Infra: Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform

Role Summary

As an Assembly Operator, you will play a hands-on, critical role in transforming mechanical and electrical components into high-precision, industrial-grade collaborative robots. Working closely with our production technicians, quality specialists, and engineering teams, you will ensure every robot leaving our facility meets strict performance, safety, and reliability standards.

Key Responsibilities

Mechatronic Assembly & Integration

• 
Assemble complex mechanical, electromechanical, and electronic sub-assemblies (e.g., robot joints, motors, gearboxes, cable harnesses, and end-of-arm interfaces) strictly following standard operating procedures (SOPs) and Bills of Materials (BOM).

• 
Safely and accurately operate specialized assembly tools, including calibrated torque wrenches, manual/pneumatic press tools, fixtures, and delicate hand tools.

•

Inspection & Quality Assurance

Preferred / Nice-to-Have

Application Process

If you are eager to contribute to building the future of collaborative robotics, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant assembly experience.

Senior Software Developer

As a Senior Software Developer at Systematic, you will help build mobile software that gives field commanders real-time situational awareness - software that has to work under pressure, on devices in the field, when there is no room for confusion.

**The job

**You will join the Mobile programme, which develops software for mounted and dismounted commanders in the field. The solutions run on vehicles and handheld devices, implement resilient network protocols so frontline units share a common operational picture, and expose APIs that let customers integrate sensors and drones.

You will work across a full-stack codebase with a frontend in Angular and a backend in Java, troubleshooting and solving complex problems while shaping new features in close collaboration with domain experts, a UX designer, and a software architect. Joining the team

You will be part of a small, focused scrum team based in Aarhus - currently three developers, a tester, and an architect, spanning a range of experience levels that makes for genuine knowledge-sharing in both directions. The team is part of a larger Mobile programme spanning seven scrum teams across Denmark and Romania, giving you access to a broad community of colleagues while still working in a setting where your contributions are visible and valued. The team has worked together for three years and has built a collaborative, open culture where ideas and feedback are actively encouraged.

**Your qualifications

Experience with Java and Angular is a strong advantage, since it is what we work with day to day - but it is not a must. If you come from another strongly typed, object-oriented language such as C#, and are motivated to make the jump to Java, that is very welcome too. Furthermore, you...

•    Are proactive, open to feedback, and comfortable communicating actively with colleagues and stakeholders

•    Offer help as readily as you ask for it, and care about writing code of good quality

•    Are fluent in written and spoken English

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables, and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international, and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1,100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

jobs.occupation: Do You Have a Passion for Strategic People-Centred Management Consulting and Digital Transformation?
jobs.description:
With more than 3,000 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology and Transformations.

Deloitte Technology & Transformation is seeking an ambitious Analyst/Consultant with a passion for strategic people-centred management consulting and digital transformation. If you’re ready to apply your expertise and make an impact, we’d love to hear from you!

About the team

Who will you be working with?

You will join Deloitte’s evolving HR Strategy & Technology practice within Deloitte Consulting (Technology & Transformation) as an analyst or consultant (level dependent on experience).

You will be part of our strategy and operations community where we focus on the advisory side of HR transformation. We help clients reimagine their HR functions and operating models by combining strategic thinking with operational excellence. From leading complex end-to-end HR transformations to advising on the latest human capital trends and best practices, our consultants collaborate closely with senior HR professionals to align organizations with strategic goals, optimize HR processes, and gain a competitive edge.

If you're passionate about making a difference on the people side of strategy in a collaborative, international environment, seize this opportunity to apply for a full-time position with Deloitte's HR Strategy & Technology team.

Job Description

What work will you be doing?

Emphasizing growth and impact, our team cultivates a supportive culture where everyone can thrive. Through social activities and collaboration within our team and across Deloitte, we prioritize delivering results for our clients while fostering a supportive environment. As an Analyst/Consultant, you will collaborate closely with experienced consultants on client projects, contributing to HR strategy and transformation initiatives for multinational corporations. Additionally, you will support business development efforts and contribute to internal initiatives such as employer branding and learning programs based on your interests and background.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Approach each engagement as a collaborative case — diagnosing client needs through stakeholder interviews and organizational analysis, leveraging AI and data-driven insights, and co-creating solutions with HR leaders and business stakeholders.

• Develop comprehensive HR strategies aligned with organisational goals and objectives, collaborating closely with clients, management teams, and stakeholders through meetings and and workshops.

• Conducting research, data collection, and analysis to provide valuable insights to clients,

• Collaborating with project teams to develop high-quality deliverables, including documents and presentations, for client projects.

Qualifications

Who we are looking for?

We’re looking for a curious and analytical thinker who enjoys crafting creative solutions to complex challenges. You communicate your ideas clearly and confidently, helping others understand and embrace your advice. You value close collaboration with clients and enjoy working in fast-paced, diverse, and multidisciplinary teams.

You have the following skills and experience:

• A Master’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Strategy, IT, or a related field.

• Good interpersonal skills, workshop facilitation, and a collaborative approach to teamwork

• A genuine interest in human capital strategies and strategic organisational development.

We are particularly interested in candidates who also bring:

• Outstanding academic achievement.

• Experience within HR transformation and HR life-cycle processes.

• Experience from the consulting industry.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can contribute to our team’s success**.

Additional Information

We're looking for someone who can start as soon as possible. If you're ready to make an impact immediately, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply, please upload your resume, bachelor's and master's degree transcripts, and any other relevant documents through our application portal.

Instead of a traditional cover letter, we request that you respond to the following two questions, with each answer limited to a maximum of 200 words. These responses will provide us with a deeper understanding of your qualifications and interest in the role:

• What interests and motivates you about pursuing a career in HR Strategy & Technology consulting, and what unique contributions do you envision bringing to this role?

• How have your educational and/or professional experiences prepared you to work as an Analyst/Consultant at Deloitte?

We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Then this could be your next opportunity at COWI.

At COWI, we are looking for a Senior Concrete Design Specialist to strengthen our expertise within complex concrete structures and large infrastructure projects within major bridges, large tunnels, marine structures. Turn challenges into sustainable solutions

Your skills. Our team. Together, we design the future.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills

• Experience working in multidisciplinary and/or international project teams

• A proactive and solution-oriented approach, with the ability to work independently while contributing actively to a team

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility, and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide for our customers. With offices primarily located in Scandinavia, the UK, North America, and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy, and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Global Talent Acquisition Partner, Shruti Gupta at srgu@cowi.com or Head of Discipline Major Structures, Rúben Marques Murargi, at rumu@cowi.com Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting up teams and fora. Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV - no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Why join COWI?

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Computational Molecular Design - DTU Chemical Engineering
jobs.description:
If you are interested about establishing your career in an interdisciplinary area related to chemical engineering, novel materials design and advanced computational methods and you are looking for the best possible foundation for fulfilling your dreams and ambitions, then you should consider this opportunity.

We invite you to apply for a PhD position on a newly established project at the Center of Energy Resources Engineering, DTU Chemical Engineering.

You will be involved in the development, parameterization and validation of new coarse-grained molecular models and the development and implementation of systematic molecular simulation methods for novel polymers, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and other advanced complex materials and composites that are promising for industrial sustainable technologies. Molecular simulation output will be used for the training of machine learning models and prediction of properties for materials not synthesized in the lab, yet. In parallel, you will be part of a project that brings together experimental and computational research groups from DTU Chemical Engineering and DTU Energy. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to contribute to the development of a powerful computational platform based on multi-scale methodologies for the design of novel materials to be used for various sustainable energy technologies, such as CO2 capture, H2 storage and others. You will work with other PhD students and post-docs with similar expertise and passion for Molecular Thermodynamics, Molecular Simulation, and/or Machine Learning. You will collaborate with researchers from other groups involved in the project. A successful candidate for this position should have strong knowledge of the fundamentals in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science or closely related discipline.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Development and validation of new molecular models at the atomistic or coarse-grained level,
• Development of new, and implementation and extension of existing simulation methodologies aiming to improve efficiency and accuracy,
• Use of these computational methods to study properties of various advanced materials,
• Dissemination of research achievements through peer-reviewed publications in top rated journals and highly prestigious international conferences,
• Successfully completion of PhD courses and pursue of teaching assistant work as part of the DTU PhD program,
• Supervision of BSc and MSc student projects.
We are looking for highly motivated and academically strong candidates who have: 

• Strong programming skills, 
• Proven research experience in molecular thermodynamics, molecular simulation and/or physics inspired-machine learning,
• Hands-on experience with one of the widely used molecular simulation platforms such as GROMACS, LAMMPS, RASPA, or similar, 
• Ability to work and think independently while contributing to successful completion of collaborative research projects,
• Good written and oral communication skills in English. 
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professors Ioannis Economou, Xiaodong Liang, Georgios Kontogeorgis and possibly other members of CERE based on the application documents, alignment of the candidates with the qualifications mentioned above, and the impressions during the interview. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years. 

Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or close to this, according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Ioannis Economou at ioannis.economou@qatar.tamu.edu or Georgios Kontogeorgis at gk@kt.dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Chemical Engineering at kt.dtu.dk and about CERE at https://www.cere.dtu.dk/ 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter),
• Curriculum vitae, 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale,
• 3 names with contact details of individuals who can provide input regarding the academic competence and research experience of the candidate. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Center for Energy Resources Engineering at DTU pursues research excellence in applied thermodynamics and biothermodynamics, carbon capture utilization and storage, resources valorization, scientific computing and other related areas. It facilitates a safe and secure transition to sustainable energy. It contributes to engineering research education and supplies excellent engineers to our industrial partners and to society at large. 

The Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering at DTU is a leader in innovative teaching and research, built on core technical subjects and engineering scientific disciplines. Teaching and research cover separation processes, reaction engineering, dynamics and process regulation, process and facility planning, unit operations, heat transmission, fluid mechanics and applied thermodynamics. The Department enjoys very close relations with international partners, including a wide range of industrial companies.  

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship in Learning and Optimization Algorithms for Carbon-Aware Datacenter Fleets - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
A Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship is available in the Embedded Systems Engineering (ESE) section at DTU Compute. You will be one of the 15 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) of the MSCA Doctoral Network AEGIS, Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets, which Prof. Paul Pop, DTU, coordinates together with 10 partners across Europe.

This is a software and algorithms project. You will design algorithms and build software that decide where AI workloads run and when datacenter sites change their power use, so that hundreds of separate sites act as one carbon-efficient grid resource. The project does not involve electronics, FPGAs, or low-level embedded development, and it does not require prior knowledge of datacenters or energy systems: with a strong background in algorithms and data structures, you can learn the optimization methods and the domain during the PhD.

Marie Skłodowska-Curie fellowships are among the most respected and best-paid PhD positions in Europe. AEGIS sits where two fast-growing fields meet: datacenters and AI infrastructure on one side, energy and power systems on the other. Few people can work across both, so the skills you build here are scarce and in high demand. Our graduates will be ready for roles at cloud and datacenter operators, energy companies, grid operators, telecom companies, and in academia.

As an MSCA Doctoral Candidate, you will receive: (i) a competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement and MSCA rules; (ii) two funded secondments, at TU Berlin and at Center Denmark; and (iii) a network-wide training program. The MSCA mobility and, where applicable, family contributions form part of the total employment remuneration and are not necessarily paid as separate supplements.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project is DC13, Fleet-Level Workload Shaping with Live Grid Signals. You will build the central orchestration engine of the AEGIS fleet: reacting to live grid signals, it decides where to place, pause, or move workloads, and which sites should change their power use with batteries, cooling, and adaptable compute. You will be responsible for:

• Designing a multi-agent orchestrator that can handle multiple datacenter sites.
• Implementing multi-timescale control, from sub-second to hourly decisions.
• Developing learning-based decision methods, such as contextual bandits with bounded-regret guarantees.
• Building a counterfactual analysis toolkit that estimates the carbon savings of different orchestration policies.
• Publishing and disseminating research in international conferences and journals.
• Collaborating with the academic and industrial partners in AEGIS, and contributing to the department with service work, including being a Teaching Assistant.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

We expect that you have:

• Strong algorithms and data structures, and solid programming skills.
• A background in one or more of: machine learning, reinforcement learning, combinatorial optimization, operations research, or distributed systems.
• Curiosity, initiative, and the drive to own a problem end to end.
• Good spoken and written English.
The standard MSCA eligibility criteria also apply:

• No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment you must not yet hold a PhD.

This is a role for someone who enjoys operating in a fast-paced, ambitious and performance-driven international environment. You will interact with senior leaders and executives across the organization and take ownership of several important global P&O processes while remaining close to the day-to-day execution.

Your role

As Senior Business Partner P&O, you will become part of Xellia’s global People & Organization function and work from our headquarters in Copenhagen.

You will act as a trusted sparring partner to senior leaders while taking direct ownership of a broad portfolio of P&O activities. A significant part of your role will be to ensure that processes are not only designed, but implemented, followed through and continuously improved.

Talent Acquisition will be an important part of your role. In addition, you will provide hands-on Talent Acquisition support to the Copenhagen site when needed and contribute to continuously strengthening Xellia’s approach to recruitment and talent attraction.

• Acting as a trusted P&O partner to leaders and providing pragmatic, business-oriented advice

• Supporting leadership development and coordinating relevant leadership training and coaching initiatives

• Contributing to employee engagement activities, including analysis, action planning and follow-up

• Supporting employer branding activities in Copenhagen

• Managing external recruitment, assessment and development partners and ensuring both quality and commercial relevance

The formal scope spans strategic and operational P&O support, talent acquisition, performance management, organizational development, leadership development and vendor management. We are looking for a passionate and committed professional who sees the opportunity in a broad portfolio of responsibilities and is motivated by taking ownership, creating momentum and successfully juggling the many different priorities the role entails.

Who are you?

• Experience managing projects and processes across functions and geographies

• An interest in how AI, data and technology can strengthen HR/P&O

You are quick-thinking, resourceful and action-oriented, and you naturally create momentum around the activities you own. You are comfortable moving between senior stakeholder discussions and very practical execution – sometimes within the same hour.

You have the maturity and robustness to navigate different perspectives and senior stakeholders in an international organization, and you communicate clearly and confidently.

At the same time, you have a strong hands-on mentality. You take ownership, follow through and do not consider operational tasks beneath your level. You thrive in a role where the breadth is significant, priorities can shift quickly, and delivering high-quality support to the business matters.

Xellia is a 120-year-old company with a refreshingly start-up feel inside. We have spent more than a century at the forefront of anti-infective medicine, making a difference to patients all over the world – and we are just as ambitious today as we were a hundred years ago.

We have recently refreshed our brand around a simple, human idea: We’re Your People. It is built on the strong relationships and trusted partnerships that have always defined Xellia, putting the real Xellians – the warm, expert and dedicated people behind the science – front and center.

Why Xellia?

Because you will be joining at a genuinely exciting moment – with a refreshed brand, real momentum and the rare combination of a 120-year heritage with start-up energy inside. The work matters. The medicines we make help patients in some of the most critical moments of their lives.

For the right person, this role offers a compelling combination of seniority, breadth, international exposure and hands-on responsibility. You will have the opportunity to influence important global P&O processes, work closely with senior stakeholders and help develop how Xellia approaches talent, performance, organizational capability and the use of new technology within P&O.

And because here, you are not just a hire – you are one of us.

We’re Your People. Come and be one of them.

Despite employing only 25, Combilent is the preferred supplier of components for critical communication to all the largest OEMs in US and Europe, providing premium and highly advanced components behind communication equipment to first responders such as police and alarm centrals. Being part of the Indutrade Group, a Swedish investment company with a vast network of technical companies, Combilent also benefit from their solid market presence and long-term approach to business, looking to grow organically, providing strong support to the companies in the group. Sales & Business Development Manager

Business Development – Driving New Business

Combilent has had a solid and profitable business within Land Mobile Radio (LMR) for more than 20 years, and this remains a strong foundation for the company. However, our growth ambitions go beyond LMR. jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Natural Product Chemistry - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial natural product research and working in a team? We have the task of charactering bioactive molecules and understanding their biosynthetic pathways. Those molecules can be further developed to help sustainable agriculture.

Responsibilities and qualifications
We are looking for an ambitious chemist with broad experience in microbial natural product chemistry and omics technologies. In this position you will have the unique opportunity to apply modern omics technologies in the investigation into bioactive natural products. The project will focus on the characterization of microbial secondary metabolites from different microbes, with the ambition to develop biofungicides. Your main analytical approach will be based on metabolomics using state-of-the-art high-resolution mass spectrometry techniques including LC/MS, MALDI imaging, NMR spectroscopy, different types of chromatography, genome-mining and microbial engineering.

This position is financed by SDC (https://sdc.university/) and you are going to carry out research collaboration with Prof. Xiujie Wang, UCAS, Beijing. In this position, you will have the unique opportunity to apply different omics technologies in natural product research.

We wish for knowledge and qualifications within

• Genome-mining and metabolomics analysis of bioactive microorganisms
• Isolation and structural elucidation of unknown and/or bioactive secondary metabolites, e.g. antifungals from microbes, using NMR and MS spectroscopy
• Biosynthesis of novel secondary metabolites using bioinformatics and genetics
• Knowledge of biofungicide
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment

• A strong background in natural product chemistry and biosynthesis
• Highly motivated by the structural complexity of microbial natural products and their applications
• Previous hands-on experience with LC-MS, MALDI-imaging and NMR is advantageous 
• Previous hands-on experience in genome-mining, biosynthesis and strain engineering is advantageous
• Previous knowledge in plant-microbe interactions is advantageous
• Strong writing and communication skills
• You are hard-working and dedicated to your work
• Interested in international collaborations
• You are a team player with a desire to work closely and help your colleagues to succeed
• Fluent in English
We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is full time for 3 years. The position starts in early 2027 and no later than 01.April 2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Ling Ding, lidi@dtu.dk 

You can read more about at https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/ 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• Contacts for two references
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC)
Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC) is a partnership between all eight Danish universities, the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Higher Education, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS), and the Chinese research institute Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). The overall aim of SDC is to promote and strengthen collaboration between Danish and Chinese research and education environments for the benefit of both countries. The PhD candidate is expected to spend his/her PhD external stay in Beijing Institute of Genomics, Beijing to carry out collaborations. A double degree from both DTU and UCAS will be awarded.

The Department of Biotechnology and Biomedicine (DTU Bioengineering) is an international leader in the fields of biotechnology and biomedicine. Our engineering approach to all aspects of biotechnology and biomedicine positions us as a valuable player with unique competences in a growing bio-based economy and in healthcare systems that are transforming towards personalized medicine.

We have a clear focus on the needs of the life sciences and biotech industries and contribute to innovation, new businesses, and scientific services for the benefit of society. The department has extensive collaborations with national and international research institutions and industry partners.

DTU Bioengineering has approximately 400 employees, of whom two-thirds are scientific staff. The department is located at DTU's Lyngby Campus.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position in Materials Chemistry at the Mads Clausen Institute, The University of Southern Denmark in Sønderborg, Denmark
jobs.description:
We are seeking an enthusiastic new colleague as a postdoctoral research associate in the field of Materials Chemistry with a strong background, particularly in Solid State Chemistry and (Photo)electrochemistry, and interest in industrial applications and cooperation to join the Mads Clausen Institute (MCI) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) in Sønderborg, Denmark. The position is for two years with an expected starting date of 01.03.2027. 

MCI is a part of the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and covers research and education, including applications of engineering sciences. Our working language is English, reflecting the fact that far more than half of our students and staff have international roots. We are located at SDU’s beautiful campus in Sønderborg, in the inspiring building of Alsion, which is a centre for science, culture and learning in the heart of Sønderborg and perched on the strait of water separating the island of Als from the mainland. The university has very close relations with industries in Sønderborg, Southern Denmark, and Northern Germany.

The successful candidate is expected to carry out research mainly within a project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The project is hosted by the nanotechnology centre NanoSYD, a part of MCI, and it is integrated into the novel, active working group CatMatX, a research laboratory focused on developing next-generation catalytic materials for sustainable energy and environmental applications,  by Professor Mirabbos Hojamberdiev. The research work involves the synthesis and characterization of novel compounds based on mixed-anion compounds (e.g., transition metal (oxy)nitrides) and the evaluation of their performance in solar water splitting. Also, the successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in the supervision of MSc and PhD students affiliated with SDU NanoSYD, preparing project reports, presentations, and publications, as well as writing project proposals to support research at SDU NanoSYD. 

Job Description and Responsibilities

• 
Implementation of research tasks related to the project;

• 
Collaborative and independent research planning, materials synthesis and characterization, and evaluation of materials performance in solar water splitting;

• 
Independent characterization, data analysis, and interpretation of research results;

• 
Scientific communication and presentation of research results at group seminars, scientific conferences, project meetings, etc.;

• 
Publishing of project results in international peer-reviewed scientific journals with high impact factors.

Potential Responsibilities 

• 
Supervision of BSc, MSc, and exchange/visiting students who perform research work on similar research topics; 

• 
Assistance in teaching activities; 

• 
Assistance in setting up the research infrastructure;

• 
Assistance in the preparation of grant proposals for external funding. 

Mandatory qualifications 

• 
PhD degree in Materials Science, Materials Chemistry, Solid State Chemistry, Solid State Physics, Electrochemistry, or related fields; 

• 
Proven hands-on experience and knowledge of various synthesis methods in solid-state chemistry, preferably the methods used for the synthesis of mixed-anion compounds;

• 
Technical skills in materials characterization techniques (e.g., XRD, XPS, SEM);   

• 
Proven track record of publishing in international peer-reviewed scientific journals as leading author;

• 
Fluency in English (both spoken and written);

• 
Ability to work in teams and also independently; 

• 
Strong communication skills; 

• 
Willingness to collaborate with other scientists and industry. 

The following qualifications are advantageous

• 
Research experience in X-ray, synchrotron, and neutron radiation facilities, DFT calculations and MD simulations;

• 
Research experience in electrochemistry and solar water splitting; 

• 
Technical skills in scientific illustration and animation to deliver visual knowledge of the project; 

• 
Proven record in participating in national and international research projects;

• 
Strong interest in a long-term commitment to a growing research group.

Contact information

For more information about the department and the position, please contact Mirabbos Hojamberdiev (mirabbos@mci.sdu.dk) and Horst-Günter Rubahn (rubahn@mci.sdu.dk)

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

Conditions of employment

Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and it starts on 01.03.2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding. (no more than 4 years at the same university)

Appointment to the position will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described herein. Please check links for more information on salary (only available in Danish) and taxation.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

The assessment and evaluation process

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. 

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

The application

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. 

To qualify for the position as postdoc you must have obtained a PhD degree by the employment date. 

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
One-page motivation letter that describes the applicant’s previous research work and experience most relevant to the offered position.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Certificates/Diplomas (Bachelor, Master, and PhD degrees) – Danish and/or English transcripts. 

• 
Complete list of publications (please highlight publications most relevant to the offered position).

• 
Research statement on developing novel transition metal-based mixed anion compounds, particularly (oxy)nitrides, for solar water splitting.

• 
A reference letter may be submitted, but is not required. 

The application and all appendices must be in English. We request files in pdf-format no more than 5 MB per file. All pdf-files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected. Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application shall be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae shall be uploaded as ‘Resume’. All other documents shall be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’.

If the application does not meet the requirements mentioned above, the faculty may reject your application without further notice. Applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated.

The application deadline is October 31, 2026 at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST).

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Apply at https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu

Most importantly, you are proactive, commercially curious and comfortable taking ownership. You enjoy an entrepreneurial environment where decisions can be made quickly and where you have the opportunity to make a visible difference.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher Position in Labour Immigration and Institutional Change
jobs.description:
Department of Sociology, University of Copenhagen

  The Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS) at the Department of Sociology, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two fixed-term postdoctoral researcher positions (2½ years) starting 1 March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  These positions are part of the project ‘Labour Migration as a Source of Institutional Change’, which investigates how companies’ use of migrant labour can cause changes in receiving countries labour market institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will undertake comparative case studies of companies’ use of migrant labour across three sectors (manufacturing, construction and hospitality) in two countries (either Austria and Netherlands or Ireland and Sweden). The case studies will contribute to all aspects of the project, including a five-country comparison.   

  The project is led by Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz (PI) and is funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The research team will consist of the two postdoctoral researchers and the PI.

  Job Description
 In many Western European countries, labour migrants’ share of employment has expanded substantially the last decades reaching beyond 25 percent in some countries. However, our current understanding of how labour market institutions change ignores labour migration. Therefore, we know little about the long-term impact of labour migration on receiving countries’ labour market institutions.

  To address this issue, this project proposes and tests a new theory of how labour migration causes institutional change: Companies pursuing deviant business strategies can use labour migrants to overcome institutional obstacles and the proliferation of such deviant business strategies can cause incremental institutional change. The cumulative effects of those changes have transformative potential for how labour markets are governed.

  To test and develop this theory, the postdoctoral researcher will conduct sector case studies in different countries focusing both on the link between deviant business strategies and the use of migrant labour, and on the cumulative effects of labour migration over time in different sectors and countries.

  Key Tasks:

   	
• Conduct comparative case studies of the use of migrant labor in three sectors across two countries. 	
• Utilize process-tracing methodologies to analyze to what extent inflow of migrant labour and proliferation of deviant business practices are related. 	
• Conduct and analyze interviews with company representatives, trade unions, labour inspectors and other authorities, and experts. 	
• Gather and analyze supplementary data such as statistics, archival data, media sources, policy documents, and studies to reconstruct historical development. 	
• Compare cross-national and cross-sectorial variations in how divergent business strategies and labour migration co-develop. 	
• Write academic articles based on findings for submission to top sociology and political science journals. 	
• Present findings at international conferences (e.g., SASE, CES, EPSA, ESA).   The project includes 1½ month research stay in each case country, hosted by members of the project’s advisory board.

  The postdoctoral researcher position is mainly a research position, but there is a 10 % teaching obligation.

  For further information, including more details on project, please contact Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz (jh@faos.dk).

  Qualifications
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  We seek candidates with the following qualifications:

   	
• A PhD in Sociology, Political Science, Comparative Political Economy, Industrial Relations or a related field (completed or near completion). 	
• Expertise in qualitative research methods, particularly comparative case study analysis, qualitative interviews and process-tracing. 	
• Knowledge of political economy, labour market institutions or labour migration. 	
• Fluency in English and either German and Dutch or Swedish is required; proficiency in Danish is desirable but not a requirement. 	
• Experience with or willingness to engage in academic collaboration.   You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS) is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better. 	
• Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.   For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.

  Work Environment & Research Team
 The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz, another postdoc and an international advisory board. The postdoctoral researcher will become a part of the Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS), which has a strong focus on labour market institutions, and the Department of Sociology, which provides a dynamic research environment, offering access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure.

  The project will provide opportunities for collaboration on high-impact publications, networking with experts in labour migration and labour markets, and participation in international research events.

  Application Process
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• Cover Letter detailing research interests and fit for the project (max. 1 page) 	
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) (max. 3 pages) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		 			
• Monographs and anthologies 			
• Articles in journals 			
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		 		 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		 			
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 		 		 	 	 	
• Research Statement (max. 2 pages) outlining past experience and future research agenda. 	
• Two Writing Samples (published papers or dissertation chapters).   Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,900/approximately EUR 5,300 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select the applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee's assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardsless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.

  Contact Information
 For further information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz at jh@faos.dk.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2642/26-2I #2.

  The application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 23:59 [CEST].

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

  We look forward to receiving your application!

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 01 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD Position in Environmental Genomics and Pollinator Ecology

Research area and project description
Pollinating insects are declining globally due to habitat loss, climate change, pesticides and emerging diseases. While conservation efforts typically focus on terrestrial habitats and floral resources, the role of freshwater ecosystems in supporting pollinator populations remains poorly understood.
Recent evidence suggests that ponds, streams and wetlands can act as important biodiversity hotspots for insect pollinators, providing hydration, microclimatic refugia, microbial resources and potentially novel nutritional supplements. However, the mechanisms linking freshwater habitats and pollinator health remain largely unexplored.

This PhD project will investigate how freshwater ecosystems influence pollinator diversity, diet, microbiomes and health. The work will combine field ecology, environmental DNA (eDNA), DNA metabarcoding, high-throughput sequencing, bioinformatics and AI-assisted monitoring technologies to uncover how aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems interact to support biodiversity.

The candidate will become part of a growing and highly interdisciplinary team working at the interface of molecular ecology, pollinator ecology and freshwater science.

Research activities:
The PhD candidate will primarily contribute to:
 
• Large-scale field surveys in Danish gardens, parks and freshwater habitats.
• Environmental DNA sampling from freshwater habitats and flowers.
• DNA metabarcoding of pollinator, plant and aquatic communities.
• Analysis of pollinator foraging networks.
• Experimental studies examining insect visitation to freshwater resources.
• Development and application of AI-assisted image-based insect monitoring approaches.
• Bioinformatic analysis of sequencing data.
• Publication of research findings in international peer-reviewed journals.
The project includes opportunities for international collaboration, and a research stay with project partners at the National Botanic Garden of Wales (UK).
Project description. For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position should have a master’s degree in ecology, biology, environmental science, bioinformatics, genomics, conservation biology or a related discipline.
 
• Demonstrated interest in biodiversity, pollinator ecology, freshwater ecology, or molecular ecology.
• Experience with molecular methods such as DNA extraction, PCR, metabarcoding or sequencing.
• Experience with bioinformatics, R programming, or ecological statistics.
• Interest in both field research and laboratory-based research.
• Effective communication skills in English.No candidate is expected to meet all criteria. We encourage applications from individuals with complementary skills and a strong interest in developing expertise across ecology, environmental genomics, and biodiversity monitoring.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, DK-4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Georgina Brennan, g.brennan@ecos.au.dk (supervisor and primary contact for project-related enquiries)
• Nikolai Friberg, niko@ecos.au.dk (supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 February 2027.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants. All interested candidates are encouraged to apply, regardless of their personal background. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with applicable collective agreement.

jobs.occupation: PhD in gas photonics - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
We are seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD candidate for a 3 year position, in the fields of gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers, ultrafast lasers, and nonlinear optics.

In this role, you will conduct cutting-edge research in ultrafast nonlinear optics using gas-filled hollow-core fiber platforms. You will develop advanced high-power near-infrared ultrafast laser sources and gas-filled fiber systems for fundamental studies and emerging photonic applications. The research will primarily be carried out in the GasLab at DTU Electro, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for exploratory gas-laser experiments and a collaborative environment for training and mentoring project personnel.

Our expectations of you
We expect the successful candidate to have:

• A MSc degree in optics/photonics, optical engineering.
• Interest and background with exploring unknown physics in the field of nonlinear photonics and ultrafast lasers. 
• Experimental experience with developing fiber lasers, with preference on gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers.
• The ability to work independently, and contribute creatively to research projects, and the ability to maintain an organized and safe work environment.
• The candidate should be fluent in English, both written and spoken.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. 

Salary and terms of employment
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years.

The position is a full-time position. The starting date will be January 01, 2027 or according to mutual agreement

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Dr. Yazhou Wang (yazwang@dtu.dk) and Assoc. Prof. Christos Markos (chmar@dtu.dk). 

You can read more about DTU Electro at https://electro.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with the industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Are you looking for an internship that combines personal development and the opportunity to support the green transition through data-based insights? Are you passionate about working hands-on with data? Are you eager to turn your theoretical knowledge into practical and customer-centred solutions?
