Turn your scientific expertise into commercial impact

Are you a scientist with a couple of years of experience in the lab, and a growing pull toward the commercial side of science? Do you want to use your analytical background as a springboard - building relationships, driving customer outcomes, and eventually growing into a broader commercial career - rather than staying in the lab? If you're energized by science but you can already picture yourself on the customer-facing side of it, this role is built for that transition.

What we do

Evosep aims to improve quality of life and patient care by radically innovating protein based clinical diagnostics. Making sample preparation and separation before MS analysis 10 times faster and 100 times more robust will enable truly large cohort studies for biomarker validation and provide the foundation for precision medicine.

Why this role is a great place to start your commercial career

Most people don't start their career knowing they want to end up in commercial roles - they discover it. If you've enjoyed the moments in your scientific work where you got to explain your results, train a colleague, or convince a skeptical reviewer, there's a good chance you'd enjoy this even more.

As a Customer Success Manager, your science degree isn't something you leave behind - it's your credibility with every customer you work with. You'll use it every day to understand their workflows, speak their language, and be trusted as someone who genuinely gets the science. On top of that, you'll build a second skillset most scientists never get the chance to develop: reading account health, spotting growth opportunities, structuring commercial conversations, and working hand-in-hand with Sales, Marketing, and Application Specialists.

It's a role at the intersection of two worlds - and a natural stepping stone if you're aiming toward Account Management, Sales, Marketing, or broader commercial leadership down the line. You won't be doing this alone: you'll be mentored by experienced colleagues in Sales and Applications, and supported by a team that wants to see you grow into the commercial side of the business.

Key tasks and responsibilities

Build and grow customer relationships

• Own the day-to-day relationship with a portfolio of accounts across Academia, Pharma, Biotech, and Clinical

• Learn to run structured account check-ins - understanding how customers are using their instruments, what's going well, and where they need more support

• Start spotting expansion opportunities (new applications, additional capacity) and hand them off to Sales - with mentoring, you'll grow into owning more of that commercial read yourself

• Track adoption and usage trends, and translate what you see into a clear read on account health

Keep customers running smoothly

• Be the customer's go-to contact for contract renewals, service timing, and logistics questions

• Coordinate with our Service and Application teams to keep installs, maintenance, and calibrations on track

• Help new customers get set up for success from day one

Represent Evosep and capture customer feedback

• Attend conferences, user meetings, and customer workshops - representing Evosep and building your own network in the field

• Capture customer feedback and feed it back to Product and Marketing - your scientific background will help you translate what customers really mean

• Help build a pipeline of reference customers and advocates within your accounts

Qualifications

• A degree in Analytical Science, Chemistry, Biotechnology, or a related field

• Around 2–3 years of experience, e.g. from a lab, research, or an early technical/commercial role - hands-on proteomics and LC-MS experience is a big plus, but not a hard requirement

• A genuine curiosity about the commercial side of science, and the drive to build a career there - not just to support it

• Strong communication skills - comfortable explaining technical topics clearly to different audiences

• A proactive, relationship-driven mindset; you follow through and you don't wait to be asked twice

• Fluent in English; additional languages are a plus

• Based in Denmark, with willingness to travel across Europe and occasionally further; happy working from home and from our HQ in Odense

• Valid Class B driver's license

What We Offer

• A genuine path from scientific expertise into a commercial career, with mentoring from experienced Sales and Applications colleagues

• A competitive compensation and benefits package — details shared during the application process

• A team of passionate, ambitious, and supportive colleagues who are genuinely driven by purpose

• A dynamic, open culture where challenging the status quo is a team sport

• The opportunity to grow with a fast-expanding company at the center of proteomics innovation

• A healthy work-life balance — we know you have a life outside the office, and we want you to enjoy it

• Modern office facilities in Odense, including a cozy atrium courtyard — perfect for sunny lunch breaks and Friday bars

• Experience working within endocrinology, rare diseases, or other specialized therapeutic areas.

• Proven ability to build trusted partnerships and work effectively in a complex global matrix organization.

You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

Job Description

Do you want to take senior hands-on technical ownership of how mission-critical data centers are designed, expanded, and handed over for operation?

GlobalConnect is expanding data center capacity across the Nordics and Northern Europe. To support this growth, we are strengthening our Large Projects organization with a Data Center Designer based in Taastrup.

This is a senior specialist role at our highest specialist level. You will act as a technical authority across large data center projects, influence design direction, challenge key technical decisions, and help shape more consistent ways of working across countries.

The role is a hands-on role. You will work directly with layouts, power and cooling concepts, system architecture, technical documentation, supplier designs, commissioning readiness, and operational handover. This is not a technician or installation role, but you should enjoy getting close to the technical solution and being present in the data center environment.

What you need to succeed

• Hands on experience with data center infrastructure or other mission-critical environments, such as energy, pharma, industrial facilities, or similar

• Strong understanding of cooling systems and power infrastructure in mission-critical environments

• Proven hands-on experience with alarm and monitoring systems, including system architecture and integration with critical infrastructure such as power, cooling, and security

• Ability to interpret, review, and challenge engineering drawings, technical documentation, specifications, supplier designs, and system architecture choices

• Fluent English. Danish or another Nordic language is an advantage

About the role and the team

You will join a small, senior, and specialized team working across Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Germany. The team works closely across borders and is building a more consistent pan-Nordic approach to data center design, expansion, and operational readiness.

In Denmark, this role closes an important capability gap. You will bring deep technical design expertise into a setup that already has strong project management capability. You will work closely with Project Managers, Sales, Procurement, external consultants, vendors, customers, and Operations.

A key part of the role is to act as a trusted technical advisor. You will help translate customer needs into technically sound solutions, challenge assumptions when needed, and ensure that design choices support long-term reliability, scalability, security, and maintainability.

What you’ll be working on

• Act as technical authority within large data center projects, from early concept through commissioning, acceptance, and handover

• Own and challenge system-level design decisions across power, cooling, controls, alarm and monitoring systems, security, and building interfaces

• Review layouts, airflow concepts, cooling capacity assumptions, power distribution principles, single-line diagrams, and supplier designs

• Develop and review technical requirements, specifications, scopes of supply, risk assessments, and design documentation

• Support FATs, site inspections, commissioning activities, acceptance testing, and operational handover

• Strengthen standardisation, repeatable technical solutions, and design quality across projects and countries

Who we are looking for

You are a senior mechanical technical specialist who enjoys working with complex systems, high expectations, and decisions that have long-term operational impact.

You are confident in your technical judgement and comfortable challenging designs, suppliers, consultants, customers, and internal stakeholders when the solution needs to be improved. You can explain complex technical choices clearly and help others understand the trade-offs between reliability, cost, schedule, scalability, and operational readiness.

You enjoy working close to the physical technical solution. You are comfortable reviewing drawings, questioning assumptions, calculating capacity, discussing design alternatives, and explaining why a solution will work in practice.

To succeed in this role, you should also be motivated by building trust across teams. The role requires close collaboration with Sales, Projects, Operations, vendors, and customers, especially where expectations, technical reality, and operational needs must be aligned.

Does this sound like you? If so, we would love to hear from you.

Our recruitment process

• Hiring Manager interview

• Personality and ability tests feedback and discussion with Talent Acquisition

• Case interview with Hiring Manager and peer/stakeholder

• Final alignment meeting

• References

Practical information

This role is based in Taastrup, Denmark, and requires strong on-site presence in the data center environment. We are only open to applicants already based in Denmark

Due to security clearance requirements, you must be able to document that you have lived and worked in an EU or NATO country for the past 7 years and we are not able to offer work visa support or sponsorship for this role

At GlobalConnect, you will play a key role in building and safeguarding critical digital infrastructure that society depends on every day. You will have real technical influence, work on complex data center projects, and help shape how we design and deliver reliable infrastructure across multiple countries.

No need for a personal letter – just send us your CV or LinkedIn profile.

Design the systems that guide satellites in orbit for new ambitious missions

We are seeking an experienced AOCS/GNC Engineer to design, develop, and validate attitude determination, orbit control, and autonomous navigation solutions for small satellite missions. In this role, you will develop guidance and control strategies across diverse and demanding mission profiles — from VLEO drag-dominated regimes to deep-space trajectories and asteroid proximity operations.

You will join our Advanced Missions global team, developing next-generation AOCS/GNC concepts while collaborating closely with GomSpace's established AOCS team in Aalborg — who built and flew the AOCS for the Juventas CubeSat on ESA's Hera mission and are currently developing full 6-DoF GNC for the Llevant (RAMSES) asteroid rendezvous mission.

**

Your Role**

As AOCS/GNC Engineer, you will own the attitude and orbit control design for advanced mission proposals — from requirements definition and algorithm design through high-fidelity simulation and hardware-in-the-loop validation.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Design and implement AOCS/GNC algorithms for attitude determination, control, and autonomous navigation across diverse mission profiles.

• Develop guidance and orbit-control strategies tailored to SSA, VLEO drag-dominated regimes, and deep-space trajectories.

• Model and simulate spacecraft dynamics, environmental disturbances, and sensor/actuator performance for mission-specific scenarios.

• Validate algorithms through high-fidelity simulations, Monte-Carlo analyses, and hardware-in-the-loop setups.

• Collaborate with systems, propulsion, and mission design teams to define control requirements and ensure end-to-end stability and performance.

**

What Success Looks Like**

In the initial phase, success means:

• Understanding GomSpace's AOCS product portfolio (GSW-600 reaction wheels, Auriga/Twinkle star trackers, STIM300 IMU, AOCS Flightcore software).

• Delivering your first AOCS sizing and mode analysis for a mission proposal and setting up a reusable MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment.

• Establishing working relationships with the Aalborg AOCS team and communicating AOCS trade-offs clearly to non-AOCS stakeholders.

Over time, you will be recognised for owning end-to-end AOCS/GNC design for advanced mission proposals, developing and maintaining GNC strategies across multiple mission regimes, and achieving successful Monte-Carlo validation campaigns that demonstrate algorithm robustness.

**

What You Bring**

You are an AOCS/GNC specialist with deep analytical rigour and a passion for solving complex spacecraft dynamics and control challenges across unconventional mission profiles.

You likely bring:

• An MSc or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Astrodynamics, Control Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. A PhD focused on GNC, spacecraft dynamics, or autonomous navigation is a strong plus.

• 3–5+ years of experience in AOCS/GNC algorithm design, simulation, and validation for spacecraft missions.

• Experience with attitude determination (gyro-stellar estimators, EKF/UKF), 3-axis control (sliding mode, PD/PID, LQR), and momentum management.

• Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink for spacecraft dynamics modelling and Monte-Carlo analysis.

• Experience with C/C++ implementation of flight algorithms and familiarity with AOCS sensors and actuators (star trackers, IMUs, reaction wheels, magnetorquers, RCS thrusters).

• Exposure to ESA/ECSS project lifecycle and AOCS design reviews (PDR, CDR) is highly valued.

**

An inclusive team

Do you want your engineering skills to directly shape how athletes understand and improve their movement? Are you excited by the opportunity of turning noisy, high-dimensional data into clean, actionable biomechanical metrics used by professionals and ambitious amateurs alike?

We are looking for an Algorithm Developer in Mathematical modelling to join our Motion Analysis team. You’ll work at the intersection of deep learning and real-world sports science, taking the raw output of our AI models and building the modelling and post-processing pipelines that make the data real. This is where the engineering meets the athlete.

As a member of our team, you will be responsible for the key step between AI prediction and product output. Our deep learning models produce body key points from video. Your job is to turn those noisy, uncertain estimates into robust skeletal fits and reliable biomechanical metrics that our users can trust and act on.

We believe it takes careful post-processing and modelling to turn raw deep learning predictions into data that is real, reliable, and actionable. You will design and develop custom algorithms that handle outlier detection, optimization, and human body model fitting, often as one integrated modelling approach rather than separate steps. You will be part of an agile, collaborative team, contributing to solutions from prototype to production and helping shape our products. You will join a team of six, with diverse backgrounds spanning deep learning, computer vision, software engineering, and mathematical modelling.

We work in a collaborative environment where team members support each other and share responsibility for moving projects forward. We believe that strong solutions emerge through open dialogue across disciplines. We also value a positive and engaging work environment, where curiosity is encouraged and people can explore problems that interest them alongside supportive colleagues.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• 
Designing and implementing mathematical models that fit skeletal structures to noisy key point data, balancing input uncertainty with anatomical constraints.

• 
Developing robust outlier detection and rejection methods that work within the modelling framework, not just as a pre-processing step.

• 
Building and refining optimization pipelines for post-processing deep learning outputs into accurate biomechanical metrics.

• 
Conducting data analysis and statistical validation to understand model performance and propose improvements.

• 
Collaborating closely with our deep learning engineers and software engineers to ensure your models integrate cleanly into the broader product pipeline.

• 
Exploring and evaluating new approaches from research literature, adapting them to our specific problem domain and data characteristics.

Job requirements

• 
A master's degree or PhD in Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Signal Processing, or a related technical field with strong mathematical foundations.

• 
Solid skills in mathematical modelling, you are comfortable formulating real-world problems as optimization, estimation, or fitting problems.

• 
Strong foundations in linear algebra, statistics, and numerical methods.

• 
Experience working with noisy, real-world data,you understand uncertainty and know how to handle it.

• 
Programming skills in Python - Familiarity with C++ is a plus.

• 
You have an entrepreneurial mindset and are driven by making your work matter in a real product, not just in a report.

• 
Communication skills, with the ability to explain mathematical choices to colleagues from different technical backgrounds.

Preferably:

• 
Experience with signal processing methods such as filtering, smoothing, or time-series analysis.

• 
Familiarity with constrained optimization techniques and solvers.

• 
Experience with human body modelling, biomechanics, or motion capture data.

• 
Exposure to deep learning, not necessarily training models, but understanding what they output and why they fail.

• 
A genuine passion for applying mathematical thinking to solve real-world challenges.

• 
An interest in sports like golf, baseball, or others is a bonus!

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo processes thousands of hours of sports video daily, powering AI analysis for teams from grassroots to professional levels. The infrastructure you build will directly enable coaches and athletes worldwide to analyze, train, and compete better.

We're building KickOff, our next-generation GitOps platform. You'll join during a pivotal moment: we're actively migrating services to KickOff, establishing new platform patterns and enabling 100+ engineers to ship faster and more reliably. We also maintain separate on-premises Kubernetes clusters running model training and video processing workloads.

This isn't a "keep the lights on" role. You'll shape platform architecture, drive technical decisions, and directly impact engineering velocity across both cloud and on-prem environments.

What You Will Do

You'll join the platform engineering team that owns these areas together. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities.

• Evolve KickOff (our GitOps platform) to improve developer experience.

• Support service migrations to KickOff, partnering with product teams.

• Maintain and optimize KickOff on AWS EKS.

• Manage our on-premises Kubernetes clusters running ML training workloads.

• Establish monitoring, alerting, and observability using LGTM.

• Debug distributed systems spanning multiple environments.

• Create documentation and tooling that makes infrastructure approachable

As the platform matures, you'll have opportunities to shape multi-cluster architecture, GPU workload scheduling, disaster recovery strategy, and cloud provider independence.

What You Could Bring

We're looking for someone with 3-5 years running production infrastructure, including:

• Production Kubernetes: You've operated K8s in production and understand the operational reality, not just tutorials.

• Platform-as-product mindset: You've built internal tooling that real teams use, gathered feedback, and measured impact on productivity.

• Infrastructure as Code: Strong Terraform, Crossplane, or similar experience.

• Observability: You've implemented monitoring and alerting that helps teams operate confidently.

• Security awareness: You know how to embed security into platform design without slowing teams down.

• Problem-solving: You debug complex distributed systems and design practical solutions.

• Collaboration: You work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively.

Nice to have: GitOps tools (Flux, ArgoCD), Cilium, multi-cloud architecture, on-prem K8s experience.

How We Work

You’ll join a Copenhagen-based platform team of 5 engineers with shared ownership of KickOff and our on-prem Kubernetes clusters. We work closely together day to day through pairing, code reviews, and a rotating ownership model for operational responsibilities and platform improvements.

You’ll collaborate regularly with the Processing Platform team on workload needs, reliability, and developer experience, and you’ll use feedback from product and engineering teams to shape platform priorities and improve how teams build and ship on KickOff.

We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

jobs.description:
Does the idea of being part of the largest pharmaceutical projects in Denmark and managing complex Process Automation projects excite you? And do you thrive on defining and executing project strategies in close corporation with highly skilled colleagues? Then you’ll fit right in!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

As a Senior Project Manager within Process Automation, you will be part of our large project portfolio in Kalundborg. You will play an important role in ensuring the successful execution of our deliveries and will be in close contact with both internal and external stakeholders.

As part of your role, you will maintain close dialogue with your team on-site and participate in regular meetings across disciplines, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and execution according to our plans.

The technical focus of this position is Process Automation, working with DCS 800xA and ECS solutions interfacing with new technologies within the Industry 4.0 domain and Manufacturing IT solutions. Our projects cover the entire project lifecycle, from conceptual and basic design phases to on-site testing activities, including FAT, Interface Testing, Wet Testing, SAT, and UAT, culminating in handover to our customers.

Based on your skills and experience, several opportunities are available within our portfolio.

How you might spend your days

As a Project Manager, you will be responsible for:

• 
Executing projects within your area in close collaboration with your team, identifying risks and implementing mitigation measures.

• 
Focusing on overall project planning, ensuring delivery quality, and planning the necessary resources to maintain schedule and cost targets.

• 
Estimating costs and planning budgets in collaboration with our engineers and specialists.

• 
Managing project scope and ensuring that changes are analysed and agreed upon with stakeholders.

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• 
Work across the boundaries and you like to work in a diverse and international environment

• 
Create results through efficient project management and communication, leveraging from your relations to your team and stakeholder

• 
Have a personal commitment, known for your effectiveness and an open management style and know the impotency to win as a team

• 
Are fluent in English both written and spoken

What you bring to the role

To be successful in this role, we expect you to have the following experience and educational background:

• 
An educational background at bachelor's level or a similar relevant technical background.

• 
6–10 years of experience with a proven track record in DCS and ECS/PLC Process Automation projects, preferably within the pharmaceutical industry.

• 
Experience with GMP project execution and preferable knowledge with S88 and S95

• 
Experience in executing Process Automation projects in collaboration with other disciplines, such as mechanical and process design, as well as end users.

• 
Experience with on-site commissioning activities, including FAT, SAT, and UAT.

• 
Project Management certification, e.g. PMP or PRINCE2, is preferred.

If you do not meet all the requirements, you are still welcome to apply and provide alternative experience that you believe would be valuable in this role.

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, it means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Experienced ServiceNow Advisor and Solution Architect
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 3,000 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About the team

Deloitte’s ServiceNow department is looking for an experienced Enterprise Service Management Advisor and Solution Architect to join our A-team of ServiceNow advisors. As a Manager in our ServiceNow department, you will serve as a trusted advisor for our clients, guiding them on their digitalization journey. In this role, you will work with industry leading professionals, guiding clients through end-to-end digital transformation initiatives and driving complex enterprise-wide service modernization.

As a trusted advisor, you will play a key role in identifying and pursuing strategic business opportunities while leading the design and implementation of innovative ServiceNow solutions. You will collaborate with clients to transform IT, HR, Finance, Risk, and core business functions into streamlined, service-based organizations. This involves assessing the client’s needs, translating business requirements into tailored technology solutions, and providing strategic and best practice advisory. You will oversee the full project lifecycle, ensuring seamless execution from strategy to deployment, while providing thought leadership and industry insights that shape best practices.

Success in this role requires a deep understanding of enterprise service management, strong leadership in project execution, and the ability to build long-term client relationships based on trust and value creation. By delivering impactful solutions and driving meaningful business outcomes, you will help position Deloitte as the premier partner for digital transformation.

Job Description

ServiceNow is its own department, and you will join a team of incredibly dedicated, ambitious and great colleagues. Our team works closely together on projects across the Nordics, combining the right expertise and competencies to deliver the best solutions for our clients. While we thrive on cross-border collaboration, you will also have a strong local presence in our Copenhagen office, where we emphasize teamwork, community, and a shared commitment to excellence.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Providing strategic advisory for some of the largest ServiceNow clients in Denmark and the Nordics.

• Engaging proactively with clients, advising on solution and problem scoping across the organization to ensure alignment with business objectives.

• Designing comprehensive solutions, including technical design using design thinking methodologies to ensure alignment with ServiceNow’s Enterprise Service Management capabilities and best practices.

• Helping our clients in defining and optimizing Service Management processes to drive efficiency.

• Offering insights and guidance on application development, agile development, software development lifecycle and cloud applications.

• Leading the delivery of solutions and support teams in corrective measures.

• Work closely with Program Leadership to oversee and lead multiple workstreams of technical design- and delivery activities, create and maintain a network of potential clients, and be known as a trusted advisor and participate in consulting sales activities, including writing service proposals.

Qualifications

By joining our team as a Manager, you will become part of and contribute to our shared success. You will build and nurture positive working relationships with teams and clients to exceed expectations. Key responsibilities and tasks will involve:

You have the following skills and experience:

• A minimum of 5 years of experience working with ServiceNow or other digitalization platforms.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Hands-on experience leading end-to-end transformation projects in areas such as IT, HR, Finance, Risk or core business operations.

• Experience with IT Project Management and have the ability to oversee complex implementations and drive successful outcomes.

• Demonstrated consulting experience or prior experience as a Platform Owner, showcasing your ability to advise and lead clients through transformation initiatives.

• Familiarity with process frameworks such as Lean, TBM, ITIL or other methodologies relevant to your area of expertise.

• A strong technical background with an advanced understanding of key technical principles and best practices.

• Experience or a solid understanding of application development and software lifecycle management.

• Knowledge of technologies using client-server model and understanding of data-modelling, SQL data structures and system integrations.

• You are fluent in written and spoken English, and you should ideally have a high proficiency in Danish or a willingness to learn the language.

• You must have the right to live and work in Denmark.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can contribute to our team’s success**.**

What we offer you:

At Deloitte, we provide an environment where you can grow, innovate, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the ServiceNow field. Joining our team means becoming part of a dynamic and supportive workplace that values both professional and personal development.

• You will work alongside experts in the ServiceNow field, gaining insights and knowledge from top professionals in the field.

• You will experience a culture of continuous growth, where feedback and learning opportunities empower you to advance at your own pace.

• You will enjoy the flexibility of a hybrid work environment, allowing you to balance work and personal commitments in a way that suits you the best.

• You will gain access to ServiceNow certifications in the areas that interest you, enhancing your expertise and career prospects.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV and cover letter. In your cover letter, please describe your motivation and answer these following questions:

• ServiceNow Experience: Can you detail your hands-on experience with ServiceNow, including specific modules and functionalities you have worked with? Please provide examples of complex implementations or customizations you have led.

• Project Management Experience: Describe your project management experience, if possible in the context of ServiceNow projects. How have you managed multiple stakeholders and ensured project success?

We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: As soon as possible.

Please do not hesitate to contact Timothy Edward Intennimeo, Consultant at tintennimeo@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. Are you an experienced project professional who excels at building structure, driving consistency, and elevating project execution?

To support our growth and expanding portfolio of projects, we are strengthening our focus on the Project Management Office (PMO). You’ll get a key role in developing, maintain, train, and educate on the processes, methodology, and tool chain used in project execution.

Your Role

As PMO Lead, you will report to the Head of Projects & Delivery. You will become responsible for all aspects of our best-practice project execution and will be deeply involved in improving and developing our methodologies.

The PMO standardizes project practices, supports project managers and project teams, and represents a highly operational function.

The PMO ensures alignment with business goals by supporting Business Management and provides oversight across the project portfolio. The PMO spans governance, methodology, reporting, process development, and process control. The PMO leads the development of methodologies used during the scale-up of the organization – and may potentially evolve into the competence center for Project Management.

Your tasks include:

• Governance & Standards: Define, maintain, and continuously improve PM methodologies, templates, and best practices, ensuring compliance with processes, quality standards, and stage-gate governance.

• Project Monitoring & Reporting: Monitor project performance across scope, schedule, budget, and risks, and consolidate insights into portfolio dashboards and KPIs for leadership decision-making.

• Resource & Capacity Support: Support resource allocation and forecasting with Team Leads and Project Managers, identify bottlenecks, and help optimize utilization across the project portfolio.

• Support & Enablement: Enable Project Managers through coaching, training, and hands-on support with documentation, planning, tools, and evaluation of new project opportunities.

• Risk, Issue & Change Management: Support structured identification and handling of risks, issues, and changes, including escalation processes and decision forums.

• PMO Development: Drive continuous improvement of PMO methodologies and capabilities to support faster, more scalable, and predictable project delivery aligned with business growth.

The PMO Lead role is highly central to harmonizing and further professionalizing our project execution capability. Running activities according to standards, ensuring quality in execution, and ensuring predictability and repeatability will be key elements of our success. This work will happen in close collaboration with the Engineering Excellence Manager. Furthermore, the PMO Lead will act as the deputy to the Head of Projects & Delivery when required.

Short- and Long-Term Success

In the first 6–12 months, success means:

• Establishing clear structure and ownership of PMO processes and methodologies

• Delivering consistent, high-quality reporting and portfolio visibility

• Building trust and strong collaboration with project managers and key stakeholders

Longer term, you’ll take ownership of maturing the PMO into a scalable capability that supports faster, more predictable project execution, while acting as a competence center for project management across the organization.

What You Bring

You have the ability to design, implement, and continuously improve processes, standards, and tools. You likely:

Who You Are

This is a role where strategic insight, relationship-building, and execution come together to create real impact in complex and dynamic markets.

Your Role and Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead, and coordinate business development activities related to offsets, acting as the go-to expert internally and externally. You will translate national offset policies and political objectives into actionable business strategies and drive collaboration across internal teams to align resources and priorities.

Your tasks will include:

• Leading the development and implementation of offset and industrial cooperation strategies that support long-term growth.

• Building and maintaining strong relationships with defense primes, governments, institutions, and political stakeholders in target markets.

• Translating national policies and political targets into meaningful offset projects that gain governmental traction.

• Developing and executing capture strategies for RFPs and offset financing aligned with GomSpace’s commercial goals.

• Collaborating closely with product, engineering, and business development teams to tailor offerings and create competitive advantage.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a results-oriented, strategic thinker who thrives in complex defense environments and can navigate diverse stakeholder landscapes with diplomacy and influence.

You will bring:

• Proven experience in defense or space business development, especially with offsets and government procurement processes.

• Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with a strong customer and value proposition focus.

• An established network within defense primes and governmental organizations, ideally across multiple regions.

• Sufficient technical understanding to align customer needs with GomSpace’s portfolio of solutions.

• Fluency in English; additional language skills such as Spanish or Arabic are a strong advantage.

Are you ready to leverage your expertise to grow GomSpace’s business and strengthen our position as a partner of choice in the global defense ecosystem? We’d love to hear from you.

Why Join Us?

As Offset Business Development Director, you’ll not only grow our business – you’ll shape the way GomSpace engages with the world’s most strategic players. You’ll operate on a high-impact level, developing offset strategies that fuel technological advancement and build sovereign capabilities across key markets.

We offer an international, mission-driven environment where innovation, purpose, and execution go hand in hand. You’ll collaborate with experts across the company – from BD and engineering to solutions and strategy – to create offset offerings that deliver real, measurable impact.

If you're ready to turn complex regulations into strategic growth and build alliances that stretch across sectors and borders, we’d love to hear from you.

Join Our Mission

We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Genmab is seeking an experienced Senior Clinical Drug Supply Manager to join our Global Clinical Drug Supply in Copenhagen. The role requires candidates to be within commuting distance of our office locations to work according to our hybrid work arrangement. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality clinical trial supplies for both early and late-stage trials.

As a Senior Manager, Global Clinical Drug Supply, you will play a pivot role supporting the development and execution of clinical drug demand forecasts and supply plans to ensure uninterrupted delivery of clinical development products across Genmab’s pipeline. Your responsibilities will include managing the demand planning and supply planning of clinical supplies. This role will partner closely with cross-functional clinical development and CMC teams to maintain accurate forecasts, support supply strategy execution, and contribute to the operational success of clinical programs. The Senior Manager will apply strong analytical, communication, and planning skills to ensure reliable clinical supply while contributing to continuous process improvement across GCDS.

As a Senior Clinical Drug Supply Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring efficient delivery of high-quality clinical trial supplies for both early and late-stage Genmab clinical trials worldwide.

The ideal candidate possesses an understanding of cGMP and a strong commitment to delivering high-quality work, demonstrating a proactive approach and willingness to go the extra mile to ensure the best outcome for patients.

This position is hybrid and requires you to be in the office 60% of the time.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Demand Planning & Forecasting

• Support the development, maintenance, and updates of clinical drug demand forecasts across assigned studies and programs.

• Collaborate with, CTT, and Finance to collect inputs and ensure forecasts reflect current enrollment trends, protocol changes, and assumptions.

• Manage the demand planning discussions as part of the Clinical Project Supply Team (CPST) and support forecasting activities within the CSIOP process.

• Identify potential demand risks and escalate issues in a timely manner, recommending mitigation actions where appropriate.

• Prepare demand plan summaries, enrollment updates, and cost forecasts to support program planning and operational reviews.

Supply Strategy & Execution

• Coordinate clinical supply–related planning activities, ensuring alignment between forecasted needs, study timelines, and supply availability.

• Support the execution of clinical supply chain sourcing strategies using third-party providers, in collaboration with Clinical Operations and Supply Leads.

• Contribute to communication of GCDS Planning Strategy within Global Clinical Teams, ensuring supply planning assumptions are clearly understood.

• Track supply readiness and highlight risks or gaps that could affect clinical trial continuity.

Supplier & Stakeholder Management

• Support Supplier Relationship Management activities by tracking supplier performance metrics and helping identify improvement opportunities.

• Build collaborative working relationships with cross-functional partners (Clinical Operations, CTT, CDM, Regulatory, CMC, QA, and Finance) to enable timely and accurate supply planning.

Budget & Cost Optimization

• Support budget development activities by preparing supply planning inputs and cost forecasts aligned with program needs.

• Monitor budget performance and identify variances, working with senior team members to implement cost-effective solutions.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

• Provide planning updates and forecasting insights to support governance forums (IRC, CTT, Asset Meetings).

• Ensure consistent use of supply chain processes, tools, and systems by adhering to established standards and contributing feedback for enhancements.

• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on advancing forecasting accuracy, operational efficiency, and collaboration across GCDS.

Quality & Regulatory Compliance

• Ensure demand planning and supply–related activities comply with GxP, regulatory standards, and Genmab quality expectations.

• Maintain accurate, audit-ready documentation for demand forecasts, planning assumptions, and supply updates.

• Support identification and resolution of compliance gaps and contribute to corrective and preventive actions as needed

• Adhere to the Genmab Quality Management System

Qualifications

•    Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Pharmaceutical Sciences, Life Sciences, Healthcare, or Supply Chain Management).

•    Minimum 8+ years of experience in clinical drug supply forecasting, supply planning, and demand planning

•    Demonstrated stakeholder management skills, both internally and externally.

•    Experience working with vendors and CMOs for clinical trial supplies will be an advantage.

•    Solid knowledge of GDP and GMP. Knowledge of GCP will be an advantage.

•    Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to excel in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

•    Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

•    Highly organized with a structured, process-oriented mindset that supports continuous improvement.

•    Ability to prioritize effectively while maintaining a high level of quality and compliance.

•    Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work both independently and within global teams.

•    Results-driven and goal-oriented, committed to contributing to Genmab’s success.

The Team

You will join a highly competent team focused on demand planning and supply planning on clinical supplies, collaborating closely with the Global Clinical Drug Supply Execution team. Together with the Global Clinical Drug Supply Systems team and Global Clinical Drug Supply Manufacturing team, these four functions form the Global Clinical Drug Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK687.888,00---1.031.832,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. Knowledge of radar, computer vision, or sensor data systems

A collaborative, cross-functional team with 40+ highly skilled colleagues from more than 35 nationalities

Based on specifications and timelines, projects are led by a Project Manager. This allows you to focus on the technical aspects of the projects as well as managing your own project timeline. Your tasks will include:

• 
Technical adjustments of the core product and components for braking systems

• 
Design and construction of braking systems and components, including hydraulic systems

• 
Leading and ensuring the execution of testing these designs in the test center and production facilities

• 
Preparing technical documentation, including drawings and bills of materials (BOMs)

• 
Participation in development projects, including new material types and customer-specific projects.

Your typical workday will be a mix of independent work and a cross-functional collaboration, as solutions are often found through interdisciplinary collaboration. Among other things, you will work closely with a technical designer who supports you by creating technical documentation.

Svendborg Brakes has its own hydraulic manufacturing and test center, where designs can be tested and where customers visit to follow the project progress. This means you will be able to see your projects through from start to finish.

You are passionate about engineering and intelligent hydraulic systems

We are looking for an engineer with a strong passion for engineering and hydraulics. You have both an interest in and experience with mechanical design, hydraulics, and electrical control systems, and you are motivated by continuously developing your skills. You most likely hold a degree in mechatronics or mechanical engineering and have at least three years of professional experience.

You take a structured approach to your work and maintain a strong overview of tasks and processes. You understand that respecting specifications and timelines leads to the best results and strongest collaboration. You communicate effectively with people from different professional backgrounds and interact effortlessly with both customers and colleagues across departments.

In addition, you are fully comfortable communicating in English, both verbally and in writing.

Do you want to join the team?

At Svendborg Brakes, you will experience a flat organizational structure and an informal culture, where you have the freedom to plan your own workday and the projects you are involved in. You will also be part of a close cross-functional collaboration, where colleagues complement each other across projects with their individual areas of expertise.

Svendborg Brakes’ willingness and motivation to explore new technologies - as one of the world leaders in this field - is evident throughout the company. In other words, you will join a team with high level of expertise and a strong dedication to continuous development. This gives you a unique opportunity to develop your skills based on your interests and motivation.

Our Business Development & Portfolio Management area has an ambitious strategy and we are looking for someone with a generic-pharma mindset or experience to drive the transformation and make sure we execute according to our plans, roadmaps and business goals within the area and along the value chain

About the job

This role is best suited for someone who knows how a generic pharma business operates. Compared with an originator company, we work with a broad portfolio, lean teams and short decision paths, and value comes from pragmatic, commercially minded execution.

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Drive the transformation in the Business Development & Portfolio Management area from process changes to new ways of working

• Identify program impacts and design adoption measures together with functional leads

• Track adoption and take corrective action when change is not landing as planned

• Own the communication plan that keeps the organization informed and engaged

• Own the strategy execution roadmap for the Business Development & Portfolio Management area, ensuring alignment with Orifarm’s overall strategy and business goals

• Translate priorities into concrete program briefs, project charters, milestones and benefit maps

• Follow up on progress against plans and goals – with a single, transparent view of status, risks, dependencies and benefit realization

• Drive cross-functional coordination along the value chain – Portfolio, Regulatory Affairs, Business Development, Commercial and Operations – and ensure timely resolution of blockers

• Run the governance rhythm: program boards, track reviews and reporting to the Executive Management Group

You will report directly to our Chief Business Development & Portfolio Strategy Officer. You will present strategy updates and projects to our Executive Management Group and hold an explicit mandate to drive execution across the organization.

Who are you

We are looking for someone with significant experience driving transformations or programs in complex organizations, and a track record of making sure plans are executed and business goals are delivered.

Additionally, you will need to have experience from a generic or off-patent pharma business – across areas such as portfolio, business development, regulatory or commercial operations and you know how it differs from an originator company: broad portfolios, lean organizations, tight margins and pragmatic decision-making. Experience from a comparable commercial healthcare environment is also relevant.

You communicate clearly with executives, build alignment across functions, markets and cultures, and are comfortable challenging when progress stalls. You also ensure the right level of structure and governance for a regulated environment without building heavier processes than the business needs

Lastly, you have strong analytical skills, hold complexity across several concurrent workstreams and master program management methods and tools. A certification such as PRINCE2, MSP or PMI-PgMP is an advantage.

Who are we?

The Business Development & Portfolio Management area covers Portfolio Strategy, Business Development, Regulatory Affairs and Pharmacovigilance. You will partner closely with Strategy, the Strategy & PPMO Office, People & Culture and other corporate functions.

What we offer

• A role at the center of strategic decision-making, with direct access to the C-level and the Executive Management Group

• A clear mandate to drive execution across the organization

• An entrepreneurial culture that celebrates can-do attitudes, smarts and hearts, and a strong feedback culture that supports your development

• Flexibility and a strong commitment to work-life balance in an international setting with opportunities for growth

• A bonus scheme that includes every employee when we have good results

• A great canteen, massage service at our Odense office and social events throughout the year

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of bringing better deals of medicine to millions.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

Job location

Odense, Denmark. You will work from our Odense office 2–3 days a week to be close to the majority of your stakeholders. We welcome candidates based outside Denmark who can commit to this whether by commuting or relocating (relocation support and expenses will be covered by Orifarm).

Application deadline

As soon as possible.

You will take cleaning from design through commissioning, qualification and validation, working closely with engineering, automation, validation and manufacturing colleagues. Your work helps build production capacity that is flexible and ready for future growth, supporting people living with serious chronic diseases around the world.

What you’ll bring

Who you’ll work with

Your closest partners will be engineering, automation and validation specialists, along with project teams, contractors and manufacturing colleagues, both internal and external. The team works across disciplines, functions and geographies, and shares knowledge to keep these strategic projects on track.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to influence technical decisions and contribute to the successful delivery of a facility that supports Novo’s future growth. You will work with state-of-the-art technologies and ambitious sustainability targets, and build new skills through hands-on experience in a large-scale pharmaceutical project.

You will be supported to perform at your best in a team where knowledge sharing and continuous learning are part of daily work, and where your voice is heard.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Start now

jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026 – Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU), Copenhagen, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Position:

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is seeking candidates for its newly established Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026. These internship opportunities are on-site at SCMU’s office in the UN City headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark.

SCMU offers specialized functional streams aligned with its operational needs, including:

• Data & Analytics

• Logistics & Supply Chain

• Procurement & Business

• Humanitarian Supplies

• Supply Chain & Customer Service

• Governance, Risk & Compliance

• Communications

• Human Resources

• Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

• Administration & Business

To ensure effective team integration and maximize the value of the internship, candidates must be logistically and financially prepared to undertake full-time, on-site work in Copenhagen for the duration of the internship.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.  UNFPA’s strategic plan (2026-2029), reaffirms the relevance of the current strategic direction of UNFPA and focuses on three transformative results: to end preventable maternal deaths; end unmet need for family planning; and end gender-based violence and harmful practices. These results capture our strategic commitments on accelerating progress towards realizing the ICPD and SDGs in the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. Our strategic plan calls upon UN Member States, organizations and individuals to “build forward better”, while addressing the negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on women’s and girls’ access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, recover lost gains and realize our goals.

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is self-funded and was made operational in January 2022. It is tasked with ensuring that UNFPA is able to effectively and efficiently support the delivery of life-saving reproductive health products and other programme supplies to the end user when and where they are needed. To achieve this, it is important to strengthen the capacity of governments and implementing partners to ensure coordination, end-to-end visibility and accountability on all supply chain and logistics management related activities, in particular for programme supplies, across all UNFPA programmes.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results.

Eligibility:

Educational requirements

a. Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year;

b. Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher);

c. Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or

d. Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Other eligibility requirements

e. Demonstrate interest in the field of development;

f.  Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and

g. Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds.

An individual whose father, mother, son, daughter, brother or sister is a UNFPA staff member is not eligible for an internship with UNFPA.

Required Competencies:

Values:

• Exemplifying integrity,

• Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,

• Embracing cultural diversity,

• Embracing change

Core Competencies:

• Achieving results,

• Being accountable,

• Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,

• Thinking analytically and strategically,

• Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,

Financial Support:

Interns who do not receive financial support from an outside party (such as an academic institution, university, government) are eligible to receive a stipend as a contribution towards living expenses. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. The stipend is normally paid in local currency at the end of each month.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA's workforce - click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants' bank accounts.

jobs.description:
Do you want to start your research career by making industrial heat clean, flexible and affordable? At DTU Construct you will work at the forefront of technologies key to decarbonizing industries: high-temperature heat pumps and high-temperature thermal energy storage.We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps and thermal energy storage. Your project will develop new Carnot Battery technologies: systems that combine heat pumps based on high temperature thermodynamic cycles together with high-temperature thermal energy storage, such as molten salts and dual-media packed beds. These systems will deliver clean process heat while also giving industry flexibility on the electricity market.Supervision: Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson with industrial secondments. Responsibilities and qualificationsYour overall goal will be to find out how industrial high temperature heat pumps can benefit from integrated thermal energy storage by developing new cost-effective, high-performance hybrid configurations. You will work with fellow doctoral candidates across the network and with industrial partners in Denmark and abroad.Your main tasks will be:
• Develop and Design new architectures comprising cycles using natural working fluids and thermal energy storage, optimised for efficiency, cost, and fast response to electricity price signals
• Carry out multi-objective optimisation and dynamic system analysis of alternative layouts
• Validate results by carrying out experiments and data comparison during industrial secondments, turning the results into innovations with real-world impact (e.g. patents, future commercial solutions) 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.You have:
• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. We offerDTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.Salary and appointment termsThe appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027, or according to mutual agreement. You can read more about career paths at DTU here.Further informationFurther information may be obtained from Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli, adrsc@dtu.dk and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson, acerl@dtu.dk. You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:
• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on high-temperature heat pumps combined with thermal energy storage (e.g. Carnot Batteries): select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making.You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development.
